units.title: Estimation and rounding
units.description: This unit helps pupils understand rounding to different decimal places, and significant figures. Pupils will also learn how to truncate numbers and understand the contexts in which these skills are useful. The unit ends will an exploration of rounding and inequality errors.

lessons.title: Checking understanding of rounding
lessons.outcome: I can round to the nearest 100 or 10 or whole number or to 1 or 2 decimal places.
keyLearningPoints: Any number can be rounded to the nearest 10, 100 or 1000.
A number with one or more decimal places can be rounded to the nearest whole number.
A number with two or more decimal places can be rounded to one decimal place.
A number with three or more decimal places can be rounded to two decimal places.

keywords.definition: To change a number into another number that is approximately the same value but is easier to work with. E.g. round 561 to the nearest 10 is 560.

starterQuiz.stem: Jun writes 378 as approximately 400.  Jun has written it to the {{ }} hundred.
starterQuiz.hint: What column is the only non-zero digit in?
starterQuiz.feedback: 378 is between 300 and 400, but it is closer to 400.  378 to the nearest hundred is 400.

starterQuiz.stem: Which digit is in the thousands column in 43 978? {{}}
starterQuiz.hint: Take a look at your place value grid.
starterQuiz.feedback: This number starts in the ten thousands column.  Therefore, the second digit is in the thousands column which is the 3.

starterQuiz.stem: Which digit is in the tens column in 3492? {{}}
starterQuiz.hint: Take a look at your place value grid.
starterQuiz.feedback: This number starts in the thousands column.  Therefore, the third digit is in the tens column which is the 9.

starterQuiz.stem: In the number 57.392, which column is the 3 in?
starterQuiz.hint: Take a look at your place value grid.
starterQuiz.feedback: The 3 is in the first column after the decimal point which is the tenths column.

starterQuiz.stem: In the number 57.392, which column is the 2 in?
starterQuiz.hint: Take a look at your place value grid.
starterQuiz.feedback: The 2 is in the third column after the decimal point which is the thousandths column.

starterQuiz.stem: The number that is halfway between 3 and 4 is {{}}
starterQuiz.hint: Try thinking of the question as "what is halfway between £3 and £4?"
starterQuiz.feedback: Halfway between 3 and 4 is 3.5

exitQuiz.stem: Rounding means to change a number into another number that is {{ }} the same value but is easier to work with.
exitQuiz.hint: Rounding does not change the value of the number by a significant amount.
exitQuiz.feedback: Rounding does not change the value of the number by a significant amount.  Therefore, the rounded value is approximately the same value.

exitQuiz.stem: 13 745 rounded to the nearest thousand is {{}}.
exitQuiz.hint: Identify the number in the thousands column and then either use a number line or place value grid.
exitQuiz.feedback: 3 is in the thousands column, and the digit in the hundreds column (the column to the right) is 5 or more.  Therefore, you round up to 14 000.

exitQuiz.stem: Lucas buys a t-shirt costing £14.75.  What is the cost of the t-shirt to the nearest pound?
exitQuiz.hint: Round to the nearest one.  Identify the number in the ones column and then either use a number line or place value grid.
exitQuiz.feedback: 4 is in the ones column, the digit in the tenths column (the column to the right) is 5 or more.  Therefore, you round up to £15.00 or £15.

exitQuiz.stem: Round 178.358 to 1 decimal place.
exitQuiz.hint: Identify the number in the first decimal place (tenths column) and then either use a number line or place value grid.
exitQuiz.feedback: 3 is in the tenths column, the digit in the hundredths column (the column to the right) is 5 or more.  Therefore, you round up to 178.4

exitQuiz.stem: Round 17.3095 to 2 decimal places.
exitQuiz.hint: Identify the number in the second decimal place (hundredths column) and then either use a number line or place value grid.
exitQuiz.feedback: 0 is in the hundredths column, and the digit in the thousandths column (the column to the right) is 5 or more.  Therefore, you round up to 17.31

exitQuiz.stem: Round 109.3978 to 2 decimal places.
exitQuiz.hint: Identify the number in the second decimal place (hundredths column) and then either use a number line or place value grid.
exitQuiz.feedback: 9 is in the hundredths column, the digit in the thousandths column (the column to the right) is 5 or more.  Therefore, you round up to 109.40.  Remember to include the zero in the hundredths column.

lessons.title: Securing understanding of rounding
lessons.outcome: I can recognise when values have been rounded and state sensible suggestions of what the unrounded value could have been.
keyLearningPoints: When a number has been rounded you can make conjectures about what the unrounded number could have been.
Rounding can be very useful in real life contexts particularly measure.
When working in some real life contexts you are often working to a certain degree of accuracy.
Numbers in different contexts will be rounded to a different degree of accuracy (e.g. distance when walking or flying).

keywords.definition: A (mathematical) statement that is thought to be true but has not been proved yet.
A degree of accuracy shows how precise a number or measurement is.  E.g. to the nearest cm, nearest 10, 1 d.p., etc.

starterQuiz.stem: Rounding means to change a number into another number that is approximately the same value, but is {{ }} to work with.
starterQuiz.hint: Often you round numbers to make estimates of calculations, which can be done quickly in your head.
starterQuiz.feedback: Rounding gives an approximate value that is easier to work with.

starterQuiz.stem: 27 345 rounded to the nearest thousand is {{ }}.
starterQuiz.hint: Identify the number in the thousands column and then either use a number line or place value grid.
starterQuiz.feedback: 7 is in the thousands column, and the digit in the hundreds column (the column to the right) is less than 5.  Therefore, you round down to 27 000.

starterQuiz.stem: Lucas buys a t-shirt costing £22.25.  What is the cost of the t-shirt to the nearest pound?
starterQuiz.hint: Round to the nearest one.  Identify the number in the ones column and then either use a number line or place value grid.
starterQuiz.feedback: 2 is in the ones column, and the digit in the tenths column (the column to the right) is less than 5.  Therefore, you round down to £22.00

starterQuiz.stem: Round 305.7298 to 1 decimal place.
starterQuiz.hint: Identify the number in the first decimal place (tenths column) and then either use a number line or place value grid.
starterQuiz.feedback: 7 is in the tenths column, and the digit in the hundredths column (the column to the right) is less than 5.  Therefore, you round down to 305.7

starterQuiz.stem: Round 0.06921 to 2 decimal places.
starterQuiz.hint: Identify the number in the second decimal place (hundredths column) and then either use a number line or place value grid.
starterQuiz.feedback: 6 is in the hundredths column, and the digit in the thousandths column (the column to the right) is 5 or greater.  Therefore, you round up to 0.07

starterQuiz.stem: Round 12.89528 to 2 decimal places.
starterQuiz.hint: Identify the number in the second decimal place (hundredths column) and then either use a number line or place value grid.
starterQuiz.feedback: 9 is in the hundredths column and the digit in the thousandths column (the column to the right) is 5.  Therefore, you round up to 12.90.  Remember to include the zero in the hundredths column.

exitQuiz.stem: Degree of accuracy shows how {{ }} a rounded number or measurement is.
exitQuiz.hint: The values have been rounded, therefore, they are not the true value.
exitQuiz.feedback: The degree of accuracy shows how precise a number or measurement is.  It is used when a rounded figure is used instead of the exact figure.

exitQuiz.stem: Select the numbers that do not round to 14 000 when rounded to the nearest thousand.
exitQuiz.hint: Identify the digit in the thousands column in each of the choices and use a number line or place value grid to round and determine whether the rounded value is 14 000
exitQuiz.feedback: Choice 1, 13 450: the digit in the hundreds column is less than 5, so it rounds down to 13 000.  Choice 5, 14 550: the digit in the hundreds column is 5, so it rounds up to 15 000

exitQuiz.stem: 54 528 is 54 500 to the nearest ...
exitQuiz.hint: Start be looking at which of the choices are factors of 54 500
exitQuiz.feedback: Only 10 and 100 are factors of 54 500.  Rounding 54 528 to the nearest 10 gives 54 530 and 54 528 to the nearest 100 gives 54 500

exitQuiz.stem: Jacob estimates how many pieces of pasta are in a bowl of pasta. Which of the following is the most appropriate degree of accuracy in this situation?
exitQuiz.hint: Estimate the number of pieces of pasta you think would be in a bag of pasta and this should help you decide.
exitQuiz.feedback: There would be fewer than 100 pieces of pasta in a bowl and you don't need to know the exact number.  Therefore, the answer is nearest ten.

exitQuiz.stem: A charity is sending thank you cards to 160 people who have made donations.  Stamps come in books of 12.  How many books of stamps do they need to buy?
exitQuiz.hint: Calculate 160 ÷ 12 and consider the appropriate degree of accuracy.
exitQuiz.feedback: 160 ÷ 12 = 13.333... . Even though 13.3333... generally rounds down to 13, the charity has to buy 14 books to have enough stamps.

exitQuiz.stem: Izzy buys a large bag of 75 chocolate bars.  She puts them into boxes of 4 to sell for charity.  How many boxes will Izzy have to sell?
exitQuiz.hint: Calculate 75 ÷ 4 and consider the appropriate degree of accuracy.
exitQuiz.feedback: 75 ÷ 4 = 18.75 even though 18.75 generally rounds up to 19, Izzy can only make 18 complete boxes.

lessons.title: Rounding to three decimal places
lessons.outcome: I can round numbers to three decimal places.
keyLearningPoints: Numbers with any number of decimal places can be represented on a number line.
Rounding is useful to estimate numbers to a degree of accuracy.
Numbers can be rounded to 3 decimal places.
Knowing a number has been rounded means you can give examples of what the unrounded number might have been.

starterQuiz.stem: What is a conjecture?
starterQuiz.hint: This is an example of a conjecture:  The girls in a class had better test scores than the boys.
starterQuiz.feedback: A conjecture is a mathematical statement that is thought to be true and has not yet been proven.

starterQuiz.stem: Select the numbers that round to 23 000 when rounded to the nearest thousand.
starterQuiz.hint: Identify the digit in the thousands column in each of the choices and use a number line or place value grid to round and determine whether the rounded value is 23 000
starterQuiz.feedback: Choice 1, 22 475: the digit in the hundreds column is less than 5, so it rounds down to 22 000.  Choice 5, 23 675: the digit in  the hundreds column is greater than 5, so it rounds up to 24 000

starterQuiz.stem: 134 578 is 135 000 to the nearest ...
starterQuiz.hint: Start by looking at which of the choices are factors of 135 000
starterQuiz.feedback: Only 10, 100 and 1000 are factors of 135 000.  Rounding 134 578 to the nearest 10 gives 134 580, 134 578 to the nearest 100 gives 134 600 and 134 578 to the nearest 1000 gives 135 000

starterQuiz.stem: Laura estimates how many cars are in a car park. Which of the following is the most appropriate degree of accuracy in this situation?
starterQuiz.hint: Estimate the number of cars you think would be in the car park and this should help you decide.
starterQuiz.feedback: The number of cars in a car park is likely to be in the hundreds.

starterQuiz.stem: A charity is sending thank you cards to 110 people who have made donations.  Stamps come in books of 12.  How many books of stamps do they need to buy?
starterQuiz.hint: Calculate 110 ÷ 12 and consider the appropriate degree of accuracy.
starterQuiz.feedback: 110 ÷ 12 = 9.1666... . Even though 9.16666... generally rounds to 9, the charity has to buy 10 books to have enough stamps.

starterQuiz.stem: Izzy buys a large bag of 50 chocolate bars.  She puts them into boxes of 4 to sell for charity.  How many boxes will Izzy have to sell?
starterQuiz.hint: Calculate 50 ÷ 4 and consider the appropriate degree of accuracy.
starterQuiz.feedback: 50 ÷ 4 = 12.5. Even though 12.5 generally rounds to 13, Izzy can only make 12 complete boxes.

exitQuiz.stem: 1.643 is 1.6 to one {{ }} place.
exitQuiz.hint: What are digits after the decimal point called?
exitQuiz.feedback: When rounding to one digit after the decimal point, you are rounding to one decimal place.

exitQuiz.stem: The midpoint of 2.2 and 2.3 is {{}}.
exitQuiz.hint: If you are not sure, find half of the sum of the 2 values.
exitQuiz.feedback: (2.2 + 2.3) ÷ 2 = 2.25. So, 2.25 is halfway between the two values.

exitQuiz.stem: The midpoint of 2.268 and 2.269 is {{}}.
exitQuiz.hint: If you are not sure, find half of the sum of the 2 values.
exitQuiz.feedback: (2.268 + 2.269) ÷ 2 = 2.2685. So, 2.2685 is halfway between the two values.

exitQuiz.stem: Round 14.5682 to 3 decimal places.
exitQuiz.hint: Identify the digit in the third decimal place and then use a number line or place value grid to round 14.5682 to three decimal places.
exitQuiz.feedback: The digit in the third decimal place is in the thousandths column. Therefore, you round to the nearest thousandth.  The digit in the ten thousandths column is less than 5, so round down to 14.568

exitQuiz.stem: Round 0.0459 to three decimal places.
exitQuiz.hint: Identify the digit in the third decimal place and then use a number line or place value grid to round 0.0459 to three decimal places.
exitQuiz.feedback: The digit in the third decimal place is in the thousandths column. The digit in the ten thousandths column is greater than 5, so rounds up to 0.046

exitQuiz.stem: Round 172.0998 to three decimal places.
exitQuiz.hint: Identify the digit in the third decimal place and then use a number line or place value grid to round 172.0998 to three decimal places.
exitQuiz.feedback: 9 is in the thousandths column, the digit in the ten thousandths column (the column to the right) is greater than 5. Therefore, you round up to 172.100. Remember to include the zeros in the hundredths and thousandths columns.

lessons.outcome: I can round numbers to any number of decimal places.
keyLearningPoints: Numbers with  any number of decimal places can be represented on a number line.
Any number can be rounded to a given number of decimal places.
It is possible to identify the most suitable number of decimal places from the context.
It can be useful to think about what the biggest and smallest values of a number rounded in context were.

exitQuiz.stem: If a degree of accuracy is not stated in a question that you are answering, you should use the {{ }} degree of accuracy as the values in the question.

exitQuiz.stem: Round 5.072 to two decimal places.

exitQuiz.stem: Calculate the cost of carpeting this area. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Find the area of the rectangle.  Multiply the area by the cost per metre and then round your answer to 2 d.p.

exitQuiz.stem: 3 friends go out for lunch and spend £28.  They pay the same amount each.  What is the smallest amount they each pay to cover the cost of the bill?
exitQuiz.hint: Divide the total cost by 3.  Take care when rounding to ensure you have paid the entire bill.
exitQuiz.feedback: 28 ÷ 3 = 9.33333..., round up to £9.34.  If you round to 2 d.p., you only have £27.99.  Therefore you need to round up to £9.34

lessons.title: Rounding integers to one significant figure
lessons.outcome: I can round integers to one significant figure.
keyLearningPoints: It is possible to use rounding and place value to know the size of a number without knowing the actual number.
The first non-zero digit of a number is the first significant figure.
You can identify the place value of the first significant figure.
A number can be located on a number line and numbers to 1 significant figure either side of it represented.
Any integer can be rounded to one significant figure and a number line can help with this.

keywords.definition: Significant figures are the digits in a number that contribute to the accuracy of the number. The first significant figure is the first non-zero digit.
To change a number into another number that is approximately the same value but is easier to work with. E.g. round 561 to the nearest 10 is 560.

starterQuiz.stem: A degree of {{ }} shows how precise a number or measurement is. Examples are: to the nearest cm, to the nearest 10, to 1 s.f. and 2 d.p.
starterQuiz.hint: The number or measurement has been rounded.
starterQuiz.feedback: A degree of accuracy shows how precise a number or measurement is. For example, the length of a room might be measured to the nearest centimetre.

starterQuiz.stem: 3 friends go out for lunch and spend £31.  They pay the same amount each.  What is the smallest amount they each pay to cover the cost of the bill?

exitQuiz.stem: Round 654 023 to one significant figure.

starterQuiz.hint: Start counting from the first non-zero digit.  Zeros are significant after the first non-zero digit.

starterQuiz.stem: Round 8096.564 to 3 significant figures.
starterQuiz.hint: Identify which column the third significant figure is in.  This will tell you what to round the number to using your number line or place value grid.
starterQuiz.feedback: The third significant figure is in the tens column.  The digit in the ones column (the column to the right) is greater than 5, therefore round up to 8100

exitQuiz.stem: The first {{ }} figure is the first non-zero digit in a number.
exitQuiz.hint: It is the most important digit in the number in terms of the size of the number.
exitQuiz.feedback: The first significant figure is the first non-zero digit.

exitQuiz.stem: Match each number to the correct statement.
exitQuiz.hint: The first significant figure is the first non-zero digit.
exitQuiz.feedback: The first significant figure is the first non-zero digit in each number.

exitQuiz.feedback: The second significant figure is in the ten thousandths column. The digit in the hundred thousandths column (the column to the right) is less than 5, therefore round down to 0.0075

exitQuiz.stem: Round 0.006083 to 3 significant figures.
exitQuiz.hint: Identify which column the third significant figure is in.  This will tell you what to round the number to using your number line or place value grid.

exitQuiz.stem: Round 0.03098 to 3 significant figures.

lessons.title: Degrees of accuracy
lessons.outcome: I can appreciate what is meant by a suitable degree of accuracy.
keyLearningPoints: When calculating often 3 significant figures is the required degree of accuracy.
When working with integers in context different degrees of accuracy may be appropriate.
When working with decimals in context different degrees of accuracy may be appropriate.

keywords.definition: A degree of accuracy shows how precise a number or measurement is.  E.g. to the nearest cm, nearest 10, 1 s.f., etc

starterQuiz.stem: A degree of accuracy shows how precise a number or {{ }} is.  For example, to the nearest cm, to the nearest 10 or to 1 significant figure.
starterQuiz.hint: What are gram, kilogram, millimetre, centimetre and litre all units of?
starterQuiz.feedback: A degree of accuracy shows how precise a number or measurement is. For example, you might measure the length  of a room to the nearest centimetre.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each number to the correct statement.
starterQuiz.hint: The first significant figure is the first non-zero digit.
starterQuiz.feedback: The first significant figure is the first non-zero digit in a number. Read the digits from left to right.

starterQuiz.stem: Round 0.0434 to 2 significant figures.
starterQuiz.hint: Identify which column the second significant figure is in.  This will tell you what to round the number to using your number line or place value grid.
starterQuiz.feedback: The second significant figure is in the thousandths column.  The digit in the ten thousandths column (the column to the right) is less than 5, therefore round down to 0.043

starterQuiz.stem: Round 0.007006 to 3 significant figures.
starterQuiz.hint: Identify which column the third significant figure is in.  This will tell you what to round the number to using your number line or place value grid.
starterQuiz.feedback: The third significant figure is in the hundred thousandths column.  The digit in the millionths column (the column to the right) is greater than 5, therefore round up to 0.00701

starterQuiz.stem: Round 0.0896 to 2 significant figures.
starterQuiz.hint: Identify which column the second significant figure is in.  This will tell you what to round the number to using your number line or place value grid.

starterQuiz.stem: Round 0.00600736 to 3 significant figures.

exitQuiz.stem: A {{ }} of accuracy shows how precise a number or measurement is.
exitQuiz.hint: This is also a measure of angles.
exitQuiz.feedback: A degree of accuracy shows how precise a number or measurement is. For example, the degree of accuracy of a measurement may be to the nearest centimetre.

exitQuiz.stem: The average size of a secondary school in 2024 was 1050.  This number is most likely to have been rounded to which degree of accuracy?
exitQuiz.hint: Look at the column that the last non-zero digit appears in.
exitQuiz.feedback: The last non-zero digit is in the tens column. Therefore, it is likely to have been rounded to the nearest ten.

exitQuiz.stem: The average temperature in the UK in 2024 was 10.93°C.  This is most likely to have been rounded to which degree of accuracy?
exitQuiz.hint: Look at the column that the last non-zero digit appears in.
exitQuiz.feedback: The last non-zero digit is in the second decimal place.  Therefore, it is likely to have been rounded to 2 decimal places.

exitQuiz.stem: Match each situation to the most appropriate degree of accuracy.
exitQuiz.hint: Consider the relative size of each of the likely numbers.
exitQuiz.feedback: Putting the options in order from smallest to largest:  buckets, school, village, Mount Everest.  Putting the answers in order from smallest to largest: integer, ten, hundred, thousand.

match.right: Buckets of water to fill a paddling pool
Number of pupils at a primary school
Number of people living in a village
Height of Mount Everest in metres

exitQuiz.stem: Use the exchange rate £1:$1.27 to convert $6.95 into pounds.  Give your answer to an appropriate degree of accuracy.
exitQuiz.hint: Use a ratio table and find the multiplier.
exitQuiz.feedback: £1 × 1.27 = $1.27, the multiplier that takes you from £ to $ is × 1.27.  So, to change dollars into pounds you divide by 1.27.  6.95 ÷ 1.27 = £5.472... . The most appropriate degree of accuracy for money is usually 2 d.p., so the answer is £5.47

exitQuiz.stem: Use your calculator to evaluate $$1.27 - \sqrt{15}\over16.8 + 0.06$$.  Give your answer to an appropriate degree of accuracy.
exitQuiz.hint: Use your scientific calculator, remember to use the fraction button and check that what is on the screen is exactly the same as the question.  An appropriate degree of accuracy will be to the greatest degree of accuracy of the values in the question.
exitQuiz.feedback: The answer on the calculator is $$-0.1543880988$$.  The greatest degree of accuracy in the question is 2 decimal places, which give the answer $$-0.15$$

lessons.title: Estimating numerical calculations
lessons.outcome: I can estimate numerical calculations.
keyLearningPoints: All numbers can be rounded to a given number of significant figures.
Estimating gives you an idea of the size of an answer in context.
To estimate an answer you will often round to one significant figure.
Sometimes it makes sense to round to a different degree of accuracy when making an estimate.

keywords.definition: A quick estimate for a calculation is obtained from using approximate values, often rounded to 1 significant figure.
Significant figures are the digits in a number that contribute to the accuracy of the number.

starterQuiz.stem:
___________ figures are the digits in a number that contribute to the accuracy of the number. 
The first __________ figure is the first non-zero digit.
starterQuiz.hint: All of these words mean the same thing, but what word is missing from the abbreviation s.f.?
starterQuiz.feedback:
Significant figures are the digits in a number that contribute to the accuracy of the number. 
The first significant figure is the first non-zero digit.

starterQuiz.stem: 5689 rounded to 1 s.f. is {{}}.
starterQuiz.hint: When rounding to significant figures, use a place value table to ensure you do not lose the size of the number.
starterQuiz.feedback: Given the first significant figure is in the thousands, you round 5689 up to the nearest thousand.

starterQuiz.stem: 428.62 rounded to 1 s.f. is {{}}.
starterQuiz.hint: When rounding to significant figures, use a place value table to ensure you do not lose the size of the number.
starterQuiz.feedback: Given the first significant figure is in the hundred, we round 428.62 down to the nearest hundred.

starterQuiz.stem: 428.62 rounded to 2 s.f. is {{}}.
starterQuiz.hint: When rounding to significant figures, use a place value table to ensure you do not lose the size of the number. Here you are rounding to 2 s.f. Which position in the place value chart is the second significant figure?
starterQuiz.feedback: Given the second significant figure is in the tens, we round 428.62 up to the nearest ten.

starterQuiz.stem: Sam correctly rounds an integer to the nearest 10. Sam's answer is 80. What could Sam's unrounded integer be?
starterQuiz.hint: Round each number to the nearest 20. If the answer is 80 then it is correct. Drawing a number line may help.
starterQuiz.feedback: Draw a number line with 80 in the centre and 70 to the left of 80 and 90 to the right of 80. Plot each number to see which is closer to 80.

starterQuiz.stem: Laura correctly rounds a number to 1 significant figure. Her answer is 8. What could Laura's unrounded number be?
starterQuiz.hint: Round each number to the nearest integer. If the answer is 8 then it is correct. Drawing a number line may help.
starterQuiz.feedback: Draw a number line with 8 in the centre and 7 to the left of 8 and 9 to the right of 8. Plot the number to see which is closer to 8.

exitQuiz.stem: A quick {{ }} for a calculation is obtained from using approximate values, often rounded to 1 significant figure.
exitQuiz.hint: The mathematical word used when you approximate a number, with no guessing involved.
exitQuiz.feedback: A quick estimate for a calculation is obtained from using approximate values, often rounded to 1 significant figure.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the following is the most accurate estimate calculation for 856 × 465?
exitQuiz.hint: Rounding to a certain degree of accuracy ensure your estimate calculation is appropriate. Can you see the degree of accuracy used?
exitQuiz.feedback: A good estimate would be $$900\times500$$ as each number has been rounded to 1 s.f.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the following are good, quick estimate calculations for 578 ÷ 1.785?
exitQuiz.hint: Rounding to a certain degree of accuracy ensure your estimate calculation is appropriate. Can you see the degree of accuracy used?
exitQuiz.feedback: The good estimates have rounded to the nearest 10, or 1 s.f. The use of 578 ÷ 1.8 will give the most accurate answer, but estimation must be efficient, accurate and speedy.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the following are good, quick estimate calculations for $${4.56\times8.95} \over {7.65}$$?
exitQuiz.hint: Rounding to a certain degree of accuracy ensure your estimate calculation is appropriate. Remember, estimation must be efficient, accurate and speedy.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$${5\times10} \over {10}$$ is good as it is rounded to the nearest 5. $${5\times10} \over {8}$$ and $${5\times8} \over {8}$$ are good because the product of the numerator can be quickly divided by 8.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the following are correct estimates for $${18.96\times2.15} \over {0.546}$$?
exitQuiz.hint: All of the rounding is correct and the estimate calculations are correct too, but the final answer is incorrect.
exitQuiz.feedback: Dividing by a number is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal. So, dividing by 0.5 is the same as multiplying by 2.

exitQuiz.stem: Given Alex is of average secondary school pupil height. An estimate of the height of the elephant is {{ }} m.  Give your answer to 1 decimal place. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The average height of a secondary school pupil is 1.5 m. How can you use this to help you estimate the height of the elephant?
exitQuiz.feedback: Any answer between 2.8 m and 3.2 m inclusive. You may see that doubling Alex's height is the approximate height of the elephant.

lessons.title: Checking by estimating
lessons.outcome: I can estimate and check if solutions to problems are of the correct magnitude.
keyLearningPoints: Estimation should give you an idea of the size of an answer.
It is useful to estimate the answer to calculations so you can check your answers make sense.
Errors in calculations can be found by using estimates.

keywords.definition: Significant figures are the digits in a number that contribute to the accuracy of the number.
A quick estimate for a calculation is obtained from using approximate values, often rounded to 1 significant figure.

starterQuiz.stem: Significant figures are the digits in a number that contribute to the accuracy of the number.  The first significant figure is the first __________ digit.
starterQuiz.hint: Think about how you would round 0.00498. What is the first significant digit?
starterQuiz.feedback: Significant figures are the digits in a number that contribute to the accuracy of the number. The first significant figure is the first non-zero digit in a number.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the following are good estimate calculations for 989 × 213.4?
starterQuiz.hint: Rounding to a certain degree of accuracy ensure your estimate calculation is appropriate. Can you see the degree of accuracy used?
starterQuiz.feedback: All except $9 × 2 are good estimates. As the 989 has been rounded to 1000, this number can be multiplied easily.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the following are good, quick estimate calculations for 432.4 ÷ 1.85?
starterQuiz.hint: Rounding to a certain degree of accuracy ensure your estimate calculation is appropriate. Also, remember the calculation must allow you to make a "quick" estimate too.
starterQuiz.feedback: 400 ÷ 2 is a good estimate, as each number has been rounded to 1 significant figure. 500 ÷ 2 is good estimate too, as 432 has been rounded to the nearest 500 without losing too much accuracy. 400 ÷ 1.85 is not a quick estimate calculation.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the following are correct estimates for $${17.9}\over {0.532}$$?
starterQuiz.hint: All of the rounding is correct and the estimate calculations are correct too, but the final answer is incorrect.
starterQuiz.feedback: Dividing by a number is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal. So, dividing by 0.5 is the same as multiplying by 2.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the following is the correct estimate for $${3.4\times3.92}\over {0.511}$$?
starterQuiz.hint: You are estimating, so the numbers should be rounded. When rounded all the estimate calculations are correct, but pay attention to the final answer.
starterQuiz.feedback: When dividing by a number, it is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal. So, dividing by 0.5 is the same as multiplying by 2. $${3.4\times3.92}\over {0.511}$$ is not an estimate as the numbers have not been rounded.

starterQuiz.stem: Horses and ponies are measured using ‘hands’ as a unit, where the width of the hand is used. This pony has a height of 9 hands. Estimate the height of the pony. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The width of a hand is approximately 10 cm.
starterQuiz.feedback: The width of a hand is approximately 10 cm so 9 hands would give an approximate height of 90 cm.

exitQuiz.stem: Match the following numbers to the correct rounded value.
exitQuiz.hint: Significant figures are the digits in a number that contribute to the accuracy of the number.  When rounding to decimal places, you include the number of decimal places stated in the degree of accuracy.
exitQuiz.feedback: 8934.894 = 9000 (1 s.f.) and 8934.894 = 8900 (2 s.f.). You identify the place value column to the right of the relevant significant figure and round up or down.  8934.894=8934.9 (1 d.p.) as you only include 1 digit to the right of the decimal place.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the following are sensible measurements for the lengths of an average house? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Ensure you know your metric conversions: 1 cm = 10 mm, 1 m = 100 cm and 1 km = 1000 m.
exitQuiz.feedback: Front: 844 cm = 8.44 m , Side:  596 cm = 5.96. These are the same lengths and good, sensible measurements for an average house.

exitQuiz.stem: A bookshop wants to buy the new sci-fi books to sell in their store. The bookshop has £789 and each book costs £18.99. Select the correct estimate for the number of books the bookshop can buy.
exitQuiz.hint: You do not even need to work out all the answer here as some of the answers are unreasonable as they are far too big or small.
exitQuiz.feedback: Working it out $${800} \over {20}$$ = $${40\times20} \over {1\times 20}$$ = $$\frac{40}{1}\times\frac{20}{20}=40$$. $${800} \over {18.99}$$ is not a good estimate as you would probably reach for your calculator to work this out!

exitQuiz.stem: Select the approximate answer to $$\frac{8}{15}\times\ 9$$.
exitQuiz.hint: $$$\frac{8}{15}$$ is more than half given 8 is more than half of 15. Therefore the answer should be a little more than half of 9
exitQuiz.feedback: 5 is the answer as $$\frac{8}{15}$$ is slightly more than half, so slightly more than half of 9 is 5

exitQuiz.stem: A bicycle costs £18.99 for 1 week's hire. Which of the following shows the estimate to hire 6 bicycles for 4 weeks?
exitQuiz.hint: Looking at the final estimate you may be able to exclude certain amounts as they seem unreasonable.
exitQuiz.feedback: The most reasonable amounts would be £480 and £240, so you only need to check these two. £20 × 6 × 4 = £120 ×  4 = £480. So, best estimate is £480.

exitQuiz.stem: Jun buys paper £3.25, USB £$$\square$$, stamps £4.95, crisps £0.85, staples £2.30 and plug £1.99. He pays with a £20 note and receives about £2 back in change. Estimate the cost of the USB.
exitQuiz.hint: Round the numbers to the appropriate degree of accuracy and subtract from £18 (This is how much all the items cost). This will give you the price of the USB.
exitQuiz.feedback: An example rounding calculation is 18 − 3 − 5 − 1 − 2 − 2 = 5, so the price of the USB should be approximately £5.

lessons.title: Truncating
lessons.outcome: I can estimate a value by truncating to a given degree of accuracy.
keyLearningPoints: When estimating ages, it is convention to use truncation.
Truncation can be used to estimate any integer to a given accuracy.
Truncation can be used to estimate any number to a given accuracy.

keywords.definition: Truncation is the simplifying a number by 'cutting off' one or more of the digits and replacing them with zeros if necessary to preserve place value.
A degree of accuracy shows how precise a number or measurement is.

starterQuiz.stem: __________ shows how precise a number or measurement is.
starterQuiz.hint: Examples of this are "to the nearest cm", "nearest 10", 1 s.f, etc.
starterQuiz.feedback: A degree of accuracy shows how precise a number or measurement is.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each number to its rounded value.
starterQuiz.hint: Significant figures are the digits in a number that contribute to the accuracy of the number. When rounding to decimal places, you include the number of decimal places stated in the degree of accuracy.
starterQuiz.feedback: 323 = 320 (2 s.f.) as the 2nd significant figure is in the tens, so you are rounding to the nearest 10. 294.82 = 294.8 (1 d.p.) as you are rounding to 1 decimal place. 294.829 = 294.83 (2 d.p.) as you are rounding to the nearest hundredth.

starterQuiz.stem: A square plot of grass has a length of 2.89 m to 2 decimal places. Select the correct estimate for the area of the square grass plot.
starterQuiz.hint: The area of a square is length × length. What should you approximate the length of 2.89 m to?
starterQuiz.feedback: 3 × 3 = 9 m² is the area. If you were summing the lengths, this would give the perimeter.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each number to its rounded value.
starterQuiz.hint: Significant figures are the digits in a number that contribute to the accuracy of the number. The first significant figure is the first non-zero digit.
starterQuiz.feedback: When rounding to significant figures, remember the first significant figure is the first non-zero digit. For example, 0.00038903 has 3 as the first significant figure.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the following are correct, quick estimate calculations for $${4.56\times8.95} \over {0.498}$$?
starterQuiz.hint: All of the rounding is correct and the estimate calculations are correct too, but the final answer is incorrect.
starterQuiz.feedback: When dividing by a number, it is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal. So, dividing by 0.5 is the same as multiplying by 2.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each calculation to its correct approximate answer.
starterQuiz.hint: Dividing by a number is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal.
starterQuiz.feedback: Dividing by 0.1 = $$\div\frac{1}{10}= \times10$$. Dividing by 0.5 = $$\div\frac{1}{2}= \times2$$. Dividing by 0.2 = $$\div\frac{1}{5}= \times5$$.

exitQuiz.stem: __________ is the simplifying a number by 'cutting off' one or more of the digits and replacing them with zeros if necessary to preserve place value.
exitQuiz.hint: This word derives from a Latin word “truncare”, which means "to shorten"
exitQuiz.feedback: Truncation is the simplifying of a number by 'cutting off' one or more of the digits and replacing them with zeros if necessary to preserve place value.

exitQuiz.stem: Match each number with its truncated value to 1 significant figure.
exitQuiz.hint: A place value chart may help to ensure you "cut off" yet preserve the magnitude of the number.
exitQuiz.feedback: When truncating, it is important to preserve the value and replace with zeros where necessary. You do not need zeros after the decimal point.

exitQuiz.stem: Truncate 49.999999 to 3 significant figures. Select the correct response.
exitQuiz.hint: A place value chart may help to ensure you "cut off" yet preserve the magnitude of the number.
exitQuiz.feedback: Laura is correct. Remember you are simply "cutting off" from the third significant figure. Jun has rounded to 3 s.f., Andeep has rounded to 3 d.p. and Aisha has rounded to 1 s.f.

exitQuiz.stem: Jacob thinks of a number. Truncated to 1 s.f. Jun's number is 100. Jun's number is a multiple of 8 and it is 105 when rounded to the nearest 5.
exitQuiz.hint: The last clue will narrow the answers down more quickly.
exitQuiz.feedback: The number must be in the 100s if it truncates to 100. "105 when rounded to the nearest 5" means the numbers are either 103, 104, 105, 106 or 107. Only one of these is a multiple of 8.

exitQuiz.stem: Match the appropriate treatment of the answer (exact, rounded to truncated) to each context.
exitQuiz.hint: You can work out the answer to $$37\div5$$ and see how the answer will fit the contact of the question.
exitQuiz.feedback: The word "equal strips" requires more accuracy, hence the exact answer is required. Given "a tip" is required, rounding up is required. Given you want to buy as many integer cubes, you must truncate.

match.left: A length of wood 37 m needs to be cut into 5 equal strips.
A meal is £37 and you share it between 5 people and want to give a tip
You have £37 and want to buy as many £5 puzzle cubes as possible.

exitQuiz.stem: In computer science, ‘INT’ or ‘int’ is used to truncate a number so to only give the integers. For example, INT(56/10) has an output of 5. Match each computer instruction to its output.
exitQuiz.hint: Work out the truncated output of each part of the calculation first before summing.

lessons.title: Overestimating vs underestimating
lessons.outcome: I can determine whether calculations using rounding or truncating will give an underestimate or overestimate.
keyLearningPoints: When multiplying or adding, using a value which has been rounded up results in an overestimate.
When dividing or subtracting, using a value which has been rounded up results in an under or overestimate.
Calculations using rounding or truncating will give an over or underestimate.
By careful consideration of the calculation, it is possible to tell if an answer is an over or underestimate.

keywords.definition: An overestimate is an estimate for a calculation which is greater than the exact answer.
An underestimate is an estimate for a calculation which is less than the exact answer.

starterQuiz.stem: __________ are the digits in a number that contribute to the accuracy of the number.  The first significant figure is the first non-zero digit.
starterQuiz.hint: An example is 3009; the first non zero digit is 3 which is in the thousands place.
starterQuiz.feedback: Significant figures are the digits in a number that contribute to the accuracy of the number.  The first significant figure is the first non-zero digit.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the following are good, quick estimate calculations for 577 ÷ 19.57?
starterQuiz.hint: Rounding to a certain degree of accuracy ensure your estimate calculation is appropriate. Can you see the degree of accuracy used?
starterQuiz.feedback: The good estimates have rounded to the nearest 10, or 1 significant figure. The use of 580 ÷ 19.5 or 600 ÷ 19.5 will give the most or a more accurate answer, but estimation must be efficient, accurate and speedy.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the following are a correct estimate for $${11.239\times3.12}\over{0.488}$$?
starterQuiz.hint: All of the rounding is correct and the estimate calculations are correct too, but some have a final answer which is incorrect.
starterQuiz.feedback: Dividing by a number is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal. Dividing by 0.5 is the same as multiplying by 2.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each calculation to its approximate answer.
starterQuiz.hint: Dividing by a number is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal. Dividing by 0.1 = $$\div\frac{1}{10}= \times10$$, Dividing by 0.5 = $$\div\frac{1}{2}= \times2$$,  Dividing by 0.2 = $$\div\frac{1}{5}= \times5$$.

starterQuiz.stem: A square plot of grass has a length of 7.88 m (2 d.p). Select the correct estimate for the area of the square grass plot.
starterQuiz.hint: To work out the area of a square it is length × length. What would you approximate the length of 7.88 m to?
starterQuiz.feedback: 8 × 8 = 64 m² is the area. If you were summing the lengths, this would give the perimeter.

starterQuiz.stem: Izzy thinks of a number. Truncated to 1 s.f., it is 500. Rounded to the nearest 50, it is 600. It is multiple of 5 and a palindrome . All of its digits are prime numbers. Izzy's number is {{}}
starterQuiz.hint: A palindrome is the same number when written in reverse: for example 2662. The digits are primes and when written in reverse it is the same.
starterQuiz.feedback: You know the number must be between 575 and 624. It must be in the 500s as it truncates to 500, therefore 575 to 599. Given the palindromes, you only have 575, 585 and 595; the latter numbers do not have a prime central digit so it must be 575.

exitQuiz.stem: An __________ is an estimate for a calculation which is greater than the exact answer.
exitQuiz.hint: The word "greater than" refers to the type of estimate.
exitQuiz.feedback: An overestimate is an estimate for a calculation which is greater than the exact answer.

exitQuiz.stem: An __________ is an estimate for a calculation which is less than the exact answer.
exitQuiz.hint: The word "less than" refers to the type of estimate.
exitQuiz.feedback: An underestimate is an estimate for a calculation which is less than the exact answer.

exitQuiz.stem: Match each calculation with a calculation that gives its overestimate.
exitQuiz.hint: Round each calculation to 1 s.f and match.
exitQuiz.feedback: All of these answers are overestimates as we have rounded all the numbers in the calculation up using 1 significant figure.

exitQuiz.stem: Match the following calculations which give an overestimated area.
exitQuiz.hint: To work out area of a square, it is length × length. To work out the perimeter of a square it is 4 × length.
exitQuiz.feedback: 7.89 m = 8 m (1 s.f.), 4.67 m = 5 m (1 s.f.) and 0.498 m = 0.5 m (1 s.f.). Therefore using these approximations the area and perimeter can be found.

Perimeter of a square with lengths 7.89 m

Perimeter of a square with lengths 4.67 m

exitQuiz.stem: Match which calculations are an overestimate, underestimate or hard to tell.
exitQuiz.hint: Think if the dividend and divisor is the biggest or smallest in order to decide if it will give an overestimate or underestimate.
exitQuiz.feedback: When dividing, to find an overestimate, the dividend must be as big as possible and the divisor must be as small as possible. To find an underestimate, the dividend must be as small as possible and the divisor must be as big as possible.

exitQuiz.stem: Match which calculations are an overestimate, underestimate or hard to tell.
exitQuiz.hint: Think if the overall dividend and overall divisor is the biggest or smallest in order to decide if it will give an overestimate or underestimate.
exitQuiz.feedback: When dividing, to find an overestimate, the dividend must be as big as possible and the divisor must be as small as possible. To find an underestimate, the dividend must be as small as possible and the divisor must be as big as possible.

lessons.title: Rounding errors
lessons.outcome: I can appreciate the impact of rounding errors when using a calculator (or other technology), and the way that these can be compounded to result in large inaccuracies.
keyLearningPoints: When given a rounded number you can say what the biggest and smallest values of the unrounded number could have been.
When using technology for multi-step calculations you might round along the way.
Rounding too early can cause answers to be incorrect
Repeated rounding in multi-step calculations can lead to large errors.

keywords.definition: Significant figures are the digits in a number that contribute to the accuracy of the number

starterQuiz.stem: An __________ is any positive or negative whole number and zero.
starterQuiz.hint: Which mathematical word should you use to describe whole numbers?
starterQuiz.feedback: An integer is any of the positive or negative whole numbers and zero. Integers are whole numbers.

starterQuiz.stem: Round 384 to the nearest 10.
starterQuiz.hint: Using a place value table can help. What is the digit in the tens column? Does this digit round up?
starterQuiz.feedback: 384 = 380 (to the nearest 10). Given the 4 is in the ones column this is not past half way of the tens so therefore 384 rounds down to 380.

starterQuiz.stem: Round 30.499999 to the nearest integer.
starterQuiz.hint: Using a place value table can help. What is the digit in the ones column? Does this digit round up? Look at the first decimal place to help you.
starterQuiz.feedback: 30.499999 = 30 (to the nearest integer). Given the 4 is in the tenths column this is not past half way of the tenths so therefore 30.499999 rounds down to 30.

starterQuiz.stem: Round 0.0002832 to 1 significant figure.
starterQuiz.hint: When rounding to significant figures, use a place value table to ensure you do not lose the size of the number.
starterQuiz.feedback: Significant figures are the digits in a number that contribute to the accuracy of the number. The first significant figure is the first non-zero digit. The first non-zero digit is 2 and you round up given the 8 in the hundred thousandths column.

starterQuiz.stem: When a number is rounded to the nearest integer it is 4. Select the possible unrounded numbers.
starterQuiz.hint: When rounding to the nearest integer, use a place value table to determine whether to round up or down.
starterQuiz.feedback: Using the place value table, the digit in the tenths column determines the rounding up or down. If the digit is the tenths column is 5 or more, the number is rounded up.

starterQuiz.stem: Round each number in the calculation to 1 significant figure and calculate the answer. $$\frac{89.7+9.58}{5.34+4.58}$$. Give your answer as an integer.
starterQuiz.hint: When rounding to significant figures, use a place value table to ensure you do not lose the size of the number.

exitQuiz.stem: State the smallest and largest integers that round to 680 when rounded to the nearest 10.
exitQuiz.hint: Draw a number line with 680 in the centre and, given the degree of accuracy is 10, put 690 and 670 either side of the 680. Identify the middle of 670 and 680 and the middle of 680 and 690.
exitQuiz.feedback: The answer is "Smallest integer = 675, largest integer = 684" This is because all the integer values between these numbers round to 680 when rounded to the nearest 10.

exitQuiz.stem: State the smallest and largest integers that round to 500 when rounded to the nearest 20.
exitQuiz.hint: Draw a number line with 500 in the centre and, given the degree of accuracy is 20, put 480 and 520 either side of the 500. Identify the middle of 480 and 500 and the middle of 500 and 520.
exitQuiz.feedback: The answer is "Smallest integer = 490, largest integer = 509" This is because all the integer values between these numbers round to 500 when rounded to the nearest 20.

exitQuiz.stem: State the smallest and largest integers that round to 700 when rounded to the nearest 50.
exitQuiz.hint: Draw a number line with 700 in the centre and, given the degree of accuracy is 50, put 750 and 650 either side of the 700. Identify the middle of 650 and 700 and the middle of 700 and 750.
exitQuiz.feedback: The answer is "Smallest integer = 675, largest integer = 724" This is because all the integer values between these numbers round to 700 when rounded to the nearest 50.

exitQuiz.stem: An advert for a magazine says 37 000 people buy the magazine rounded to the nearest 1000. The fewest people who buy the magazine is {{ }} people.
exitQuiz.hint: Draw a number line with 37 000 in the centre and, given the degree of accuracy is 1000, put 37 500 and 36 500 either side of the 37 000. Identify the middle of 36 500 and 37 000 and the middle of 37 000 and 37 500.
exitQuiz.feedback: When rounding 36 500 to the nearest 1000, the answer is 37 000. A place value chart will confirm this.

exitQuiz.stem: A plot of rectangular land measure 2.39 km (1 d.p.) by 5.78 km (1 d.p.). Five pupils work out the area of the plot of land. Whose working out and answer shows the most accurate answer to 1 d.p?
exitQuiz.hint: When calculating answers, use each value to as many decimal places as possible or use the ANS button on the calculator. Ideally, only round in the last stage of working out.
exitQuiz.feedback: Andeep rounded each length, then rounded the answer again causing loss of accuracy. Sofia rounded each length to 1 s.f. first which caused a loss of accuracy. Jun's working out is correct, but incorrectly rounded. Lucas and Laura are correct.

exitQuiz.stem: A large plot of land has an area of 20 km². A small, rectangular lake with lengths 3.254 km by 4.814 km is planned, leaving the rest of the land as grass. Work out the area of grass to 1 d.p.
exitQuiz.hint: When calculating answers, use each value to as many decimal places as possible or use the ANS button on the calculator. Ideally, only round in the last stage of working out.
exitQuiz.feedback: As a complete calculation in the calculator, you can do 20 − 3.254 × 4.814 or work out 3.254 × 4.814 and then 20 − ANS. Both will equal 4.3 km² ( 1 d.p.)

lessons.title: Inequality notation to express error
lessons.outcome: I can calculate possible errors expressed using inequality notation a ≤ x < b.
keyLearningPoints: When given a rounded number you can say what the biggest and smallest values of the unrounded number could have been.
You can use $$a ≤ x < b$$ notation to express the range of values the unrounded number could have taken.

keywords.definition: A range of values where every value in the range estimates to the given value.
An error interval for a number $$x$$ shows the range of possible values of $$x$$.  It is written as an inequality $$a ≤ x < b$$

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the following is not an integer?
starterQuiz.hint: An integer is any of the positive or negative whole numbers and zero.
starterQuiz.feedback: Any number with a non-zero digit in a decimal place is not an integer.

starterQuiz.stem: State the smallest and largest integers that round to 520 when rounded to the nearest 10.
starterQuiz.hint: Drawing a number line with 520 in the centre and, given the degree of accuracy is 10, put 510 and 530 either side of the 520. Identify the middle of 510 and 520 and the middle of 520 and 530.
starterQuiz.feedback: The answer is "Smallest integer = 515, largest integer = 524" This is because all the integer values between these numbers round to 520 when rounded to the nearest 10.

starterQuiz.stem: State the smallest and largest integers that round to 3900 when rounded to the nearest 100.
starterQuiz.hint: Drawing a number line with 3900 in the centre and, given the degree of accuracy is 100, put 3800 and 4000 either side of the 3900. Identify the middle of 3800 and 3900 and the middle of 3900 and 4000.
starterQuiz.feedback: The answer is "Smallest integer = 3850, largest integer = 3949" This is because all the integer values between these numbers round to 3900 when rounded to the nearest 100.

starterQuiz.stem: When does 0.4999999 NOT round to give 0.5?
starterQuiz.hint: A place value chart may help.
starterQuiz.feedback: Using a place value chart 0.4999999 rounded to the nearest integer gives 0.

options.text: When rounded to the nearest integer.

starterQuiz.stem: Work out 3.4 km + 348 m + 6000 cm. Give your answer in metres.
starterQuiz.hint: The conversions you may use are 1 cm = 10 mm, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 km = 1000 m. A conversion table may help.
starterQuiz.feedback: Converting all to metres: 3.4 km + 348 m + 6000 cm = 3400 m + 348 m + 60 m = 3808 m.

starterQuiz.stem: Work out 0.05 km + 6.32 m + 123 cm. Give your answer in centimetres.
starterQuiz.hint: The conversions you may use are 1 cm = 10 mm, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 km = 1000 m. A conversion table may help.
starterQuiz.feedback: Converting all to cm :  0.05 km + 6.32 m + 123 cm = 5000 cm + 632 cm + 123 cm = 5755 cm.

exitQuiz.stem: An error interval for a number $$x$$ shows the range of possible values of $$x$$. It is written as:
exitQuiz.hint: You want to include the number $$a$$, but not include the number $$b$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$ a\leq x < b$$  means you are including the values of $$a$$ as the smallest and not including the value of $$b$$ as the largest.

exitQuiz.stem: When a number is rounded to the nearest integer the result is 8. Identify the correct range for the unrounded number.
exitQuiz.hint: Draw a number line with 8 in the centre and, given the degree of accuracy is an integer, put 7 and 9 either side of the 8. Identify the middle of 7 and 8 and the middle of 8 and 9.
exitQuiz.feedback: The smallest number is 7.5 because when rounding this to the nearest integer it gives 8. The largest is $$8.4 \dot 9$$ as this rounded to the nearest integer gives 8.

exitQuiz.stem: When a number is rounded to the nearest integer the result is 19. Identify the correct range for the unrounded number.
exitQuiz.hint: Draw a number line with 19 in the centre and, given the degree of accuracy is an integer, put 18 and 20 either side of the 19. Identify the middle of 18 and 19 and the middle of 19 and 20.
exitQuiz.feedback: The smallest number is 18.5 because when rounding this to the nearest integer it gives 19. The largest is $$19.4 \dot 9$$ as this rounded to the nearest integer gives 19.

exitQuiz.stem: When a number, $$x$$, is rounded to the nearest integer the result is 8. Identify the error interval for $$x$$.
exitQuiz.hint: Draw a number line with 8 in the centre and, given the degree of accuracy is an integer, put 7 and 9 either side of the 8. Identify the middle of 7 and 8 and the middle of 8 and 9.
exitQuiz.feedback: The smallest number when rounded to the nearest integer is 7.5, but the largest cannot be 8.5 as this rounds to 9. You can show a number which is infinitely smaller than 8.5 but not equal to 8.5 using this error interval: $$7.5\leq x< 8.5$$

exitQuiz.stem: When a number, $$x$$, is rounded to 2 significant figures the result is 7.8. Identify the error interval for $$x$$.
exitQuiz.hint: Draw a number line with 7.8 in the centre and, given the degree of accuracy is 0.1, put 7.7 and 7.9 either side of the 7.8. Identify the middle of 7.7 and 7.8 and the middle of 7.8 and 7.9.
exitQuiz.feedback: The smallest number when rounded to the nearest integer is 7.75, but the largest cannot be 7.85 as this rounds to 7.9. You show a number which is infinitely smaller than 7.85 but not equal to 7.85 using this error interval:  $$ 7.75\leq  x < 7.85$$

exitQuiz.stem: A distance $$x$$ km is given as 2.345 km correct to the nearest metre. Identify the error interval for $$x$$.
exitQuiz.hint: Convert 2.345 km into metres first. This is 2345 m. The question is then asking for the error interval of 2345 m rounded to the nearest integer.
exitQuiz.feedback: The smallest number when rounded to the nearest integer is 2344.5, but the largest cannot be 2345.5 as this rounds to 2346. The error interval is $$ 2344.5\leq x < 2345.5$$. Then convert back to kilometres.

lessons.title: Using inequality notation for errors in calculations
lessons.outcome: I can use inequality notation a ≤ x < b to express errors in calculations.
keyLearningPoints: You can use the values of a and b to see what the biggest and smallest answers to a calculation could have been.
The range of possible answers is the error interval.

keywords.definition: An error interval for a number $$x$$ shows the range of possible values of $$x$$. It is written as an inequality $$a ≤ x < b$$

starterQuiz.stem: An error interval for a number $$x$$ shows the range of possible values of $$x$$. It is written as  $$ a\leq x < b$$. Explain what this means.
starterQuiz.hint: $$$\leq$$ means less than or equal to. $$<$$ means less than.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$ a\leq x < b$$ means you include $$a$$ and not include $$b$$.

options.text: The range of values include $$a$$ and $$b$$
The range of values include $$a$$ and not $$b$$
The range of values includes all the numbers strictly in between $$a$$ and $$b$$
The range of values do not include $$a$$ but include $$b$$

starterQuiz.stem: When a number, $$x$$, is rounded to the nearest integer the result is 63. Select the numbers which complete the error interval for $$x$$: $$\square \leq x <\square$$
starterQuiz.hint: Drawing a number line with 63 in the centre and, given the degree of accuracy is an integer, put 62 and 64 either side of the 63. Identify the middle of 62 and 63 and the middle of 63 and 64.
starterQuiz.feedback: The smallest number when rounded to the nearest integer is 62.5, but the largest cannot be 63.5 as this rounds to 64. You show a number which is infinitely smaller than 63.5 but not equal to 63.5 using this error interval: $$62.5\leq x< 63.5$$

starterQuiz.stem: When a number, $$x$$, is rounded to the nearest integer the result is 5. Select the numbers which complete the error interval for $$x$$: $$\square \leq x <\square$$
starterQuiz.hint: Drawing a number line with 5 in the centre and, given the degree of accuracy is an integer, put 4 and 6 either side of the 5. Identify the middle of 4 and 5 and the middle of 5 and 6.
starterQuiz.feedback: The smallest number when rounded to the nearest integer is 4.5, but the largest cannot be 5.5 as this rounds to 6. You show a number which is infinitely smaller than 5.5 but not equal to 5.5 using this error interval: $$4.5\leq x< 5.5$$

starterQuiz.stem: When a number, $$x$$, is rounded to the nearest integer the result is 10. Select the numbers which complete the error interval for $$x$$: $$\square \leq x <\square$$
starterQuiz.hint: Drawing a number line with 10 in the centre and, given the degree of accuracy is an integer, put 9 and 11 either side of the 10. Identify the middle of 9 and 10 and the middle of 10 and 11.
starterQuiz.feedback: The smallest number when rounded to the nearest integer is 9.5, but the largest cannot be 10.5 as this rounds to 11. You show a number which is infinitely smaller than 10.5 but not equal to 10.5 using this error intervals $$9.5\leq x< 10.5$$

starterQuiz.stem: Jun rounds a number to the nearest integer and the result is 5. Izzy rounds a number to 1 d.p. and the result is 5.0. Jun says, "We must both have rounded the same number." Is Jun correct?
starterQuiz.hint: What are the error intervals for 5 to 1 s.f and what are the error intervals for 5.0 to 1 d.p? Are they the same or different?
starterQuiz.feedback: Given the error intervals are different, this means the ranges of values are different so they cannot be the same numbers if they have different error intervals.

options.text: Jun is correct as both are the same when rounded to 1 d.p
Jun is correct as both values will be the same when inputting into a calculator.
Jun is incorrect as they have different error intervals.

starterQuiz.stem: $$$x$$ and $$y$$ are both integers. $$x$$ = 650 (rounded to the nearest 10) and $$y$$ = 800 (rounded to the nearest 100). The greatest possible integer value of $$x+y$$ is {{}}.
starterQuiz.hint: Looking at error intervals for integers, $$645\leq x< 655$$ and $$750\leq x< 850$$

exitQuiz.stem: __________ are the digits in a number that contribute to the accuracy of the number. The first significant figure is the first non-zero digit.
exitQuiz.hint: An example is 389 = 400 to 1 s.f. as the first digit indicates the hundreds column. Therefore you have rounded to the nearest 100.
exitQuiz.feedback: Significant figures are the digits in a number that contribute to the accuracy of the number.  The first significant figure is the first non-zero digit in the number.

exitQuiz.stem: When a number, $$x$$, is rounded to the nearest integer the result is 35. Select the numbers which complete the error interval for $$x$$: $$\square \leq x <\square$$
exitQuiz.hint: Drawing a number line with 35 in the centre and, given the degree of accuracy is an integer, put 34 and 36 either side of the 35. Identify the middle of 34 and 35 and the middle of 35 and 36.
exitQuiz.feedback: The smallest number when rounded to the nearest integer is 34.5, but the largest cannot be 35.5 as this rounds to 36. You show a number which is infinitely smaller than 35.5 but not equal to 35.5 using this error interval: $$ 34.5\leq  x < 35.5 $$

exitQuiz.stem: A long road is made up of 3 sub roads. The 1st road measures 35 m (2 s.f), the 2nd road is 41 m (2 s.f) and the 3rd road is 48 m (2 s.f). Find the error interval for the length $$x$$ of the long road.
exitQuiz.hint: Identify the error interval of all three roads, then sum the lowest limits and the upper limits to make the error interval.
exitQuiz.feedback: The error intervals of the three roads are $$ 34.5\leq  x < 35.5 $$, $$ 40.5 \leq  x < 41.5 $$ and $$ 47.5\leq  x < 48.5 $$. Therefore summing the lower and upper limits gives $$ 122.5 \leq  x < 125.5 $$

exitQuiz.stem: A wall is in an L-shape. All the lengths are given to 1 d.p or the nearest integer. Work out the error interval for the area of the wall. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Identify the error interval of the wall, but breaking it up into two areas, then sum the lowest limits and the upper limits to make the error interval for the area.
exitQuiz.feedback: The error interval of one area is $$3.15\times5.25 \leq  x < 3.25\times5.35 $$giving $$16.5375 \leq  x <17.3875 $$. The other area $$1.5^2 \leq  x < 2.5^2 $$giving $$2.25 \leq  x <6.25 $$.

exitQuiz.stem: A square has lengths in cm given to 1 decimal place. The error interval of the perimeter of the square is $$31 \leq  x <31.4 $$. Work out the length of the square correct to 1 d.p.
exitQuiz.hint: Given the shape is a square and has 4 equal length, dividing the lower and upper limits by 4 will give you the lower and upper limits of the length.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$31\div4 \leq  x <31.4\div4 $$ gives  $$7.75 \leq  x <7.85$$. So the length of the square is between the error interval which is 7.8 cm.

exitQuiz.stem: A square has lengths in cm to 1 decimal place. The error interval of the area of the square is $$30.8025 \leq  x <31.9225 $$. Work out the length of the square to 1 d.p.
exitQuiz.hint: Square root the limits to the error interval. This will give you the upper and lower limits of the length.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$\sqrt{30.8025} \leq  x <\sqrt{31.9225} $$ gives  $$5.55\leq  x <5.65$$. Therefore the length of the square halfway between giving 5.6 cm.

lessons.title: Problem solving with estimation and rounding
lessons.outcome: I can use my knowledge of estimation and rounding to solve problems.
keyLearningPoints: It may be helpful to estimate an answer to check the magnitude is correct.
It can be useful to use rounding to significant figures when dealing with very big or very small numbers in context.
Estimates can help when making decisions about maximum or minimum possible answers in real life contexts.
You can use Fermi estimation to find approximate solutions to problems.

keywords.definition: A quick estimate for a calculation is obtained from using approximate values, often rounded to 1 significant figure.

starterQuiz.stem: A degree of accuracy shows how precise a {{}} or measurement is. For example, to the nearest cm, nearest 10, 1 s.f. and so on.
starterQuiz.hint: Gram, kilogram, millimetre, centimetre, litre are all units of measurement. What other things do you round?
starterQuiz.feedback: A degree of accuracy shows how precise a number or measurement is. For example you may round the number of people in a cinema to the nearest 10.

starterQuiz.stem: Alex buys paper £4.95, USB £$$\square$$, stamps £5.20, crisps £0.95, staples £1.10 and plug £1.99. He pays with a £20 note and receives about £2 back in change. Estimate the cost of the USB.
starterQuiz.hint: Round the numbers to the appropriate degree of accuracy and subtract from £18 (This is how much all the items cost). This will give you the price of the USB.
starterQuiz.feedback: An example rounding for this question is 18 − 5 − 5 − 1 − 1 − 2 = 4, so the price of the USB should be approximately £4.

starterQuiz.stem: An error interval for a number $$y$$ shows the range of possible values of $$y$$. It is written as:
starterQuiz.hint: You want to include the number $$a$$, but not include the number $$b$$.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$ a\leq y < b$$  means you are including the values of $$a$$ as the smallest and not including the value of $$b$$ as the largest.

starterQuiz.stem: When a number, $$x$$, is rounded to the nearest integer the result is 88. Identify the error interval.
starterQuiz.hint: Drawing a number line with 88 in the centre and, given the degree of accuracy is an integer, put 89 and 87 either side of the 88. Identify the middle of 87 and 88 and the middle of 88 and 89.
starterQuiz.feedback: The smallest number when rounded to the nearest integer is 87.5, but the largest cannot be 88.5 as this rounds to 89. You show a number which is infinitely smaller than 88.5 but not equal to 88.5 using this error interval $$87.5\leq x<88.5$$

starterQuiz.stem: A triangle has lengths 3.5 cm (2 s.f), 4.1 cm (2 s.f) and 4.8 cm (2 s.f). Write the error interval for the perimeter $$p$$ of the triangle.
starterQuiz.hint: Identify the error interval of all three lengths then sum the lowest limits and the upper limits to make the error interval.
starterQuiz.feedback: The error intervals of the three sides are $$ 3.45\leq  x < 3.55 $$, $$ 4.05 \leq  x < 4.15 $$ and $$ 4.75\leq  x < 4.85 $$. Therefore summing the lower and upper limits the answer is $$ 12.25 \leq  p < 12.55 $$

starterQuiz.stem: A square has lengths in centimetres to 1 decimal place. The error interval of the area of the square is $$17.2225 \leq  x <18.0625 $$. Work out the length of the square to 1 d.p.
starterQuiz.hint: Square root the limits to the error interval. This will give you the upper and lower limits of the length.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$\sqrt{17.2225} \leq  x <\sqrt{18.0625} $$ gives  $$4.15\leq  x <4.25$$. Therefore side length is the number in between giving an answer of 4.2 cm

exitQuiz.stem: Work out an estimate for the area of the shape. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Work out the estimate area of each part of the compound shape and sum.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$5.3 \approx 5$$ and $$3.2 \approx 3$$, therefore the area is approximately $$5\times3 + 2\times2= 19$$ m²

exitQuiz.stem: Here is a grassed garden with a summer house in the centre. Using estimation and rounding, estimate the area of the grass. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Work out an estimate for the area of the whole garden and subtract the estimate area of the summer house.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$10.47 \approx 10$$, $$19.87 \approx 20$$, $$3.89 \approx 4$$, $$8.52 \approx 9$$, therefore area of the garden is approximately $$20\times10 - 9\times4= 164$$ m²

exitQuiz.stem: A piece of string was 32 cm measured to the nearest cm. A length of 5.6 cm (to 1 d.p) was cut off. What is the error interval for the remaining length $$x$$ cm?
exitQuiz.hint: The lower limit is the lower limit of length subtract upper limit of what is cut. The upper limit is the upper limit of length subtract lower limit of what is cut.
exitQuiz.feedback: The length error interval is $$31.5\leq x<32.5$$. The error interval of what is cut is $$5.55\leq x<5.65$$. Therefore the error interval of what is remaining is $$31.5-5.65 < x<32.5-5.5$$

exitQuiz.stem: Complete the statement. Fermi problems encourage:
exitQuiz.hint: These problems are named after Fermi as he was known for his ability to make good approximate calculations.
exitQuiz.feedback: Fermi problems embrace a variety of strategies to estimate an answer using some initial information as a basis and then a structured approach is used to calculate an estimation.

options.text: critical thinking and well calculated estimates using data or information
openness of answers and flexibility so answers can be achieved in different ways
an appreciation there are a range of answers, the focus is on the working out
random guesses but use estimation and or rounding

exitQuiz.stem: Fermi problem : How long will it take to count to 1 million (without breaks, sleep, etc)?
exitQuiz.hint: Assuming you count 1 second for each number, how many seconds would it take to count to 1 000 000? Then convert to minutes, hours and then days.

exitQuiz.stem: Fermi problem : If you put 1 million pound coins in a box, what is the volume of the box in m³ ?
exitQuiz.hint: A £1 coin has a diameter of 22 mm and a thickness of 3 mm.
exitQuiz.feedback: Diameter = 22 mm and a thickness = 3 mm. Treat each coin as a cuboid. So volume is  $$22\times22\times3\approx 20\times20\times3=1200$$ mm$$^3$$. Therefore $$1200\times 1\;000\;000 = 1\;200\;000\;000$$ mm³ = 1.2 m³

units.title: Sequences
units.description: In this unit we develop knowledge of sequences to be able to identify, determine, and continue arithmetic sequences. We finish the unit by looking at how sequences may be reprsented graphically.

lessons.title: Checking understanding of sequences
lessons.outcome: I can appreciate the structure of patterns and sequences.
keyLearningPoints: Multiplication tables are an example of a sequence.
Sequences might have a specific difference which can be found.
Sequences can have a specific multiplier which can be found.
Written methods can be used to find larger numbers in a sequence.

keywords.definition: A sequence is a succession of objects, diagrams or values usually formed according to a rule.

starterQuiz.stem: Which calculation will find the difference between 37 and 83?
starterQuiz.hint: The difference between 4 and 10 is 6. What calculation gives you this answer?
starterQuiz.feedback: Difference is the result of subtracting one number from another.

starterQuiz.stem: Calculate $$482 - 267$$
starterQuiz.hint: Use a written method for subtraction to help you. For example column subtraction. Remember to start by subtracting the ones digits and if this is going to give you a negative value, use the tens column to help.
starterQuiz.feedback: Written methods can be really helpful when subtracting larger numbers. $$2-7$$ does not give a positive value so we can calculate $$12-7 = 5$$  then $$7 - 6 = 1$$ then $$4-2 = 2$$ to give  an answer of 215.

starterQuiz.stem: Calculate $$7.4 - 5.06$$
starterQuiz.hint: What do you need to add on to 5.06 to get 6. What more do you need to add on to get 7.4?
starterQuiz.feedback: You need to add on 0.94 to get from 5.06 to 6, then another 1.4. In total $$0.94 + 1.4 = 2.34$$

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these is the answer to $$10\div 4$$
starterQuiz.hint: Division can be written as a fraction. $$a\div b$$ is the same as $$a\over b$$
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$10\div 4$$ is the same as $$10\over 4$$ which simiplifies to $$5\over 2$$

starterQuiz.stem: Dividing 21 by 3 will find the __________ from the number 3 to the number 21
starterQuiz.hint: The inverse of division is multiplication
starterQuiz.feedback: Dividing 21 by 3 will give the multiplier to get from 3 to 21.

starterQuiz.stem: Match the fraction calculations to their answers.
starterQuiz.hint: To divide by a fraction, you can multiply by its reciprocal.
starterQuiz.feedback: To multiply by a fraction, we multiply by the numerator and divide by the denominator. To divide fractions, we can multiply by the reciprocal.

exitQuiz.stem: A {{}} is a succession of objects, diagrams or values usually formed according to a rule.
exitQuiz.hint: 3, 5, 7, 9... is an example of one with an additive pattern.
exitQuiz.feedback: A sequence is a succession of objects, diagrams or values usually formed according to a rule. Rules can include additive patterns and multiplicative patterns.

exitQuiz.stem: What sort of pattern does this sequence have 12, 6, 3, 1.5, ...
exitQuiz.hint: What calculation gets the value 6 from the previous value 12?
exitQuiz.feedback: This sequence is halving each time which is a multiplicative rule of $$\times {1\over 2}$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these additive rules would create a decreasing pattern?
exitQuiz.hint: Adding a negative number decreases the value of the original number.
exitQuiz.feedback: Sequences with a constant additive pattern will be decreasing if a negative value is being added each time.

exitQuiz.stem: What is the next number in this constant multiplicative pattern?   1, 4, 16, {{}} ...
exitQuiz.hint: The values in this sequence multiply by 4 each time
exitQuiz.feedback: The multiplier is 4, $$16\times 4 = 64$$

exitQuiz.stem: Starting with the first value, sort these numbers into a sequence with constant multiplicative pattern of $$\times 0.1$$
exitQuiz.hint: Multiplying a number by a value between 0 and 1 will decrease the value of the number.

exitQuiz.stem: Match the sequence with its constant multiplier.
exitQuiz.hint: Dividing the second number by the first will tell you the multiplier.

lessons.title: Securing understanding of sequences

starterQuiz.stem: What do we call the expression in a fraction, written below the fraction line?

starterQuiz.feedback: In the fraction $$a\over b$$, $$a$$ is the numerator and $$b$$ is the denominator.

starterQuiz.hint: Calculating $$9-5$$ will tell you what value is being added each time.
starterQuiz.feedback: This sequence is adding 4 each time.

starterQuiz.hint: Calculating $$6\div 2$$ will tell you the multiplier
starterQuiz.feedback: The multiplier is 3. $$6\times 3 = 18$$

starterQuiz.stem: Match the calculation to the value it will find for the sequence ..., ?, 2,10, ...
starterQuiz.hint: $$$ 10\div 2$$ will find the multiplier to get from 2 to 10. $$10-2$$ will find the value which is added to 2 to get 10.
starterQuiz.feedback: Once a multiplier is found, multiplying a value by the multiplier gives the next term. Dividing a value by the multiplier gives the previous term.

starterQuiz.stem: Match these directed number calculations to their answers.
starterQuiz.hint: Dividing a negative number by a negative number gives a positive value. Dividing a positive number by a negative number gives a negative value.
starterQuiz.feedback: Subtracting a negative is the same as adding the positive $$(-12)-(-6) = (-12) + 6$$. Multiplying or dividing a negative number by a negative number gives a positive value and a positive number by a negative number gives a negative value.

starterQuiz.stem: Match the answers to their corresponding fraction calculation.
starterQuiz.hint: $$${4\over 5}-{3\over 10}= {8\over 10}-{3\over 10} $$ $${4\over 5}\div {3\over10}= {4\over 5}\times {10\over 3}$$. Don't forget to simplify your answers.
starterQuiz.feedback: To add or subtract, it's easiest if you convert your fractions to have common denominators. To divide by a fraction, you can multiply by its reciprocal.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these best describes what a sequence is?

exitQuiz.stem: Which representation is the same sequence as this? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: For sequences to be identical they must start on the same value and follow the same rule.
exitQuiz.feedback: Sequences which have most of the same values but start on a different value are not the same sequence. This sequence starts with one red and one green block and adds a red block each time.

exitQuiz.stem: What would the next number in this sequence be if it had a constant additive rule?  2, -4, {{}},...
exitQuiz.hint: Work out what value is added to 2 to get (-4) and add it on again. This is a decreasing sequence.
exitQuiz.feedback: To follow a constant additive rule, this sequence adds (-6) each time $$(-4) + (-6) = (-10)$$

exitQuiz.stem: What would the next number in the sequence be if it had a constant multiplicative rule? 2, -4, {{}}, ...
exitQuiz.hint: $$$2\times (-2) = -4$$ you need to multiply by (-2) to get the next value.
exitQuiz.feedback: The multiplier is (-2). $$(-4)\times (-2)= (8)$$

exitQuiz.stem: Match the next 2 numbers in the sequence which starts 5, 15, ... with the rule the sequence is following.
exitQuiz.hint: Pick a rule and use it to generate the next 2 numbers in the sequence. E.g double the previous value and add 5 $$15\times 2 + 5 = 35$$, $$35\times 2 + 5 = 75$$
exitQuiz.feedback: Different rules can produce the same 3 start numbers in a sequence. We need to try the rule out on every value to see if it gives the desired next value.
