lessons.title: Formalising a sequence
lessons.outcome: I can appreciate that a sequence is a succession of terms usually formed according to a rule.
keyLearningPoints: A pattern of objects can be made by following a rule.
These rules can be described in words.
The number of objects each time is the term.
Missing terms in the sequence can be found using the rule.

keywords.definition: Each value or pattern in a sequence is called a term.

starterQuiz.stem: Here are the first and second pattern in a pictorial sequence. Which is the third pattern if the sequence had a constant additive relationship? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Work out how many dots are added on to pattern 1 to get pattern 2. Make sure the third pattern adds the same number of dots.
starterQuiz.feedback: Three dots have been added to pattern one to get pattern 2. So pattern 3 needs to add on 3 dots again to form a constant additive relationship.

starterQuiz.stem: Which word best completes this description of a sequence: 'A sequence is a succession of diagrams, objects or __________, usually formed according to a rule.'
starterQuiz.hint: Sequences can be formed from pictures or from numbers. Fractions and decimals can be part of a sequence, as well as whole numbers.
starterQuiz.feedback: A sequence is a succession of diagrams, objects or values, usually formed according to a rule.

starterQuiz.stem: What would be the next value in this sequence if it has a constant additive rule? 18, 6, ...
starterQuiz.hint: $$$6-18$$ will tell you the value that is added each time. It will be a negative value as the sequence is decreasing.
starterQuiz.feedback: The sequence is decreasing by 12 $$6-12=-6$$

starterQuiz.stem: What would be the next value in this sequence if it has a constant multiplicative rule? 18, 6, ...
starterQuiz.hint: $$$6\div 18$$ will tell you the multiplier to get from 18 to 6. This will be a fraction between 0 and 1 as the sequence is decreasing.
starterQuiz.feedback: the multiplier is $$1\over 3$$ $$6\times {1\over3}=2$$

starterQuiz.stem: Calculate the perimeter of this rectangle [image]
starterQuiz.hint: A rectangle has 4 sides; the perimeter is the length of all 4 sides added together.
starterQuiz.feedback: Opposite sides in a rectangle are the same length $$5 + 5 + 2 + 2 = 14$$

starterQuiz.stem: Calculate the perimeter of this L shape [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Each small square is 1 cm by 1 cm. You can count the length of the squares round the outside of the pattern.
starterQuiz.feedback: The perimeter is 16, 4 squares down the left side, 4 squares along the bottom $$1 + 3=4$$ squares in total up the right hand side. $$1 + 3 = 4$$ squares in total along the top.

exitQuiz.stem: What do we call each value or pattern in a sequence?
exitQuiz.hint: We call the first value or picture in the sequence the first. __________ .
exitQuiz.feedback: Each value or pattern in a sequence is called a term

exitQuiz.stem: Here is the beginning of a pictorial sequence with a constant additive rule. Which picture is term 5? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: How many dots are being added on each time? Remember you want the 5th pattern.
exitQuiz.feedback: 2 dots are being added each time. The 5th term will have 4 more dots than the 3rd (two on each end)

exitQuiz.stem: Here is a sequence of connected 'N' shape patterns made out of dots. How many dots would there be in term 4 of this pattern? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Work out how many dots are added on each time in the pattern.
exitQuiz.feedback: 6 dots are being added each time. Term 3 has 22 dots $$22 + 6 = 28$$

exitQuiz.stem: Here is a sequence of connected 'N' shape patterns made out of dots. Which of these could be a rule for the number of dots in each term? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: You could describe how to get from one term to the next- count how many dots are being added each time? Or you could describe how many more dots are needed for each N shape.
exitQuiz.feedback: Each N shape adds 6 new dots. There are 4 dots making up the start of the first N shape.

options.text: The number of dots increase by 4 each time.
The number of dots increases by 6 each time.
There are 6 dots per N shape.
There are 6 dots per N shape add 4.
There are 10 dots per N shape.

exitQuiz.hint: 6 dots are needed for each N shape but there are also some extra ones that make the first vertical line of the first N.
exitQuiz.feedback: The rule could be 6 dots per N shape plus 4 for the start. $$6\times 10 + 4 = 64 $$

exitQuiz.stem: For this pictorial sequence, match up the rule with the element of the pattern it is describing. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Write down how many diagonal lines there are in each pattern and see if you can spot a rule. Do the same for horizontal lines, overall lines and the height of the pattern.
exitQuiz.feedback: 5 lines are being added each time, 4 diagonal and a vertical line. The height is increasing by 2 squares.

lessons.title: Generating a sequence using a term-to-term rule
lessons.outcome: I can appreciate that a sequence can be generated and described using term-to-term approaches.
keyLearningPoints: Sequences can be created using a rule that tells you how to find the next term from the current one.
These sequences could be related additively or multiplicity.
These sequences could be related in other ways.
This term-to-term method is time-consuming when you want to find higher terms in the sequence.
It is possible to describe the rule when given some of the terms although this may not be unique.

keywords.definition: A term-to-term rule describes how to calculate the next term in the sequence from the previous term.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these best describes what a term in a sequence is?
starterQuiz.hint: A sequence is an ordered list of terms, usually formed according to a rule.
starterQuiz.feedback: Each value, object or diagram in a sequence is called a term.

options.text: The number of patterns in a sequence
The first number in a sequence
The multiplier to get from one value to the next
An individual diagram or value in a sequence

starterQuiz.stem: What would be the next value in this sequence if it has a constant additive rule? -1, 6, {{}}, ...
starterQuiz.hint: What do you need to add to -1 to get 6? You can calculate this by doing $$6-(-1)$$

starterQuiz.stem: What would be the next value in this sequence if it has a constant multiplicative rule? -1, 6, {{}}, ...
starterQuiz.hint: What is the multiplier to get from -1 to 6? You can calculate this by doing $$6\div -1$$

starterQuiz.stem: Match the next 2 numbers in the sequence which starts 16, 4, ... with the rule the sequence is following.
starterQuiz.hint: Pick a rule and use it to generate the next 2 numbers in the sequence. E.g halve the previous term and subtract 4 $$ 4\times {1\over 2} - 4 $$
starterQuiz.feedback: Sequences can be continued different ways with different rules

match.left: halve the previous term and subtract 4

starterQuiz.stem: Calculate the number halfway between 16 and 34
starterQuiz.hint: $$$34 - 16 = 18$$ 16 and 34 have a difference of 18. Halving that difference will help you find the number in between them.
starterQuiz.feedback: The difference between 16 and 34 is 18. Half of 18 is 9. $$16+9=25$$. $$25 + 9 = 34$$.

starterQuiz.stem: Match these calculations to the correct answers.
starterQuiz.hint: Multiplying by 0.1 is the same as multiplying by $$1\over 10$$ or finding one tenth of a number.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$\times 0.1 is the same as \div 10$$ and $$\div 0.1 is the same as \times 10$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these best describes what a term-to-term rule is?
exitQuiz.hint: Term-to-term rules can be used for different types of sequences, not just constant additive or constant multiplicative patterns.
exitQuiz.feedback: A term-to-term rule describes how to find the next term in the sequence from the previous term.

options.text: A rule to find any term in a sequence
A rule to find the first term in a sequence
A rule to find the next term in a sequence from the previous term
A rule to find the multiplier for a sequence
A rule to find the constant additive pattern for a sequence

exitQuiz.stem: Match the term-to-term rules with the sequences
exitQuiz.hint: Make sure you check the rule works for all successive terms. Some different term-to-term rules can produce the same first few terms. E.g $$8\times {3\over 2} = 12, 12\times {3\over 2}=18, 18\times {3\over 2} = 27$$
exitQuiz.feedback: Term-to-term rules are not always unique for the first 3 terms. 8, 12, 20, 32,...is 'add 4, add 8, add 12, ...'  whereas 8, 12, 20, 36, ... is  'double the previous term then subtract 4'

exitQuiz.stem: A sequence starts 7,10, ... What is the 10th term if the term to term rule is 'add 3 to the previous term'?
exitQuiz.hint: How many times do you need to add 3 to get from the first term to the tenth term?
exitQuiz.feedback: To get from the first term to the tenth term you need to add 3, nine times. $$3\times 9 = 27, 7 + 27 = 34$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the statements below is a limitation of using term-to-term rules?
exitQuiz.hint: Term-to-term rules help you find the next term from the previous term for any sequence which follows a mathematical pattern.
exitQuiz.feedback: Term-to-term rules are useful for finding the next term. They can be complicated to use when wanting to find a larger term number and they are not always unique.

options.text: They can be time consuming or complex to use when finding a larger term number.
They can be difficult to use when you want to find the next term.
Different sequences can be made from the same rule with different 1st terms.
Different rules can apply to the same few terms.
They only work for constant additive patterns.

exitQuiz.stem: What is the term-to-term rule for this sequence with a constant additive pattern?  17, ?, 29, ?, 41, ...
exitQuiz.hint: Find the value which is being added each time. You need to start by finding the difference between the first and third terms and then work out the difference between the first and second term.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$29-17 = 12,  12\div 2 = 6$$; the term-to-term rule is 'add 6'.

exitQuiz.stem: What is the term-to-term rule for the constant additive sequence with 2nd term = 63 and 7th term = 23?
exitQuiz.hint: There are 5 additions between term 2 and term 7. The value being added each time will be negative as the sequence is decreasing.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$23- 63 = -40$$; there are 5 additives between term 2 and term 7. $$-40\div 5 = -8$$

lessons.title: Arithmetic sequences
lessons.outcome: I can appreciate the features of an arithmetic sequence and be able to recognise one.
keyLearningPoints: Finding the difference between each term can help you identify different types of sequence.
Sequences with a constant difference are arithmetic sequences.
Arithmetic sequences can be uniquely described with an initial term and a common difference.
It is possible to identify which sequences are arithmetic.

keywords.definition: An arithmetic (or linear) sequence is a sequence where the difference between successive terms is a constant.

starterQuiz.stem: Which sequences have a constant additive pattern?
starterQuiz.hint: What do you add to term 1 to get term 2? If you add the same value on to term 2, do you get term 3? Adding negative values produce a decreasing sequence.
starterQuiz.feedback: The differences between successive terms should be the same $$-8 + 16 = 8$$ but $$8 + 16 = 24$$ not -8 so -8, 8, -8, 8, ... does not have a constant additive pattern.

starterQuiz.stem: Which sequences have a constant multiplicative pattern?
starterQuiz.hint: Dividing term 2 by term 1 will find the multiplier for those two terms. See if multiplying term 2 by this value then gets term 3.
starterQuiz.feedback: Multiplying by a negative multiplier will form a sequence which alternates between positive and negative values. Multiplying by a value between 0 and 1 will form a decreasing sequence.

starterQuiz.stem: Calculate the perimeter of this rectangle. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The perimeter is the length around the outside of the rectangle. All 4 side lengths need to be added together.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$ 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20$$ so the perimeter is 20 cm

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these is the area of this rectangle? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Area of a rectangle is the base multiplied by the height
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$6\times 4 = 24$$ The area is 24 cm$$^2$$

starterQuiz.stem: What is the term-to-term rule for a sequence with a constant additive pattern which has first term = 23 and  4th term = 41.
starterQuiz.hint: Write the sequence as 23, ?, ?, 41. What is the difference between 23 and 41? How many additions are there between 23 and 41?
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$41-23=18$$ $$18\div 3 = 6$$ The term-to-term rule is 'add 6 to the previous term to get the next term'.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the value of $${6\over 7} - 2{1\over2}$$
starterQuiz.hint: $$$2{1\over2}$$ is equivalent to $$5\over 2$$ Write the fractions $$6\over 7$$  and $$5\over 2$$ with a common denominator of 14
starterQuiz.feedback: $$${6\over 7} - {5\over 2}$$ is the same as $${12\over 14}- {35\over 14}= {-23\over 14}$$

exitQuiz.stem: Match the keyword to its definition.
exitQuiz.hint: An arithmetic sequence can be uniquely defined by its initial term and the common difference.
exitQuiz.feedback: An arithmetic sequence is a sequence where the difference between successive terms is constant. Each term increases or decreases by the same amount.

match.left: a sequence that increases or decreases by the same step
the constant additive rule from one term to the next
the first term in a sequence
terms that are next to each other in a sequence

exitQuiz.stem: Match the arithmetic sequences with their descriptions.
exitQuiz.hint: Sequences with a negative common difference will be decreasing.
exitQuiz.feedback: You can use the common difference and any term to work out the initial term.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these sequences are arithmetic?
exitQuiz.hint: For the fractional sequence, convert all fractions to equivalent fractions with a denominator of 10. Then see if successive terms have a common difference.
exitQuiz.feedback: '$$7, 2, -3, -8,$$ ...' has a common difference of -5. $${4\over 5}, {1\over 2}, {1\over 5}, -{1\over 10}, ...$$ has a common difference of $$-{3\over 10}$$

exitQuiz.hint: Write the sequence out with gaps for the unknown terms. The difference between 41 and 65, is 24. Use this to find the common difference between successive terms.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these sequences are arithmetic?
exitQuiz.hint: Arithmetic sequences have the same difference between all the terms. E.g. $$(3a+4)-(5a+3) =  -2a+1$$ so check whether adding $$-2a + 1$$ onto each term gives the next term.
exitQuiz.feedback: As long as successive terms have a common difference, sequences are arithmetic. These common differences can be expressions as well as constants.

lessons.title: Expressing an arithmetic sequence

starterQuiz.stem: In sequences, a position-to-term rule describes what?
starterQuiz.hint: A position-to-term rule describes the relationship between term numbers and the terms themself.

How many terms there are in a sequence
How many positions there are in a sequence

starterQuiz.feedback: For the 100$$^\text{th}$$ term number we do $$(100) \times 3 -2 = 300 - 2 = 298$$

order.text: The 101$$^\text{st}$$ term of the sequence $${1 \over 2} n + 50$$.

keywords.definition: The nth term of a sequence is the position of a term in a sequence where n stands for the term number.

starterQuiz.stem: The n$$^\text{th}$$ term is the position of a term in a sequence ($$n$$ is the term number). It can be used to calculate any term so is also known as a __________ for finding the n$$^\text{th}$$ term.
starterQuiz.hint: Consider the definitions of each of the options.
starterQuiz.feedback: A formula is a rule that links variables in context. The n$$^\text{th}$$ term is also known as a formula for finding the n$$^\text{th}$$ term in a given sequence.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the term-to-term rule for this pattern sequence? [image]

starterQuiz.stem: What is the position-to-term rule for this pattern sequence? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: A position-to-term rule describes how to generate the term from the term number.
starterQuiz.feedback: The first pattern is $$(1) \times 3 + 1 = 4$$ squares. The second is $$(2) \times 3 + 1 = 7$$ squares and so on.

options.text: Multiply the term number by 3 and add 1

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these are arithmetic (linear) sequences?
starterQuiz.hint: An arithmetic (linear) sequence is a sequence where the difference between successive terms is a constant.
starterQuiz.feedback: 1, 4, 7, 10, ... has a constant difference +3. For 10, 7, 4, 1, ... it's -3, and for 0.4, 0.7, 1, 1.3, ... it's +0.3, whereas 1, 2, 4, 8, ... and 1, 4, 8, 13, ... do not have a constant difference.

starterQuiz.stem: This pattern represents people seated around an increasing number of tables. If you were asked to find the number of people around 50 tables, which calculation would you do? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Whichever rule you choose substitution should tell you that 1 table =  six people and 2 tables = 10 people.
starterQuiz.feedback: There would be $$50 \times 4 + 2=202$$ people because there are always 2 people on the ends and every table adds 4 people.

starterQuiz.stem: Order these arithmetic sequences in terms of the size of their common difference. Start with the greatest common difference.
starterQuiz.hint: Arithmetic (linear) sequences have a common difference between terms which is a constant. Subtract term one from term two to find it.
starterQuiz.feedback: Despite starting with negative terms -101, -87, -73, -59, ... had the highest common difference of +14 and, despite having large terms, 2190, 2180, 2170, 2160, ... had the lowest common difference of -10

exitQuiz.hint: Every arithmetic sequence can be expressed in terms of it's $$n^\text{th}$$ term.
exitQuiz.feedback: The $$n^\text{th}$$ term of a sequence is the position of a term in a sequence where $$n$$ stands for the term number but, it is also a formula for finding the $$n^\text{th}$$ term.

exitQuiz.stem: To find the $$n^\text{th}$$ term of an arithmetic sequence, which of the following do we need?
exitQuiz.hint: The common difference is the most useful starting point when finding the $$n^\text{th}$$ term.
exitQuiz.feedback: If we know the common difference and the translation we can write an $$n^\text{th}$$ term formula for any arithmetic sequence.

exitQuiz.stem: 17, 21, 25, 29, ... is a translation of what from the sequence 4$$n$$?
exitQuiz.hint: The sequence 4$$n$$ starts 4, 8, 12, 16, ... How far would we need to translate it on a number line to make it land on 17, 21, 25, 29, ...?

options.text: It is not a translation of 4$$n$$.

exitQuiz.stem: What is the $$n^\text{th}$$ term of the arithmetic sequence 10, 15, 20, 25, ...?
exitQuiz.hint: Start by finding the common difference. Then, consider the translation.
exitQuiz.feedback: 10, 15, 20, 25, ... has a common difference of +5 and is a translation of +5 from the sequence $$5n$$.

exitQuiz.stem: The sequence $$17-7n$$ has a common difference of what?
exitQuiz.hint: The coefficient of $$n$$ tells us the common difference in an arithmetic sequence.
exitQuiz.feedback: The coefficient of $$n$$ tells us the common difference in an arithmetic sequence so this is a decreasing sequence with a constant difference of -7

exitQuiz.stem: Find the $$n^\text{th}$$ term of the sequence 2.31, 2.22, 2.13, 2.04, ...
exitQuiz.hint: Start by finding the common difference. Then, consider the translation.
exitQuiz.feedback: The sequence 2.31, 2.22, 2.13, 2.04, ... has a constant difference of -0.09 and a translation of +2.4 from the sequence $$-0.09n$$

keywords.definition: An arithmetic (or linear) sequence is a sequence where the difference between successive terms is a constant.

starterQuiz.stem: An arithmetic (linear) sequence has a __________ difference.
starterQuiz.hint: Arithmetic sequences are also known as linear sequences because they change by a constant, common difference.
starterQuiz.feedback: Arithmetic (linear) sequences have a constant difference.

starterQuiz.stem: Which two pairs of coordinates are shown here? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: We read and write the $$x$$ coordinate first and the $$y$$ coordinate second. Use the labels on the axes to help you.
starterQuiz.feedback: The closest coordinate to the origin is $$(2,1)$$ and the other is $$(4,2)$$.

starterQuiz.stem: Match the letters with the correctly plotted coordinates. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: We read and write the $$x$$ coordinate first and the $$y$$ coordinate second.
starterQuiz.feedback: A and B have positive $$x$$ and $$y$$ coordinates whereas C and D have positive $$x$$ coordinates and negative $$y$$ coordinates.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these are true for this sequence? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: In sequences $$n$$ represents the term number and $$T$$ the respective term value.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$n=1, T=3$$ means that the first term in the sequence has a value of 3. $$n=5, T=11$$ means that the fifth term in the sequence has a value of 11.

starterQuiz.stem: Match the sequences with the common difference.
starterQuiz.hint: In an arithmetic sequence the difference between successive terms is the common difference.
starterQuiz.feedback: -39, -33, -27, -21, ... is an example of an increasing sequence (common difference +6) with some negative terms. 36, 30, 24, 18, ... is an example of a decreasing sequence (common difference -6) with some positive terms.

starterQuiz.stem: What is true of this set of coordinates? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Having this set of coordinates as a list will help you identify patterns.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$(1,2), (2,4), (3,6), (4,8), (5,10)$$ means that the $$y$$ coordinate is always double the $$x$$ coordinate and increase by 2 for every increase of 1 in the $$x$$ coordinate.

options.text: The $$x$$ coordinate is always double the $$y$$ coordinate.
The $$y$$ coordinate is always double the $$x$$ coordinate.

As the $$x$$ coordinate increases by 1, $$y$$ increases by 2

exitQuiz.stem: When you plot an arithmetic sequence graphically the coordinates form a straight line, hence they are also known as __________ sequences.
exitQuiz.hint: In maths, when something increases by a constant difference we call it linear.
exitQuiz.feedback: Arithmetic sequences are also known as linear sequences. We can see this when we graph them because the points form a straight line.

exitQuiz.stem: If you completed this table of values before plotting the arithmetic sequence $$2n-7$$ which values would you put in the 'Term value' places? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Start by substituting in $$n=1$$ into $$2n-7$$ to find the first term. Then $$n=2$$ to find the second.
exitQuiz.feedback: When $$n=1$$, $$2n-7=2(1)-7=-5$$. When $$n=2$$, $$2n-7=2(2)-7=-3$$. Hence the values -5, -3, -1, 1, 3 are the first five terms of the sequence.

exitQuiz.stem: This is a table of values for the sequence $$4n-11$$. If you were going to graph this sequence which of these coordinates are correct? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: When plotting sequences we plot them in the form $$(n,T)$$ where $$n$$ is the term number and $$T$$ the term value.
exitQuiz.feedback: (-3,2) and (5,4) we would not plot for $$4n-11$$ because they have the term number and term value the wrong way round.

exitQuiz.stem: Which sequence is represented by this graph? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: A decreasing sequence has a negative $$n$$ coefficient.
exitQuiz.feedback: The difference is -3 between each term so it is a decreasing, $$-3n$$ sequence. 4 - 3(1) = 1 so it can't be $$4-3n$$. 7 - 3(1) = 4 which is the first term hence, $$7-3n$$ is this sequence.

exitQuiz.stem: This structure represents which sequence? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: What is constant? What is varying?
exitQuiz.feedback: You can see a constant 5 and a varying number of threes, hence it's $$3n+5$$ which is the same as $$5+3n$$. It is the number of 3's that varies.

exitQuiz.stem: The sequence $$3n$$ is translated by +6 in the vertical direction. What sequence is now shown? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The black crosses are $$3n$$ "plus another 6".
exitQuiz.feedback: Translating all the terms of the sequence $$3n$$ by +6 will give you the position of the sequence $$3n+6$$

starterQuiz.stem: Calculate the 200$$^\text{th}$$ term of $$17.96-0.32n$$. You may use a calculator.

exitQuiz.stem: The sequence 37, 47, 57, 67, 77, ... could be described as which?

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the below statements supports the justification that 6941 is not in the arithmetic sequence starting 14, 19, 24, 29, 34, ...?

The sequence will always end in the digit 4 or 9 in the ones position.
6941 is an odd number, and the sequence begins with an even number.

keywords.definition: An arithmetic (or linear) sequence is a sequence where the difference between successive terms is a constant.

starterQuiz.stem: Which words would describe the sequence 1,4,9,16,25, ...?
starterQuiz.hint: An arithmetic (or linear) sequence is a sequence where the difference between successive terms is a constant. Find the differences for this sequence.
starterQuiz.feedback: The sequence 1,4,9,16,25, ... does not have a common difference so it is non-linear.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the next term in the arithmetic sequence starting -19,-12,-5,2 ...
starterQuiz.hint: If it is arithmetic there is a common difference.
starterQuiz.feedback: With a common difference of +7 the next term is 2 + 7 = 9

starterQuiz.stem: Buses leave for Finchley Park every 25 minutes. If a bus just left at 7:41 am what time will the next bus leave?
starterQuiz.hint: A common error in questions like this is to forget that there are only 60 minutes in an hour.
starterQuiz.feedback: 19 minutes from 7:41 am to 8:00 am plus the other 6 minutes takes us to 8:06 am.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the $$n^\text{th}$$ term of the arithmetic sequence 8,9,10,11, ...?
starterQuiz.hint: To find the $$n^\text{th}$$ term of an arithmetic sequence you need to know the common difference, and the translation.
starterQuiz.feedback: Common difference of +1 making it a $$1n$$ sequence. 8,9,10,11, ... is a translation of +7 from the sequence 1,2,3,4, ... so this sequence is $$1n+7$$ which we write more simply as $$n+7$$.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the $$n^\text{th}$$ term of the arithmetic sequence 8,11,14,17 ...?
starterQuiz.hint: To find the $$n^\text{th}$$ term of an arithmetic sequence you need to know the common difference, and the translation.
starterQuiz.feedback: Common difference of +3 making it a $$3n$$ sequence. 8,11,14,17 ... is a translation of +5 from the sequence 3,6,9,12, ... so this sequence is $$3n+5$$.

starterQuiz.stem: The 118$$^\text{th}$$ term of the sequence $$5050-7n$$ is 4224. What is the 113$$^\text{th}$$ term?
starterQuiz.hint: The coefficient of $$n$$ tells us the common difference in the $$n^\text{th}$$ term of an arithmetic sequence.

exitQuiz.stem: Which would describe the sequence 1,3,6,10,15, ...?
exitQuiz.hint: An arithmetic (or linear) sequence is a sequence where the difference between successive terms is a constant.
exitQuiz.feedback: The sequence 1,3,6,10,15, ... does not have a common difference so it is non-linear.

exitQuiz.stem: The 2$$^\text{nd}$$ term of an arithmetic sequence is 11 and the 6$$^\text{th}$$ term is 47. What is the 1$$^\text{st}$$ term of the sequence?
exitQuiz.hint: What is the difference between 11 and 47 and over how many steps was it taken?
exitQuiz.feedback: 47 - 11 = 36 From $$n=2$$ to $$n=6$$ there are 4 steps. $$36 \div 4=9$$ so we have a common difference of +9. If the 2$$^\text{nd}$$ term is 11 the first term must be 2

exitQuiz.stem: Buses leave Wallsend for Byker at regular intervals. The second bus of the day leaves at 6:44 am. You just missed the seventh bus of the day which left at 8:04 am. What time is the next bus?
exitQuiz.hint: How many minutes from 6:44 am to 8:04 am and how many buses in that time period?
exitQuiz.feedback: From 6:44 am to 8:04 am there are 80 minutes. $$80 \div 5=16$$ minute intervals. Adding 16 minutes to 8:04 am gives is a time of 8:20 am.

exitQuiz.stem: The 24$$^\text{th}$$ term of an arithmetic sequence is 281. The 37$$^\text{th}$$ term is 437. Which calculation will be the starting point to finding the $$n^\text{th}$$ term of the sequence?
exitQuiz.hint: How do we find the difference between 281 and 437? How do we find how many steps this was taken over?
exitQuiz.feedback: $$${437 - 281}\over{37-24} $$ tells us that it is actually $$12n-7$$.

exitQuiz.stem: What is the $$n^\text{th}$$ term of this sequence? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The numerators 2, 9, 16, 23, ... form an arithmetic sequence. So too do the denominators 3,8,13,18, .... Find the $$n^\text{th}$$ term of each sequence.
exitQuiz.feedback: The numerators 2, 9, 16, 23, ... form an arithmetic sequence of $$n^\text{th}$$ term $$7n-5$$. The denominators 3,8,13,18, ... are the sequence $$5n-2$$ so this fractional sequence is $${7n-5} \over {5n-2}$$

options.text: It's not an arithmetic (linear) sequence we can't write an $$n^\text{th}$$ term.

exitQuiz.stem: How many triangles are there in this pattern? Don't forget to count all triangles of all sizes. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Use a systematical approach. Start with base length 1 triangles. Then do base length 2, base length 3 and so on.
exitQuiz.feedback: Base length 1: 15 pointing up, 10 pointing down. Base length 2: 10 up, 3 down. Base length 3: 6 up, 0 down.  Base length 4: 3 up, 0 down.  Base length 5: 1 up.  15 + 10 + 10 + 3 + 6 + 3 + 1 = 48 triangles

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these best describes the gradient?
exitQuiz.hint: To measure gradient we pick a coordinate on the line, draw a line of length 1 in the positive $$x$$  direction, then draw a vertical line until we meet the original line again.
exitQuiz.feedback: The gradient is a measure of how steep a line is. It is calculated by finding the rate of change in the $$y$$ direction with respect to the positive $$x$$ direction.

options.text: How much the $$y$$ values change for every 1 increase in $$x$$
How much the $$x$$ values change for every 1 increase in $$y$$
How much the $$y$$ values change for every 1 decrease in $$x$$
How much the $$x$$ values change for every 1 decrease in $$y$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these lines have a positive gradient? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Lines have a positive gradient if $$y$$ increases as $$x$$ increases.
exitQuiz.feedback: A and C have positive gradients as the $$y$$ values increase as the $$x$$ value increases. The graphs go from bottom left to top right.

exitQuiz.stem: The gradient of this line is {{ }}. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: What are the lengths of the arrows on the diagram? The gradient is the change in $$y$$ for each increase of 1 in the $$x$$ direction.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$y$$ increases by 2 when $$x$$ increases by 1 so the gradient is 2.

exitQuiz.stem: Match the lines labelled A, B, C, D with the correct gradient. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Pick an integer coordinate on the line. Move 1 in the positive $$x$$ direction. How much do you need to move in the $$y$$ direction to get back to the line?
exitQuiz.feedback: The pink graph moves right 2 and up 1 so for each increase of 1 in the positive $$x$$ direction it increases by $$1\over 2$$ in the $$y$$ direction.

exitQuiz.stem: What is the gradient of this line? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Start on the coordinate (0, -3). When $$x$$ increases by 2, $$y$$ increases by 5.
exitQuiz.feedback: When $$x$$ increases by 2 $$y$$ increases by $$5$$. For each increase of 1 in the $$x$$ direction, $$y$$ increases by $$5\over 2$$

exitQuiz.stem: What is the gradient of this line? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Read the scales carefully. One square in the $$x$$ direction represents 2. One square in the $$y$$ direction represents 10.
exitQuiz.feedback: For every increase of 2 in the $$x$$ direction, the $$y$$ values increase by 10. So for every increase of 1 in the $$x$$ direction, the $$y$$ values increase by 5.

lessons.title: Negative rate of change from a graph
lessons.outcome: I can calculate the negative rate of change (gradient) from a graph.
keyLearningPoints: Graphs can be described by looking at how quickly they fall.
The amount y decreases when x increases by one is the rate of change and is called the gradient.
The gradient will be negative if y decreases as the graph moves to the right.
The gradient can be found from any linear graph.
The gradient tells us important information about the relationship.

keywords.definition: The gradient is a measure of how steep a line is.
The absolute value of a number is its distance from zero.
Two lines are parallel if they are straight lines that are always the same (non-zero) distance apart.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these is the correct explanation for how gradient is calculated?
starterQuiz.hint: We measure gradient by looking at what happens to $$y$$ when $$x$$ increases by 1.
starterQuiz.feedback: The gradient is a measure of how steep a line is. It is calculated by finding the rate of change in the $$y$$ direction with respect to the positive $$x$$ direction.

options.text: rate of change in $$x$$ direction with respect to positive $$y$$ direction
rate of change in $$x$$ direction with respect to negative $$y$$ direction
rate of change in $$y$$ direction with respect to negative $$x$$ direction
rate of change in $$y$$ direction with respect to positive $$x$$ direction

starterQuiz.stem: The gradients of all 4 lines are {{ }}. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: For all 4 lines the graph is increasing as $$x$$ increases.
starterQuiz.feedback: If the value of $$y$$ increases as $$x$$ increases, the gradient of the line is positive.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the gradient of this line? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Pick an integer coordinate on the line. Move one in the positive $$x$$ direction, how much do you need to move in the $$y$$ direction to get back to the line?
starterQuiz.feedback: This line has a gradient of 4. For each increase of 1 in the positive $$x$$ direction, there is an increase of 4 in the $$y$$ direction

starterQuiz.stem: What is the gradient of this line? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Be careful of the scale on the $$y$$ axis. Each square represents 2.
starterQuiz.feedback: As $$x$$ increases by 1, $$y$$ increases by 6 so the gradient is 6.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these tables of values show a relationship which will have a positive gradient when plotted? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The gradient will be positive if the $$y$$ values are increasing as the $$x$$ values increase. ($$-12<-10<-8$$ , so these values are increasing)
starterQuiz.feedback: A, C and E are tables of values for relationships with positive gradients as the $$y$$ values are increasing as the $$x$$ values increase

starterQuiz.stem: Which is the correct ratio table for this graph? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Use the coordinate (0,2) as a starting point. A step on the $$x$$ axis is 3 and a step on the $$y$$ axis is 2.
starterQuiz.feedback: When $$x$$ increases by 3, $$y$$ increases by 4.  Dividing both by 3 means that $$y$$ must be increasing by $$4\over 3$$ when $$x$$ increases by 1.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these graphs have a negative gradient? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Graphs have a negative gradient if $$y$$ decreases as $$x$$ increases
exitQuiz.feedback: A, B and D all have negative gradients as the graphs are decreasing as they move right. C has a positive gradient as the graph is increasing as it moves right.

exitQuiz.stem: Match the graphs to the correct gradient. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Positive gradients will be increasing as the graph moves right and negative gradients will be decreasing as the graph moves right.
exitQuiz.feedback: The steepest line (purple) has a gradient of 3. The black and pink have positive gradients and the blue and green have negative gradients.

exitQuiz.stem: What is the gradient of this line? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The gradient will be negative because the $$y$$ values decrease as the $$x$$ values increase.
exitQuiz.feedback: As $$x$$ increases by 1, $$y$$ decreases by 3 so the gradient is -3.

exitQuiz.stem: What is the gradient of this line? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: When $$x$$ increases by 3, $$y$$ decreases by 2.
exitQuiz.feedback: For every 1 in the positive $$x$$ direction, the graph decreases by $$2\over 3$$ in the $$y$$ direction. The gradient is $$-{2\over 3}$$.

exitQuiz.stem: Starting with the steepest, put these gradients in order of steepness.
exitQuiz.hint: The larger the absolute value, the steeper the gradient. A gradient of -3 will be steeper than a gradient of 2.
exitQuiz.feedback: -8 is the steepest gradient as it has the largest absolute value. $${5\over 2} > 1$$ so $$5\over 2$$ is steeper than -1. $${1\over 2} < {2\over 3}$$ so $$-{2\over 3}$$ is steeper.

exitQuiz.stem: Which lines would be parallel to the one shown if drawn on the same axes? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Calculate the gradient of each line paying attention to the scales on the axes. Graphs with the same gradient are parallel.
exitQuiz.feedback: Lines which have the same gradient are parallel. A graph with negative gradient cannot be parallel to a graph with positive gradient.

lessons.title: Rate of change from a coordinate pair
lessons.outcome: I can calculate the rate of change (gradient) from two coordinate pairs.
keyLearningPoints: Two coordinate pairs can be plotted and joined with a line.
The gradient of this line can be calculated.
The gradient between two points can be calculated without drawing the line.
The gradient between two points can be calculated without drawing the points.
The gradient between any two points on a straight line is the gradient of the line.

keywords.definition: Two lines are parallel if they are straight lines that are always the same (non-zero) distance apart.
The gradient is a measure of how steep a line is.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the missing number in this ratio table? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The multiplicative relationship between 5 and 1 is $$\times {1\over 5}$$. The same multiplicative relationship will link 7 and the missing value.
starterQuiz.feedback: The multiplicative relationship between 5 and 1 is $$\times {1\over 5}$$ , $$7\times {1\over 5} = {7\over 5}$$.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the gradient of this line? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Pick two integer coordinates on the line. The gradient is the change in the $$y$$ coordinates for every 1 increase in the positive $$x$$ direction.
starterQuiz.feedback: The $$y$$ values increase by 2 for every increase of 1 in the $$x$$ direction. The gradient is therefore 2.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the gradient of this line? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The $$y$$ axis has a step of 2. The line is decreasing as $$x$$ increases.
starterQuiz.feedback: As $$x$$ increases by 1, $$y$$ decreases by 6. The gradient is -6.

starterQuiz.stem: Match the points on the graph below with their corresponding coordinates. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The $$x$$ coordinate tells you how far horizontally from the origin the coordinate is. The smallest $$x$$ coordinate will be the furthest left point on the graph.
starterQuiz.feedback: Even without labelled axis, we can tell the position of coordinates in relation to each other. If a coordinate has a smaller $$x$$ coordinate it will be further left. If a coordinate has a smaller $$y$$ coordinate it will be further down.

starterQuiz.stem: Match the directed number calculations with the correct answer.
starterQuiz.hint: Subtracting a negative value is the same as adding the positive value.

starterQuiz.stem: Which is the correct ratio table for the graph shown? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The $$x$$ axis has a step of 2, the $$y$$ axis has a step of 5.
starterQuiz.feedback: For every 4 increase in $$x$$ (2 squares), $$y$$ increases by 15 (3 squares).

exitQuiz.stem: Work out the gradient of the line which passes through (6,20) and (7,25). [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Gradient is the change in $$y$$ for an increase of 1 in the positive $x$$ direction.
exitQuiz.feedback: As $$x$$ increases by 1, $$y$$ increases by 5. The gradient is 5.

exitQuiz.stem: Calculate the gradient of this line which goes through the origin. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: When $$x$$ increases by 3, $$y$$ increases by 21. What does $$y$$ increase by for every $$1$$ increase in $$x$$?
exitQuiz.feedback: When $$x$$ increases by 3, $$y$$ increases by 21. Dividing both values by 3 shows that when $$x$$ increases by 1, $$y$$ increases by 7. The gradient is therefore 7.

exitQuiz.stem: A line with negative gradient is drawn through ( -4, 5) and one of these coordinates. Which coordinate could it be?
exitQuiz.hint: Sketch the coordinates to help you. The other coordinate needs to be to the right but lower or to the left but higher, to give a negative gradient.
exitQuiz.feedback: To get a negative gradient, the other coordinate must have a larger $$x$$ coordinate and smaller $$y$$ coordinate, or a smaller $$x$$ coordinate and a larger $$y$$ coordinate.

exitQuiz.stem: Work out the gradient of the line joining the coordinates (-5,11) and (-2,2). [image]
exitQuiz.hint: When $$x$$ increases by 3, $$y$$ decreases by 9.
exitQuiz.feedback: When $$x$$ increases by 3, $$y$$ decreases by 9. For each increase of 1 in the $$x$$ direction, $$y$$ decreases by 3. The gradient is -3.

exitQuiz.stem: Match the two coordinate pairs to the gradient of the line passing through them.
exitQuiz.hint: Sketch the coordinates to help you. Rearrange the coordinate pairs so the one with the smaller $$x$$ coordinate is first. Then find the change in $$x$$ and change in $$y$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: Gradient is the change in $$y$$ for each increase of 1 in the positive $$x$$ direction. Ratio tables help us when the difference between $$x$$ coordinates is not 1.

exitQuiz.stem: Which set of 3 coordinates lie on a straight line?
exitQuiz.hint: Calculate the gradient between the first and second coordinate, then the second and third coordinate. Are they the same?
exitQuiz.feedback: If the gradient between A and B then B and C are the same, all three coordinate lie on the same straight line. The gradient between (-5,-3) and (-3,3) is 3 but the gradient between (-3,3) and (2,13) is 2 so they are not all on the same line.

lessons.title: The intercept point
lessons.outcome: I can calculate the intercept point from a graph and from two coordinate pairs.
keyLearningPoints: The y-intercept can be found by considering the graph.
The y-intercept occurs when the x value is zero.
The gradient can be found from two points.
The y-intercept can be found using the gradient and one of the points.
It is useful to check using the second point while understanding the limitations of this check.

keywords.definition: The gradient is a measure of how steep a line is.
An intercept is the coordinate where a line or curve meets a given axis.
The relationship between two variables is linear if, when plotted on a pair of axes, a straight line is formed.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these sequences are linear?
starterQuiz.hint: Linear sequences will have a constant difference between terms. You could work out the first few terms of each sequence as see if the difference remains constant.
starterQuiz.feedback: Linear sequences have an $$n$$ exponent of 1. In $$3n +1 , 7 - 5n$$ and $$2n - 5$$ the variable $$n$$ has an exponent of 1.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these best describes an intercept point?
starterQuiz.hint: On most lines it is possible to find an $$x$$ intercept and a $$y$$  intercept. Where on the graph will you find these?
starterQuiz.feedback: An intercept is the coordinate where a line or curve meets a given axis.

options.text: A point on the line where the $$x$$ and $$y$$ coordinates are the same
A point on the line which you use to find the gradient.
A point on the line where both values are positive.
A point on the line where it meets an axis.

starterQuiz.stem: The tables shown have been labeled A,B,C,D,E. Match the table with the correct gradient. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The gradient is the amount the $$y$$ values increase or decrease when the $$x$$ values increase by 1.
starterQuiz.feedback: If $$y$$ increases as $$x$$ increases the gradient will be positive. If the $$y$$ values decrease when the $$x$$ values increase the gradient will be negative.

starterQuiz.stem: In a linear sequence the common difference is 3 and the tenth term is 32. What is the first term? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: There are nine additions of 3 between the first term and the tenth.
starterQuiz.feedback: Adding 3 nine times is the same as adding 27. $$32-27 = 5$$.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the gradient of the line which passes through the coordinates (4, 7) and (6,11) ?
starterQuiz.hint: The change in $$x$$ is +2 and the change in $$y$$ is +4.
starterQuiz.feedback: When $$x$$ increases by 2, $$y$$ increases by 4. For every increase of 1 in the $$x$$ direction, $$y$$ increases by 2. The gradient is 2.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the gradient of the line which passes through the coordinates (2, -6) and (0,-1) ?
starterQuiz.hint: Sketch the coordinates to help you. Rearrange the coordinate pairs so the one with the smaller $$x$$ value is first.
starterQuiz.feedback: As $$x$$ increases by 2, $$y$$ decreases by 5. The gradient is $$-{5\over 2}$$.

exitQuiz.stem: What is the $$y$$-intercept for the line formed when this table of values is plotted? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The $$y$$ intercept is the coordinate on the line where the $$x$$ value is 0.
exitQuiz.feedback: When $$x$$ is 0, $$y$$ is 6 so the $$y$$ intercept is the coordinate (0,6).

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these coordinates could be a $$y$$-intercept?
exitQuiz.hint: Any coordinate on the $$y$$ axis has an $$x$$ coordinate of 0.
exitQuiz.feedback: (0,0), (0,-7) and (0,$$2\over5$$) all have $$x$$ coordinates of 0 so must lie on the $$y$$ axis. This means they could represent a $$y$$ intercept of a line.

exitQuiz.stem: The graph shows 5 lines labelled A, B, C, D, E. Match the line to its corresponding $$y$$ intercept. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The $$y$$ intercept is the coordinate where the line crosses the $$y$$ axis.
exitQuiz.feedback: All $$y$$ intercepts will have an $$x$$ coordinate of 0. The larger the $$y$$ coordinate the higher up the axis the $$y$$ intercept is.

exitQuiz.stem: What is the $$y$$ intercept for the line belonging to this table of values? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The gradient of the line is 4. Use that to count back to the coordinate when $$x$$ is 0.
exitQuiz.feedback: The gradient of the line is 4. subtracting 4 from the $$y$$ value twice gives the coordinate (0,-7).

exitQuiz.stem: What is the $$y$$ intercept for the line belonging to this table of values? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: There are 10 additions of (-2) between the $$y$$-intercept and the coordinate (10,6).

exitQuiz.stem: Match up the $$y$$-intercepts with the corresponding lines.
exitQuiz.hint: Start by working out the gradient of each line. Use a broken table to help you count forward or back to the $$y$$ intercept.
exitQuiz.feedback: The gradient and one coordinate can be used to work out the $$y$$ intercept of the line.

lessons.title: The equation of a straight line
lessons.outcome: I can appreciate that writing linear equations in the form y = mx + c helps to reveal the structure.
keyLearningPoints: Linear relationships can be written in a variety of algebraic forms.
It is possible to identify the gradient and y-intercept when the equation is written in the form y=mx+c.
The m comes from the French "monter" (to climb/ascend) and the c from "commencer" (to start).
Linear equations can be rearranged in order to reveal the gradient and y-intercept.

keywords.definition: Any equation whose graph forms a straight line.
A constant numerical multiplier of the variables in a term.
A term that does not change; it contains no variables.

starterQuiz.stem: Which equations are represented by the bar model shown? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The length of the top and bottom bar are the same so $$a + 7$$ is equal to 20.
starterQuiz.feedback: When we know the additive relationship $$a + 7 = 20$$ it is possible to write other equations from the same relationship, including $$20 - 7 = a$$ and $$20 - a = 7 $$.

starterQuiz.stem: Fill in the missing value for the $$y$$  intercept of this line $$(0,$$ {{ }}$$)$$. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The $$y$$ intercept is the coordinate where the line crosses the $$y$$ axis. Find it on the graph.
starterQuiz.feedback: The line crosses the $$y$$ axis at $$(0,-4)$$ which is the $$y$$ intercept.

starterQuiz.stem: Match up the coordinate with the relationship it satisfies.
starterQuiz.hint: Substitute the $$x$$ and $$y$$ coordinates into the equation and see if the relationship is true for those values.
starterQuiz.feedback: We can generate coordinates which are on a line by finding $$x$$ and $$y$$ values that fit the relationship.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the gradient of this line? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: For every 2 squares right. The graph rises 7 squares. However, each square in the $$y$$ direction is worth 2.
starterQuiz.feedback: When $$x$$ increases by 2, $$y$$ increases by 14. The gradient is therefore 7.

starterQuiz.stem: Match up the expressions containing brackets with their expanded forms.
starterQuiz.hint: Multiply every term inside the bracket with the term outside the bracket.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$ 6(2x + 4)$$ is the same as $$6\times 2x + 6\times 4$$  or $$12x + 24$$.

starterQuiz.stem: Fill in this coordinate, $$(5,$$ {{ }}$$)$$, so it satisfies the equation $$2x + 2y = 10$$.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$2x = 10 , 10 + 0 = 10$$. So $$2y = 0$$. The only number that can be multiplied by 2 and still equal zero is 0.

exitQuiz.stem: Match the keywords to their definitions.
exitQuiz.hint: In the equation $$y = 3x - 4$$ the coefficient of $$x$$ is 3 and the constant is -4.
exitQuiz.feedback: When an equation of a straight line is written in the form $$y = mx + c$$ the coefficient of $$x$$ is $$m$$ and represents the gradient. The constant is $$c$$ and represents the $$y$$-intercept.

match.left: a term that does not vary
a numerical multiplier of a specific variable in a term
a measure of how steep a line is
the coordinate where a line crosses the $$y$$ axis
a relationship which, when plotted, forms a straight line

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these relationships are represented by this bar model? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Because the top and bottom bar are the same length, $$y + 5$$ must be equal to $$x$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: When we know the additive relationship $$y + 5 = x$$ it is possible to write other equations from the same relationship, including $$x - 5 = y$$ and $$x - y = 5 $$.

exitQuiz.stem: The graph shows 5 lines labelled A, B, C, D and E. Match the line to its gradient and $$y$$ intercept. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The $$y$$ intercept is the coordinate where the line crosses the $$y$$ axis. Lines with negative gradients will be decreasing as the values of $$x$$ increase.
exitQuiz.feedback: Any non-vertical straight line can be defined by its $$y$$ intercept (where it crosses the $$y$$ axis) and its gradient (the steepness of the line).

exitQuiz.stem: Match the equations of lines to their key features.
exitQuiz.hint: All these are in the form $$y = mx + c$$. Be careful of negative values: in $$y = 7 - 2x $$ the gradient would be -2 and the $$y$$-intercept $$(0,7)$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: All these are in the form $$y = mx + c$$. The coefficient of $$x$$ represents the gradient and the constant is the $$y$$-intercept.

exitQuiz.stem: What are the key features of the graph with equation $$y= 3(5 - 2x)$$ ?
exitQuiz.hint: Expand the bracket to write the equation in the form $$y = mx + c$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: This is the same as $$y = 15 - 6x$$ so the gradient is -6 and the $$y$$-intercept is $$(0,15)$$.

exitQuiz.stem: Which coordinates are on the line $$2x - y = 5$$ ?
exitQuiz.hint: Substitute the $$x$$ and $$y$$ coordinates into the expression $$2x - y$$ and see if it equals 5.
exitQuiz.feedback: This is actually the same relationship as $$y = 2x - 5$$ so the $$y$$ coordinates of points on this line will be double the $$x$$ coordinate minus 5.

lessons.title: Finding the equation of the line y = mx + c
lessons.outcome: I can find the equation of the line in the form y = mx + c
keyLearningPoints: Linear equations can be rearranged into the form y  =mx + c.
The gradient and intercept can be identified from the graph.
The equation of the line can be written in the form y = mx + c.

keywords.definition: An equation of a line is any equation whose graph forms a straight line.
The gradient is a measure of how steep a line is.
An intercept is the coordinate where a line or curve meets a given axis.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the $$y$$-intercept of the line with equation $$y = 5x - 1$$ ?
starterQuiz.hint: When in the form $$y = mx + c$$, the $$y$$-intercept is the value of the constant.
starterQuiz.feedback: This equation is in the form $$y = mx + c$$ so the constant $$-1$$ is the value of $$y$$ when $$x$$ is zero. The $$y$$-intercept therefore is (0,-1).

starterQuiz.stem: What is the gradient of the line with equation $$y = x + 7$$ ?
starterQuiz.hint: This equation could also be written as $$y = 1x + 7$$.
starterQuiz.feedback: This equation is in the form $$y = mx + c$$ so the coefficient of $$x$$ is the gradient. In $$y = x + 7$$, the coefficient of $$x$$ is 1.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the gradient of this line? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The $$y$$ axis has a step of 5.
starterQuiz.feedback: As $$x$$ increases by 1, $$y$$ decreases by 5. So the gradient is -5.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the value of the expression $$10 - 3x$$ when $$x=2$$ ?
starterQuiz.hint: Substitute $$x=2$$ into the expression e.g. $$10 - 3(2)$$.

starterQuiz.stem: Which coordinates are on the line $$ y = 5x - 6 $$ ?
starterQuiz.hint: Substitute the $$x$$ and $$y$$ coordinates into the equation and see if they satisfy the rule.
starterQuiz.feedback: The $$y$$ coordinate is 5 times the $$x$$ coordinate minus 6.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the $$y$$-intercept for the line formed when these coordinates are plotted? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The gradient of the line is -3. There are 5 additions of the gradient between the $$y$$-intercept and coordinate (5,4).

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these is an equation for the line which has $$y$$-intercept (0,-4) and gradient 3?
exitQuiz.hint: When in the form $$y = mx + c$$, $$m$$ represents the gradient.
exitQuiz.feedback: When in the form $$y = mx + c$$ the coefficient of $$x$$ is the gradient and the constant is the $$y$$-intercept.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these is an equation for the line which has gradient -1 and $$y$$-intercept 5?
exitQuiz.hint: The lines $$y=-x, y= -x + 2, y = 3 - x$$, all have gradients of -1.
exitQuiz.feedback: When in the form $$y = mx + c$$ the coefficient of $$x$$ is the gradient and the constant is the $$y$$-intercept.

exitQuiz.stem: The equation of this line is: $$y =$$ {{}}$$x - 1$$. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: When in the form $$y = mx + c$$ the coefficient of $$x$$ is the gradient.
exitQuiz.feedback: For each increase of 1 in the $$x$$ direction, the graph increases by 3 so the gradient is 3.

exitQuiz.stem: The equation of the line formed by plotting these coordinates is: $$y =$$ {{}} $$- 2x$$. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The gradient is -2 so the equation contains the term $$-2x$$ The constant term is missing.
exitQuiz.feedback: The $$y$$ intercept is (0,6) so the constant term must be 6. This can be written before or after the term $$-2x$$.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these is the equation of this line? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: This line has a negative gradient and a negative $$y$$-intercept.
exitQuiz.feedback: The gradient is -3 and the $$y$$-intercept (0,-4) so the equation can be written as $$y = -3x - 4$$.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these is the equation of the line joining the coordinates (-4,1) and (2,-2)? Use the broken table to help. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The gradient of the line is $$-{1\over 2}$$. Use this to find the $$y$$ intercept.
exitQuiz.feedback: The gradient of the line is $$-{1\over 2}$$. Using the coordinate (2,-2): $$2\times {1\over2} = 1, -2 + 1 = -1$$.

lessons.title: Finding the equation of the line ay + bx + c = 0
lessons.outcome: I can appreciate that writing linear equations in the form ay + bx + c = 0 may be more appropriate.
keyLearningPoints: Linear equations can be written in multiple forms.
One of these forms is ay + bx + c = 0.
This form can be more appropriate in some contexts and situations.

keywords.definition: An equation of a line is any equation whose graph forms a straight line.

starterQuiz.stem: The equation of this line is: $$y =$$ {{}} $$- 2x$$. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The gradient is -2 so the equation contains the term $$-2x$$. The constant term is missing.
starterQuiz.feedback: The $$y$$ intercept is (0,3) so the constant term must be 3. This can be written before or after the term $$-2x$$.

starterQuiz.stem: This coordinate, ({{ }}, 0), lies on the line $$y + x = 4$$. What is the missing $$x$$ coordinate?
starterQuiz.hint: 0 plus what number gives the answer 4?
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$(0) + x = 4$$, $$0 + 4 = 4$$ so the $$x$$ coordinate must be 4.

starterQuiz.stem: This coordinate, ({{ }}, 0), lies on the line $$y + x = 7$$. What is the missing $$x$$ coordinate?
starterQuiz.hint: 0 add what number gives the answer 7?
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$(0) + x = 7$$, $$0 + 7 = 7$$ so the $$x$$ coordinate must be 7.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these coordinates lie on the $$x$$ axis?
starterQuiz.hint: The $$x$$ axis is the horizontal axis. Coordinates on this line have not moved vertically from the origin, only horizontally.
starterQuiz.feedback: Coordinates on the $$x$$ axis will have a $$y$$ coordinate of 0.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these equations could be represented by this bar model? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The top and bottom bars are the same length so $$y + 8$$ must be the equal to $$5x$$.
starterQuiz.feedback: When we know the additive relationship $$y + 8 = 5x$$ we can find other equivalent relationships. E.g. $$5x - y =8$$ and $$5x - 8 = y$$.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these equations are written in the form $$y = mx + c$$ ?
starterQuiz.hint: The variable term and constant term can be written either way round.
starterQuiz.feedback: Equations in the form $$y = mx + c$$ are written so one side of the equation has a single positive $$y$$, the other side of the equation has a variable term and/ or a constant term (no constant is equivalent to having a constant of 0).

exitQuiz.stem: The graph shows 5 lines labelled A, B, C, D and E. Match the lines to the equations. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Horizontal lines can be written in the form $$y=a$$ where $$a$$ is a constant. Vertical lines can be written in the form $$x = a$$ where $$a$$ is a constant.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$x = -4$$ is a vertical line with $$x$$ intercept (-4,0). The other lines are written in the form $$y = mx + c$ where $$m$$ is the gradient and $$c$$ is the $$y$$-intercept.

exitQuiz.stem: Which equations are represented in this bar model? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Use the bar model to find the equation in the form $$y = mx + c$$ and $$ay + bx + c = 0$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: The length of the top and bottom bars are the same so the equation can be written as $$y = 2x + 4 $$. The whole of one bar subtract the whole of the other will equal zero $$(2x + 4) - y = 0$$.

exitQuiz.stem: Which equations are represented in this bar model? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: To write an equation equal to zero, the whole of one bar must be subtracted from the other. $$4x-(y+2)=0$$ or $$(y + 2) - 4x = 0$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: We can use the bar model to write in the form $$y = mx + c$$. The whole of the top bar subtract the bottom bar gives the equation $$y + 2 - 4x = 0$$. The whole of the bottom bar subtract the top bar gives $$4x - y - 2 = 0$$.

exitQuiz.stem: Match the $$y$$-intercepts to the correct graph in the form $$y + x + c = 0$$
exitQuiz.hint: A line crosses the $$y$$ axis when $$x=0$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: Substituting $$x=0$$ into each equation gives the $$y$$-intercept. E.g. $$y + (0) + 7 = 0$$, $$y + 7 = 0 $$, $$-7 + 7 = 0 $$ so $$y$$ must be -7. This gives the coordinate (0,-7).

exitQuiz.stem: Match the $$x$$-intercepts to the correct graph in the form $$y + x + c = 0$$
exitQuiz.hint: A line crosses the $$x$$ axis when $$y=0$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: Substituting $$y=0$$ into each equation gives the $$x$$-intercept. E.g. $$(0) - x + 5 = 0$$, $$-x + 5 = 0 $$, $$5 - x = 0 $$ so $$x$$ must be 5. This gives the coordinate (5,0).

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these are the correct $$x$$ and $$y$$-intercepts for the equation $$3x + y - 6 = 0$$ ?
exitQuiz.hint: Substitute $$y=0$$ to get the $$x$$ intercept. Once you know what $$3x$$ must equal you can use a bar model and split in 3 pieces to see what $$1x$$ is equal to.

lessons.title: Using dynamic software to explore linear relationships
lessons.outcome: I can solve a range of problems involving graphical and algebraic aspects of linear relationships using dynamic software.
keyLearningPoints: Dynamic software can be used to investigate how the gradients affects the line.
Dynamic software can be used to investigate how the intercept affects the line.
Dynamic software can be used to investigate connections between lines, coordinates, tables and algebraic representations

keywords.definition: The gradient is a measure of how steep a line is.
An intercept is the coordinate where a line or curve meets a given axis.

starterQuiz.stem: Relationships in the form of $$y=mx+c$$ will give us a {{ }}.
starterQuiz.hint: When plotting graphs on cartesian coordinate grids if the exponents of $$x$$ and $$y$$ are $$1$$ we will have a linear relationship.
starterQuiz.feedback: Relationships in the form of $$y=mx+c$$ will give us a straight line (linear) graph because both the $$x$$ and $$y$$ exponents are $$1$$.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the gradient of this line? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The gradient is the change in $$y$$ for every change of $$1$$ in the positive $$x$$-direction.
starterQuiz.feedback: The gradient is $$+3$$. The rate of change of $$y$$ is $$+3$$ for every change of $$+1$$ in $$x$$.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these coordinates is $$(0,3)$$? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Coordinates are written in the form $$(x,y)$$ with the $$x$$ coordinate written first, the $$y$$ coordinate second.
starterQuiz.feedback: B is coordinate $$(0,3)$$.  $$0$$ in the $$x$$-direction and $$+3$$ in the $$y$$-direction from the origin.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these coordinates sits on the $$y$$-axis? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The $$x$$-axis is the horizontal axis. The $$y$$-axis is the vertical one.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$(0,-6)$$ is the coordinate which sits on the $$y$$-axis.

starterQuiz.stem: This table of values will plot a linear relationship with what gradient? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The gradient is the change in $$y$$ for every change of $$1$$ in the positive $$x$$-direction.
starterQuiz.feedback: The gradient is $$+4$$. The rate of change of $$y$$ is $$+4$$ for every change of $$+1$$ in $$x$$.

starterQuiz.stem: This table of values will plot a linear relationship with what gradient? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The gradient is the change in $$y$$ for every change of $$1$$ in the positive $$x$$-direction.
starterQuiz.feedback: The gradient is $$+2$$. The rate of change of $$y$$ is $$+4$$ for every change of $$+2$$ in $$x$$ which gives us a rate of change of $$+2$$ for every $$+1$$ in $$x$$.

exitQuiz.stem: For relationships in the form $$y=mx+c$$ the value of $$m$$ determines the {{ }}.
exitQuiz.hint: The line $$y=5x-3$$ would have a gradient of $$5$$ and a $$y$$ intercept of $$(0,-3)$$
exitQuiz.feedback: For lines in the form $$y=mx+c$$ the value of $$m$$ determines the gradient. For example, the line $$y=5x-3$$ would have a gradient of $$5$$.

exitQuiz.stem: What of these statements will be true about the lines $$y=3x$$, $$y=7x$$, and $$y=-2x$$?
exitQuiz.hint: Go to Desmos.com, click 'Graphing calculator' and draw these lines to compare them.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$y=3x$$, $$y=7x$$, and $$y=-2x$$ have differing gradients of $$+3$$, $$+7$$, and $$-2$$ respectively but, they all share the same $$y$$-intercept of $$(0,0)$$.

options.text: They will all have a different gradient.
One and only one of the lines will have a negative gradient.
They will all have a different $$y$$-intercept.

exitQuiz.stem: What is the equation of this line? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Lines in the form $$y=mx$$ all have a $$y$$-intercept of $$(0,0)$$ but varying gradients.
exitQuiz.feedback: A gradient of $$1\over2$$ and a $$y$$-intercept of $$(0,0)$$ makes this the line $$y={1\over2}x$$.

exitQuiz.stem: Which statements are true about the lines $$y=x+5$$, $$y=x+9$$, and $$y=x+0.5$$?
exitQuiz.hint: Go to Desmos.com, click 'Graphing calculator' and draw these lines to compare them.
exitQuiz.feedback: The lines $$y=x+5$$, $$y=x+9$$, and $$y=x+0.5$$ all have the same gradient of $$+1$$ making them parallel lines. However, they have different $$y$$-intercepts of $$(0,5)$$, $$(0,9)$$, ad $$(0,0.5)$$ respectively.

exitQuiz.stem: The lines $$y=4-7x$$ and $$y=-0.1-7x$$ have the same {{ }}.
exitQuiz.hint: For lines in the form $$y=mx+c$$ or $$y=c+mx$$ the value of $$m$$, the coefficient of $$x$$, determines the gradient.
exitQuiz.feedback: For lines in the form $$y=mx+c$$ or $$y=c+mx$$ the value of $$m$$, the coefficient of $$x$$, determines the gradient. Both $$y=4-7x$$ and $$y=-0.1-7x$$ have an $$x$$ coefficient of $$-7$$ therefore have the same gradient.

exitQuiz.stem: Calculate the equation of the line. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: For lines in the form $$y=mx+c$$ and $$y=c+mx$$ the gradient is determined by the value of $$m$$ and the $$y$$-intercept the determined by the value of $$c$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: This is the line $$y=0.45-0.3x$$ with a $$y$$-intercept of $$(0,0.45)$$ and a gradient of $$-0.3$$.

lessons.title: Problem solving with graphing linear relationships
lessons.outcome: I can use my knowledge of graphing linear relationships to solve problems.
keyLearningPoints: Real life relationships can be represented using a linear graph.
Real life problems can be solved using a linear graph.
Switching between algebraic and graphical representations can help solve real life problems.

keywords.definition: The rate of change is how one variable changes with respect to another. If constant, there is a linear relationship.
The gradient is a measure of how steep a line is.

starterQuiz.stem: The gradient is a measure of how __________ a line is.
starterQuiz.hint: The gradient is the rate of change in the $$y$$-direction with respect to the positive $$x$$-direction.
starterQuiz.feedback: The gradient is a measure of how steep a line is.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the values are missing from the table of values for the first five terms of the sequence $$7n-10$$? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Substitute $$n=1$$, $$n=2$$, and $$n=4$$ into the expression $$7n-10$$ to find the respective terms.
starterQuiz.feedback: The first term, when $$n=1$$ is $$7(1)-10=-3$$ and there is a common difference of $$+7$$ from there giving us the sequence $$-3,4,11,18,25, ...$$

starterQuiz.stem: A pupil is saving money. They start with $$£30$$ and save $$£8$$ per week. How much will they have after $$5$$ weeks?
starterQuiz.hint: Substitute $$w=5$$ into the expression $$30+8w$$ to find the amount saved after $$5$$ weeks.

starterQuiz.stem: At what coordinates do these two lines intersect? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The intersection is where the lines cross each other.
starterQuiz.feedback: The lines intersect each other at coordinates $$(5,15)$$.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these lines has the steeper gradient? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The gradient is the rate of change in the $$y$$-direction with respect to the positive $$x$$-direction.
starterQuiz.feedback: Line A has the steepest gradient. It has the greatest rate of change in the $$y$$-direction for every change of $$+1$$ in $$x$$.

starterQuiz.stem: Will this table of values plot a linear relationship? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: In order to have a linear relationship both variables need to change at a constant rate with respect to one another.
starterQuiz.feedback: These values will not plot a linear relationship. The $$x$$ coordinates do not have a constant difference whilst the $$y$$ ones do have a constant difference. This means the points will not align.

options.text: Yes. The $$y$$ values have a constant difference of $$+5$$.
No. Both variables are not changing at a constant rate.
It's impossible to tell until plotted.

exitQuiz.stem: On a time distance graph a greater speed is represented by a steeper {{ }}.
exitQuiz.hint: The gradient of a time distance graph shows us the rate of change of distance with respect to time.
exitQuiz.feedback: On a time distance graph a greater speed is represented by the steeper gradient.

exitQuiz.stem: The graph shows the cost of two taxi companies for miles travelled. Which firm is cheapest for a $$3$$ mile journey? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Miles $$(m)$$ are on the horizontal axis. Look for $$3$$ and take readings from the lines directly above.
exitQuiz.feedback: After $$3$$ miles firm B's charge ($$£10$$) is less than that of firm A.

options.text: They cost the same price for that many miles.
It's impossible to tell from the graph.

exitQuiz.stem: The graph shows the cost of two taxi companies for miles travelled. At how many miles do they cost the same price? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The intersection of the two lines will be the moment when they have the same distance travelled and the same cost in $$£$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: At $$5$$ miles the lines intersect. At this moment the two firms have the same distance travelled and the same cost in $$£$$.

exitQuiz.stem: The graph shows the cost of two taxi companies for miles travelled. How much do firm A charge per mile in $$£$$? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: What is the rate of change of $$c$$ with respect to every change of $$+1$$ in $$m$$?
exitQuiz.feedback: A cost of $$£10$$ for $$0$$ miles and $$£25$$ for $$10$$ miles sees a change of $$£15$$ across $$10$$ miles which, at a constant rate, is $$£1.50$$ per mile.

exitQuiz.stem: This graph shows the time $$(t)$$ and distance $$(d)$$ of a car journey. For how long did the car stop? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The car is stopped when there is not change in distance over time.
exitQuiz.feedback: The car stops after $$10$$ minutes and stays stopped until $$25$$ minutes meaning a stop of $$15$$ minutes.

exitQuiz.stem: This graph shows the time $$(t)$$ and distance $$(d)$$ of a car journey. When is the car moving fastest? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Where is the rate of change of $$d$$ with respect to $$t$$ greatest? That is the fastest speed.
exitQuiz.feedback: The gradient is steepest between $$25$$ to $$30$$ minutes which is $$8$$ to $$16$$ kilometres. This is when the car is moving the fastest.

units.title: Solving linear equations
units.description: In this unit pupils will learn how to find a value that satisfies a linear relationship when one value is known both with a single step operation, and multiple step operations. A variety of cases are explored including using brackets and rearranging.

lessons.title: Checking understanding of algebraic notation
lessons.outcome: I can represent situations using algebra.
keyLearningPoints: Missing numbers can be found in context.
Missing number problems can be expressed algebraically.
Pairs of numbers that satisfy an equation with two unknowns can be found.
Real life situations can be expressed using algebra.

keywords.definition: An integer is any positive or negative whole number or zero
An expression contains one or more terms, where each term is separated by an operator.
An equation is used to show 2 expressions that are equal to each other.

starterQuiz.stem: Here is a number line with two numbers shown. What calculation will work out the length of the arrow? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The arrow is the difference between 134 and 98
starterQuiz.feedback: To find the difference between two values, you can subtract the values.

starterQuiz.stem: Which calculation represents a half of 8?
starterQuiz.hint: In mathematics 'of' means multiply.
starterQuiz.feedback: A half of a value is the same as a half times a value so half of 8 is $${1\over 2} \times 8. $$ Multiplying by $$1\over 2$$ is the same as dividing by 2 so $$8\over 2$$ is also correct.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these are integers?
starterQuiz.hint: Integers can include negative values.
starterQuiz.feedback: An integer is any positive or negative whole number or zero.

starterQuiz.stem: A bag of sweets costs 5 p, which of these could represent the cost of buying any number of bags of sweets?
starterQuiz.hint: How would you calculate the cost of 3 bags of sweets?
starterQuiz.feedback: To calculate the cost of any number of bags of sweets you multiply the number of bags ($$a$$) by 5. $$a$$ multiplied by 5 is written as $$5a$$. Numbers are always written before letter symbols.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each calculation to its answer.
starterQuiz.hint: Priority of operations dictates that multiplication has priority over addition.
starterQuiz.feedback: Brackets can be used to group calculations and change the priority of operations. Multiplication should be evaluated before addition.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each calculation to its answer.
starterQuiz.hint: When evaluating, it can help to write the numerator and denominator as a single value rather than a calculation.
starterQuiz.feedback: In fractional notation, the entire numerator and the entire denominator are grouped so brackets are not needed.

exitQuiz.stem: Which equations are represented by this bar model? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The top and bottom bars are the same length so the sum of the terms in both bars are equal.
exitQuiz.feedback: The top and bottom bars are equal so $$y + 7 = 4x.$$ It does not matter which side of the equals sign the expressions $$y + 7$$ and $$4x$$ are on.

exitQuiz.stem: Which diagram could represent a rectangle that has a length 3 times its width?
exitQuiz.hint: If the rectangle has width $$x$$, the length will be 3 lots of $$x$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: If the rectangle has length $$x$$ then its width will be $$3x$$ or $$x + x + x$$.

exitQuiz.stem: Match up equivalent terms.
exitQuiz.hint: A negative value divided by a negative value gives a positive value.
exitQuiz.feedback: Division is equivalent to multiplying by the reciprocal, dividing two negative values gives a positive answer.

exitQuiz.stem: Match each expressions to its description.
exitQuiz.hint: Subtraction is not commutative so make sure your terms are written the correct way round.
exitQuiz.feedback: Describing situations in English can be ambiguous, when writing mathematically we adhere to priority of operations to remove ambiguity.

match.left: a number multiplied by 3 then subtract 7
a number subtract 7 then multiplied by 3
a number subtract the product of 7 and 3
a number multiplied by 3 then subtracted from 7
a number subtracted from 7 then multiplied by 3

exitQuiz.stem: Select the values of $$a$$ and $$b$$ that satisfy the equation $$2a + 6b = 12$$.
exitQuiz.hint: Substitute the values for $$a$$ and $$b$$ and see if the expression on the left equals 12
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$2(4.5) + 6(0.5)$$, $$9 + 3 = 12$$ so $$a=4.5$$ and $$b=0.5$$ satisfies the equation. $$2(3) + 6(1)$$, $$6 +6 = 12$$ so $$a=3$$ and $$b=1$$ also satisfies the equation.

exitQuiz.stem: Andeep has 2 blocks, one block is 5 cm smaller than the other. The blocks have a combined height of 121 cm. How tall is the larger block? {{ }} cm
exitQuiz.hint: Draw a diagram to help, one block on top of the other will be 121 cm tall.
exitQuiz.feedback: One block is 5 cm taller than the other. $$121 - 5 = 116$$, so two of the smaller block are 116 cm tall. $$116\div 2 = 58$$. The smaller block is 58 cm, so the larger block is $$58 + 5 = 63$$, which is 63 cm.

lessons.title: Securing understanding of equality
lessons.outcome: I can appreciate how to maintain equality between two statements.
keyLearningPoints: Bar models can be used to compare expressions.
If the expressions are equal the bars will be the same length.
Operations can be performed on the bars that maintain equality.
This can be extended to operations on statements expressed algebraically.

keywords.definition: An equation is used to show two expressions that are equal to each other.
A variable is a quantity that can take on a range of values, often denoted by a letter.
A constant is a term that does not change; it contains no variables.
Like terms are terms that have the same set of variables and corresponding exponents.

starterQuiz.stem: Aisha is $$a$$ years old. Which of these is an expression for her age 2 years ago?
starterQuiz.hint: What is your age now? how would you calculate your age two years ago?
starterQuiz.feedback: Subtracting 2 from her current age will give her age 2 years ago.

starterQuiz.stem: Andeep is thinking of a number, when he adds 2 then multiplies by 5 he gets 27. Which of these equations represents his number?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider priority of operations. Its the whole of the value of his number add 2 that he wants to multiply.
starterQuiz.feedback: The total value of his number add 2 needs to be multiplied by 5, so brackets need to be written around the expression $$a + 2$$ giving $$5(a + 2)=27$$

starterQuiz.stem: Which equations are represented by this bar model? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The top and bottom bars are the same length, so the sum of the terms in both bars are equal.
starterQuiz.feedback: The top and bottom bars are equal, so $$y + 6 = 3x.$$ It does not matter which side of the equals sign the expressions $$y + 6$$ and $$3x$$ are on.

starterQuiz.stem: Select the calculation that is equivalent to $$8+4\over 4$$.
starterQuiz.hint: Check your answer by trying the calculations. $$\frac{8+4}{4} = 3$$
starterQuiz.feedback: Dividing the sum of two terms by 4 is the same as dividing each term by 4. $$8+4\over 4$$ is equivalent to $${8\over 4}+{4\over 4}$$

starterQuiz.stem: Which expression is represented by this bar model? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The bar shows 3 lots of the expression $$2a + 2$$
starterQuiz.feedback: The bar shows 3 lots of the expression $$2a + 2$$ which is written as $$3(2a + 2)$$ Grouping like terms in the bar model shows this is the same as $$6a + 2 + 2 + 2$$ or $$6a + 6$$

starterQuiz.stem: Match each expressions containing brackets with its expanded form.
starterQuiz.hint: Multiply every term inside the bracket with the term outside the bracket.
starterQuiz.feedback: A negative value multiplied by a negative value gives a positive value so $$-2(-3x - 4)$$ is the same as $$-2\times -3x + -2 \times -4$$ giving $$6x + 8$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these is the best definition for like terms?
exitQuiz.hint: $$$5x$$ and $$5y$$ are not like terms. $$3x$$ and $$3x^2$$ are not like terms.
exitQuiz.feedback: Like terms are terms that have the same set of variables and corresponding exponents.  $$5xy, 3xy, -2xy$$ and $$xy$$ are all like terms.

options.text: Terms which when added, sum to zero.
Terms with the same coefficient for each variable.
Terms with the same set of variables and corresponding exponents.
Identical terms which have the same coefficient and same variables.
Terms with the same variable and different exponents.

exitQuiz.stem: These 5 bar models represent operations performed on the equation $$x + 9 = 22$$. Match the bar models labelled A, B, C, D and E with the equivalent equation they represent.  [image]
