exitQuiz.hint: Check to see if the same thing has been added to both bars. If not, check if both bars been multiplied by the same amount.
exitQuiz.feedback: Because $$x + 9 = 22$$ adding $$x + 9$$ and adding $$22$$ have the same effect. If $$x + 9$$ has been added to the top bar and 22 to the bottom bar, the equation has doubled.

exitQuiz.stem: This bar model represents the initial equation $$2a + 6 = 14.$$ What needs to be done to the bottom bar to maintain equality? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The top bar has not been doubled. There is double the value of $$a$$ but the 6 has not been doubled.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$2a$$ has been added to the top bar so $$2a$$ needs to be added to the bottom bar. This is not the same as doubling as the 6 has not been doubled on the top bar.

exitQuiz.stem: If $$x + 5 =2$$, which of these equations have maintained equality?
exitQuiz.hint: The some operation needs to have been performed to the entire left hand expression and the right hand expression.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$2x + 5 = 4$$ has not maintained equality as the whole of the left hand expression has not been doubled. $$x + 12 = 10$$ has not maintained equality as 7 has been added to the LHS but 8 has been added to the RHS.

exitQuiz.stem: If $$a = b$$, which of the following are true?
exitQuiz.hint: To maintain equality, the same operation must be performed to both sides of the equation.
exitQuiz.feedback: If $$a = b$$ then $$a + c = b + c,    a - c = b - c,    ac = bc $$ and $$  {a\over c}={b\over c}$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which expression could fill the blank on the right hand side of this equation to maintain equality? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Think about what has been added to the left hand side. Could this also be written as a multiplication of the left hand side?
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$2a$$ and $$2b$$ have been added to the left hand side, so they need to be added to the right hand side to maintain equality. This is equivalent to multiplying the LHS by 3 so the RHS could be multiplied by 3 to maintain equality.

lessons.title: Different types of equations
lessons.outcome: I can recognise that there are many different types of equations of which linear is one type.
keyLearningPoints: An equation is a statement that two expressions are equal, indicated by =.
Linear expressions can be represented by a straight line on a graph.
Non-linear expressions can be identified from their graphical form.
Equations can be grouped as linear or non-linear.

keywords.definition: The gradient is a measure of how steep a line is
Expressions contain one or more terms, where each term is separated by an operator.
An equation is used to show that one number or calculation is equal to another.
The relationship between two variables is linear if, when plotted on a pair of axes, a straight line is formed.

starterQuiz.stem: Work out the value of $$(−4)^2$$.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$(−4)\times (−4) = 16$$ as a negative number multiplied by a negative number gives a positive number. So a negative number squared will be positive.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these is the best description of the gradient of a line?
starterQuiz.hint: The gradient is a rate of change between the $$x$$ and $$y$$ values.
starterQuiz.feedback: The gradient is a measure of how steep a line is. It is calculated by finding the rate of change in the $$y$$ direction with respect to the positive $$x$$ direction.

options.text: the $$x$$ value where the line crosses the $$x$$-axis
the vertical distance from the origin to the line

starterQuiz.stem: Select the coordinates that lie on the line $$y = 2x − 3$$.
starterQuiz.hint: Substitute the $$x$$ coordinate into the expression on the right hand side of the equation and see if it equals the $$y$$ coordinate.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$2(1) − 3 = −1$$ so (1, −1) is on the line. $$2(4) − 3 = 5$$ so (4, 5) is on the line.

starterQuiz.stem: The table shows values for the equation $$y = 5 − 3x$$. The missing number is {{ }}. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Substitute $$x=2$$ into the equation $$y = 5 − 3x$$

starterQuiz.stem: When the equation of a straight line is written in the form $$y = mx + c$$, ($$m$$) is the coefficient of $$x$$ and represents the {{ }}.
starterQuiz.hint: Straight lines can be uniquely defined by their gradient and $$y$$ intercept.
starterQuiz.feedback: When in the form $$y = mx + c,$$ the coefficient of $$x$$ is the gradient and the constant is the $$y$$ intercept.

starterQuiz.stem: Work out the value of $$y$$ that satisfies the equation $$3x + y = 6(x − 2)$$ when $$x = 5$$. $$y =$$ {{ }}
starterQuiz.hint: Substituting $$x = 5$$ gives the equation $$3(5) + y = 6 (3) $$
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$3(5) + y = 6(5 − 2)$$, $$15 + y = 18$$. The equation is balanced when $$y = 3$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these equations are linear? The graphs of the equations are shown. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The relationship between two variables is linear if it forms a straight line when plotted.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$y = {3^2} − {x\over 4}$$ is a linear equation because it forms a straight line when plotted. It is also in the form $$y = mx + c$$ with gradient $$−{1\over 4}$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which is the correct graph of the expression $$2 − 4t$$ as $$t$$ varies? The table of values for $$2 − 4t$$ is shown. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Which graph goes through all 3 points from the table of values? Think about where the coordinates will be in relation to the $$x$$ and $$y$$ axes.
exitQuiz.feedback: The expression $$2 − 4t$$ will be a straight line when plotted with gradient $$−4$$ and $$y$$ intercept (0, 2)

exitQuiz.stem: The table of values for $$y = {30\over x}$$ is shown. The missing value is {{ }}. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Substitute 2 for $$x$$ in the equation $$y = {30\over x}$$

exitQuiz.stem: Select the correct graph of the expression $$y = {x^3} − 5$$. The table of values for $$y = {x^3} − 5$$ is shown. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: $$$y = {x^3} − 5$$ is not a linear relationship.
exitQuiz.feedback: The coordinates (−1, −6), (0, −5), (1, −4) and (2, 3) all lie on the curve with equation $$y = {x^3} − 5$$

exitQuiz.stem: The table of values for $$ 2x + y = 5(x − 1)$$ is shown. The missing value is {{ }}. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Substitute $$x=2$$ into the equation and find a value of $$y$$ which satisfies the relationship.

exitQuiz.stem: The table of values for $$ xy = 12$$ is shown. The missing value is {{ }}. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: $$$xy$$ means $$x\times y$$ What must $$y$$ be when $$x$$ is 2?

lessons.title: Equality in an equation
lessons.outcome: I can appreciate that in an equation the two sides of the equals sign balance.
keyLearningPoints: The equals sign means that the two sides of the equation have the same value.
This can be described as the expressions balancing.
The equality of the expressions can be represented with a bar model.
It is possible to rearrange equations to find the family of alternative versions of the equation.

keywords.definition: An equation is used to show two expressions that are equal to each other.

starterQuiz.stem: Which expression is represented by this bar model? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The bar shows 2 lots of the expression $$3x +6$$
starterQuiz.feedback: The bar shows 2 lots of the expression $$3x +6$$ which can be written as $$2(3x+6)$$. Grouping like terms in the bar model shows this is equivalent to $$6x + 12$$

starterQuiz.stem: Select the bar model that correctly represents the equation $$3x + 15 = x + 32$$.
starterQuiz.hint: All the $$x$$ tiles should be the same width in the same bar model.
starterQuiz.feedback: Both sides of an equation have equal value so a bar representing $$3x + 15$$ and a bar representing $$x + 32$$ should be equal in length. All $$x$$ tiles should be the same length.

starterQuiz.stem: Given that $$2.4 + 3.7 = 6.1$$, which of these are also true?
starterQuiz.hint: Subtraction is the inverse operation to addition. If $$2 + 4 = 6$$ then you also know $$6 − 4 = 2$$
starterQuiz.feedback: If $$a + b = c$$ then $$b + a = c$$, $$c − b = a$$ and $$c − a = b$$

starterQuiz.stem: This bar model represents the initial equation $$x + 16 = 27$$. What needs to be done to the top bar to maintain equality? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: $$$x + 16$$ has the same value as 27. The same value has to be added to both bars to maintain equality.
starterQuiz.feedback: 27 has been added to the bottom bar so 27 could be added to the top bar to maintain equality. $$x + 16$$ has the same value as 27, so $$x + 16$$ could be added to the top bar to maintain equality, (this is equivalent to doubling both bars).

starterQuiz.stem: This bar model represents the initial equation $$2x + 5 = 9$$. What needs to be done to the top bar to maintain equality? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The bottom bar now represents $$3(2x+5)$$
starterQuiz.feedback: The bottom bar has been multiplied by 3, so multiplying the top bar by 3 will maintain equality. The bottom bar is now $$4x + 10$$ longer so adding $$4x + 10$$ to the top bar will also maintain equality.

starterQuiz.stem: These 4 bar models represent operations performed on the equation $$x + 12 = 19$$. Match the bar models labelled A, B, C, D  with the equivalent equation they represent . [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Check to see if the same thing has been added to both bars. If not, have both bars been multiplied by the same amount?
starterQuiz.feedback: Because $$x + 12 = 19$$ adding $$x + 12$$ and adding $$19$$ have the same effect. Adding 2 lots of $$x + 12$$ to $$x + 12$$  is equivalent to adding 38 or multiplying by 3.

exitQuiz.stem: Which equations are represented by this bar model? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The top and bottom bars are the same length. If you start with the entire bottom bar and subtract part of the top bar, what are you left with?

exitQuiz.stem: Which equations are represented by this bar model? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Find the expression on the left hand side of the equation in the bar model (shading it may help). How can you get that part of the bar model from the rest?
exitQuiz.feedback: The top and bottom bars are the same length. If you start with the entirety of one bar and subtract part of the other bar, you get the remainder of that bar.

exitQuiz.stem: If $$31 − x = 17$$, which of these equations are also true?
exitQuiz.hint: Draw a bar model to help you.
exitQuiz.feedback: If $$31 − x = 17$$ then 31 must equal $$17 + x$$ that means that $$31 − x = 17$$. This can be easier to see in a bar model.

exitQuiz.stem: These scales are not balanced. The mass of all the square objects are the same. Which statements are definitely true? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: When both sides of the balance have 4 squares they are balanced. One triangle has been added to the left and 2 squares have been added to the right.
exitQuiz.feedback: Adding 2 squares to one side and 1 triangle to the other side has not kept the scales balanced. The right hand side is now heavier so two squares are heavier than a triangle. There is no way to tell if the triangle is lighter than one square.

options.text: The triangle is lighter than 1 square.
The triangle is lighter than 2 squares.
The triangle has the same mass as 1 square.
The triangle has the same mass as 2 squares.
The triangle is heavier than 1 square.

exitQuiz.stem: The diagram shows a balanced scale on the left. When an operation is performed to the RHS, it is not balanced. What operation must be performed to the LHS to maintain equality? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: What has been added to the right hand side?
exitQuiz.feedback: 3 has been added to the right hand side. To maintain equality, 3 must be added to the left hand side too.

exitQuiz.stem: The diagram shows a balanced scale on the left. When an operation is performed to the LHS, it is not balanced. What operation must be performed to the RHS to maintain equality? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The left hand side has been divided by 2. In this example, what operation is that the same as?
exitQuiz.feedback: The LHS has been halved, so to maintain equality you can multiply the RHS by $$1\over 2$$. Alternatively, the LHS has had $$2x$$ and 1 subtracted from it, so you could subtract $$2x$$ and subtract 1 from the RHS.

lessons.title: Solution to an equation
lessons.outcome: I can appreciate that a solution is a value that makes the two sides of an equation balance.
keyLearningPoints: In an expression the variable can take any value.
In a linear equation there is a particular value that makes the equation balance.
The value is the solution to the linear equation.
When graphing a linear expression this value represents a single point.

keywords.definition: A solution to an equality with one variable is a value which, when substituted, maintains the equality between the expressions.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the value of the expression $$5x − 4$$ when $$x = 3$$?
starterQuiz.hint: Substitute 3 for the $$x$$ in the expression $$5x − 4$$
starterQuiz.feedback: Substituting gives $$5(3) − 4 = 15 − 4 = 11$$. So the expression has a value of 11 when $$x$$ is 3

starterQuiz.stem: What is the value of the expression $$5x − 4$$ when $$x = −1$$?
starterQuiz.hint: $$$5\times −1 = −5$$. Use a number line to help you with negative number calculations.
starterQuiz.feedback: Substituting gives $$5(−1) - 4$$. So, $$−5 − 4 = -9$$. The expression has a value of $$−9$$ when $$x$$ is $$−1$$

starterQuiz.stem: The table of values for the equation $$y = 7 − 2x$$ is shown. The missing number is {{ }}. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Substitute $$x = −2$$ into the expression $$7 − 2x$$
starterQuiz.feedback: Substituting gives $$7 − 2(−2)$$. So, $$7 − (−4)=11$$. So when $$x = −2 , y = 11$$

starterQuiz.stem: To find the value of the expression $$21 − 1.5a$$ when $$a = 5$$, you should {{}} the variable $$a$$ for the number 5.
starterQuiz.hint: What do we call it when we replace a variable with a specific value for the variable?
starterQuiz.feedback: Substitute means to put in place of another. In algebra, substitution is used to replace variables with values.

starterQuiz.stem: The graph shows 5 lines labelled A, B, C, D and E. Match each line to the equation for that line. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Horizontal lines can be written in the form $$y = a$$ where a is a constant and the $$y$$ intercept is $$(0, a)$$.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$y = −1$$ and $$y = 1$$ are horizontal lines. $$x = −1$$ is a vertical line, $$y = x$$ is a diagonal line with gradient 1 and $$y$$ intercept (0, 0). $$y = −x$$ has gradient $$−1$$ and $$y$$ intercept (0, 0).

starterQuiz.stem: Match  each fraction calculation to its answer.
starterQuiz.hint: Multiply 4 by the numerator and divide by the denominator.
starterQuiz.feedback: To multiply a whole number by a fraction you can multiply the whole number by the numerator and divide by the denominator. It does not matter which order you do this in.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these best describes what a solution is?
exitQuiz.hint: If you substitute the solution in for the variable, the equation will balance.
exitQuiz.feedback: A solution to an equation with one variable is a value for the variable which, when substituted, maintains the equality between the expressions.

options.text: The value of the expressions on both sides of the equals sign when the same.
The value of the expressions of both sides when the variable is zero.
The value of the variable which makes both sides of the equation equal.
The value of the variable which makes both sides equal to zero.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these equations have a solution when $$x = 4$$?
exitQuiz.hint: Substitute $$x = 4$$ into each equation and see if the left and right hand sides balance.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$2(4) + 1 = 9$$ and $$7 − 2(4) = −1$$ so the equations $$2x + 1 = 9$$ and $$7 − 2x = -1$$ both have solutions when $$x = 4$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these is a solution to the equation $$3a + 5 = 2a + 2$$?
exitQuiz.hint: Substitute each value into the equation and see if both sides of the equation balance.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$3(−3) + 5 = −4$$ and $$2(−3) + 2 = −4$$ so equation is balanced when $$a = −3$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these equations have no solution?
exitQuiz.hint: $$$3a + 1 = 3a + 4$$ will have no solutions as both expressions have the same coefficient of $$a$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$5x + 1 = 5x + 15$$ has no solutions as both expressions have the same coefficient of $$x$$. The graphs of $$y=5x + 1$$ and $$y= 5x + 15$$ are parallel. $$4(2x + 1)= 8x$$ is the same as $$8x + 4 = 8x$$ so no solutions.

exitQuiz.stem: The graph shows the lines with equations $$y = 2 − 2x$$ and $$y = 2x - 2$$. What is the solution to the equation $$2x − 2 = 2 − 2x$$? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: You are looking for a value of $$x$$ which makes both sides of the equation balance, this can be found on the graph.
exitQuiz.feedback: The lines meet at (1, 0) so both expressions have the same value when $$x=1$$

exitQuiz.stem: Use the graph to match each equation to its solution. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Find the points where the graph of the expression on the left hand side meets the value on the right hand side.
exitQuiz.feedback: The lines with equations $$y = 1 − x$$ and $$y = 2$$ meet at $$(−1, 2)$$, so the equation $$1 − x = 2$$ has a solution when $$x = −1$$

lessons.title: Many equations, one solution
lessons.outcome: I can understand that a family of linear equations can all have the same solution.
keyLearningPoints: Starting from a single value for a variable you can write equations that are equivalent.
A solution to a linear equation is a value that makes the two sides equal .
All the equivalent equations will have the same solution.

keywords.definition: A solution to an equality with one variable is a value which, when substituted, maintains the equality between the expressions.
An equation is used to show two expressions that are equal to each other.

starterQuiz.stem: This bar model represents the initial equation $$2x + 3 = 9$$. What needs to be done to the top bar to maintain equality? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: $$$2x + 3$$ has the same value as 9. The same value has to be added to both bars to maintain equality.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$2x +3$$ has been added to the bottom bar, so the same could be added to the top bar to maintain equality. $$2x + 3$$ has the same value as 9 so 9 could be added to the top bar to maintain equality. This is equivalent to doubling both bars.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these calculations show '6 plus 3 all multiplied by 2'?
starterQuiz.hint: Multiplying a whole expression by 2 is the same as multiplying each term by 2
starterQuiz.feedback: The whole of 6 + 3 needs to be multiplied by 2 so brackets are needed e.g. 2(6 + 3). Using the distributive property, this is the same as 2 × 6 + 2 × 3

starterQuiz.stem: Lucas manipulates the equation $$2x + 8 = 6$$. Which of these equations could he obtain and maintain equality?
starterQuiz.hint: Both sides of the equation need to be multiplied by the same value or both sides of the equation need to have the same value added.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$10x + 8 = 30$$ has not maintained equality as the whole expression on the left hand side has not been multiplied by 5. $$2x =6$$ has not maintained equality as 8 has been subtracted from the left but not the right.

starterQuiz.stem: Which expression could fill the blank on the right hand side of this equation to maintain equality? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The RHS has been divided by 2. This is equivalent to subtracting 3 in this example.
starterQuiz.feedback: If both sides have been divided by 2, the equation becomes $${2x + 4}\over 2 = 3$$ or $$x + 2 = 3$$. If 3 has been subtracted from both sides the equation becomes $$2x + 1 = 3$$

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these equations has a solution of $$x = 6$$?
starterQuiz.hint: Substitute $$x = 6$$ into each equation and see if the expressions on both sides balance.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$2(6) − 3 = 9$$ so $$x = 6$$ is a solution to the equation $$2x − 3 = 9$$ $$5 + 3(6) = 23$$ and $$2(6) + 11= 23$$ so the equation $$5 + 3x = 2x + 11$$ is balanced when $$x = 6$$

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these is a solution to the equation $$18 − 6x = 12 − 4x$$?
starterQuiz.hint: You need to find a value of $$x$$ which gives both expressions the same value.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$18 − 6(3) = 0$$ and $$12 − 4(3) = 0$$ so both expressions are equal when $$x = 3$$. Therefore there is a solution when $$x = 3$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these equations are equivalent to $$x = 5$$?
exitQuiz.hint: The same value must be added to both sides of the equation to form an equivalent equation. Or both sides of the equation must be multiplied by the same value.
exitQuiz.feedback: For $$x − 2 = 7$$, 2 has been subtracted from the LHS but added to the RHS, so this is not equivalent to $$x = 5$$. In $$x + 5 = 0$$, 5 has been added to the LHS but subtracted from the RHS so this is also not equivalent to $$x = 5$$

exitQuiz.stem: If $$8x + 4 = 12$$, which of these equations has maintained equality?
exitQuiz.hint: Both sides of the equation need to be divided by 4
exitQuiz.feedback: If dividing the LHS by 4, brackets must be used to show the whole expression is divided, or each term must be divided by 4. The RHS needs to be divided by 4 as well.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these equations are equivalent to  $$12x + 2 = 8x − 6$$?
exitQuiz.hint: The same value must be added to both sides or both sides must be multiplied by the same value.
exitQuiz.feedback: In $$12x = 8x − 4$$, 2 has been subtracted from the LHS but added to the RHS, so this is not equivalent to the initial equation. In $$3x + 1 = 2x + 3$$, the same operation has not been applied to both sides of the equation, so it is not equivalent.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these is a solution to the equation $$5x − 5 = 9 − 2x$$?
exitQuiz.hint: Substitute the value of $$x$$ into both sides of the equation and see if it balances.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$5(2) − 5 = 5$$ and $$9 − 2(2) = 5$$ so the equation is balanced when $$x = 2$$

exitQuiz.stem: What operation is missing from this diagram? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The operation must be applied to both sides of the equation.
exitQuiz.feedback: Both sides of the equation have been divided by 4, this is the same as multiplying by a quarter.

exitQuiz.stem: What operation is missing from this diagram? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The operation must be applied to the whole expression on both sides of the equation.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$x$$ has been added to both sides and 3 has been subtracted. This is the same as adding $$(x − 3)$$.

lessons.title: Solving simple linear equations with an additive step
lessons.outcome: I can solve a linear equation requiring a single additive step.
keyLearningPoints: An equation involving an additive step can be represented with a bar model.
Using the bar model you can write all the arrangements of the equation with an additive step.
One of the arrangements will give the solution to the equation.
This can be written algebraically to find the solution.

keywords.definition: The additive inverse of a number is a number that, when added to the original number, gives the sum of 0

starterQuiz.stem: Which equations are represented by this bar model? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: If you know an additive relationship between values, you can also write equivalent relationships. E.g. if 8 + 2 = 10 then 10 − 2 = 8

starterQuiz.stem: Which equations are represented by this bar model? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Subtraction is not commutative, make sure you use the bar model to write your subtraction calculations the correct way round.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each value with its additive inverse.
starterQuiz.hint: A value add its additive inverse equals zero.
starterQuiz.feedback: Adding a number to its additive inverse equals zero. E.g. $$0.3 + (−0.3) = 0$$ $${10\over 3} + −{10\over 3} = 0$$

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these are zero pairs?
starterQuiz.hint: Zero pairs are two numbers that sum to zero.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$2\over 5$$ is equivalent to 0.4 so $${2\over 5} + (−0.4) = 0$$ this means $$2\over 5$$ and $$(−0.4)$$ are zero pairs. $$5 + (−5) = 0$$. so 5 and (−5) are zero pairs.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the value of the expression $$2(3x + 5)$$ when $$x = −3$$ ?
starterQuiz.hint: Substitute $$x = −3$$ into the expression and evaluate according to priority of operations.
starterQuiz.feedback: Substituting gives $$2(3(−3) + 5)$$ , $$2(−9 + 5)$$, $$2 \times −4 = −8$$. When $$x = −3$$ this expression equals −8

starterQuiz.stem: The diagram shows a balanced scale on the left. When an operation is performed to the RHS, it is not balanced. What operation must be performed to the LHS to maintain equality? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The whole of the right hand expression has not been doubled.
starterQuiz.feedback: 9 has been added to the right hand side, so 9 needs to be added to the left hand side to maintain equality.

exitQuiz.stem: What is the value of the unknown in this bar model? $$x=$${{ }} [image]
exitQuiz.hint: What equations can you write from this bar model? One of them should tell you how to calculate $$x$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: The equation $$x = 13 − 3$$ can be written from the bar model. That means $$x = 10$$ .

exitQuiz.stem: Which best describes the mistake that has been made when solving the equation below? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: To isolate $$x$$ on one side of the equation you need to add the additive inverse of (−8). The same needs to be done to the RHS to maintain equality.
exitQuiz.feedback: The additive inverse of (−8) is +8 so the wrong value has been added to isolate $$x$$. $$x − 8 + (−8)$$ is equivalent to $$x − 16$$ not $$x$$.

options.text: The same operation has not been applied to both sides of the equation.
The correct additive inverse has not been added.
The (−8) has not been added to the $$x$$ term and the constant term on the LHS.

exitQuiz.stem: The solution to the equation $$x − 5 = 15$$ is when $$x$$ = {{}}
exitQuiz.hint: What is the additive inverse of (−5)? Make sure you add the same value to both sides of the equation to find the value of $$x$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these shows the correct working to solve the equation $$x + 3.8 = 2.3$$ in one additive step?
exitQuiz.hint: You need to pick the correct additive inverse to isolate $$x$$ on the LHS. To maintain equality the same value has to be added to both sides of the equation.
exitQuiz.feedback: To isolate one positive $$x$$ on the LHS, $$−3.8$$ needs to be added correctly to both sides of the equation. This gives the new equation $$x = −1.5$$

exitQuiz.stem: The solution to the equation $$x + 7.2 = 14.6$$ is when $$x$$ = {{}}
exitQuiz.hint: The additive inverse of 7.2 is −7.2

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these is the solution to the equation $$x − {2\over 3} = {5\over 6}$$ ?
exitQuiz.hint: Convert your fractions into equivalent fractions with a common denominator before calculating anything. You may need to simplify your final answer.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$x − {2\over 3} + {2\over 3} = {5\over 6} + {2\over 3}$$, $$x = {5\over 6} + {4\over 6}$$ so there is a solution when $$x = {9\over 6}= {3\over 2}$$

lessons.title: Solving simple linear equations with a multiplicative step
lessons.outcome: I can solve a linear equation requiring a single multiplicative step.
keyLearningPoints: An equation involving an multiplicative step can be represented with a bar model.
Using the bar model you can write all the arrangements of the equation with an multiplicative step.
One of the arrangements will give the solution to the equation.
This can be written algebraically to find the solution.

keywords.definition: The reciprocal is the multiplicative inverse of any non-zero number.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these equations can be written from this bar model? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: If you know an additive relationship between values, you can also write equivalent relationships. E.g. if $$8 + 2 = 10$$ then $$10 − 2 = 8$$

starterQuiz.stem: The solution to the equation $$x + 3 = 17$$ is when $$x$$ = {{}}
starterQuiz.hint: To find the value of one positive $$x$$ you need to isolate $$x$$ on the left hand side by adding the additive inverse of +3
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$x + 3 + (−3) = 17 + (−3)$$ so there is a solution when $$x = 14$$

starterQuiz.stem: The solution to the equation $$x − 8.6 = 10$$ is when $$x$$ = {{}}
starterQuiz.hint: The additive inverse of −8.6 is +8.6
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$x − 8.6 + 8.6 = 10 + 8.6$$ so there is a solution when $$x = 18.6$$

starterQuiz.stem: Any non-zero number multiplied by its reciprocal is equal to {{}}
starterQuiz.hint: $$${1\over 3}$$ and 3 are reciprocals of each other. $$5\over 2$$ and $$2\over 5$$ are reciprocals of each other.
starterQuiz.feedback: Any non zero number multiplied by its reciprocal is equal to 1

starterQuiz.stem: Match each number to its reciprocal.
starterQuiz.hint: A number multiplied by its reciprocal is 1
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$−{1\over 5}$$ and $$−5$$ are reciprocals because $$−{1\over 5} \times −5 = 1$$

starterQuiz.stem: Match each calculation to an equivalent calculation.
starterQuiz.hint: Dividing by a value is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$\div (−{2\over 7})$$ is the same as $$\times( −{7\over 2})$$ because dividing by a value is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal.

exitQuiz.stem: Using this bar model, the solution to the equation $$6x = 30$$ is when $$x= $${{}} [image]
exitQuiz.hint: What number multiplied by 6 equals 30?

exitQuiz.stem: Using this bar model, the solution to the equation $${1\over 4}x = 8$$ is when $$x=$$ {{}} [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Four lots of the top white bar will be equivalent to one $$x$$
exitQuiz.feedback: $$${1\over 4} x \times 4 \equiv x$$ $$8\times 4 = 32$$ so $$x = 32$$

exitQuiz.stem: The solution to $$3x = 396$$ is when $$x=$$ {{}}
exitQuiz.hint: Multiplying both sides by $$1\over 3$$ or dividing both sides by 3 will find the value of one positive $$x$$.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these show the correct working to isolate one positive $$x$$ for the equation $$0.5x = 3.5$$?
exitQuiz.hint: Multiplying by 2 and dividing by 0.5 are equivalent.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$0.5x \equiv {1\over 2}x$$ So one positive $$x$$ can be isolated by dividing by 0.5 or multiplying by 2

exitQuiz.stem: The solution to $$-9x = 36$$ is when $$x =$$ {{}}
exitQuiz.hint: You could find the value of $$−x$$ first, then multiply both sides by $$−1$$ to find the value of $$x$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$−9x \div 9 = 36 \div 9$$ so $$−x = 4$$ multiplying by −1 gives the equation $$x = −4$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these is the solution to $${4\over 5} x = 20$$?
exitQuiz.hint: Dividing by $$4\over 5$$ and multiplying by $$5\over 4$$ are equivalent.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$${4\over 5}x \times {5\over 4}= 20 \times {5\over 4}$$ so $$x = {100\over 4} = 25$$

lessons.title: Preparing to solve two step linear equations
lessons.outcome: I can understand that an equation needs to be in a format to be ready to be solved, through collecting like terms on each side of the equation.
keyLearningPoints: An equation with both a multiplicative and additive step can be solved using a bar model.
The solution can be formalised using algebra.
Any linear equation written in the form Ax + B = C can be solved.
Any linear equation can be written in the form Ax + B = C by collecting like terms.

keywords.definition: Like terms are terms that have the same set of variables and corresponding exponents

starterQuiz.stem: The solution to the equation $$x + 16 = 11$$ is $$x$$ = {{}}.
starterQuiz.hint: To find the value of one positive $$x$$, you need to isolate $$x$$ on the left hand side by adding the additive inverse of +16
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$x + 16 + (−16) = 11 + (−16)$$ so there is a solution when $$x = −5$$

starterQuiz.stem: The solution to $$12x =−48$$ is $$x=$$ {{}}.
starterQuiz.hint: Multiplying both sides by $$1\over 12$$ or dividing both sides by 12 will find the value of one positive $$x$$.

starterQuiz.stem: {{}} terms are terms that have the same set of variables and corresponding exponents.
starterQuiz.hint: For example, $$3x$$ and $$−5x$$ have the same variables and corresponding exponents.
starterQuiz.feedback: Like terms are terms which have the same variables and corresponding exponents. $$5x^2$$ and $$0.3x^2$$ are examples of like terms.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each term with a like term.
starterQuiz.hint: When multiplied together, variables can be written in any order. Try rewriting each term so the variables are in alphabetical order to help you spot like terms.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$2xy^2$$ and $${3y^2}x$$ are like terms as they have the same set of variables and corresponding exponents. The variables can be written either way round, but like terms are easier to spot if you write the variables alphabetically.

starterQuiz.stem: Fully simplify $$5x − 9x + 3x − x$$
starterQuiz.hint: These are all like terms so they can be added and written as a single term. $$-x$$ is equivalent to $$−1x$$
starterQuiz.feedback: As they are all like terms, you can simplify by adding the coefficients $$(5 − 9 + 3 − 1)x\equiv −2x$$

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these is equivalent to $$−4(2x − 5)$$?
starterQuiz.hint: To expand a bracket, each term inside the bracket needs to be multiplied by the term outside the bracket.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$−4(2x − 5)$$ is the same as $$−4\times 2x + (−4)\times (−5)$$. This can be written more simply as $$−8x + 20$$.

exitQuiz.stem: Which equations are represented by this bar model? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The top bar represents 3 lots of the expression $$2x + 6$$
exitQuiz.feedback: This can be written as $$3(2x + 6) = 58$$ or rearranged to group like terms giving $$6x + 18 = 58$$.

exitQuiz.stem: Which equations are represented by this bar model? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: There are 2 lots of the expression $$2x + 3$$ and 3 lots of $$x + 2$$
exitQuiz.feedback: There are two lots of $$2x + 3$$ and 3 lots of $$x + 2$$, so this could be written as $$2(2x + 3) + 3(x + 2) = 39$$ or $$7x + 12 = 39$$

exitQuiz.stem: For this bar model, there is a solution to the equation $$5x + 15 = 55$$ when $$x =$$ {{}}. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: What operation will remove the 15 bar from the top? The same must be done to the bottom bar to keep them equal length.
exitQuiz.feedback: Adding (−15) to both bars gives the equation $$5x = 40$$. Splitting the bar in 5 gives the equation $$x = 8$$.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these are equivalent to the equation $$7(x − 1) − 3(x − 1) = 50$$ ?
exitQuiz.hint: As both brackets are the same, you can write this as a multiple of a single bracket.
exitQuiz.feedback: Unitising the bracket and adding the multipliers gives $$4(x − 1) = 50$$. This can be expanded to give $$4x − 4 = 50$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these is equivalent to the equation $$5(2x+1) − 3(3x − 2) = 50$$ ?
exitQuiz.hint: The brackets do not contain the same expression, so you cannot write this as a multiple of a single bracket without expanding. Remember when expanding, a negative value multiplied by a negative value gives a positive value.
exitQuiz.feedback: Expanding the brackets gives $$10x + 5 − 9x + 6 = 50$$. Then collecting like terms gives $$x + 11 = 50$$

exitQuiz.stem: This shape is made out of a rectangle and two rhombuses (one on each end of the rectangle). Which of these is the correct expression for the perimeter of the shape? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: There are 2 lengths of $$3x − 5$$ and 6 lengths of $$x + 5$$
exitQuiz.feedback: The perimeter can be written as $$2(3x − 5) + 6(x + 5)$$. Expanding the brackets gives $$6x − 10 + 6x + 30$$. Then collecting like terms to give $$12x + 20$$

lessons.title: Solving two step linear equations
lessons.outcome: I can see that when an additive step and a multiplicative step are required to solve an equation, the order of operations will not affect the solution.
keyLearningPoints: When an equation is in the form Ax + B = C you can solve by first subtracting B from both sides.
When an equation is in the form Ax + B = C you can solve by first dividing both sides by A.
These two options give the same solution.
In any particular situation one way may be more efficient than the other and it useful to think carefully about this.

keywords.definition: An equation is used to show two expressions that are equal to each other.

starterQuiz.stem: An equation is used to show two expressions that are {{}} to each other.
starterQuiz.hint: Equations have equality.
starterQuiz.feedback: Both sides of an equation are equal, so an equation is used to show two expressions that are equal to each other.

starterQuiz.stem: Work out the value of $$13+7+(−7)$$
starterQuiz.hint: What effect does adding a negative have?
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$13+7+(−7)=13$$ The $$+7$$ and the $$−7$$ become a 'zero pair' and cancel each other out.

starterQuiz.stem: Work out the value of $${20 \over 4}$$
starterQuiz.hint: $$$20$$ 'over' $$4$$ means what mathematical operator?
starterQuiz.feedback: $$${20 \over 4}=5$$. This has the same effect as $$20 \div 4$$

starterQuiz.stem: Solve the equation $$x + 9 = 21$$
starterQuiz.hint: Undo the operation $$+9$$ by doing the additive inverse.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$x+9=21$$ becomes $$x+9+(−9)=21+(−9)$$ which gives you the solution $$x=12$$

starterQuiz.stem: Solve the equation $$5x = 15$$
starterQuiz.hint: Undo the operation $$\times 5$$ by doing the multiplicative inverse.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$5x=15$$ becomes $${{5x}\over5}={15\over5}$$ giving you the solution $$x=3$$

starterQuiz.stem: Solve the equation $$7x = 3$$
starterQuiz.hint: Undo the operation $$\times 7$$ by doing the multiplicative inverse.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$7x=3$$ becomes $${{7x}\over7}={3\over7}$$ giving you the solution $$x={3\over7}$$

options.text: It can't be solved because $$7$$ is not divisible by $$3$$

exitQuiz.stem: The solution to an equation is the value which, when substituted, maintains the {{}} between the two expressions.
exitQuiz.hint: An equation is used to show two expressions that are equal to each other. Any manipulations need to be done accurately so both sides remain equal.
exitQuiz.feedback: The solution to an equation is the value which, when substituted, maintains the equality between the two expressions.

exitQuiz.stem: Which is the most useful additive first step to apply to both sides when solving $$7y − 3=18$$?
exitQuiz.hint: One way to solve is to 'undo' the $$−3$$ operation first.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$7y−3+(3)=18+(3)$$ becomes $$7y=21$$ which isolates the variable term. From there you can solve the equation.

exitQuiz.hint: 'Undo' both the $$+7$$ and $$\times 3$$ operations to solve.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$3y+7+(-7)=19+(-7)$$ becomes $$3y=12$$. Divide both sides by $$3$$ to find the solution $$y=4$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which is the most useful multiplicative first step to apply to both sides when solving $$6y−12=18$$?
exitQuiz.hint: What is the HCF of $$6y$$, $$12$$ and $$18$$?
exitQuiz.feedback: $$${{6y−12}\over 6}={18\over 6}$$ becomes $$y−2=3$$ which is simple to solve.

exitQuiz.stem: Match each equation to its solution.
exitQuiz.hint: Take an additive step first, then a multiplicative step.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$2x+3+(−3)=4+(−3)$$ becomes $$2x=1$$ which has a fractional solution of $$$$x={1\over2}$$. Many equations have non-integer solutions.

exitQuiz.stem: $$$x=$${{}} is the solution to the equation $${x\over8}+{1\over4}={1\over2}$$
exitQuiz.hint: A multiplicative step of $$\times 8$$ applied to all terms will simplify this equation.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$8({x\over8}+{1\over4})=8({1\over2})$$ becomes $$x+2=4$$ which has the solution $$x=2$$

lessons.title: Rearranging to solve linear equations
lessons.outcome: I can recognise that equations with unknowns on both sides of the equation can be manipulated so that the unknowns are on one side and then solve this equation.
keyLearningPoints: Any linear equation written in the form Ax + B = C can be solved.
Like terms can be collected onto one side of an equation in order to write it in the form Ax + B = C.
An equation that had unknowns on both sides can then be solved.

keywords.definition: An equation is used to show two expressions that are equal to each other.

starterQuiz.stem: In order to maintain {{}} in an equation, any manipulation must be applied to both sides of the equation.
starterQuiz.hint: An equation is used to show two expressions that are equal to each other. Through all manipulations you must be careful to make sure that both sides remain equal.
starterQuiz.feedback: In order to maintain equality in an equation any manipulation must happen to both sides.

starterQuiz.stem: What must be added to both sides of the equation to turn $$x=7$$ into $$x+3=10$$?
starterQuiz.hint: Look at the LHS. What additive step turns $$x$$ into $$x+3$$?
starterQuiz.feedback: Adding $$3$$ to both sides turns $$x=7$$ into $$x+(3)=7+(3)$$ which is $$x+3=10$$

starterQuiz.stem: What must be added to both sides of the equation to turn $$x+3=10$$ into $$5x+3=4x+10$$?
starterQuiz.hint: Look at the LHS. What additive step turns $$x+3$$ into $$5x+3$$?
starterQuiz.feedback: Adding $$4x$$ to both sides turns $$x+3=10$$ into $$x+3+(4x)=10+(4x)$$ which is $$5x+3=4x+10$$

starterQuiz.stem: $$$(−4)$$ is added to both sides of the equation $$9x+4=6$$. What is the resulting equation?
starterQuiz.hint: In algebra only 'like terms' can be simplified.

starterQuiz.stem: $$$y=$${{}} is the solution to the equation $$29=6y−7$$
starterQuiz.hint: An additive first step of $$+7$$ will simplify this equation.
An additive first step of $$+4$$ will simplify this equation.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$2y−4+(4)=−8+(4)$$ becomes $$2y=−4$$ so the solution is $$y=−2$$

exitQuiz.stem: An equation is used to show two {{}} that are equal to each other.
exitQuiz.hint: $$$7x + 3 = 10$$ is an equation. What should you call each side of the equation?
exitQuiz.feedback: In an equation the expression on the LHS and the expression on the RHS have to be equal. An equation is used to show two expressions that are equal to each other.

exitQuiz.stem: What equation is represented by this balance model? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Balance models represent equations because the LHS and the RHS are equal.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$3x+1$$ on the LHS and $$2x+3$$ on the RHS. Both expressions being equal, giving you the equation $$3x+1=2x+3$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which additive step will manipulate the equation $$7x−3=2x+18$$ so that it has unknowns on only one side?
exitQuiz.hint: Which manipulation leaves only an integer value in either the LHS or RHS expression?

exitQuiz.stem: Add $$3x$$ to both sides of the equation $$x+2=7−3x$$
exitQuiz.hint: First write $$x+2+(3x)=7−3x+(3x)$$ then simplify.

exitQuiz.stem: $$$x=$${{}} is the solution to the equation $$5x+21=9x+5$$
exitQuiz.hint: Start with the additive step $$+(−5x)$$ on both sides.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$5x+21+(−5x)=9x+5+(−5x)$$ becomes $$21=4x+5$$. If $$4x=16$$ then $$x=4$$ is the solution.

exitQuiz.hint: Start with the additive step $$+(3x)$$ on both sides.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$6x−1+(3x)=7−3x+(3x)$$ becomes $$9x−1=7$$. From there $$9x−1+(1)=7+(1)$$ becomes $$9x=8$$ to which the solution is $$x={8\over{9}}$$

lessons.title: Solving complex linear equations
lessons.outcome: I can solve complex linear equations, including those involving reciprocals.
keyLearningPoints: Any linear equation written in the form Ax + B = C can be solved.
Equations involving division by a constant can be manipulated to reach the form Ax + B = C.
Equations involving division by a variable can be manipulated to reach the form Ax + B = C.

keywords.definition: An equation is used to show two expressions that are equal to each other.

starterQuiz.hint: What is the multiplicative inverse called?
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$1\over7$$ is the reciprocal of $$7$$

starterQuiz.hint: Manipulate the equation to isolate the unknown term.
starterQuiz.feedback: Subtract 9 from both sides so $$6x+9=27$$ becomes $$6x=18$$. Therefore $$x=3$$

starterQuiz.stem: Solve $${x\over3}=15$$
starterQuiz.hint: $$$x\over3$$ means $$x\div3$$. What is the inverse operation of $$\div3$$?
starterQuiz.feedback: Multiply both sides by $$3$$ to 'undo' the $$\div3$$ therefore $$x=45$$

starterQuiz.stem: Calculate $${2\over3}\times{4\over5}$$
starterQuiz.hint: To multiply fractions, you multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$${{2\over3}\times{4\over5}}={{2\times4}\over{3\times5}}={8\over15}$$

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these expressions are equivalent to $${{x+1}\over3}\times{2\over3}$$ ?
starterQuiz.hint: To multiply fractions you multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators. Multiplying algebraic fractions is no different.

starterQuiz.stem: Expand and simplify $$8({{x}\over8})$$
starterQuiz.hint: Re-writing this as $${8\over1}\times{x\over8}$$ makes it look more like a regular multiplication of two fractions.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$8({{x}\over8})=x$$. Whilst $$8({{x}\over8})={{8x}\over8}$$ is true, $${{8x}\over8}$$ can be simplified to $${{x}\over1}$$ which is just $$x$$

exitQuiz.stem: $$${{56}\over{y}}=7$$ is an example of a {{}} equation.
exitQuiz.hint: A rational equation is an equation that contains fractions with unknowns in the numerator, denominator, or both.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$${{56}\over{y}}=7$$ is an example of a rational equation with an unknown in the denominator.

exitQuiz.stem: The solution to $${{6x−2}\over{4}}=7$$ is $$x=$${{}}
exitQuiz.hint: What is the inverse operation of $$\div 4$$ ?
exitQuiz.feedback: Multiply both sides by $$4$$ to get $$6x−2=28$$. From there $$6x=30$$, therefore $$x=5$$

exitQuiz.hint: Start by adding $$(−1)$$ to both sides.
exitQuiz.feedback: Add $$(-1)$$ to both sides to simplify the equation to $${{2x}\over{3}}=10$$. Multiply both sides by $$3$$ to get to $$2x=30$$ therefore $$x=15$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which is the most efficient first step when solving the equation $${{x+7}\over{9}}={{x-1}\over{3}}$$ ?
exitQuiz.hint: For an equation in this form, multipling both sides by the LCM of the denominators is the most efficient first step.
exitQuiz.feedback: Multiplying both sides by $$9$$ leaves you with $$x+7=3(x−1)$$ which is far easier to solve.

exitQuiz.stem: Solve $${{x+7}\over{9}}={{x−1}\over{3}}$$. The solution is $$x=$${{}}
exitQuiz.hint: Multiplying both sides by the LCM of the denominators is an efficient first step.
exitQuiz.feedback: Multiply both sides by $$9$$ gives $$x+7=3(x−1)$$ which becomes $$x+7=3x−3$$. Therefore $$2x=10$$ and $$x=5$$

exitQuiz.hint: Multiply both sides by $$3x$$ to make the equation easier to solve.
exitQuiz.feedback: Multiply both sides by $$3x$$ to get $$3x({{32}\over{3x}})=3x(8)$$ which simplifies to $$32=24x$$. Therefore $$x={32\over24}={4\over3}$$

lessons.title: Brackets in equations
lessons.outcome: I can appreciate the significance of the bracket in an equation.
keyLearningPoints: Multiplying both sides of an equation by the same term can be shown using brackets.
An expression involving brackets can be expanded.
Equations involving brackets can be expressed in words.
Equations involving brackets can be represented using bar models.

keywords.definition: An equation is used to show two expressions that are equal to each other.

starterQuiz.stem: Turning the expression $$5(y-2)$$ into $$5y-10$$ is known as {{}} the brackets.
starterQuiz.hint: When an expression is in the form $$2(a+b)$$, you can remove the brackets to write it in a different form if you need to.
starterQuiz.feedback: Turning $$5(y-2)$$ into $$5y-10$$ is known as multiplying out, or expanding, the brackets.

starterQuiz.stem: $$$2(x+4)$$ and $$2x+4$$ are the equivalent expressions. True or false?
starterQuiz.hint: $$$2(x+4)$$ means $$2\times(x+4)$$. This is "Two lots of $$(x+4)$$". What is $$(x+4)+(x+4)$$?

options.text: True. There is a $$2$$, an $$x$$, and a $$+4$$. That means they are the same.
False. $$2$$ lots of $$(x+4)$$ is $$(x+4)+(x+4)$$ which is $$2x+8$$ not $$2x+4$$
You cannot know until you know the value of $$x$$.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these are expressions for the perimeter of this square? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: In a square, all edges have the same length.
starterQuiz.feedback: Four equal lengths of $$5y+3$$ could be written as $$4\times(5y+3)$$ which is more simply written as $$4(5y+3)$$. $$(5y+3)+(5y+3)+(5y+3)+(5y+3)=20y+12$$

starterQuiz.stem: What equation does this bar model represent? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: In this bar model the length of the top row is the same, or equal to, the length of the bottom row. Your equation should represent the fact they are equal.
starterQuiz.feedback: The top row of $$4y+12$$ is equal in length to $$20$$ creating the equation $$4y+12=20$$

starterQuiz.stem: Expand $$7(y+8)$$.
starterQuiz.hint: You need $$7$$ lots of $$(y+8)$$. If you wrote $$(y+8)$$ out $$7$$ times how many $$y$$ would you have and how many $$8$$s would you have?
Both terms inside the bracket need to be multiplied by $$-7$$

exitQuiz.stem: If you multiply both sides of an equation by $$2$$, you will maintain {{}}.
exitQuiz.hint: An equation is used to show two expressions that are equal to each other. When manipulating you must take care to preserve that equality.
exitQuiz.feedback: If you multiply both sides of an equation by $$2$$, you have performed the same operation on both sides, so you have maintained equality.

exitQuiz.stem: True or false? Multiplying by $$5$$ and then adding $$10$$ is the same as adding $$10$$ then multiplying by $$5$$.
exitQuiz.hint: You could test this by substituting a value into both functions.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$x \times 5 + 10=5x+10$$ whereas $$(x+10) \times 5=5(x+10)=5x+50$$, hence they are not the same thing. Order matters.

options.text: True. Both have $$\times 5$$ and $$+10$$ so they are the same function.

exitQuiz.stem: What equation does this bar model represent? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Write an expression for the top row, an expression for the bottom row, and use an equation to show that they are equal.
exitQuiz.feedback: In the top row you have $$3$$ lots of $$x$$ and a $$5$$ which can be expressed as $$3\times x + 5$$, or more simply as $$3x+5$$. Hence $$3x + 5 = 17$$

exitQuiz.stem: What does this bar model represent? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Write an expression for the top row, an expression for the bottom row, and use an equation to show that they are equal.
exitQuiz.feedback: In the top row you have $$3$$ lots of $$(x+5)$$ which can be expressed as $$(x + 5) \times 3$$ or more simply as $$3(x+5)$$. Hence $$3(x + 5) = 17$$. In expanded form that is $$3x+15=17$$

exitQuiz.stem: Multiply both sides of this equation $${1\over3}x-5 = 2x+7$$ by $$3$$.
exitQuiz.hint: Ensure every term on both sides is multiplied by $$3$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: To show the step $$\times3$$, you can write $$3({1\over3}x-5) = 3(2x+7)$$. Expand the brackets and you get $$x-15=6x+21$$.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the below is the most efficient first step to solve the equation $${3\over{x}}= 10$$ ?
exitQuiz.hint: What is the inverse operation of $$\div x$$ ?
exitQuiz.feedback: Multiplying both sides by $$x$$ gives $$x({3\over{x}})= x(10)$$ which simplifies to $$3=10x$$. This is now in a far easier form to solve.

lessons.title: Solving linear equations where brackets are used
lessons.outcome: I can recognise that there is more than one way to remove a bracket when solving an equation.
keyLearningPoints: It is possible to divide by the coefficient of the bracket first when solving an equation.
When there are common factors this may be the most efficient method.
When the coefficient is a fraction it may be helpful to rewrite the equation.
It is possible to expand the bracket before solving an equation.
You will need to be able to make decisions about the most efficient method to a solution.

keywords.definition: An equation is used to show two expressions that are equal to each other.

starterQuiz.stem: $$$3\over2$$ is the {{}} of $$2\over3$$.
starterQuiz.hint: $$$2\over3$$ is the multiplicative inverse of $$3\over2$$ because $$\frac{2}{3}\times\frac{3}{2}=1$$
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$3\over2$$ is the reciprocal of $$2\over3$$

starterQuiz.hint: $$$7(2x-3)$$ means $$7\times(2x-3)$$. Be sure to multiply both terms inside the bracket by $$7$$.
Multiply both terms inside the bracket by $$1\over5$$

starterQuiz.stem: The solution to $$8y+20=4$$ is $$y=$${{}}.
starterQuiz.hint: Subtract 20 from both sides to isolate the unknown term on one side.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$8y+20=4$$ becomes $$8y=-16$$ therefore $$y=-2$$

starterQuiz.hint: Rearrange so that the unknowns are on one side. Then you will have a two-step equation to solve.
starterQuiz.feedback: Remove $$2x$$ from both sides of $$7x-3=2x+12$$ to leave $$5x-3=12.$$ From there $$5x=15$$, therefore $$x=3$$.

starterQuiz.hint: Rearrange so that the unknowns are on one side. Then you will have a two-step equation to solve.
starterQuiz.feedback: Remove $$2x$$ from both sides of $$7x-3=2x+11$$ to leave $$5x-3=11.$$ From there $$5x=14$$, therefore $$x={14\over5}$$

exitQuiz.stem: $$$8(x+5)=5(2x-4)$$ is an example of {{}}.
exitQuiz.hint: What is used to show two expressions that are equal to each other?
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$8(x+5)=5(2x-4)$$ is an example of equation; two expressions that are equal to each other.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these show a correct method and solution for the equation $$9(y-3)=45$$?
exitQuiz.hint: One option is to divide both sides by 9 to remove the bracket. Another method is to expand those brackets then solve.
exitQuiz.feedback: Dividing both sides by $$9$$ leaves the equation $$y-3=5$$ therefore $$y=8$$. Alternatively, expand the brackets to get $$9y-27=45$$ therefore $$9y=72$$ and $$y=8$$.

exitQuiz.stem: The solution to $$8(x+5)=5(2x-4)$$ is $$x=$${{}}.
exitQuiz.hint: Expand both sets of brackets, be careful to multiply both terms inside the brackets. Then, manipulate the equation to isolate the unknown terms on one side.
exitQuiz.feedback: Expanding the brackets gives the equation $$8x+40=10x-20$$. Add $$(-8x)$$ and $$(+20)$$ to both sides to leave $$2x=60$$, therefore $$x=30$$.

exitQuiz.hint: Expand both sets of brackets, be careful to multiply both terms inside the brackets. Then, manipulate the equation to isolate the unknown terms on one side.
exitQuiz.feedback: Expanding the brackets gives the equation $$7x+35=10x-20$$. Add $$(-7x)$$ and $$(+20)$$ to both sides to leave $$3x=55$$, therefore $$55\over3$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which is the most efficient start to solving the equation $${5\over4}(3x+1)=20$$?
exitQuiz.hint: Multiplying by the reciprocal of $${5\over4}$$ is the most efficient first step in this case.
exitQuiz.feedback: Multiply both sides by $$4\over5$$ to get the equation $${4\over5}\times{5\over4}(3x+1)={4\over5}\times20$$ which simplifies to $$3x+1=16$$. This is a simpler form of the equation to solve.

exitQuiz.stem: The solution to the equation $${5\over4}(3x+1)=20$$ is $$x=$${{}}.
exitQuiz.hint: Multiply both sides by the reciprocal of $${5\over4}$$ to put the equation in a more simple form.
exitQuiz.feedback: Multiply both sides by $$4\over5$$ to get the equation $${4\over5}\times{5\over4}(3x+1)={4\over5}\times20$$. This simplifies to $$3x+1=16$$, therefore $$x=5$$

lessons.title: Solving complex linear equations involving brackets
lessons.outcome: I can solve equations involving brackets where simplification is necessary first.
keyLearningPoints: Brackets where an expression is multiplied by a term can be expanded.
Like terms can then be collected so the equation is in a form that can be solved.
Multiple identical expressions can be collected together to simplify an equation.

keywords.definition: An equation is used to show two expressions that are equal to each other.

starterQuiz.stem: The command word to turn $$-2(5-3y)$$ into $$6y-10$$ is {{}}.
starterQuiz.hint: What word is used to tell you to multiplying out the brackets?
starterQuiz.feedback: The command word to turn $$-2(5-3y)$$ into $$6y-10$$ is 'expand'.

starterQuiz.stem: The command words to turn $$5(x+7)-3(x+2)$$ into $$2x+29$$ are  {{}}.
starterQuiz.hint: The brackets have been multiplied out and then like terms have been gathered together. What is this process called?
starterQuiz.feedback: The command words to turn $$5(x+7)-3(x+2)$$ into $$2x+29$$ are 'expand and simplify'. The brackets in $$5(x+7)-3(x+2)$$ expand to $$5x+35-3x-6$$ which simplifies to $$2x+29$$.

starterQuiz.stem: Simplify $$4x+9+x-11$$
starterQuiz.hint: Commute $$4x+9+x-11$$ to the order $$4x+x+9-11$$ to make simplifying easier.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$4x+9+x-11$$ commutes to $$4x+x+9-11$$ which simplifies to $$5x-2$$

starterQuiz.stem: Expand and simplify $$8(x-3)+3(5x+7)$$.
starterQuiz.hint: Expand $$8(x-3)$$ then expand $$3(5x+7)$$. Now gather the like terms together.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these expressions can be simplified before the brackets are expanded?
starterQuiz.hint: If the expressions inside the brackets are identical you can simplify before expanding.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$3(x-7)+2(x-7)$$ simplifies to $$5(x-7)$$ because the expressions inside the bracket were identical. $$3(2x+5)+2(2x+5)$$ simplifies to $$5(2x+5)$$ and $$3(5-x)+2(5-x)$$ simplifies to $$5(5-x)$$

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the below are expressions for the perimeter of this rectangle? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: An expression for the perimeter of the rectangle must express the sum of all four lengths.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$2(7x+3)+2(4x+1)$$ and $$2(7x + 3 + 4x+1)$$ express the perimeter of the rectangle.

exitQuiz.stem: You can expand brackets in the expression $$2(y+9)+2(3y-7)$$ to get the expression $$2y+18+6y-14$$. You now have like terms that can be {{}}.
exitQuiz.hint: Expressions containing like terms can be gathered together. What is this process called?
exitQuiz.feedback: In the expression $$2y+18+6y-14$$, you have like terms so the expression can be simplified by gathering the like terms.

exitQuiz.stem: The perimeter of this rectangle is $$154$$ units. Which equation can be used to find $$x$$? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The expression on the LHS needs to be the perimeter which is the sum of all four lengths.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$2(4x+15) + 2(5x-1)=154$$ shows two lots of both lengths being equal to the perimeter of $$154$$

exitQuiz.stem: The perimeter of this rectangle is $$154$$ units. The value of $$x$$ is {{}}. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Form an expression for the perimeter, then make that equal to $$154$$ to form an equation which you can solve.
exitQuiz.feedback: You could form the equation $$2(4x+15) + 2(5x-1)=154$$ then expand to get $$8x+30+10x-2=154$$. Therefore, $$18x+28=154$$, so $$x=7$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these are accurate first steps when solving $$4(3x-1)-2(x+2)=72$$ ?
exitQuiz.hint: There are many ways to solve this equation. Expanding the brackets first is one option. Dividing through by a common factor is another.
exitQuiz.feedback: Expanding $$4(3x-1)-2(x+2)$$ gives you $$12x-4-2x-4$$ on the LHS. Alternatively, divide both sides by the common factor of $$2$$ to leave $$2(3x-1)-(x+2)=36$$ which is now simpler to solve.

exitQuiz.hint: There are many ways to solve this equation. Expanding the brackets first is one option. Dividing through by a common factor is another.
exitQuiz.feedback: Divide both sides by $$2$$ to get $$2(3x-1)-(x+2)=36$$ which simplifies to $$6x-2-x-2=36$$. Therefore, $$5x=40$$ and $$x=8$$.

exitQuiz.hint: When the expressions inside the brackets are identical you can simplify before solving the equation.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$8(3x-6)-5(3x-6)=9$$ simplifies to $$3(3x-6)=9$$ which simplifies to $$3x-6=3$$. Therefore, $$x=3$$.

lessons.title: Solving linear equations graphically using technology
lessons.outcome: I can explore how to solve linear equations graphically via dynamic software.
keyLearningPoints: A linear expression expressed on a graph represents a straight line.
This line can be used to find one variable when given the other.
A horizontal or vertical line represents a particular value of a variable.
Where this meets the linear graph the solution of a linear equation.

keywords.definition: An equation is used to show two expressions that are equal to each other.
The solution to an equality is the value which, when substituted, maintains the equality between expressions.

starterQuiz.stem: $$$x=5$$ is the {{}} to the equation $$7x-3=32$$
starterQuiz.hint: 5 is the value of $$x$$ which, when substituted into $$7x-3=32$$, maintains the equality between the expressions.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$x=5$$ is the solution to the equation $$7x-3=32$$. It is the value of $$x$$ which, when substituted, maintains the equality between the expressions.

starterQuiz.stem: Which is the solution to the equation $$16-3x=7$$?
starterQuiz.hint: A solution, when substituted, maintains equality between the expressions in an equation.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$x=3$$ is the solution to $$16-3x=7$$. $$16-3(3)=16-9=7$$ which gives the expressions equality.

starterQuiz.stem: The relationship $$y=2x+6$$ when plotted produces a {{}} graph.
starterQuiz.hint: $$$y=2x+6$$ is a linear relationship.
starterQuiz.feedback: The relationship $$y=2x+6$$ when plotted makes a straight line which is called linear graph.

starterQuiz.stem: Andeep plots the graph of the equation $$y=3x-10$$. What is the $$y$$ coordinate when the $$x$$ coordinate is $$-5$$?
starterQuiz.hint: Substitute $$x=-5$$ into the expression $$3x-10$$ to get $$3(-5)-10$$ then evaluate.

starterQuiz.stem: Find the coordinates of the point where the lines $$y=5-x$$ and $$y=2x-1$$ intersect. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The intersection is where the two lines meet each other.
starterQuiz.feedback: The lines $$y=5-x$$ and $$y=2x-1$$ intersect at coordinate $$(2, 3)$$.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the $$x$$ coordinate of this point? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Read down from the coordinate to the $$x$$ axis. What is that number and how many ways can it be communicated?
starterQuiz.feedback: The $$x$$ coordinate of this point is $${2.5}={2\frac{1}{2}}={5\over2}$$

exitQuiz.stem: This graphical representation shows that $$x=2$$ is the {{}} to the equation $$3x-2=4$$ [image]
exitQuiz.hint: A solution is the value which, when substituted, maintains the equality between the expressions.
exitQuiz.feedback: This graphical representation shows you that $$x=2$$ is the solution to the equation $$3x-2=4$$.

exitQuiz.stem: Use this graphical representation to solve the equation $$7-3x=-5$$ [image]
exitQuiz.hint: A solution is the value which, when substituted, maintains the equality between the expressions.
exitQuiz.feedback: The $$x$$ coordinate of the intersection of the two lines, $$x=4$$, is the solution to the equation $$7-3x=-5$$

exitQuiz.stem: Use this graphical representation to solve the equation $$3x+1={1\over2}x-4$$ [image]
exitQuiz.hint: A solution is the value which, when substituted, maintains the equality between the expressions.
exitQuiz.feedback: The $$x$$ coordinate of the intersection of the two lines, $$x=-2$$, is the solution to the equation $$3x+1={1\over2}x-4$$

exitQuiz.stem: This graph shows that $$x=-2$$ is the solution to the equation $$5x+13=1-x$$ and that $$3$$ is the value of the {{}} when they are equal. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: When you substitute a solution into an equation you have equality between the expressions.
exitQuiz.feedback: The coordinates of the intersection $$(-2,3)$$ tell you that $$x=-2$$ is the solution to the equation and that $$3$$ is the value of the expressions when they are equal.

exitQuiz.hint: To graphically solve an equation you need the coordinate of the intersection. The lines must intersect.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$y=2.7x+1$$ and $$y=2.7x-5.4$$ are parallel lines, they do not intersect. Therefore there is no solution to this equation.

exitQuiz.stem: Use the graphical representation to solve the equation $$3x+4=x-4$$ [image]
exitQuiz.hint: You need the $$x$$ coordinate of the intersection of the two lines $$y=3x+4$$ and $$y=x-4$$
exitQuiz.feedback: The lines $$y=3x+4$$ and $$y=x-4$$ intersect at $$(-4,-8)$$ so the solution is $$x=-4$$

lessons.title: Problem solving with linear equations
lessons.outcome: I can use my knowledge of solving linear equations to solve problems.
keyLearningPoints: Problems in context can be expressed algebraically as equations.
These equations can be solved.
The solution can be interpreted in context.
Real life problems can be solved using linear equations.

keywords.definition: An equation is used to show two expressions that are equal to each other.
The solution to an equality is the value which, when substituted, maintains the equality between the expressions.

starterQuiz.stem: $$$4(7x-13)$$ is an {{}} for the perimeter of this square. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Algebra is a versatile tool. It allows you to express the perimeter or area of a shape, even if you don't know it's exact dimensions.
starterQuiz.feedback: To find the perimeter of a square you can multiply the length of one side by 4. So, $$4(7x-13)$$ is an expression for the perimeter of this square.

starterQuiz.stem: Evaluate $$2(3x-4)+2(5x+9)$$ when $$x=6$$. The value of the expression is {{}}.
starterQuiz.hint: Start by substituting $$x=6$$ into the terms $$3x$$ and $$5x$$. Replace those variable terms with numbers first.

starterQuiz.stem: Expand and simplify $$2(6x-4)+2(x-7)$$.
starterQuiz.hint: Expand each bracket separately and be sure to multiply every term inside the bracket.

starterQuiz.stem: The solution to the equation $$4(7x-3)=128$$ is $$x=$${{}}.
starterQuiz.hint: Start by either expanding the bracket on the LHS, or by dividing both sides of the equation by $$4$$.
starterQuiz.feedback: One method: $$4(7x-3)=128$$ becomes $$7x-3=32$$ therefore $$7x=35$$ so $$x=5$$

starterQuiz.hint: Manipulating the equation to isolate the unknown terms on one side.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$4x+7=8x-9$$ could be manipulated to $$7=4x-9$$ which becomes $$16=4x$$. Therefore, $$x=4$$

starterQuiz.stem: Laura thinks of a number. She multiplies it by 8 and subtracts 12. Her answer is 60. Laura's number is {{}}.
starterQuiz.hint: Work backwards to 'undo' the operations.
starterQuiz.feedback: Undoing the operations: $$60+(12)=72$$ and $${72\div8}=9$$ therefore $$9$$ is the number.

exitQuiz.stem: The perimeter of this square is $$80$$ units. You can find the value of $$x$$ using the {{}} $$4(7x-8)=80$$. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: An equation is used to show two expressions that are equal to each other.
exitQuiz.feedback: You can use the equation $$4(7x-8)=80$$ to find $$x$$.

exitQuiz.stem: The perimeter of this square is $$80$$ units. What is the value of $$x$$? $$x=$${{}}. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Form the equation $$4(7x-8)=80$$ then solve.
exitQuiz.feedback: Divide both sides of $$4(7x-8)=80$$ by 4 to give $$7x-8=20$$. Now add 8 to both sides: $$7x=28$$, therefore $$x=4$$

exitQuiz.stem: Find the perimeter of this square. $$P=$${{}}. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Squares have equal lengths so start with the equation $$2x+5=4x$$
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$2x+5=4x$$ therefore $$5=2x$$ and $$x=2.5$$. One side is therefore $$4(2.5)=10$$ giving a perimeter of $$40$$ units.

exitQuiz.stem: An electrician has a call-out fee of £120 and then charges an hourly rate for their work. For a six hour job they charge £480. Calculate their hourly rate.
exitQuiz.hint: Forming the equation $$120+6x=480$$ will help find the unknown hourly rate.
exitQuiz.feedback: Form the equation $$120+6x=480$$. From there $$6x=360$$, therefore $$x=60$$. The hourly rate is £60.

exitQuiz.stem: Sofia thinks of a number. She multiplies it by 6 and then subtracts 24. Sofia multiplies her original number by 4 and adds 6. She gets the same answer both times. Sofia's number is {{}}.
exitQuiz.hint: This problem can be represented by the equation $$6x-24=4x+6$$. Solve to find this unknown number.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$6x-24=4x+6$$ becomes $$2x-24=6$$. So $$2x=30$$, therefore the number is $$15$$

exitQuiz.stem: Three children share 65 sweets. Lucas takes 5 more sweets than Jacob does. Izzy takes four times as many sweets as Jacob does. Jacob takes {{}} sweets.
exitQuiz.hint: Jacob has $$x$$ sweets which means Lucas has $$(x+5)$$ sweets and Izzy has $$4x$$ sweets. Use these expressions to form an equation.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$(x)+(x+5)+(4x)=65$$ simplifies to $$6x+5=65$$ therefore $$x=10$$. Jacob has $$10$$ sweets.

units.title: Understanding multiplicative relationships: percentages and proportionality
units.description: In this unit pupils explore multiplicative relationships with percentages, direct and inverse proportion.

lessons.title: Checking understanding of percentages
lessons.outcome: I can manipulate percentages of an amount without a representation.
keyLearningPoints: Percent relates to the number of parts per hundred.
Percentages can be written as a fraction out of 100.
The equivalence of fractions, decimals and percentages can be used to solve problems.
Percentages of amounts can be calculated by using known fractions.

keywords.definition: Two fractions are equivalent if they have the same value.

starterQuiz.stem: Two fractions are __________ if they have the same value.
starterQuiz.hint: What is another word meaning the "same"?
starterQuiz.feedback: Two fractions are equivalent if they have the same value - this means they are equal.

starterQuiz.hint: To find 10%, divide what you know is 100% by 10.
To find 10%, divide what you know is 100% by 10.
To find 10%, divide what you know is 100% by 10. Then once you have 10%, divide by 2.
starterQuiz.feedback: 5% is half of 10%. 400 ÷ 10 = 40, so 10% is 40. Halving this gives 5%, so 5% is 20.

starterQuiz.hint: To find 10%, divide what you know is 100% by 10. Then once you have 10%, divide by 2.
starterQuiz.feedback: 5% is half of 10%. 940 ÷ 10 = 94, so 10% is 94. Halving this gives 5%, so 5% is 47.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each percentage calculation to its answer.
starterQuiz.hint: To find 10%, divide what you know is 100% by 10. Then once you have 10%, divide by 2 to find 5%. 15% = 10% + 5%.
starterQuiz.feedback: Finding 10% by dividing by 10, then halving this to give 5% is a good basis to find any multiple of 10% or 5%. For example, 10% of 60 is 60 ÷ 10 = 6, 5% of 60 is 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 15% of 60 is 6 + 3 = 9 since 15% = 10% + 5%.

exitQuiz.stem: Percent comes from the Latin phrase “per centum” meaning “by the __________ .”
exitQuiz.hint: You make the denominator of the fraction this amount when trying to find a percentage.
exitQuiz.feedback: Percent comes from the Latin phrase “per centum” meaning "by the hundred." "Cent" often means 100, for example a century is 100 years.

exitQuiz.stem: The percentage of this grid that is shaded is {{ }}%. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Each square represents 1%. How many squares are shaded?
exitQuiz.feedback: There are 32 squares shaded from the hundred grid. This means 32% is shaded.

exitQuiz.stem: What fraction of this grid is shaded? Select your answer in its simplified form. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Ensure you write the numerator as  the number that are shaded over the total number of squares.  Do not forget to simplify.
exitQuiz.feedback: There are $$ {{32} \over {100}}$$ shaded. Simplifying gives $$ {{32} \over {100}}= {{8\times4} \over {25\times4}}={{8} \over {25}}\times{{4} \over {4}}={{8} \over {25}} $$

exitQuiz.stem: Match each percentage question with the calculation needed to work it out.
exitQuiz.hint: You can work out the answer to each question and the calculations and match from there.
exitQuiz.feedback: Working out the answer is one method, but understanding what the calculation is working out is important. When you divide, what percentage are you finding out? E.g. When you divide the amount by 10, this is 10%; when you divide by 2, this is 50%.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the following are valid calculations to work out 55% of 400?
exitQuiz.hint: Understanding what the calculation is working out is important. When you divide, what percentage are you finding out? E.g. When you divide the amount by 10, this is 10%; when you divide by 2, this is 50%; when you divide by 20, this is 5%.
Have a strategy in mind. 35% can be achieved in so many different ways e.g. 10% + 10% + 10% + 5% = 35%, 50% − 10% − 5% and so on.

lessons.title: Securing understanding of percentages
lessons.outcome: I can manipulate percentages of an amount with a representation.
keyLearningPoints: Percentages of amounts can be found by combining known percentages
Percentages of amounts can be represented and found using a bar model
Percentages of amounts can be represented and found using double number lines
Percentages of amounts can be represented and found using ratio tables

keywords.definition: Variables are in proportion if they have a constant multiplicative relationship.
Two fractions are equivalent if they have the same value.

starterQuiz.stem: Proportionality means two variables have a constant __________ relationship so the variables are in proportion to each other.
starterQuiz.hint: Bar models, double number lines and ratio tables all display this constant relationship between numbers.
starterQuiz.feedback: Proportionality means two variables have a constant multiplicative relationship. For example, if you walk 5 km every hour then the distance you walk is in proportion to the time you spend walking. If you walk twice as long, you will go twice as far.

starterQuiz.hint: Have a strategy in mind.  40% can be achieved in so many different ways e.g find 10% by dividing by 10 and then find 40% by multiplying by 4.
To work out 1%, you divide the amount which is 100% by 100

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the following are correct strategies to find 75% of 200?
starterQuiz.hint: You can work out the answer to each of the calculations and sums and match from there.
starterQuiz.feedback: Working out the answer is one method, but understanding what the calculation is working out is important. When dividing, what percentage are you finding out? Multiplying by $$\frac{1}{4}$$ is the same as finding 25%.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each percentage question to its answer.
starterQuiz.hint: Once you work out 10% of an amount and 5% of an amount, you can easily work out any multiple of 5% or 10%.

starterQuiz.stem: Starting with the calculation with the largest answer, put these percentage calculations in descending order.
starterQuiz.hint: Once you work out 10% of an amount and 5% of an amount, you can easily work out any multiple of 5% or 10%.

exitQuiz.stem: __________  means two variables have a constant multiplicative relationship.
exitQuiz.hint: Bar models, double number lines and ratio tables all display this constant relationship between numbers.
exitQuiz.feedback: Proportionality means two variables have a constant multiplicative relationship. For example, if you walk 5 km every hour then the distance you walk is in proportion to the time you spend walking. If you walk twice the time, you will go twice as far.

exitQuiz.stem: Match each representation of proportion to its advantages.
exitQuiz.hint: Which description matches the process of drawing a bar model, double number line or ratio table.
exitQuiz.feedback: Bar models are good visual representation and bars can be split in any way needed. Double number lines are good visual representation with scaled lines. Ratio table are concise without visual representation and quick to construct.

match.left: Good visual representation. Bars can be split in any way needed.
Good visual representation with scaled lines.
Concise without visual representation and quick to construct.

exitQuiz.stem: What percentage of 800 is represented by the calculation: 800 ÷ 2 − 8?
exitQuiz.hint: Dividing by 2 is the same as finding 50%
exitQuiz.feedback: Dividing 800 by 2 is the same as finding 50%.  1% of 800 is 8 so subtracting 8 is the same as subtracting 1%. 50% − 1% = 49%, so 49% has been found.

exitQuiz.stem: What percentage of 650 is represented by the calculation: 650 − 6.5?
exitQuiz.hint: What percentage of 650 does 650 represent? What percentage of 650 does 6.5 represent? Find the difference between these percentages.
exitQuiz.feedback: 650 represents 100% and 6.5 represents 1%. Subtracting give 99% of 650.

exitQuiz.stem: Use the double number line to work out 45% of 700. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Using the double number line, there are different strategies to find 35% of 700. You can subtract 15% from 50%.
exitQuiz.feedback: An example strategy is 50% is 350, 10% is 70 and 5% is 35.  So 45% = 50% − 5% = 350 − 35 = 315.

exitQuiz.stem: Using the ratio table or another representation, work out 98% of 860. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: There are lots of different ways to work out 98%. Which way is the most efficient using subtraction?

lessons.title: Multiplicative relationships presented graphically
lessons.outcome: I can use a graph to represent a multiplicative relationship and connect to other known representations.
keyLearningPoints: A multiplicative relationship given algebraically can be represented on a graph.
From the graph you it is possible to find one value given another.
From a graph it is possible to describe the multiplicative relationship.

keywords.definition: Proportionality means when variables are in proportion if they have a constant multiplicative relationship.
A ratio shows the relative sizes of two or more values and allows you to compare a part with another part in a whole.
Two fractions are equivalent if they have the same value

starterQuiz.stem: $$$\frac{3}{4}$$ and $$\frac{9}{12}$$ are examples of {{ }} fractions as they have the same value.
starterQuiz.hint: The two fractions are equal to each other.
starterQuiz.feedback: Two fractions are equivalent if they have the same value. You can simplify $$\frac{9}{12}$$ to give $$\frac{3}{4}$$.

starterQuiz.stem: Select all the fractions that are equivalent to the fraction of this grid that is shaded. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Two fractions are equivalent if they have the same value. The correct equivalent fractions will all simplify to the same fraction.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$\frac{19}{20}$$ of the grid is shaded. $$\frac{2\times19}{2\times20}=\frac{38}{40}$$, $$\frac{4\times19}{4\times20}=\frac{76}{80}$$ and $$\frac{5\times19}{5\times20}=\frac{95}{100}$$

starterQuiz.stem: Select the fractions that are equivalent to $$\frac{7}{20}$$.
starterQuiz.hint: Two fractions are equivalent if they have the same value. The correct equivalent fractions will all simplify to the same fraction.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$\frac{2\times7}{2\times20}=\frac{14}{40}$$ and $$\frac{5\times7}{5\times20}=\frac{35}{100}$$ are all equivalent to $$\frac{7}{20}$$

starterQuiz.stem: Match each percentage calculation to its answer.
starterQuiz.hint: Find 10% by dividing by 10 and then halve this to give 5%. You can use 5% and 10% to find any multiple of 5% or 10%.
Find 10% by dividing by 10 and then halve this to give 5%. You can use 5% and 10% to find any multiple of 5% or 10%.
Working out 1% allows you to subtract it from 100% to give 99%.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the following are equivalent to 20%?
exitQuiz.hint: Fractions, decimals and percentages all show proportion. Converting between them is important. Converting a percentage to a decimal and then fraction maybe easier here.

exitQuiz.stem: Use the ratio table to help you work out 31% of 860. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Have a strategy to work out 31%. You could use 3 × 10% then add 1%.

exitQuiz.stem: Use the double number line to work out 55% of 700. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Have a strategy to work out 55%. You could use 50% + 5%.

exitQuiz.stem: The amount that represents 100% on this graph is {{ }}. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Find 100% on the axis and read across.
exitQuiz.feedback: Read across (vertical axis) from 100% to the line, and then read straight down to the amount (horizontal axis). So, 200 is 100%.
