exitQuiz.stem: The graph shows the grades achieved by pupils in a maths test. Aisha earned 61 marks in the test. What grade did Aisha achieve? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Find approximately 61 mark on the axis and read up and across.
exitQuiz.feedback: Read up from 61 marks on the horizontal axis to the line and then read across to the percentage 100%. So 61 marks is in the same region as a grade A.

exitQuiz.stem: Match each mark or percentage with the correct information from the graph. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Ensure to read from the correct axis, the horizontal axis is the marks attained and the vertical axis is the percentage.
exitQuiz.feedback: Reading from the graph gives these approximate regions Grade D: 20% to 39%, 13 to 26 marks. Grade C: 40% to 59%, 27 to 39 marks. Grade B: 60% to 79%, 40 to  52 marks. Grade A: 80+% or 53+ marks

lessons.title: Scaling diagrams for multiplicative relationships
lessons.outcome: I can use a scaling diagram to represent a multiplicative relationship and connect to other known representations.
keyLearningPoints: A double number line can be used to represent a multiplicative relations.
Double number lines and graphs of multiplicative relationships can be compared.
A ratio table can be used to represent multiplicative relationships.
The representations can be compared to see what is the same and what is different.

keywords.definition: If two things are proportional then the ratio of part to whole is maintained and the multiplicative relationship between parts is also maintained.

starterQuiz.stem: Proportion is a part to whole comparison. If two things are proportional then the ratio of part to whole is maintained and the ___________ relationship between parts is also maintained.
starterQuiz.hint: Bar models, double number lines and ratio tables all display this constant relationship between numbers.
starterQuiz.feedback: Proportionality means two variables have a constant multiplicative relationship. For example, if you walk 5 km every hour then the distance you walk is in proportion to the time you spend walking. If you walk twice the time, you will go twice as far.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these diagram types give a good representation of a proportional relationship?
starterQuiz.hint: Proportion can be represented in lots of different ways. What can you draw to show a proportional relationship?
starterQuiz.feedback: Bar models, double number lines, ratio tables and graphs are just a few excellent visual ways to show a proportional relationship. A calculator is an instrument you use to calculate answers.

starterQuiz.hint: Working out 10% and then 5% can help you find any multiple of 10% or 5%.
starterQuiz.feedback: One method to work out 85% is to use 85% = 100% − 10% − 5%.  10% of 40 is 4 and 5% of 40 is 2. 40 − 4 − 2 = 34

starterQuiz.stem: Match each percentage of a number with its answer.
starterQuiz.hint: Working out 10% and then 5% can help you find any multiple of 10% or 5%.

starterQuiz.stem: Using this ratio table, work out 99% of 860. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Work out 1% then use the fact that  100% − 1% = 99%

starterQuiz.stem: Match the start of each statement to its correct conclusion.
starterQuiz.hint: Anything referencing scales and axis is referring to double number lines and graphs.
starterQuiz.feedback: Understanding the different representations is important as they help you to decide which approach to use to tackle a question. The context of question may mean one type of representation is more helpful than another.

match.left: good visual representations but must be scaled.
match.right: A double number line and graph are

match.left: concise and neat way to show proportion.
good visual representation, but it takes time to draw the bars.

match.right: A double number line and graph must

match.left: have a constant multiplier between columns or rows.

exitQuiz.stem: A scaling diagram allows you to see ___________ as a scaling as it shows how one number maps to another.
exitQuiz.hint: When you are scaling number, which operation are we using?
exitQuiz.feedback: A scaling diagram allows you to see multiplication as a scaling as it shows how one number maps to another. You can use scaling diagrams to help you solve problems involving multiplicative reasoning.

exitQuiz.stem: Using the scaling diagram, match each percentage to the corresponding amount. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Can you see the multiplier? I.e. what do you multiply each percentage by to give the amount?
exitQuiz.feedback: The scaling diagram shows the multiplier to change the percentage into the amount is ×2. So, you can multiply each percentage by 2 to find the corresponding amount.

exitQuiz.stem: Using the scaling diagram, match each percentage to the corresponding amount. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Can you see the multiplier? I.e. what do you multiply the percentage by to give the amount?
exitQuiz.feedback: The scaling diagram shows the multiplier to change the percentage into the amount is ×1.5. So, you can multiply each percentage by 1.5 to find the corresponding amount.

exitQuiz.stem: Using the scaling diagram, match each percentage to the corresponding amount. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Can you see the multiplier? I.e. what do you multiply the percentage by to give the amount?
exitQuiz.feedback: The scaling diagram shows the multiplier to change the percentage into the amount is ×0.8. So, you can multiply each percentage by 0.8 to find the corresponding amount.

exitQuiz.stem: Using the scaling diagram to find the multiplier, match each amount or percentage with the corresponding value. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Start by finding the multiplier. I.e. what do you multiply the percentage by to give the amount?
exitQuiz.feedback: The scaling diagram shows the multiplier to change the percentage into the amount is ×0.8. So, you can divide each amount by 0.8 to find the corresponding percentage. This is the same as multiplying by 1.25.

exitQuiz.stem: Use the scaling diagram to work out 60%. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Using the scaling diagram, you may have spotted the multiplier to change the percentage into the amount is ×3.2. Use this to find the exact amounts or percentages.

lessons.title: Expressing one number as a percentage of another
lessons.outcome: I can describe one number as a percentage of another.
keyLearningPoints: Percentages can be written as a fraction out of 100
One number can be written as a fraction of another.
Using equivalent fractions this can be written as a fraction out of 100
One number can be written as a percentage of another.
Decimals can also be used to write one number as a percentage of another.

keywords.definition: Two fractions are equivalent if they have the same value.

starterQuiz.stem: Two fractions are ____________ if they have the same value.
starterQuiz.hint: Another word for the same. For example, $$\frac{3}{4}$$ is the same value as $$\frac{6}{8}$$, but you use a mathematical word to describe them being the same.
starterQuiz.feedback: Two fractions are equivalent if they have the same value. This means both fractions will simplify to give the same fraction.

starterQuiz.stem: What is 20% as a simplified fraction?
starterQuiz.hint: A percentage means per hundred. You can rewrite the percentage  20% as a fraction out of 100 and simplify.

starterQuiz.stem: What is 30% as a simplified fraction?
starterQuiz.hint: A percentage means per hundred. You can rewrite the percentage  30% as a fraction out of 100 and simplify.

starterQuiz.stem: What is 42% as a simplified fraction?
starterQuiz.hint: A percentage means per hundred. You can rewrite the percentage  42% as a fraction out of 100 and simplify.

starterQuiz.stem: Using short division or otherwise, work out the decimal answer to 25 ÷ 4.
starterQuiz.hint: Set up the division by putting the divisor of 4 outside of the division set up. Ask yourself, how many times does 4 go into 2? What is the remainder? How many times does 4 go into 25? What is the remainder? Do not forget those trailing zeros.
starterQuiz.feedback: When using short division, the 4 divided into 25 six times , with a remainder of 1. With the trailing zero, the next division is 10 by 4, giving 2 and a remainder of 2. The final division is 20 by 4 which is 5. Thus resulting in 6.25.

starterQuiz.stem: Using short division or otherwise, work out the decimal answer to 1 ÷ 6.
starterQuiz.hint: Set up the division by putting the divisor of 6 outside of the division set up. Ask yourself, how many times does 6 go into 1?  Do not forget those trailing zeros.
starterQuiz.feedback: When using short division, the 6 does not divide into 1, so it has a remainder of 6. With the trailing zero, the next division is 10 by 6, giving 1 and a remainder of 4. The next division is 40 by 6, giving 6 with a remainder of 4. This repeats.

exitQuiz.stem: $$$\frac{7}{20}$$ as a percentage is {{ }}%.
exitQuiz.hint: A percentage means per hundred. You need to use your knowledge of equivalent fractions to make the denominator of the fraction 100.

exitQuiz.stem: Which decimal is equivalent to 1%?
exitQuiz.hint: Percent comes from the Latin phrase “per centum” meaning “by the hundred.” If 1% is one square from a hundred and the whole hundred represents 1, what is each 1 square worth?
exitQuiz.feedback: 1% is 1 hundredth which is 0.01

exitQuiz.stem: $$$\frac{6}{25}$$ as a percentage is {{}}%.
exitQuiz.hint: A percentage means per hundred. You need to use your knowledge on equivalent fractions to make the denominator of the fraction 100.

exitQuiz.stem: Match each percentage to its decimal equivalent.
exitQuiz.hint: Percent comes from the Latin phrase “per centum” meaning “by the hundred.” If 1% is one square from a hundred and the whole hundred represents 1 then each 1% = 0.01
exitQuiz.feedback: You can divide each percentage by 100 to give the decimal equivalent.

exitQuiz.stem: $$$\frac{3}{8}$$ as a decimal is {{ }}.
exitQuiz.hint: Set up the division by putting the divisor of 8 outside of the division set up. Ask yourself, how many times does 8 go into 3?  Do not forget those trailing zeros.
exitQuiz.feedback: When using short division, the 8 did not divide wholly into 3, so a remainder of 3. With the trailing zeros, the next division is 30 by 8, giving 3 and a remainder of 6. The next is 60 by 8 giving 7 remainder of 4 and finally 40 by 8 giving 5.

exitQuiz.stem: Using short division or otherwise, write $$\frac{7}{9}$$ as a percentage.
exitQuiz.hint: Set up the division by putting the divisor of 9 outside of the division set up. Ask yourself, how many times does 9 go into 7?  Do not forget those trailing zeros.
exitQuiz.feedback: When using short division, the 9 did not divide wholly into 7, so a remainder of 7.  With the trailing zeros, the next division is 70 by 9, giving 7 and a remainder of 7. The next is 70 by 9 giving 7 remainder of 7. This repeats.

keywords.definition: The associative law states that a repeated application of the operation produces the same result regardless of how pairs of values are grouped. We can group using brackets.

starterQuiz.stem: __________, __________, __________ and __________ all represent proportion and you can interchange between them; this means there are lots of different ways to work out a percentage of an amount.
starterQuiz.hint: They can all represent the same number or proportion but are written in different ways.
starterQuiz.feedback: Fractions, decimals, percentages and ratio all represent proportion and we can interchange between them; this means there are lots of different ways to work out a percentage of an amount.

options.text: Fractions, proper fractions, improper fractions and mixed numbers
Positive numbers, negative numbers, squares and cubes

starterQuiz.stem: 1% is equivalent to the decimal {{ }}.
starterQuiz.hint: Percent comes from the Latin phrase “per centum” meaning “by the hundred.” If 1% is one square from a hundred and the whole hundred represents 1, what is each 1 square worth?
starterQuiz.feedback: 1% is the same as one hundredth which is 0.01

starterQuiz.stem: $$$\frac{3}{50}$$ as a percentage is {{ }}%.
starterQuiz.hint: A percentage means per hundred. You need to use your knowledge of equivalent fractions to make the denominator of the fraction 100.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each percentage to its decimal equivalent.
starterQuiz.hint: Percent comes from the Latin phrase “per centum” meaning “by the hundred.” If 1% is one square from a hundred and the whole hundred represents 1, then each 1% = 0.01
starterQuiz.feedback: You can divide each percentage by 100 to give the decimal equivalent.

starterQuiz.stem: What percentage of 98 is represented by this calculation: 98 − 9.8?
starterQuiz.hint: What percentage of 98 does 98 represent? What percentage of 98 does 9.8 represent?
starterQuiz.feedback: 98 represents 100% and 9.8 represents 10%, subtracting gives 90% of 98.

starterQuiz.hint: Understanding what the calculation is working out is important. When dividing, what percentage are you finding out? E.g. when dividing by 10 finds 10%. When you divide by 100, you are finding 1%.
starterQuiz.feedback: Dividing 400 by 2 gives 50% = 200. Dividing 400 by 100 gives 1% = 4, therefore 51% = 200 + 4  = 204

exitQuiz.stem: What percentage is equivalent to the decimal 0.01?
exitQuiz.hint: Percent comes from the Latin phrase “per centum” meaning “by the hundred.” If 1% is one square from a hundred and the whole hundred represents 1, what is each small square worth?
exitQuiz.feedback: 0.01 is one hundredth which is 1%.

exitQuiz.hint: Work out 50% and work out 1%. What do you do with these quantities to work out 49%?
Using decimal multipliers, the calculation is 0.22  × 650
exitQuiz.feedback: Using any method you prefer to work this out. For example, 0.22 × 650 = 143

exitQuiz.stem: Match each percentage question with the correct calculation.
exitQuiz.hint: Remember  0.01 = 1% and "of" means multiply.
exitQuiz.feedback: There are lots of different ways to phrase the same question. It is important to know the fractional, percentage and decimal equivalents.

exitQuiz.hint: Using decimal multipliers, the calculation is 0.27 × 830
exitQuiz.feedback: Using any method you prefer to work this out: 0.27 × 830 = 224.1

exitQuiz.stem: The UK government distributed approximately £720 billion to the a number of sectors. How much money does "Transport" receive? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Transport receives 4% of £720 billion.
exitQuiz.feedback: The decimal calculation is 0.04 × 720 = 28.8

starterQuiz.stem: Match each percentage statement to its value.
starterQuiz.hint: To work out 10%, divide by 10. From here you can find any multiple of 10%.
starterQuiz.feedback: 10% of 300 is 30 and 10% of 240 is 24. You can then find any multiple of these percentages.

starterQuiz.hint: There are a few methods to choose from. For example, 0.22 × 84 or work out 20% and 2% and sum.
There are a few methods to choose from. For example, 0.31 × 750 or work out 30% and 1% and sum.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the following calculations is equivalent to 12% of 300?
starterQuiz.hint: Remember the word “of” means multiply. What is 12% as a decimal equivalent?
starterQuiz.feedback: 30 + 6 is 10% + 2% and 0.12 × 300 has the “of” replaced with the × and 12% written as a decimal.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each calculation with the correct percentage statement.
starterQuiz.hint: Remember 0.01 = 1% and "of" means multiply.
starterQuiz.feedback: There are lots of different ways to phrase the same question. You can change a decimal to a percentage by multiplying by 100. Remember that "of" means multiply.

starterQuiz.hint: There are a few methods to choose from. For example,  0.19 × 84 or work out 20% and 1% and subtract.

exitQuiz.stem: Increase 400 by 20%.
exitQuiz.hint: There are a few methods to choose from: 1.2 × 400 or work out 20% and 100% and sum.

exitQuiz.stem: Increase 70 by 30%.
exitQuiz.hint: There are a few methods to choose from: 1.3 × 70 or work out 30% and 100% and sum.

exitQuiz.stem: Match each percentage increase question with an equivalent question.
exitQuiz.hint: Add the percentage you are increasing by to 100%. This is the equivalent percentage of the amount.
exitQuiz.feedback: Increasing by 20% is the same as finding 100% + 20% = 120%.

exitQuiz.stem: Match each statement with the correct multiplier.
exitQuiz.hint: Add the percentage you are increasing by to 100%. This is the equivalent percentage of the amount.  How can you change this to a decimal?
exitQuiz.feedback: Increasing by 8% is the same as finding 100% + 8% = 108%. 108% as a decimal is 1.08, so the multiplier is ×1.08

exitQuiz.hint: The most efficient method is to use decimal multipliers. 1.39 × 600
exitQuiz.feedback: Using an area model or column method to work out 1.39 × 600 = 834

exitQuiz.stem: Increase 800 by 11% and then by 10%.
exitQuiz.hint: The most efficient method is to use decimal multipliers. An 11% increase is the same as finding 111% which means multiplying by 1.11
exitQuiz.feedback: Using an area model or column method to work out 1.11 × 1.1 × 800 = 976.8

keywords.definition: If two things are proportional then the ratio of part to whole is maintained and the multiplicative relationship between parts is also maintained.

starterQuiz.hint: There are a few methods to choose from: 0.4 × 120 or work out 10% and multiply by 4.
starterQuiz.feedback: One method is 0.4 × 120 = 48. Another method is 10% of 120 = 12, so 40% = 4 × 12 = 48.

starterQuiz.hint: There are a few methods to choose from: 0.2 × 520 or work out 20% and 2% and sum.
There are a few methods to choose from: 0.31 × 440 or work out 30% and 1% and sum.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the following calculations is equivalent to 49% of 200?
starterQuiz.hint: Remember the word “of” means multiply and you need to write 49% as a decimal equivalent.
starterQuiz.feedback: 100 − 2 is 50% − 1%. 49% as a decimal is 0.49 and “of”  can be replaced “×”, so 0.49 × 200 is another equivalent calculation.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each calculation with the equivalent percentage statement.
starterQuiz.hint: Remember 0.01 = 1% and "of" means multiply.
starterQuiz.feedback: There are lots of different ways to phrase the same question. It is important to know the fractional, percentage and decimal equivalents. You can convert from a percentage to a decimal by dividing by 100 and “of”  can be replaced “×”.

starterQuiz.hint: There are a few methods to choose from: 0.19 × 840 or work out 20% and 1% and subtract.

exitQuiz.stem: Decrease 40 by 20%.
exitQuiz.hint: There are a few methods to choose from: 0.8 × 40 or work out 20% and 100% and subtract.
exitQuiz.feedback: 100% − 20% = 80%, so decreasing by 20% is the same as finding 80%.  0.8 × 40 = 32 or 10% = 4, 20% = 8 so a decrease of 20% is 40 − 8 = 32.

exitQuiz.stem: Decrease 700 by 30%.
exitQuiz.hint: There are a few methods to choose from: 0.7 × 700 or work out 30% and 100% and subtract.
exitQuiz.feedback: 100% − 30% = 70%, so decreasing by 30% is the same as finding 70%. 0.7 × 700 = 490 or 10% = 70, 30% = 210 so a decrease of 30% is 700 − 210 = 490

exitQuiz.stem: Match each question to an equivalent question.
exitQuiz.hint: Subtract the percentage you are decreasing from 100%. This is the equivalent percentage of the amount.
exitQuiz.feedback: When increasing (or decreasing) an amount by a percentage, it is important to know the equivalent question can be phrased in different ways. 100% − 12% = 88%, so decreasing by 12% is the same as finding 88%.

exitQuiz.stem: Match each statement with the correct multiplier.
exitQuiz.hint: Subtract the percentage you are decreasing from 100%. Then convert this percentage into a decimal.
exitQuiz.feedback: 100% − 22% = 78%, so decreasing by 22% is the same as finding 78%. Finding 78% of an amount is the same as multiplying by 0.78

exitQuiz.stem: Decrease 600 by 39%.
exitQuiz.hint: The most efficient method is to use decimal multipliers. What is 100% − 39%?
exitQuiz.feedback: 100% − 39% = 61%, so the multiplier is 0.61. Using an area model or the column method to work out the 0.61 × 600 = 366

exitQuiz.stem: Match each calculation to its answer.
exitQuiz.hint: Knowing the decimal multipliers will help you work out the answer.

keywords.definition: The reciprocal is the multiplicative inverse of any non-zero number.  Any non-zero number multiplied by its reciprocal is equal to 1.

starterQuiz.stem: A multiplier is the decimal equivalent of a __________.
starterQuiz.hint: ×0.62 is an example of a multiplier.
starterQuiz.feedback: A multiplier is the decimal equivalent of a percentage. To find 62%, you use the multiplier 0.62.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each question to the correct multiplier.
starterQuiz.hint: The multiplier is the decimal equivalent of the percentage you are finding.
starterQuiz.feedback: 100% + 2% = 102%, multiplier of 1.02.  100% − 2% = 98%, multiplier of 0.98.  100% + 20% = 120%, multiplier of 1.2.  100% − 20% = 80%, multiplier of 0.8.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the following is the correct calculation for calculating 360 increased by 5%?
starterQuiz.hint: Increase 100% by 5% and convert this into a multiplier.
starterQuiz.feedback: 1.05 × 360 is a 5% increase, 0.5 × 360 is a 50% decrease, 0.95 × 360 is a 5% decrease, 1.5 × 360 is a 50% increase.

starterQuiz.stem: 240 increased by 2% is {{ }}.
starterQuiz.hint: Increase 100% by 2% and convert this into a multiplier.
starterQuiz.feedback: 100% + 2% = 102%. This means the multiplier is ×1.02. So, 240 × 1.02 = 244.8

starterQuiz.stem: 240 decreased by 20% is {{ }}.
starterQuiz.hint: Decrease 100% by 20% and convert this into a multiplier.
starterQuiz.feedback: 100% − 20% = 80%. This means the multiplier is ×0.8. So, 240 × 0.8 = 192

starterQuiz.stem: A box of washing powder contains 20% extra free.  The box usually contains 6.5 kg.  The special offer box contains {{ }}kg.
starterQuiz.hint: This is an increase of 20%.
starterQuiz.feedback: 100% + 20% = 120%. This means the multiplier is ×1.2. So, 6.5 × 1.2 = 7.8 kg

exitQuiz.stem: ‘Of’ can be exchanged for which operation in maths?
exitQuiz.feedback: 'Of' can be exchanged for multiplication in maths. So, 50% of 24 = 0.5 × 24 = 12

exitQuiz.stem: A number is increased by 20%.  One part is 20%. What is the total number of parts representing the new number?
exitQuiz.hint: To find 20% you would split the bar model into how many parts?  How many parts will there be in TOTAL?
exitQuiz.feedback: 100% ÷ 5 = 20%. So the original number is 5 parts and increasing by 20% means an extra 1 part, giving 6 parts in total.

exitQuiz.stem: The cost of a TV increases by 15%.  The new price is £460.  What was the cost of the TV before the price increase?  Without calculating the answer, decide whose answers cannot possibly be correct?
exitQuiz.hint: Decide if the price before would have been bigger or smaller.
exitQuiz.feedback: If the price has increased, the original price must have been lower than £460, so Laura and Sam are definitely wrong.

exitQuiz.stem: Alex thinks of a number and increases it by 5%.  His new number is 252.  What was Alex's original number?
exitQuiz.hint: Divide by the multiplier for an increase of 5%.
exitQuiz.feedback: An increase of 5% is 100% + 5% = 105% which is a multiplier of 1.05. To 'undo' the multiplier, you need to divide. 252 ÷ 1.05 = 240

exitQuiz.stem: The cost of a TV increases by 15%.  The new price is £460.  The cost of the TV before the price increase was £{{ }}.
exitQuiz.hint: Divide by the multiplier for an increase of 15%.
exitQuiz.feedback: An increase of 15% is 100% + 15% = 115% which is a multiplier of 1.15. To 'undo' the multiplier, you need to divide. £460 ÷ 1.15 = £400

exitQuiz.stem: This year the cost of a concert ticket is £94.50.  This is an increase of 26% on last year.  The cost of the ticket last year was £{{ }}.
exitQuiz.hint: Divide by the multiplier for an increase of 26%.
exitQuiz.feedback: An increase of 26% is 100% + 26% = 126% which is a multiplier of 1.26. To 'undo' the multiplier, you need to divide.  £94.50 ÷ 1.26 = £75

keywords.definition: The reciprocal is the multiplicative inverse of any non-zero number. Any non-zero number multiplied by its reciprocal is equal to 1.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the following is the correct calculation for finding 20% of 300?
starterQuiz.hint: Rewrite 20% as a multiplier.
starterQuiz.feedback: The decimal equivalent of 20% is 0.2, so 0.2 is the multiplier. The correct calculation is 300 × 0.2

starterQuiz.stem: A number is increased by 25%.  1 part is equal to 25%. What will be the total number of parts representing the new number?
starterQuiz.hint: To find 25%, you would split the bar model into how many parts?  How many parts will there be in TOTAL?
starterQuiz.feedback: 100% ÷ 4 = 25% so the original is 4 parts. Increasing by 25% means an extra 1 part, giving 5 parts in total.

starterQuiz.stem: The cost of a TV increases by 20%.  The new price is £420.  What was the cost of the TV before the price increase?  Without calculating the answer, decide whose answers cannot possibly be correct?
starterQuiz.hint: Decide if the price before would have been bigger or smaller.
starterQuiz.feedback: If the price has increased, the original price must have been lower than £420 so Andeep and Izzy are definitely wrong.

starterQuiz.stem: Jun thinks of a number and increases it by 20%.  Jun's new number is 720.  What was his original number?
starterQuiz.hint: Divide by the multiplier for an increase of 20%.
starterQuiz.feedback: An increase of 20% is the same as 100% + 20% = 120% which is a multiplier of 1.2. So, 720 ÷ 1.2 = 600

starterQuiz.stem: The cost of a TV increases by 20%.  The new price is £420. The cost of the TV before the price increase is £{{ }}.
starterQuiz.hint: Divide by the multiplier for an increase of 20%.
starterQuiz.feedback: An increase of 20%, 100% + 20% = 120% which is a multiplier of 1.2. £420 ÷ 1.2 = £350

starterQuiz.stem: The cost of a concert ticket is £80.  This is an increase of 25% on last year.  The cost of the ticket last year was £{{}}.
starterQuiz.hint: Divide by the multiplier for an increase of 25%.
starterQuiz.feedback: An increase of 25% is 100% + 25% = 125% which is a multiplier of 1.25. £80 ÷ 1.25 = £64

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the following words indicate an increase?
exitQuiz.hint: Which would give a higher value than the original value?
exitQuiz.feedback: Interest and profit both indicate an increase.  Interest is money paid on bank and savings accounts and profit is when you sell something for more money than you paid for it.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the following is the correct calculation for finding 3% of 300?
exitQuiz.hint: Rewrite 3% as a multiplier.
exitQuiz.feedback: The decimal equivalent of 3% is 0.03, so 0.03 is the multiplier. The correct calculation is  300 × 0.03.

exitQuiz.stem: Match each percentage question to the correct multiplier.
exitQuiz.hint: Start with 100% and increase or decrease by the percentage and convert this to a multiplier.
exitQuiz.feedback: 100% + 2% = 102% which is 1.02 as a multiplier.  100% + 30% = 130% which is 1.3 as a multiplier.  100% − 20% = 80% which is 0.8 as a multiplier.  100% − 3% = 97% which is 0.97 as a multiplier.

exitQuiz.stem: A t-shirt costs £12 in a sale offering a 25% discount.  The cost of the t-shirt before the discount was £{{ }}.
exitQuiz.hint: Divide by the multiplier for an decrease of 25%.
exitQuiz.feedback: An decrease of 25%, 100% − 25% = 75% which is a multiplier of 0.75. So, £12 ÷ 0.75 = £16

exitQuiz.stem: The value of a motorbike depreciates by 14% each year.  It is now worth £5590.  Last year the motorbike was worth £{{ }}.
exitQuiz.hint: Divide by the multiplier for an decrease of 14%.
exitQuiz.feedback: An decrease of 14%, 100% − 14% = 86% which is a multiplier of 0.86. So last year the motorbike was worth £5590 ÷ 0.86 = £6500

exitQuiz.stem: Mr. Oak sells a vase is sold for £102.  This gives him a profit of 20%.  Mr. Oak originally purchased the vase for £{{ }}.
exitQuiz.hint: Divide by the multiplier for an increase of 20%.
exitQuiz.feedback: An increase of 20%, 100% + 20% = 120% which is a multiplier of 1.2. So, the vase originally cost £102 ÷ 1.2 = £85.

lessons.title: Finding the percentage change

keywords.definition: Variables are in proportion if they have a constant multiplicative relationship.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the following words indicate an decrease?
starterQuiz.hint: Which would give a lower value than the original value?
starterQuiz.feedback: Discount, loss and depreciate all indicate an decrease.  A discount is money saved on an item, profit is when you sell something for less money than you paid for it and depreciate is a term used when an item loses its value.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the following is the correct calculation for finding 5% of 300?
starterQuiz.hint: Rewrite 5% as a multiplier.
starterQuiz.feedback: The decimal equivalent of 5% is 0.05, so 0.05 is the multiplier. The correct calculation is 300 × 0.05

starterQuiz.stem: Match each question to the correct multiplier.
starterQuiz.hint: Start with 100% and increase or decrease by the percentage and convert this to a multiplier.
starterQuiz.feedback: 100% + 4% = 104% which is 1.04 as a multiplier.  100% − 40% = 60% which is 0.6 as a multiplier.  100% − 6% = 94% which is 0.94 as a multiplier.  100% + 60% = 160% which is 1.6 as a multiplier.

starterQuiz.stem: A t-shirt costs £13.50 in a sale offering a 25% discount.  The cost of the t-shirt before the discount was £{{ }}
starterQuiz.hint: Divide by the multiplier for an decrease of 25%.
starterQuiz.feedback: An decrease of 25%, 100% − 25% = 75% which is a multiplier of 0.75. £13.50 ÷ 0.75 = £18

starterQuiz.stem: The value of a motorbike depreciates by 12% each year.  It is now worth £6512. Last year the motorbike was worth £{{ }}.
starterQuiz.hint: Divide by the multiplier for an decrease of 12%.
starterQuiz.feedback: An decrease of 12%, 100% − 12% = 88% which is a multiplier of 0.88. So last year the motorbike was worth £6512 ÷ 0.88 = £7400.

starterQuiz.stem: Mr. Oak sells a vase for £72.  This gives him a 20% profit.  Mr. Oak originally purchased the vase for £{{ }}.
starterQuiz.hint: Divide by the multiplier for an increase of 20%.
starterQuiz.feedback: An increase of 20%, 100% + 20% = 120% which is a multiplier of 1.2. So, the vase originally cost £72 ÷ 1.2 = £60.

exitQuiz.stem: __________ is the decimal equivalent of a percentage.
exitQuiz.hint: Percentages share a multiplicative relationship.
exitQuiz.feedback: A multiplier is the decimal equivalent of a percentage. For example to find 50%, you use the multiplier 0.5.

exitQuiz.stem: 100% = 36 and 120% = 43.2. The percentage change is {{ }}%.
exitQuiz.hint: By what percentage has 36 been changed?
exitQuiz.feedback: 120% − 100% = 20%, so the percentage has changed by 20%.

exitQuiz.stem: The cost of a laptop decreases from £450 to £360.  What is the percentage change?
exitQuiz.hint: $$$p$$% of 450 = 360, find $$p$$ and then find the change in percentage.

exitQuiz.stem: Jun thinks of a number and decreases it by a percentage.  The number Jun thought of was 160 and his new number is 136.  Jun changed  160 by {{ }}%
exitQuiz.hint: $$$p$$% of 160 = 136, find $$p$$ and then find the change in percentage.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$p$$ = 136 ÷ 160 × 100 = 85%, 100% − 85% = 15%. So, Jun changed his number by 15% (decrease).

exitQuiz.stem: Jacob’s score on a game increases from 3450 to 3726.  The percentage change in Jacob's score is {{ }}%.
exitQuiz.hint: $$$p$$% of 3450 = 3726, find $$p$$ and then find the change in percentage.

exitQuiz.stem: A reduced sugar bar of chocolate contains 35 g of sugar.  The normal bar contains 15 g more of sugar.  The sugar has been reduced by {{}}%.
exitQuiz.hint: The normal bar contains 35 g + 15 g. $$p$$% of normal bar = reduced sugar bar, find $$p$$ and then find the change in percentage.

lessons.title: Multiplicative relationships and direct proportion
lessons.outcome: I can appreciate the connection between multiplicative relationships and direct proportion.
keyLearningPoints: Direct proportion can be represented on a graph.
Direct proportion can be represented on a double number line.
Direct proportion can be represented with a ratio table.
Direct proportion is a multiplicative relationship.

keywords.definition: Two variables are in direct proportion if they have a constant multiplicative relationship.

starterQuiz.stem: When you use a ratio table, you are using __________ relationship.
starterQuiz.hint: What type of relationship connects these pairs of numbers: 4 and 8, 9 and 18, 10 and 20 ?
starterQuiz.feedback: When using a ratio table you use the multiplicative relationship. For example the multiplier ×2 connects these pairs of numbers: 4 and 8, 9 and 18, 10 and 20.

starterQuiz.stem: 100% = 40 and 70% = 28. The percentage change is {{ }}%.
starterQuiz.hint: By what percentage has 40 been changed?
starterQuiz.feedback: 100% − 70% = 30%, the percentage has changed by 30%.

starterQuiz.stem: The cost of a laptop increases from £540 to £702.  What is the percentage change?
starterQuiz.hint: $$$p$$% of 540 = 702, find $$p$$ and then find the change in percentage.

starterQuiz.stem: Jun thinks of a number and increases it by a percentage.  The number Jun thought of was 80 and his new number is 100.  Jun has increased his original number by {{ }}%.
starterQuiz.hint: $$$p$$% of 80 = 100, find $$p$$ and then find the change in percentage.

starterQuiz.stem: Jacob’s score on a game increases from 2450 to 2744. The percentage that Jacob's original score has changed by is {{ }}%.
starterQuiz.hint: $$$p$$% of 2450 = 2744, find $$p$$ and then find the change in percentage.

starterQuiz.stem: A reduced fat bag of crisps contains 3 g of fat.  The normal bag of crisps contains 2 g more of fat.  The percentage that the fat has been reduced by is {{ }}%.
starterQuiz.hint: The normal bag contains 3 g + 2 g of fat. $$p$$% of normal bag = reduced fat bag, find $$p$$ and then find the change in percentage.
starterQuiz.feedback: The normal bag has 2 g + 3 g = 5g of fat. $$p$$ = 3 ÷ 5 × 100 = 60%, 100% − 60% = 40% decrease.

exitQuiz.stem: Two variables are in direct proportion if they have a {{ }} multiplicative relationship.
exitQuiz.hint: To be in direct proportion the relationship must not change.
exitQuiz.feedback: Two variables are in direct proportion if they have a constant multiplicative relationship. For example, one variable might be always double the other variable.

keywords.definition: Two variables are inversely proportional if there is a constant multiplicative relationship between one variable and the reciprocal of the other.

starterQuiz.stem: Two variables are in proportion if they have a __________.
starterQuiz.hint: As one variable increase the other also increases at the same rate.
starterQuiz.feedback: Two variables are in proportion if they have a constant multiplicative relationship. For example, one variable might always be twice the other.

starterQuiz.hint: Draw a ratio table and find the multiplicative relationship between 5 miles and 12 miles or 5 miles and 8 kilometres.

starterQuiz.stem: Convert 1 m³ into cm³.
starterQuiz.hint: Imagine a 1 m by 1 m  by 1 m cube. Convert the length, width and height into centimetres.

exitQuiz.stem: Two variables are inversely proportional if there is a constant multiplicative relationship between one variable and the __________ of the other variable.
exitQuiz.feedback: Two variables are inversely proportional if there is a constant multiplicative relationship between one variable and the reciprocal of the other. This means as one variable increases, the other variable decreases.

exitQuiz.feedback: Choice 2:  if you write down the coordinates of any point on the curve, the product of the coordinates is 10

units.title: Graphical representations of data
units.description: In this unit pupils will interpret and construct a range of representations of data including bar charts, pie charts and scatter graphs.

lessons.title: Checking understanding of pictograms and bar charts
lessons.outcome: I can interpret both pictograms and bar charts.
keyLearningPoints: Pictograms represent data through images.
Bar charts represent data using the heights of bars.
A key and/or labelled axes are important for interpreting the representation.

keywords.definition: The number of times an event occurs; or the number of individuals (people, animals etc.) with some specific property.

starterQuiz.feedback: You could have multiplied four by three and then added two.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these have an answer of 24?
starterQuiz.hint: Complete each calculation. Which ones are equal to 24? If you are unconfident with multiplication remember it is repeated addition, e.g. $$3\times8=8+8+8$$
starterQuiz.feedback: The answer when two numbers are multiplied is called the product. There are different combinations of numbers that can have the same product.

starterQuiz.stem: What is $${{{1}\over{2}} \text{ of 6}}$$?
starterQuiz.hint: To find half of a number, divide it by 2.
starterQuiz.feedback: As $${{{1}\over{2}} \text{ of 6}}$$ means $${{{1}\over{2}} \times {6}}$$, this can also be thought of as $${\text {6 lots of } \frac {1} {2}}$$

starterQuiz.stem: How many times is the word 'star' in this list? $$\text{moon, star, moon, star, star,}$$$$\text{planet, planet, moon, star,}$$$$\text{planet, asteroid, star, asteroid,}$$$$\text{planet, moon, star}$$
starterQuiz.hint: To find the frequency of the word star count how many times it appears in the list.
starterQuiz.feedback: Star appears 6 times in the list in total. For a small data set like this counting is relatively quick but in a large data set technology such as spreadsheets can do the counting for you.

starterQuiz.stem: This is an example of a {{ }} chart. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The chart is named after the marks. Each group with a bar, represents five.
starterQuiz.feedback: A tally chart is often made during a survey or experiment and counts the frequencies of certain things (how many red/green/blue cars drove past in 10 minutes). It is useful to tally up as things are still changing.

starterQuiz.stem: How many giraffes are represented in this frequency table? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: 12 lions are represented in the frequency table.
starterQuiz.feedback: Tally charts are often converted into frequency tables as it is much quicker to read the frequencies without having to count tallies. With big data and technology it is possible not to do a tally chart at all.

exitQuiz.stem: The {{ }} is the number of times an event occurs; or the number of individuals (people, animals etc.) with some specific property.
exitQuiz.hint: The height of each bar in a bar chart represents the _________.
exitQuiz.feedback: Frequency is "how many" and is something data scientists find very interesting. How many days of sunshine? How does that compare to last year? How many people like extra salt? How many packets of salt are used each year?

exitQuiz.stem: Put the stages of a data investigation in order.
exitQuiz.hint: You cannot analyse the data until you have collected and presented it.
exitQuiz.feedback: It is common to find further questions and then need to collect further data.

exitQuiz.stem: Which pictogram matches this frequency table? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: A pictogram needs a key.
exitQuiz.feedback: Each row should match the frequency for that category.

exitQuiz.stem: Which table matches the bar chart? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The height of the bar shows the frequency.
exitQuiz.feedback: The ticks on the vertical axis are two units apart. Museum is halfway between 14 and 16 so must represent 15. Both theatre and zoo sit on a line and have frequencies of 18 and 12 respectively.

exitQuiz.stem: Which statements are true? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The month with the least number of icons, is the month where the least amount of reading took place.
exitQuiz.feedback: Pictograms are very visual. It is easy to see which is the most or least common as long as the icons are the same size and evenly spaced.

options.text: The most time spent reading was in month 1.
The least amount of time spent reading was in month 3.
In month 1 half as much time was spent reading as in month 3.
In month 3 twice as much time was spent reading as in month 2.
Over the three months there was 70 hours of reading.

exitQuiz.stem: This bar chart shows that {{ }} has visited the most countries out of the four pupils. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Which pupil has the tallest bar?
exitQuiz.feedback: Laura has visited seven countries which is more than any of the others. The bar chart also shows that all four pupils have visited at least two countries.

lessons.title: Securing constructing pictograms
lessons.outcome: I can construct pictograms from data.
keyLearningPoints: Data presented as a list can be represented as a pictogram
Data presented in a table can be represented as a pictogram
The icons chosen should not be distracting or ambiguous

keywords.definition: The frequency is the number of times an event occurs; or the number of individuals (people, animals etc.) with some specific property.
A pictogram (pictograph) is a graph consisting of pictures to visually represent the frequency of objects or groups
Data are a collection of information.

starterQuiz.stem: How many 'asteroids' are in the list? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Count the number of times 'asteroid' appears in the list. Checking line by line might help.
starterQuiz.feedback: This is known as the frequency. Asteroid has a frequency of 2.

starterQuiz.stem: How many groups of 6 are in 36?
starterQuiz.hint: You can work this out by doing $${36 \div 6}$$.
starterQuiz.feedback: This is because $${6 \times 6 = 36}$$.

starterQuiz.stem: The frequency is the {{ }} of times an event occurs; or the {{ }} of individuals (people, animals etc.) with some specific property.
starterQuiz.hint: If 8 pupils had a pet dog, then 8 is the frequency. 8 is the ______ of pupils with a pet dog.
starterQuiz.feedback: After data has been collected in a tally chart, a frequency table is often created to show the number for each category.

starterQuiz.stem: What number does this tally show? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Each group with a bar represents 5.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$3\times5+3=18$$. Tally is a convenient way of keeping track of the amount whilst collecting data.

starterQuiz.stem: The chart shows how many times some zoo animals were seen in an hour. The {{ }} was seen 9 times. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Frequency is the number of times each animal has been seen.
starterQuiz.feedback: The frequency of 9 is in the elephant row. The data in a frequency table can be represented using different statistical diagrams.

starterQuiz.stem: What is $${{\frac {1} {4}} \times 20}$$ ?
starterQuiz.hint: Dividing the amount by four is a method of finding a quarter.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$${{\frac {1} {4}} \times 20}$$ can be thought of as $${{\frac{1}{4}}\text{of} 20}$$ Another method you could have used: half of 20 = 10. Half of 10 = 5.

exitQuiz.stem: This type of representation is known as a {{ }}. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: It makes use of pictures/icons to show the frequency.
exitQuiz.feedback: A pictogram is a visual representation of data.

exitQuiz.stem: A pictogram is going to be drawn where each icon represents a frequency of 4. How many icons would be needed to show a frequency of 32?
exitQuiz.hint: How many 4s make 32?
exitQuiz.feedback: The value of each icon is shown in the key. In this case $$4+4+4+4+4+4+4+4=32$$ so 8 icons are needed.

exitQuiz.stem: {{}} need to be fairly simple in design and representative of the data.
exitQuiz.hint: How is the data represented in a pictogram?
exitQuiz.feedback: The icon is a key element of a pictogram as they aid the visual nature and give context.

exitQuiz.stem: Izzy, Sam and Jacob have 24 pens between them. Therefore each icon represents {{ }} pens. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The total frequency is 24. How many icons represent this total?
exitQuiz.feedback: If Alex had 15 pens in his pencil case then you would use 7.5 icons to represent this.

exitQuiz.stem: Which frequency table matches this pictogram? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: If one full brick represents 20, what does half a brick represent? What does $$\frac{3}{4}$$ of the brick icon represent?
exitQuiz.feedback: The pictogram shows Alex had the most Lego bricks, without calculating the frequencies. For Alex $$2\frac{3}{4}\times20=55$$ For Laura $$2\times20=40$$ and for Aisha $$2.5\times20=50$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these statements are true for the data shown in this pictogram? (IMG: ) [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Remember to check the key to see what each leaf icon represents.
exitQuiz.feedback: Depending on what this data was collected for, it may suggest that plant 1 had the best growing conditions.

options.text: Plant 3 had 45 leaves fewer than plant 1.

lessons.title: Securing constructing bar charts by hand
lessons.outcome: I can construct bar charts from data.
keyLearningPoints: Data presented as a list can be represented as a bar chart
Data presented in a table can be represented as a bar chart
The type of data determines how the bars should be drawn

keywords.definition: The frequency is the number of times an event occurs; or the number of individuals (people, animals etc.) with some specific property.
A bar chart (bar graph) is a graph consisting of bars visually representing the frequency of objects or groups.
Data are a collection of information.

starterQuiz.stem: Rectangle {{ }} is the longest. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Which rectangle is the tallest?
starterQuiz.feedback: This is easily comparable because their bottom edges are lined up.

starterQuiz.stem: These tally marks show a value of {{ }}. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Each line represents 1, a group with a bar is made up of 5 lines.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$1\times 5+1=6$$. Using tally is a convenient way of collecting data. Once the data has been collected, then a frequency table can be created.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these numbers are multiples of 15?
starterQuiz.hint: Multiples of 15 are the 15 times table, keep adding 15. You can start from any number you are confident is in the 15 times table, and even count back wards too.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$30=15\times2$$ and $$75=15*5$$). 95 can't be a multiple since 30 is, so 90 must be a multiple of 15 too, and then the next multiple of 15 would be 105. 130 isn't a multiple, it is 20 less than 150 ($$10\times15$$).

starterQuiz.stem: A pictogram (pictograph) is a graph consisting of pictures to visually represent the {{ }} of objects or groups.
starterQuiz.hint: It means number of times.
starterQuiz.feedback: Pictograms are just one chart that represents frequency.

starterQuiz.stem: Select the frequency table that has a total frequency of 46.
starterQuiz.hint: Add up the three frequencies.
starterQuiz.feedback: Summing the frequencies is the way to find the total frequency. $$15+18+13=46$$.

starterQuiz.stem: Some things are measured and some are counted. Which of these are counted?
starterQuiz.hint: You measure your height, you do not count it.
starterQuiz.feedback: Some types of data can be counted and others can be measured. This can affect how we go on to deal with it.

options.text: heights of a group of people
number of cars that drive past
photographs with an elephant on them

exitQuiz.stem: The total frequency for this data set is {{ }}. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Frequency means the number of something. The data set is the list words.
exitQuiz.feedback: There are $$5+4+3+4=16$$ words in this list.

exitQuiz.stem: If a bar chart was to be constructed for data about favourite pizza toppings in a class, the bars would have a specific order. True or false?
exitQuiz.hint: Pizza toppings do not have a known order to them. (If you disagree still, can you persuade someone else that your order would be the best way to arrange a bar chart on this topic?)
exitQuiz.feedback: There will be some contexts where data should be ordered as there is a known order. In this case there isn't an obvious order so the bars can be in any order.

options.text: True - order from the most favourite to the least favourite topping
False - there is no relevant order to pizza toppings so they can be in any order

exitQuiz.stem: This is an example of a __________ bar chart. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: This data would be presented like this to compare the data.
exitQuiz.feedback: This type of comparison bar chart can be known as a dual bar chart as there are two bars for each category.

exitQuiz.stem: The frequency axis needs to have a suitable scale for the data it is presenting. The scale will go up in {{ }} increments.
exitQuiz.hint: Scales go up like this : 0, 5, 10, 15 ... the increments are all the same.
exitQuiz.feedback: If the scale does not go up in equal increments then it will produce a misleading bar chart.

exitQuiz.stem: Three pupils are discussing this bar chart. Who is correct with their observation? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The most common way of travelling will be the tallest bar and the least common way of travel will be the shortest bar.
exitQuiz.feedback: The comparison bar chart allows easy analysis of travel methods per year group. It is less easy to see which year group has the most pupils, a stacked bar chart would show this better..

exitQuiz.stem: Which bar chart matches this data? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Check the height of each bar is correct for that pupil.
exitQuiz.feedback: A misread of data or an incorrectly drawn bar could cause a problem with the conclusions and outcomes.

keyLearningPoints: Bar charts can be constructed quickly using spreadsheets.
Bar charts can be constructed quickly using Desmos.

keywords.definition: The frequency is the number of times an event occurs; or the number of individuals (people, animals etc.) with some specific property.

starterQuiz.stem: A {{ }} is a graph consisting of bars visually representing the frequency of objects or groups.
starterQuiz.hint: You can get comparison and stacked versions of them.
starterQuiz.feedback: The bars can be either horizontal or vertical.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the frequency of 'planet' according to this bar chart? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: What is the height of the bar?
starterQuiz.feedback: The top of the bar representing the planet category is on the line which reads 4 on the vertical axis. By adding up the heights of all the bar charts, you can find the total frequency.

starterQuiz.stem: Starting with the least amount of time spent reading put the months in order from least to greatest. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The month with the greatest frequency has the most icons.
starterQuiz.feedback: You did not need to work out the frequencies to have completed this task.

starterQuiz.stem: The {{ }} had the same amount of visitors on both Saturday and Sunday. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Look for the venue that has both bars the same height.
starterQuiz.feedback: Both bars for theatre are the same height. It is possible to hypothesise that the weather was better on Saturday than Sunday. What further data might you need to test this hypothesis?

starterQuiz.stem: Which charts represent this data? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The order of the bars for this context doesn't matter.
starterQuiz.feedback: Pictograms and bar charts both show frequency or amounts.

starterQuiz.stem: Frequency is always found on the vertical axis of a bar chart. True or false?
starterQuiz.hint: If a bar chart is horizontal, then the frequency would be the horizontal axis.
starterQuiz.feedback: Often the orientation of the bar chart is chosen dependent on space limitations.

options.text: True - the categories are along the horizontal axis. e.g. food types
False - bar charts can be horizontal rather than vertical

keyLearningPoints: Data presented as a list can be represented as a pie chart.
Data presented in a table can be represented as a pie chart.
A larger data set requires considering the proportion of the total.

keywords.definition: A sector is the region formed between two radii and their connecting arc.

starterQuiz.stem: Match the descriptions for amounts of rotation with the number of degrees each is equivalent to.
starterQuiz.hint: A quarter turn is 90°, and an eighth of a turn is half this amount.
starterQuiz.feedback: A quarter, half, three-quarter, and full turn are all multiples of 90°, whilst an eighth of a turn is half of a quarter turn. A half of 90° is 45°.

starterQuiz.stem: Find $${2}\over{5}$$ of 40
starterQuiz.hint: To find a fraction of an amount, you can find $${1}\over{5}$$ of 40 first by dividing by 5.

starterQuiz.stem: If 8 tennis balls cost £3, then how much would 24 tennis balls cost? Make sure to include units in your answer.
starterQuiz.hint: How many 8s are there in 24? Check you included a unit in your answer.
starterQuiz.feedback: There are three 8s in 24, and so £3 multiplied by 3 = £9.

starterQuiz.stem: If 5 footballs cost £30, then how much would 8 footballs cost?
starterQuiz.hint: First find the multiplier that gets you from 5 footballs to £30. This can be done by calculating £30 $$\div$$ 5.
starterQuiz.feedback: The multiplier is 6, as 5 footballs multiplied by 6 = £30. This same multiplier is applied to 8 footballs. 8 $$\times$$ 6 = £48.

starterQuiz.stem: If 80 table tennis balls cost £16, then how many table tennis balls would cost £3?
starterQuiz.hint: First find the multiplier that gets you from £16 to 80 table tennis balls. This can be done by calculating 80 $$\div$$ 16.
starterQuiz.feedback: The multiplier is 5, as £16 multiplied by 5 = 80 table tennis balls. This same multiplier is applied to £3. 3 $$\times$$ 5 = 15 tennis balls.

options.text: There would be a non-integer number of table tennis balls.

starterQuiz.stem: Sofia and Lucas both purchase books at a secondhand bookstore to donate to their school. Each book costs the same amount. How much, in pounds, did Lucas spend on books? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: First find the multiplier that gets you from 18 books to £45. Or you might prefer to find the multiplier to get from 18 to 20. They may be an integer, fraction or decimal.
starterQuiz.feedback: The multiplier is 2.5, as 2.5 multiplied by 18 books = £45. The same multiplier is applied to 20 books. 20 $$\times$$ 2.5 = £50.

exitQuiz.stem: 36 people were asked: "what do you drink whilst at work". The results will be placed in a pie chart with a total of 12 pre-defined sectors. How many sectors would represent water? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: What is the multiplier that takes you from a frequency of 36 to 12 sectors?
exitQuiz.feedback: The multiplier is $${\times}{1\over3}$$ or $$\div $$ 3. 21 $$\div$$ 3 = 7 sectors.

exitQuiz.stem: 36 people were asked: "what do you drink whilst at work". The results will be placed in a pie chart with a total of 12 pre-defined sectors. How many people voted for milk? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: What is the multiplier that takes you from 12 sectors to a frequency of 36?
exitQuiz.feedback: The multiplier is $${\times}$$ 3. Therefore, 3 $$\times$$ 2 = 6 people.

exitQuiz.stem: A large set of information is collected and represented in a pie chart of 20 equally-sized sectors. Each one sector represents a frequency of 45. What is the total frequency of this dataset?
exitQuiz.hint: 1 sector represents a frequency of 45, while 20 sectors will represent a frequency of what?
exitQuiz.feedback: 20 × 45 = 900. The dataset has a total frequency of 900.

exitQuiz.stem: The incomplete ratio table shows a dataset being converted into angles to represent each subgroup as sectors on a pie chart. Match the letters to the correct missing values. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Totals can be found by summing the columns. The multiplier between columns can be found in any row where there are two known elements.
exitQuiz.feedback: After finding the total frequency of 60 and stating the total angles in a pie chart equal 360°, we can find the multiplier is ×6. We can then use this multiplier to multiply 11 and 18 to find the angles of d and e, respectfully.

exitQuiz.stem: Starting with the first step, put these steps for constructing a sector of a pie chart in order.
exitQuiz.hint: You need to use your ruler, then correctly align the protractor before you focus on finding any angles on the protractor.
exitQuiz.feedback: It is important to place your protractor carefully, aligning it with the centre of the circle and the most recent line you've drawn as a priority. If this is not done, then any angle found will not be drawn in the correct location.

order.text: Draw a straight line from the centre of the circle to its circumference.
Line the bottom centre of the protractor with the centre of the circle.
Line the 0° on the protractor with the most recent straight line drawn.
Starting from 0°, find the angle you want to draw on the protractor.
Plot an × at this point on the protractor.
Draw a straight line from centre of the circle through the × you plot.

exitQuiz.stem: The incomplete ratio table shows a dataset being converted into angles to represent each subgroup as sectors on a pie chart. Find the value of angle a, in degrees. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Start by finding the total frequency.
exitQuiz.feedback: The total frequency is 48. You can find that the multiplier is ×7.5 or $$15\over2$$. You can then use this multiplier to multiply 14 to find the angle of a.

starterQuiz.stem: 60 people were asked: "what do you most frequently drink whilst at work". The results will be placed in a pie chart with a total of 12 pre-defined sectors. How many sectors would represent water? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: What is the multiplier that takes you from a frequency of 60 to 12 sectors?
starterQuiz.feedback: The multiplier is $${\times}{1\over5}$$ or $$\div 5 $$ . $$40 \div 5 = 8$$ sectors.

starterQuiz.stem: 60 people were asked: "what do you most frequently drink whilst at work". The results will be placed in a pie chart with a total of 12 pre-defined sectors. How many people voted for milk? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: What is the multiplier that takes you from 12 sectors to a frequency of 60?
starterQuiz.feedback: The multiplier is $${\times}$$ 5. Therefore, 3 $$\times$$ 5 = 15 people.

starterQuiz.stem: A large set of information is collected and represented in a pie chart of 24 equally-sized sectors. Each one sector represents a frequency of 15. What is the total frequency of this dataset?

starterQuiz.stem: The incomplete ratio table shows a dataset being converted into angles to represent each subgroup as sectors on a pie chart. Match the letters to the correct missing values. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: We know that there is a total of 360° in a pie chart, and that the total frequency can be found by adding up all of the frequencies for each subgroup.
starterQuiz.feedback: After finding the total frequency of 90 and stating the total angles in a pie chart equal 360°, you can find the multiplier is ×4. You can then use this multiplier to multiply 12 and 2 to find the angles of d and e, respectfully.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these parts of a circle are essential when forming one sector of a circle?
starterQuiz.hint: A sector of a circle involves drawing two lines from the centre of the circle to its circumference, enclosed by the part of the circumference that intersects the two lines from the centre.
starterQuiz.feedback: A sector of a circle is the region formed between two radii and their connecting arc.

options.text: the whole circumference / perimeter of a circle
part of the circumference of a circle, called an arc
two radiuses / radii of a circle (distance from centre to circumference)
two diameters of a circle (distance across the whole circle and through centre)
two tangents of a circle (line that touches the circumference at one point)

starterQuiz.stem: The incomplete ratio table shows a dataset being converted into angles to represent each subgroup as sectors on a pie chart. Find the value of angle a, in degrees. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Start by finding the total frequency.
starterQuiz.feedback: The total frequency is 480. We can find that the multiplier is ×0.75 or $$3\over4$$. We can then use this multiplier to multiply 260 to find the angle of a.

exitQuiz.stem: Which symbol must be typed into a cell first in order to start any mathematical calculation?
exitQuiz.hint: This symbol always features in an equation, which is used to show that one number or calculation is equal to another.
exitQuiz.feedback: The equals symbol = tells the spreadsheet to start a mathematical equation.

exitQuiz.stem: Match the mathematical operation to the symbol used to represent these operations in a spreadsheet
exitQuiz.hint: The multiplication symbol is the most common operation to be incorrectly used. The symbol for multiplication is not a letter.
exitQuiz.feedback: Each of these operations are commonly used across all spreadsheet software. It is important to become familiar with them in order to use spreadsheets effectively.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these spreadsheet functions will correctly calculate 63 add 117 in the cell C3? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The addition symbol must be used, not a word with the same meaning.
exitQuiz.feedback: Addition between two cells or several cells spread out over a worksheet is best written as = A3 + B3, but if you have several values to add in a list or as a rectangle of data, then = sum(A3 : B3) is quicker at selecting large sets of data.

exitQuiz.stem: Select the spreadsheet function and answer which correctly show the multiplier being calculated for this ratio table in the cell D17. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: What do I multiply 120 (total frequency) by to get the total angle, 360? The multiplier can be found by dividing 360 by the total frequency.
exitQuiz.feedback: To find the multiplier, you must divide 360 by the total frequency. For any fixed number, you can just type in that number (360), but for any variable, you can click the cell this variable value lies. =360 / C15. The multiplier is 3.

exitQuiz.stem: Select the spreadsheet function and answer which correctly shows and updates the angle for Ireland, calculated in the cell N23. The values in the frequency column may be updated. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: You need to multiply the frequency by the multiplier. Is it better to type in numbers (such as 90) or reference cell names (such as M23) in a spreadsheet?
exitQuiz.feedback: Whilst = 90 * 0.625 is correct, =M23 * N28 is preferred, as if a cell's value changes, using a cell name (such as M23) in a spreadsheet function will automatically update the value of the cell with the function in it.

exitQuiz.stem: Match the descriptions with the correct spreadsheet functions and output values for this ratio table written in a spreadsheet. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: All spreadsheet functions begin with the = equals sign, whilst all output values are the calculated numerical value.
exitQuiz.feedback: Each spreadsheet function is just the same calculation as you would do if you found the angles for a pie chart by hand, but rather than using the numbers for frequency, the multiplier, etc. you're referencing the cell, instead.

starterQuiz.stem: 120 people were asked: "what do you most frequently drink whilst at work". The results will be placed in a pie chart with a total of 20 pre-defined sectors. How many sectors would represent water? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: What is the multiplier that takes you from a frequency of 120 to 20 sectors?
starterQuiz.feedback: The multiplier is $${\times}{1\over6}$$ or $$\div $$ 6. 72 $$\div$$ 6 = 12 sectors.

starterQuiz.stem: 120 people were asked: "what do you most frequently drink whilst at work". The results will be placed in a pie chart with a total of 20 pre-defined sectors. How many people voted for milk? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: What is the multiplier that takes you from 20 sectors to a frequency of 120?
starterQuiz.feedback: The multiplier is $${\times}$$ 6. Therefore, 4 $$\times$$ 6 = 24 people.

starterQuiz.stem: A large set of information is collected and represented in a pie chart of 30 equally-sized sectors. Each sector represents a frequency of 40. What is the total frequency of this dataset?
starterQuiz.hint: 1 sector represents a frequency of 40, what frequency will 30 sectors represent?
starterQuiz.feedback: 30 × 40 = 1200. The dataset has a total frequency of 1200.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these words is not an essential feature of a pie chart or the calculations required to construct a pie chart?
starterQuiz.hint: One of these words may be linked to a circle, but is not relevant to pie charts, specifically.
starterQuiz.feedback: A pie chart requires several radiuses (radii) to be drawn, each helping to define the region of each sector. In order to calculate the angle of a sector, the total frequency or total value must be compared multiplicatively to 360°.

starterQuiz.stem: The incomplete ratio table shows a dataset being converted into angles to represent each subgroup as sectors on a pie chart. Match the letters to the correct missing values. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: We know that there is a total of 360° in a pie chart, and that the total frequency can be found by adding up all of the frequencies for each subgroup.
starterQuiz.feedback: After finding the total frequency of 120 and stating the total angles in a pie chart equal 360°, we can find the multiplier is ×3. We can then use this multiplier to multiply 18 and 44 to find the angles of d and e, respectfully.

starterQuiz.stem: The incomplete ratio table shows a dataset being converted into angles to represent each subgroup as sectors on a pie chart. Find the value of angle a, in degrees. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Start by calculating the total frequency.
starterQuiz.feedback: The total frequency is 990. We can find that the multiplier is $$4\over11$$. This multiplier is best kept in fractional form. We can then use this multiplier to multiply 440 to find the angle of a.

exitQuiz.stem: The table shows the number of people at Location 1 and their preferred cooking style for potatoes. By choosing an appropriate row to perform calculations on, find the value of the unknown multiplier. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: To find the correct multiplier, you can perform a calculation on the numbers in the "boiled" row.
exitQuiz.feedback: To find the multiplier, you find what you multiply 13 by to get 39. This can be figured out by calculating 39 ÷ 13 = 3. Therefore, the multiplier is 3.

exitQuiz.stem: The table shows the number of people at Location 2 and their preferred cooking style for potatoes. Find the multiplier linking frequency and angle. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: To find the correct multiplier, you must perform a calculation on the numbers in the "mashed" row.
exitQuiz.feedback: To find the multiplier, you find what you multiply 81 by to get 162. This can be figured out by calculating 162 ÷ 81 = 2. Therefore, the multiplier is 2.

exitQuiz.stem: Find the number of people who preferred boiled potatoes. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: If the multiplier is a $$\times 2$$ going from frequency to angle, then going in the opposite direction the multiplier will be $${\times} {1\over2}$$
exitQuiz.feedback: Half of 72 is 36, so 36 people voted for boiled potatoes.

exitQuiz.stem: Match the missing number (labelled by a letter) in the ratio table with its correct value. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: To find the multiplier (which is the unknown value labelled with a), look at the roasted row and calculate how many 40s go into 160.
exitQuiz.feedback: The multiplier (a) was essential to find first. From there, you could have found either e or b next by using the multiplier of ×4. c can be found by subtracting 160 and 128 from 360, and similarly d can be found by subtracting 40 and 32 from 90.

exitQuiz.stem: Below are correctly drawn pie charts showing the preferred cooking methods for potatoes for people at Locations 4 and 5. Select the statements that are always true. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Pie charts show proportion, not frequency. It is not possible to find out how many people voted in either Locations 4 or 5 from the pie chart alone.
exitQuiz.feedback: Only the statements talking about proportion or percentage are correct. It is possible the total frequency for Locations 4 and 5 are the same, but it is not guaranteed.

options.text: The same number of people (25 people) voted for boiled at both Locations 4 and 5
The same percentage of people (25%) voted for boiled at both Locations 4 and 5
A greater number of people voted for roasted in Location 5 than Location 4
A greater proportion of people voted for roasted in Location 5 than Location 4
The same number of people voted in Locations 4 and 5

exitQuiz.stem: 75 people voted for roasted in Location 4. By using a protractor and this information, calculate the total frequency of the people who voted in Location 4. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Using a protractor, the roasted segment measures 135°.
exitQuiz.feedback: The multiplier (found by the calculation 135° ÷ 75 people) is 1.8 or $$9\over5$$. If the total angle in a pie chart is 360, then the total frequency is 360 ÷ 1.8 = 200. 200 people voted in Location 4.

lessons.title: Constructing scatter graphs
lessons.outcome: I can construct scatter graphs from data presented in a number of different ways.
keyLearningPoints: Data presented as a paired list can be represented as a scatter graph.
Data presented in a table can be represented as a scatter graph.
The independent variable is placed on the horizontal axis.

keywords.definition: A visual representation for bivariate data. It can be useful when determining the nature of the relationship between the two variables.
An independent (explanatory) variable is a measure that is predicted to have an effect on another variable
A dependent (response) variable is a measure whose value is predicted to be affected by an explanatory variable
Bivariate data has two variables, where each data point for one variable has a corresponding data point for the other variable.

starterQuiz.stem: Which line is horizontal? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The word 'horizontal' is related to the word horizon, which is the line that is visible where the sky meets the sea.
starterQuiz.feedback: Line B runs from left to right and is level. This is a horizontal line.

starterQuiz.stem: Which point on the graph has the coordinates (8, 2)? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The first number tells you the horizontal position; the second number tells you the vertical position.
starterQuiz.feedback: Point D is 8 across and 2 up.

starterQuiz.stem: What are the coordinates of the point marked on this graph? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Read the value on the horizontal axis first, followed by the value on the vertical axis. Remember to write coordinates you need brackets and a comma e.g. (-2, 12)
starterQuiz.feedback: The point is 5 across and 3 up, which is much more efficiently written in coordinate form $$(5, 3)$$

starterQuiz.stem: What is the value of $$a$$ on the horizontal axis?  [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Look at the size of the first interval on the scale. Every interval on the scale must also have the same size.
starterQuiz.feedback: The scale is going up in 20s, so five intervals along the horizontal axis would be $$5 \times 20$$.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the value of $$a$$ on the vertical axis?  [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Look at how many intervals there are to get to 200. Each interval is the same. You can use proportional reasoning here so a ratio table might help. $$\begin{matrix}     4 & 200  \\    1 & ?    \end{matrix} $$
starterQuiz.feedback: Since 4 intervals represent 200, 1 interval will be represented by $$\frac{1}{4}\times200=50$$. You can check by imagining the value on each tick on the axis. 0, 50, 100, 150, 200.

starterQuiz.stem: {{ }} are a set of information which shows counts or measurements.
starterQuiz.hint: Examples of this could be heights, ages, test scores, number of pets or what products people buy.
starterQuiz.feedback: The word data describes a set of information which shows counts or measurements. Data can be plotted onto graphs. It is worth noting that data is plural, as this often catches people out.

exitQuiz.stem: Data which has two variables that are paired together is called {{ }} data.
exitQuiz.hint: Each data point for one variable has a corresponding data point for the other variable.
exitQuiz.feedback: Bivariate data has two variables, where each data point for one variable has a corresponding data point for the other variable.

exitQuiz.stem: Which is another term to describe the explanatory variable in bivariate data?
exitQuiz.hint: Changes in the explanatory variable are assumed to explain changes in the response variable.
exitQuiz.feedback: The explanatory variable can also be called the independent variable. In science experiments it may also be called the input variable.

exitQuiz.stem: Which two terms describe a measure in bivariate data whose value is predicted to be affected by the other measure?
exitQuiz.hint: This variable would be plotted on the vertical axis of your scatter plot.
exitQuiz.feedback: The dependent/response variable is predicted to change in response to changes in independent/explanatory variable. This may be a direct, A increase causes B decrease, or could have other factors that influence it, e.g. C causes both A and B to change

exitQuiz.stem: Which variable should be represented on vertical axis of a scatter graph?
exitQuiz.hint: A scatter graph usually shows how the variable on the vertical axis is responding to the variable on the horizontal axis.
exitQuiz.feedback: The vertical axis usually shows how the dependent variable is responding to the independent variable.

exitQuiz.stem: A set of bivariate data measures children's ages and shoe sizes. Which variable is most likely to be the dependent variable?
exitQuiz.hint: Which variable is likely to change depending on the value of the other?
exitQuiz.feedback: Children's shoe sizes usually change as they get older. So shoe sizes are likely to be dependent on age.

exitQuiz.stem: Look at the second column in the table. Which scatter graph has chosen the most appropriate scale to plot this data? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The scale on the vertical axis needs to capture the greatest value while not having too much unused space.
exitQuiz.feedback: A scale that goes up to 1250 would capture the greatest value of 1116 and make good use of the available space.

starterQuiz.stem: Which two options below are examples of spreadsheet software?

starterQuiz.stem: Which type of graph is a visual representation for bivariate data?

starterQuiz.stem: Which is another term to describe the response variable in bivariate data?

starterQuiz.stem: A set of bivariate data measures hours of daylight in a day and maximum temperature for each day. Which variable is most likely to be the independent variable?

starterQuiz.feedback: The hours of daylight in a day is independent of the temperature. It is likely that the maximum temperature is affected by the hours of daylight during the day. In fact both are affected by the time of year but the hours of light more predictably so.

starterQuiz.feedback: Point C is 3 across and 2 up.

starterQuiz.stem: Which is another term to describe the independent variable in bivariate data?
starterQuiz.hint: Changes to the independent variable is sometimes predicted to be the cause of changes to the other variable.
starterQuiz.feedback: The independent variable can also be called the explanatory variable. In these cases, it is predicted that the value of the independent variable affects the value of the other variable in the bivariate data.

starterQuiz.stem: A {{ }} graph is a visual representation for bivariate data, which can be useful when determining the nature of the relationship between the variables.
starterQuiz.hint: Bivariate data can be represented visually by plotting points or crosses on a grid with two axes.
starterQuiz.feedback: A scatter graph represents bivariate data visually by plotting points or crosses on a grid with two axes.

starterQuiz.stem: A set of bivariate data measures the length of an obstacle course and the time it takes for people to complete it. Which variable is most likely to be the dependent variable?
starterQuiz.hint: The values of the dependent variable are affected by the values of the independent variable.
starterQuiz.feedback: The time taken to complete the course is the dependent because it would be affected by the length of the obstacle course.

options.text: time taken to complete the course

starterQuiz.stem: A set of bivariate data measures the length of an obstacle course and the time it takes for people to complete it. Which variable should go on the horizontal axis of a scatter graph?
starterQuiz.hint: The horizontal axis of a scatter graph usually represents the independent variable.
starterQuiz.feedback: The length of obstacle course would go on the horizontal axis because it is the independent variable.

options.text: time taken to complete the course

exitQuiz.stem: The scatter graph show minimum and maximum temperatures for different months in a town. Which statement best describes the trend in the data? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Pick a point which has a low minimum temperature and look at its maximum temperature. Pick a point which has a high minimum temperature and look at its maximum temperature.
exitQuiz.feedback: The further across a point is in the horizontal axis, the higher up it tends to be in the vertical axis.

options.text: Months with higher minimum temperature have higher maximum temperatures.
Months with higher minimum temperature have lower maximum temperatures.
There is no connection between the variables.

exitQuiz.stem: Which scatter graphs shows a case where as one variable increases the other variable tends to decrease?
exitQuiz.hint: Look from left to right on the horizontal axis. Consider if the points should be getting higher or lower.
exitQuiz.feedback: The further across a point is in the horizontal axis, the lower down it tends to be in the vertical axis.

exitQuiz.stem: Look at the scatter graph. A new month records a minimum temperature of 10 degrees Celsius. Which range could we expect the maximum temperature to be in? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Look at 10 on the horizontal axis and then look up at the points above.
exitQuiz.feedback: Most of the points above 10 on the horizontal axis have maximum temperatures between 14 and 17 degrees Celsius.

exitQuiz.stem: Look at the scatter graph. A new month records a maximum temperature of 10 degrees Celsius. Which range could we expect the minimum temperature to be in? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Look at 10 on the horizontal axis and then look across at the points.
exitQuiz.feedback: Most of the points in line with 10 on the vertical axis have minimum temperatures between 4 and 6 degrees Celsius.

exitQuiz.stem: {{ }} is the process of estimating unknown values that are inside the range of existing data.
exitQuiz.hint: It shares a prefix with other words that indicate being inside or between.
exitQuiz.feedback: Interpolation is the process of estimating unknown values that are inside the range of existing data.

exitQuiz.stem: Which statement is true?
exitQuiz.hint: Interpolation is estimating inside the range of existing data; extrapolation is estimating outside the range of existing data.
exitQuiz.feedback: Interpolation is more reliable than extrapolation for estimating data because it is based on observations that lie inside the range of existing data.

options.text: Extrapolation is more reliable than interpolation for estimating data.
