Interpolation is more reliable than extrapolation for estimating data.
Extrapolation and interpolation are equally reliable for estimating data.

lessons.title: Problem solving with graphical representations of data
lessons.outcome: I can use my understanding of various graphical representations to solve problems.
keyLearningPoints: Data can be presented in various formats.
A fuller picture can be obtained when considering more data.
Multiple representations may be unnecessary.

keywords.definition: A bar chart (bar graph) is a graph consisting of bars visually representing the frequency of objects or groups.
A pie chart (pie graph) is a circular graph where sectors represent different groups proportionally.
A scatter graph is a visual representation for bivariate data. It can help determine the nature of the relationship between the variables.

starterQuiz.stem: Which type of graph uses pictures of objects to visually represent the frequency of objects or groups.
starterQuiz.hint: An example of this graph would be to use a picture of a ball to represent a certain number of goals scored.
starterQuiz.feedback: A pictogram uses pictures of objects to visually represent the frequency of objects or groups.

starterQuiz.stem: Which is a circular graph where sectors represent different groups proportionally?
starterQuiz.hint: Drawing this graph by hand would involve calculating angles and using a protractor.
starterQuiz.feedback: A pie chart is a circular graph where sectors represent different groups proportionally.

starterQuiz.stem: The {{ }} is the number of times an event occurs or the number of individuals (people, animals etc.) with some specific property.
starterQuiz.hint: The word is related to a non-mathematical word to mean something that happens often.
starterQuiz.feedback: Frequency is the number of times an event occurs or the number of individuals (people, animals etc.) with some specific property.

starterQuiz.stem: Look at the bar chart. How many countries has Laura visited? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: In this context, the word frequency on the vertical axis refers to how many countries a person has visited.
starterQuiz.feedback: The bar for Laura is halfway between the 6 and 8 on the vertical axis, meaning Laura has visited 7 countries.

starterQuiz.stem: Look at the bar chart. Which is the most common mode of travel for pupils in Year 10? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Look at the five bars for Year 10 and see which one is the highest.
starterQuiz.feedback: Over 100 pupils in Year 10 travel to school by bus. The mode of travel with the next highest frequency is walk, which is just under 75.

starterQuiz.stem: Look at the line graph. What is the distance at 20 seconds? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Go to 20 on the horizontal axis, go up to the line and see how high the point is on the vertical axis.
starterQuiz.feedback: The point on the line above 20 seconds is level with 2 on the vertical axis.

exitQuiz.stem: Which two population pyramids show cases where the number of male and female residents is approximately equal?
exitQuiz.hint: When a population pyramid is symmetrical, it suggests that the populations are similar for both groups.
exitQuiz.feedback: We can see that the number of male and female residents are approximately equal in these two graphs because they are nearly symmetrical.

exitQuiz.stem: Which population pyramid shows the population whose largest age group is 30 to 34 year-olds?
exitQuiz.hint: The length of the bar shows how many people are in each age group.
exitQuiz.feedback: The largest age groups are the ones with the longest bars.

exitQuiz.stem: The graphs show average temperature in three towns for each month of the year. Which town is the warmest?
exitQuiz.hint: The closer the line is to the centre, the colder the temperature. The further out the line is to the edge, the warmer the temperature.
exitQuiz.feedback: The graph with the largest ring represents the warmest town.

exitQuiz.stem: The graph show the maximum temperature of a town for each month of the year. What was the maximum temperature in April? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The centre of the circle represents 0 degrees Celsius. Each circle, going outward from the centre, represents an additional 5 degrees Celsius.
exitQuiz.feedback: We can see the point for April is 14 degrees Celsius because it is slightly before the line that represents 15 degrees Celsius.

exitQuiz.stem: The graph show the maximum temperature of a town for each month of the year. Which town has a mean temperature of 16 degrees Celsius in July? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Look at July on the horizontal axis. Which of the lines is level with 16 in the vertical axis?
exitQuiz.feedback: The mean temperature for Town B is July is 16 degrees.

exitQuiz.stem: The graph show the maximum temperature of a town for each month of the year.  The mean temperature for Town A in September is {{ }} degrees Celsius. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Look at September on the horizontal axis. Town A is represented by the line with circular points.
exitQuiz.feedback: The mean temperature for Town A in September is 10 degrees Celsius.

units.title: Numerical summaries of data
units.description: In this unit pupils explore the concept of measures of central tendancy, developing understanding of different types of average and their relative benefits and drawbacks. We then investigate other summaries of data such as the range and data comparison techniques.

lessons.title: Checking understanding of the mean
lessons.outcome: I can understand what the mean is measuring, how it is measuring it and calculate the mean from data presented in a list.
keyLearningPoints: The mean can be seen as a redistribution of values such that everything is the same.
The mean is the sum of all values divided by the number of values.
The mean is a measure of central tendency.

keywords.definition: a summary measure that attempts to describe a whole set of data with a single value that represents the middle of its distribution

starterQuiz.stem: The sum of 6, 8, 3, 5, and 7 is {{ }}.
starterQuiz.hint: Sum means to add the numbers together.
starterQuiz.feedback: Finding the total of a group of numbers is also finding the sum. 6 + 8 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 29

starterQuiz.stem: 6 friends share 42 sweets equally. Each friend receives {{ }} sweets.
starterQuiz.feedback: Division is the operation that shares equally. $$42 \div 6 = 7$$

starterQuiz.stem: Match each word with the correct operation.
starterQuiz.hint: The product of 8 and 3 is 24.
starterQuiz.feedback: Word problems often need you to work out which operation needs to be used. Product means multiply, difference means subtract, sum means add or total. Sharing means you need to use division.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the following has an answer of 5?
starterQuiz.hint: Remember the order of operations.

starterQuiz.stem: Eight pupils each roll a dice seven times. There are {{ }} rolls of the dice altogether.
starterQuiz.feedback: The 8 students have each rolled the dice 7 times. $$ 8 \times 7 = 56$$

starterQuiz.stem: There are 40 students that need to be sorted into equal groups.  How many different group sizes could there be? {{ }}
starterQuiz.hint: The groups need to be equal, so how many different ways can you share 40 equally?
starterQuiz.feedback: The group sizes are the factors of 40: 40 groups of 1, 20 groups of 2, 10 groups of 4; 8 groups of 5; 5 groups of 8; 4 groups of 10; 2 groups of 20; 1 group of 40

exitQuiz.stem: The (arithmetic) mean for a set of numerical data is the sum of the values {{ }} by the number of values. It is a measure of central tendency representing the average of the data.
exitQuiz.hint: The mean shares the total across the number of data values.
exitQuiz.feedback: The mean includes all the data points and shares the total evenly across them.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these towers of blocks have a mean of 4?
exitQuiz.hint: If the mean is 4 over three towers, then there needs to be a total of 12 blocks.
exitQuiz.feedback: Different distributions can have the same mean value. 4 × 3 = 12, so you are looking for towers with 12 blocks altogether.

exitQuiz.stem: The mean for this data set: 5, 4, 7, 5, 8, 2, 9, 3, 5, 2 is {{ }}
exitQuiz.hint: The mean value is the even distribution of the total.

exitQuiz.stem: What is the mean of the data shown on this dot plot? {{ }} [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Each dot on the dot plot is a value. Find the total and divide by how many dots there are.
exitQuiz.feedback: The total of the data is (-2) + (-2) + 0 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 5 + 6 + 7 + 7 + 8 + 10 = 48. There are 12 data values, so the mean is 48 ÷ 12 = 4

exitQuiz.stem: Match each total with the number of data values and mean.
exitQuiz.hint: If there are 10 values with a mean of 5, then the total is 10 × 5 = 50.
exitQuiz.feedback: Multiplying the mean of a set of data by the number of pieces of data gives the total of the data set.

exitQuiz.stem: A large data set has 620 pieces of data and a total of 3906. The mean of the data set is {{ }} .
exitQuiz.hint: The mean value is the even distribution of the total.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$ 3906 \div 620 = 6.3 $$. Large data sets will often be on a spreadsheet software with built in formulae to calculate the mean.

lessons.title: Calculating the mean
lessons.outcome: I can calculate the mean from data presented in a frequency table and different graphs.
keyLearningPoints: The mean can be calculated from a line graph.
The mean can be calculated from an ungrouped frequency table.
The mean can be calculated from a bar chart.

keywords.definition: The frequency is the number of times an event occurs; or the number of individuals (people, animals etc.) with some specific property.
Data are a collection of information.
The sum of the values divided by the number of values. It is a measure of central tendency representing the average of the values.
A summary measure that attempts to describe a whole set of data with a single value that represents the middle of the distribution.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these frequency tables shows 49 pieces of data?
starterQuiz.hint: Add up the frequencies.
starterQuiz.feedback: The total frequency is how many pieces of data there are in the data set: 18 + 14 + 17 = 49

starterQuiz.stem: The bar chart shows the number of children who have visited different attractions in the summer holidays. The bar for {{ }} has a frequency of 12. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The frequency is the height of the bar.
starterQuiz.feedback: The bar with a height of 12 is zoo.

starterQuiz.stem: Laura times her bus journey to school every day for a week. On which day did Laura's journey take 28 minutes? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Find 28 minutes on the vertical scale and go across until you find a data point at that height, then drop down to the horizontal scale to find the day.
starterQuiz.feedback: Line graphs (or time series graphs) are useful to look at trends over a period of time. The data point that lines up with 28 minutes is on Thursday.

starterQuiz.stem: A measure of central tendency is a summary measure that attempts to describe a whole set of {{ }} with a single value that represents the middle or centre of its distribution.
starterQuiz.hint: This word means a collection of information.
starterQuiz.feedback: The (arithmetic) mean is a measure of central tendency for a set of data however there are other measures of central tendency as well.

starterQuiz.stem: A large data set has 452 data values which have a total of 16 724. The mean of the data is {{ }}.
starterQuiz.hint: To calculate the mean you divide the total by the number of values.
starterQuiz.feedback: Spreadsheet software can calculate the mean by using the formula =AVERAGE. $$16 724 \div 452 = 37$$

starterQuiz.stem: The mean for the data shown on this dot plot is {{ }}. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Find the total of the dots then divide by the number of dots.
starterQuiz.feedback: The total of the dots is 0 + 0 + 1 + 1 + 4 + 4 + 9 + 9 + 10 + 14 + 14 = 66. There are 11 dots so the mean is 66 ÷ 11 = 6

exitQuiz.stem: Select all the data sets that have a mean.
exitQuiz.hint: You need to have a total to calculate the mean.
exitQuiz.feedback: Other measures of central tendencies can be used on non-numerical data.

options.text: tea, coffee, tea, tea, coffee, tea, water

exitQuiz.stem: The (arithmetic) mean for a set of {{ }} data is the sum of the values divided by the number of values. It is a measure of central tendency representing the average of the values.
exitQuiz.hint: The mean can only be calculated for data such as 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 or 7.3, 6.5, 2.1 but not cat, dog, hamster, horse.
exitQuiz.feedback: Often when companies or individuals say "the average is ..." they are using the mean average. The mean can only be found for numerical data.

exitQuiz.stem: Without any further calculation, which of these could be the mean? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: If this was a list of data, what would the values of the data be? Which answer best represents the data?
exitQuiz.feedback: It is always a good idea to 'sense' check your answers. The mean has to be between 1 and 4 as the number of bedrooms is always between 1 and 4 for this set of data.

exitQuiz.stem: Laura records how long her journey is to school each day for a week. The line graph shows her results. Laura's mean journey time is {{ }} minutes. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: line graph shows individual data plots, so to find the mean you total the data and divide by how many points there are.
exitQuiz.feedback: The total time taken is 32 + 29 + 27 + 28 + 25 = 141 minutes. There are 5 data points. So the mean is 141 ÷ 5 = 28.2 minutes.

exitQuiz.stem: The bar chart shows the number of goals scored by a club in a season. 192 goals were scored in total. The mean number of goals per match is {{ }} rounded to 1 decimal place. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The total needs to be divided by the total frequency. The heights of the bars tell you the frequencies.
exitQuiz.feedback: The total frequency is the total heights of the bars. 12 + 18 + 19 + 20 + 19 = 88. So the mean is 192 ÷ 88 = 2.18... = 2.2 to 1 d.p.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these calculations is correct for finding the mean from this frequency table? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: You need to find the total number of goals scored by the number of matches. 12 matches had 3 × 12 goals per match. A quick way of adding 3 twelve times is 3
exitQuiz.feedback: Multiply each frequency by the number of goals and then add the results. This gives the total number of goals. Adding all the frequencies gives you the number of matches. Mean is total goals ÷ number of matches.

lessons.title: Understanding the median
lessons.outcome: I can understand what the median is measuring, how it is measuring it and find the median from data presented in a list.
keyLearningPoints: The median is a measure of central tendency.
The median is the middle (or average middle) value in an ordered data set.
The median can be seen as the halfway point of a set of values.

keywords.definition: the central (middle) piece of data when the data is in numerical order. A measure of central tendency representing the average of the values

starterQuiz.hint: A written method such as column method can be useful when subtracting numbers.
starterQuiz.feedback: This calculation finds the difference between the two numbers.

starterQuiz.stem: Starting with the highest number, put the numbers in descending order.
starterQuiz.hint: They are all numbers that have an eight in the hundreds column so compare the final two digits of each number.
starterQuiz.feedback: Ordering from largest to smallest is known as descending order.

starterQuiz.stem: {{ }} is exactly half way between 64 and 86.
starterQuiz.hint: There is a gap of 22 between 64 and 86. The number exactly half way will have a gap of 11 with both numbers.
starterQuiz.feedback: 75 is the mean of the two numbers: $${{64+86}}\over {2}$$

starterQuiz.stem: The mean of 34 and 56 is {{ }}.
starterQuiz.hint: To find the mean, add the two numbers and then divide by two.
starterQuiz.feedback: 45 is the mean of the two numbers and is exactly half way between them.

starterQuiz.stem: Starting with the lowest number, put the numbers in ascending order.
starterQuiz.hint: Rewrite the numbers so that they all have three decimal places by using zeros.
starterQuiz.feedback: Ordering from smallest to largest is known as ascending order.

starterQuiz.stem: A measure of {{ }} tendency is a summary measure that attempts to describe a whole set of data with a single value that represents the middle or centre of its distribution.
starterQuiz.hint: The measure is trying to describe the middle or centre of the distribution of data.
starterQuiz.feedback: The word average is used more commonly to mean a measure of central tendency.

exitQuiz.stem: The median is the {{ }} piece of data when the data are in numerical order. It is a measure of central tendency representing the average of the values.
exitQuiz.hint: Imagine a group of students lined up in order of height. Which student will be the most representative of the group?
exitQuiz.feedback: The value does not have to be exactly middle numerically but it terms of position it is in the centre.

exitQuiz.stem: Match the number of data points with the position of the median.
exitQuiz.hint: Even amounts of data require the two most central pieces of data to calculate the median.
exitQuiz.feedback: To find the position of the median you can use $$ {n+1} \over {2}$$ where $$ n $$ is the number of data points.

exitQuiz.hint: There are the two data values in the middle. The median is halfway between these two values.
exitQuiz.feedback: The median is the mean of 2.6 and 2.7, as they are the two most central data values. So, the median is halfway between 2.6 and 2.7

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these data sets can you find the median for?
exitQuiz.hint: The median can only be used on numerical data.
exitQuiz.feedback: The data needs to be in order to find the median.

options.text: cat, dog, rabbit, dog, dog, cat, cat, hamster, fish
red, orange, yellow, blue, green, yellow, white, black, purple

exitQuiz.stem: Sam wants to calculate the median of this data set. Is Sam's working correct? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The median is a measure of central tendency, so needs to represent the central distribution of the data.
exitQuiz.feedback: The median position is the middle value when the data is ordered.

options.text: Yes - the middle number has been identified
No - the data has not been ordered first

exitQuiz.stem: Data is presented in a dot plot. The median value is {{ }}. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: There are 12 pieces of data, so locate the 6th and 7th data value, then find the mean of them.
exitQuiz.feedback: Counting from left to right gives: the 6th piece of data is 3 and the 7th piece of data is 5. The median is halfway between 3 and 5 which is 4.

lessons.title: Calculating the median
lessons.outcome: I can calculate the median from data presented in a frequency table and different graphs.
keyLearningPoints: The median can be calculated from a line graph.
The median can be calculated from an ungrouped frequency table.
The median can be calculated from a bar chart.

keywords.definition: Data are a collection of information

starterQuiz.stem: A vet records how many of each type of pet she sees in a week. Which category of pet did the fewest people have? {{ }} [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The lowest frequency indicates the pet type that least people had.
starterQuiz.feedback: The lowest frequency is 6 which is for hamster.

starterQuiz.stem: How many pieces of data are represented by this bar chart? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The first bar has a frequency of 12. Find the total frequency of all the bars.
starterQuiz.feedback: The total frequency is the number of data values in the set. Add the heights of all the bars: 12 + 15 + 16 + 15 = 58

starterQuiz.stem: The median is the central (middle) piece of data when the data are in numerical {{ }}. It is a measure of central tendency representing the average of the values.
starterQuiz.hint: The median can only be found when the data is arranged from smallest to biggest or biggest to smallest first.
starterQuiz.feedback: The data must be ordered before you can work out the median.

starterQuiz.stem: The median of these data: 1, 1, 1, 3, 5, 5, 5, 6, 6, 7, 7, 8, 8, 9 is {{ }}.
starterQuiz.hint: There are 14 items of data so the median is halfway between the 7th and 8th data values.
starterQuiz.feedback: The two most central pieces of data are 5 and 6. The median is the mean average of these two numbers..

starterQuiz.hint: Put the data in order first.
starterQuiz.feedback: In order the data is: 2.2, 3.1, 3.4, 4.5, 4.6, 5.7, 8.0, 8.2, 8.9. The data set had 9 pieces of data so the median is the 5th value.

starterQuiz.stem: A large data set has 455 values. The median is the {{ }}th data value when the data is in order of size.
starterQuiz.hint: There is an odd number of pieces of data so the median is the middle value when the data is in order of size.
starterQuiz.feedback: To find the position use $$ {n+1}\over {2} $$, where $$ n $$ is the number of data points.$$ {455+1}\over {2} =228 $$

exitQuiz.stem: A measure of central tendency is a summary measure that attempts to describe a whole set of data with a {{ }} value that represents the middle or centre of its distribution.
exitQuiz.hint: The mean, mode and median are measures of central tendency. The median is one value.
exitQuiz.feedback: The data set determines which of the measures of central tendency is the most useful to describe the data. The measure is one single value.

exitQuiz.stem: An ordered data has 4751 pieces of data. The median is in the {{ }}th position.
exitQuiz.hint: The median is in the middle of the ordered data set.
exitQuiz.feedback: To find the position use $$ {n+1}\over {2} $$, where $$ n $$ is the number of data points. $$ {4751+1}\over {2} $$ = 2376

exitQuiz.stem: An estate agent records how many bedrooms each house has on their sales list. The number of houses with 2 bedrooms or fewer is {{ }}. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Add up the frequencies for 1 bedroom houses and 2 bedroom houses.
exitQuiz.feedback: 15 houses have 1 bedroom and 16 houses have 2 bedrooms so (15 + 16) houses have 2 bedrooms or fewer.

exitQuiz.stem: A football coach records the number of goals scored in the last 45 matches. What is the median number of goals scored? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Imagine writing out all the data. You need the 23rd data value that you would write down.
exitQuiz.feedback: If you wrote out all the data, the median is the $${45+1}\over {2}$$th data value. The first 6 numbers are all 0, the next 7 are all 1, the next 6 are all 2. You have written 19 numbers. The next 4 numbers are all 3, so the median is 3.

exitQuiz.stem: The median will __________ be in the middle bar on a bar chart.
exitQuiz.hint: The distribution of the data will impact the location of the median.
exitQuiz.feedback: The median could be in any of the bars. If the vast majority of the data is the first value, then it would be in the first bar, similarly if over 50% of the data is the last value then it would be in the last bar.

exitQuiz.stem: Jun records how long it takes him to get to school each day for a week. Jun's results are shown on the line graph. Jun's median journey time is {{ }} minutes. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: There are five data points which means the median is third data value, when in order.
exitQuiz.feedback: A common misconception is to think the median is the data point that is middle of the horizontal axis. You need to put the journey times in order: 25, 27, 28, 29, 32 and then find the middle time.

lessons.title: Understanding the mode
lessons.outcome: I can understand what the mode is measuring, how it is measuring it and find the mode from data presented in a list.
keyLearningPoints: The mode is a measure of central tendency.
The mode is the most frequently occurring value in a data set.
There can be more than one mode.

keywords.definition: the most frequent value. It is a measure of central tendency representing the average of the values.
Sets of data which have two modes are known as bimodal data
Trimodal data has three modes

starterQuiz.stem: Which is larger:  5 902 or 5 920?
starterQuiz.hint: Compare the tens digit as the thousand and hundred digits are the same.

starterQuiz.stem: Starting with the lowest number, put these numbers in order of size.
starterQuiz.hint: Write all the numbers with the same amount of decimal places. e.g. 2.41 = 2.4100
starterQuiz.feedback: Ordering from smallest to biggest is called ascending order.

starterQuiz.stem: Select the symbols that could be correctly written in the box. $${3} \square {3}$$
starterQuiz.hint: $$${3}\geq{3}$$ is read as 3 is greater than or equal to 3. Is that true?
starterQuiz.feedback: The inequality symbols let us compare values.

starterQuiz.stem: The letter 's' appears {{ }} times in the tongue twister "She sells seashells on the seashore".
starterQuiz.hint: Count the letter s. You could do a tally mark for each letter s you read.
starterQuiz.feedback: In the full tongue twister the letter 's' occurs 34 times.

starterQuiz.stem: An {{ }} is a single number expressing the central or typical value in a set of data.
starterQuiz.hint: A synonym for typical, norm or standard.
starterQuiz.feedback: The averages are also known as measures of central tendency.

starterQuiz.stem: In a non-leap year, which calendar month has the same number of Mondays as Tuesdays as Wednesdays as Thursdays as Fridays as Saturdays as Sundays? {{ }}
starterQuiz.hint: The total days needs to be a multiple of 7.
starterQuiz.feedback: In a leap year, the extra day in February would mean that one of the days has to be repeated.

exitQuiz.stem: The mode is the most {{ }} value. It is a measure of central tendency representing the average of the values.
exitQuiz.hint: The mode can be used for qualitative (non-numerical) data unlike mean and median.
exitQuiz.feedback: The highest frequency indicates the mode.

exitQuiz.hint: Which value appears the most?
exitQuiz.feedback: When lists are ordered it highlights repeats more easily than unordered lists.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these data sets has no mode?
exitQuiz.hint: If there is no mode, then no value occurs more often than any of the others.
exitQuiz.feedback: Each value in the data set 13, 15, 17, 14, 18, 12, 11, 16 occurs once only, so there is no mode.

options.text: cat, dog, cat, mouse, spider, horse

exitQuiz.stem: Which is the best description for the data set shown in this dot plot? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: There is only one value that occurs most often.
exitQuiz.feedback: Look for the 'tallest' number of dots. There is only one value, 3, that occurs most often so there is only one mode.

exitQuiz.stem: Match each data set to the description of its modes.
exitQuiz.hint: Bimodal means two modes and trimodal means three modes.
exitQuiz.feedback: When all the values are different there is no mode. When one value occurs more than any other value there is 1 mode. When 2 values occur an equal number of times and more than any other values, there are 2 modes (bimodel). Trimodel means 3 modes.

match.right: a, b, b, c, c, d, e, e, f, g

exitQuiz.stem: The mode of the data shown on this dot plot is {{ }}. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Which value on the scale has the most dots above it?
exitQuiz.feedback: 3 occurs most often as it has 3 dots. So, 3 is the mode.

lessons.title: Calculating the mode
lessons.outcome: I can calculate the mode from data presented in a frequency table and different graphs.
keyLearningPoints: The mode can be calculated from an ungrouped frequency table.
The mode can be calculated from a bar chart.
The mode can be calculated from a line graph.

keywords.definition: The frequency is the number of times an event occurs; or the number of individuals (people, animals etc.) with some specific property.
The mode is the most frequent value. It is a measure of central tendency representing the average of the values.

starterQuiz.stem: Sets of data which have {{ }} modes are known as bimodal data.
starterQuiz.hint: How many wheels does a bicycle have?
starterQuiz.feedback: The prefix bi- means two. In large data sets, bimodality may indicate that there are subgroups within the data.

starterQuiz.stem: Select the frequency table that shows the data represented in this bar chart. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The height of the bar should match the frequency.
starterQuiz.feedback: The heights of the bars are 12, 15, 16 and 15. The bars are in the same order as the frequency tables.

starterQuiz.stem: Select the data set that matches the line graph. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Five data points about journey times are shown on the line graph. The vertical axis is the time taken.
starterQuiz.feedback: Reading the journey times in order gives the data set.

starterQuiz.stem: This list of data: 4, 6, 3, 6, 2, 8, 2, 9, 2 6, 3, 6, 5 has a mode of {{ }}.
starterQuiz.hint: Which value occurs more than any other?
starterQuiz.feedback: Order the data to groups the values: 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 6, 6, 6, 6, 8, 9. The most common value is 6, so this is the mode.

starterQuiz.stem: The data represented on this dot plot has __________ mode(s). [image]
starterQuiz.hint: How many times does the tallest stack of dots appear?
starterQuiz.feedback: There are more 3s than any other data value so this is the only mode.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these are trimodal data sets?
starterQuiz.hint: Trimodal means 3 modes.
starterQuiz.feedback: Trimodal data has three values that occur the same amount as each other and more than all the other values.

exitQuiz.stem: The {{ }} is the most frequent value. It is a measure of central tendency representing the average of the values.
exitQuiz.hint: The mean and median are other measures of central tendency.
exitQuiz.feedback: The mode is an average that can be used on qualitative data, unlike the mean and median.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these frequency tables has no mode?
exitQuiz.hint: The highest frequency indicates the mode.
exitQuiz.feedback: When all the frequencies are equal, there is no mode.

exitQuiz.stem: This line graph shows data about the time taken for the journey to school in one week. Which of the following statements is correct? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The data set represented here is 32, 29, 27, 28, 25. What is the mode?
exitQuiz.feedback: There is only a mode if on a horizontal level there is more than one data point.

options.text: The mode time is 32 minutes as this is the journey which took the most time.
There is no mode as no journey time occurred more than once in the week.

exitQuiz.stem: The modal pet type is {{ }}. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Which pet has the highest frequency?
exitQuiz.feedback: If this data was represented as a pictogram, the mode would be identifiable by having the most icons.

exitQuiz.stem: This bar chart shows data about the goals scored in matches over a season. The modal number of goals scored in a match is {{ }} goals. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Which bar is the tallest?
exitQuiz.feedback: It does not matter that 1 goal, 2 goals and 4 goals have the same frequency, as the frequency is less than that of 3 goals.

exitQuiz.stem: Select all the data sets that show bimodal data.
exitQuiz.hint: Remember 'bi' means two and mode is the data value with the highest frequency.
exitQuiz.feedback: Bimodal means that the highest frequency appears twice.

lessons.title: Understanding and calculating the range
lessons.outcome: I can understand what the range is measuring, how it is measuring it and calculate the range from data presented in a range of different ways.
keyLearningPoints: The range is a measure of spread.
The range is difference between the highest and lowest data point.
The range shows how spread out (far apart) the extreme values in the data set are.

keywords.definition: The range is a measure of spread. It is found by finding the difference between the highest and lowest values.
The spread/dispersion of data values describes how far apart the pieces of data are.

starterQuiz.hint: You can calculate this by using column method.
starterQuiz.feedback: This calculation finds the difference between the two values.

starterQuiz.hint: On a number line, what is the distance between (-28) and (-47)?
starterQuiz.feedback: This is equivalent to $$ (-28) + 47 $$.

starterQuiz.hint: You can calculate this by using column method. Make sure you line up the decimal point.
starterQuiz.feedback: You can check your answer by adding 19.7 to it and making sure you get 63.8

starterQuiz.stem: {{ }} are a collection of information.
starterQuiz.hint: Favourite colours or shoe size are examples of information that you might collect in a statistical inquiry.
starterQuiz.feedback: Data can be either numerical or non-numerical.

starterQuiz.stem: Two numbers have a difference of 10. The smaller number is 53. The other number is {{ }}
starterQuiz.hint: Work out $$ 53 + 10 $$
starterQuiz.feedback: If you were not told that the 53 was the smallest number, there could have been two answers.

starterQuiz.stem: Two positive numbers have a difference of 8. One of the numbers is 6. The other number is {{ }}
starterQuiz.hint: The two numbers are both positive.
starterQuiz.feedback: If they were not both positive, then the other number could have been (-2) as that has a difference of 8 from 6.

exitQuiz.stem: The range is a measure of spread. It is found by finding the {{ }} between the two extreme points; the lowest and highest values.
exitQuiz.hint: You subtract the lowest value from the highest to calculate the range.
exitQuiz.feedback: There are other measures of spread available mathematically.

exitQuiz.stem: Select the data sets where you can calculate a range.
exitQuiz.hint: There needs to be a lowest and highest value to calculate the range.
exitQuiz.feedback: The range can only be used on qualitative (numerical) data. When all the data values are the same the range is 0.

options.text: cat, dog, rabbit, dog, cat, rabbit, hamster
ash, birch, oak, maple, sycamore, oak

exitQuiz.stem: A large data set has the extreme values of 24.6 and 59.2. The range of the data set is {{ }}.
exitQuiz.feedback: The other values in the data set are not considered when calculating the range.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these dot plots is most varied?
exitQuiz.hint: Which of the dot plots has the largest range?
exitQuiz.feedback: The range is useful to compare consistency of data. The range for each plot are: 14 − 0 = 14; 9 − (-3) = 12 and 10 − (-2) = 12. The plot with a range of 14 is most varied.

exitQuiz.stem: This line graph shows data about journey times to school over a week. The range of the journey times is {{ }} minutes. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The two extreme values will be the longest journey time and the shortest journey time.
exitQuiz.feedback: Line graphs show single data points, so the range is the vertical distance between the highest point and the lowest point.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these bar charts show data with a range of 4?
exitQuiz.hint: The difference between the tallest and shortest bar on a frequency bar chart is not finding the range. You need to look at the data values, not the frequencies.
exitQuiz.feedback: Range in number of goals is 4 − 0 = 4. Range in hygiene rating is 5 − 1 = 4. Range in number of bedrooms is 4 − 1 = 3.

lessons.title: Summarising data
lessons.outcome: I can see that the different measures of central tendency offer a summary of a set of data.
keyLearningPoints: The mode is a useful measure of central tendency for certain data sets.
The median is a useful measure of central tendency for certain data sets.
The mean is a useful measure of central tendency for certain data sets.

keywords.definition: Data are a collection of information.
The (arithmetic) mean for a set of numerical data is the sum of the values divided by the number of values.
The median is the central (middle) piece of data when the data are in numerical order.
Mode is the most frequent value. It is a measure of central tendency representing the average of the values.
A summary that attempts to describe a whole set of data with a single value that represents the middle of the distribution.

starterQuiz.stem: Match the summary statistic to its definition.
starterQuiz.hint: A modal value represents the most frequent value in a dataset, whilst the mean value requires a calculation that uses all data points in a dataset.
starterQuiz.feedback: It is important to remember which summary statistic is found using which method.

match.left: is the sum of the values divided by the number of values
is the middle piece of data when the data are in order

starterQuiz.stem: Find the mode of this list of numbers: 4, 7, 16, 16, 22, 23, 24, 28
starterQuiz.hint: The mode is the most frequent value in a list of data.
starterQuiz.feedback: 16 is the only number that appears more than once in this list, therefore it must be the mode.

starterQuiz.stem: Find the median of this list of numbers. 4, 7, 16, 16, 22, 23, 24, 28
starterQuiz.hint: If there are two numbers at the centre of a dataset, the median is at the midpoint of those two numbers.
starterQuiz.feedback: You can find the midpoint of 16 and 22 by taking the sum of 16 and 22 (which is 38), and then halving the result (half of 38 is 19).

starterQuiz.stem: Find the modal value of this dataset from its dot plot. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: If the mode is the most frequent value in a dataset, then the modal value in a dot plot is the value with the most amount of dots.
starterQuiz.feedback: The value 29 has the most number of dots, therefore it is the most frequently occurring value.

starterQuiz.stem: Work out the mean of this dataset: (-6), (-5), (-3), (-3), 1, 4, 5, 7
starterQuiz.hint: To find the mean, you must add up all the data points in a dataset, then divide by the number of datapoints.
starterQuiz.feedback: The mean is allowed to be zero, a decimal, and a negative number.

starterQuiz.stem: Dataset A and dataset B both show the minimum temperatures in two different locations. How much bigger is the range of dataset A than the range of dataset B? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: To find the range of a frequency table, you do not look at the frequency column - you find the difference in value between the maximum and minimum data points you have collected.
starterQuiz.feedback: The range of dataset A is 21, whilst the range of dataset B is 10.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these most closely describe a "measure of central tendency"?
exitQuiz.hint: The three measures of central tendency you are most likely to be familiar with are: the mean, the median, the mode.
exitQuiz.feedback: Most of the time, a measure of central tendency will be a single value, however there are certain situations where more than one value will be given, such as when a dataset is bimodal.

options.text: A single value that summarises how spread out or varied a dataset is
Always a single value that calculates the middle number in an ordered dataset
Usually a single value that calculates the middle number in an ordered dataset
Always a single value representing a central property of a distribution
Usually a single value representing a central property of a distribution

exitQuiz.stem: Describe the modal properties of this dataset: 2, 2, 6, 5, 6, 6, 3, 4, 0, 9, 2
exitQuiz.hint: It can be helpful to order the dataset, so that data points with the same value are grouped together.
exitQuiz.feedback: Both 2 and 6 appear three times, whilst 5 only appears twice. Therefore, both 2 and 6 are modal values, and the dataset is bimodal.

exitQuiz.stem: For the following dataset, match the summary statistic to its value: 10, 14, 14, 18, 19, 21, 23
exitQuiz.hint: It can be helpful to order the dataset, so that the median can be found, and the mode and range can more easily be identified.
exitQuiz.feedback: Each summary provides a different insight into a dataset, and therefore can have a different value. It is not sensible to assume that all summary statistics will have the same answer.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these is the most likely value of the mean for this dataset, represented by a dot plot? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The mean is a measure of central tendency, and therefore a representative mean is one whose value is close to the centre of the values of a dataset. The mean can never be above the maximum value, or below the minimum value.
exitQuiz.feedback: Whilst 86 is still within the range of values in the dataset, it is both not fairly central, and is not around common, or frequent, data points. 80 is the only option that is central and represents common data points.

exitQuiz.stem: In which of these dot plots would the mode be a representative summary of the dataset? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The mode is most likely to be a representative summary of a small dataset if there are one or two distinct peaks.
exitQuiz.feedback: On dot plot a, the mode is barely more frequent than other values, and on dot plot c, there are too many peaks for any of them to be representative.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the following statements are true for this dot plot when evaluating whether the median is a representative summary of the data? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The median is usually close to the centre of a distribution, and is representative of a dataset if the centre of a distribution is close to frequent values in the dataset.
exitQuiz.feedback: Even if a summary is not representative of a dataset, it may still have use. With this dot plot, the median of 21 is far away from many data points, but is still useful in separating the dataset into two halves, one greater than and one less than 21.

options.text: The median may not be the most representative summary.
The median will never be a useful summary for this dataset.
The median can still be a useful summary for this dataset.

lessons.title: Changing a data point
lessons.outcome: I can see how certain statistical measures may change as a result of changes in the data.
keyLearningPoints: Changing the value of one data point can affect the mode.
Changing the value of one data point can affect the median.
Changing the value of one data point can affect the mean.

keywords.definition: Sets of data which have two modes are known as bimodal data.
The (arithmetic) mean for a set of numerical data is the sum of the values divided by the number of values.
The median is the central (middle) piece of data when a set of numerical data is in numerical order.
The mode is the most frequent value in a dataset.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these statements defines the median?
starterQuiz.hint: The median is most easily found if a data is placed into numerical order.
starterQuiz.feedback: The median is the centremost data point in an ordered dataset. If there are two centremost values, then the arithmetic mean is found from those two data points.

options.text: The most frequent value when the data are put into numerical order.
The distance on a number line between the smallest and largest data point.
The sum of values divided by the number of values in a data set.
The middle piece of data when the data are put into numerical order.

starterQuiz.stem: Calculate the mean for this data set. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: To find the mean, you first need to add together the values of all the data points.
starterQuiz.feedback: The sum of all the data points is 140. Then, 140 ÷ 8 = 17.5

starterQuiz.stem: Match the summary statistic to its value. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: It can be helpful to order the data set, so that the median can be found, and the mode and range can more easily be identified.
starterQuiz.feedback: Mean = $${(-2)+(-1)+(-1)+4+5+6+10}\over{7}$$; the mode is (-1) as this is the most common value. The median is the middle value which is 4. The range is 10 − (-2) = 12

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these statements is true for this dot plot? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: A summary does not need to be representative in order for it to be a useful piece of information when interpreting a dataset.
starterQuiz.feedback: The data set is bimodal at 68 and 70. However, they are only just the modal values, as many other values have almost the same frequency. This reduces how representative the mode is as a summary of the data.

options.text: The data set has a single mode.
The mode does not appear to be the most representative summary.
Because the mode is not representative, it is not a useful summary.
Even though the mode isn't representative, this information can still be useful.

starterQuiz.stem: First calculate the mean for this dot plot, then select the correct statements. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The mean is found by adding up the value of each dot, then dividing by the number of dots. For example, there are two 7s on the dot plot, therefore you add 7 twice.
starterQuiz.feedback: The sum of the dots on the dot plot is 80. The mean of 10 isn't very representative, as it does not represent a very populated region of the dot plot. However, the mean can still be useful when using it as an average and comparing it to other data.

options.text: The mean is representative because many data points share the same value.
The mean isn't very representative because not many data point are close to it.
The mean isn't very representative because the range is bigger.

starterQuiz.stem: Without carrying out any calculations select which of these statements are likely to be true for this dot plot. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The value of the median is never greater than the largest data point, or less than the smallest data point.
starterQuiz.feedback: The data set has two halves, so the median is around 83. This is not a very representative summary of the data set, since there is no data point of 83, and not many data points close to it.

options.text: The median is close to the two peaks of high frequency values in the data set.
The median is in the dip of low or no frequency values in the data set.

exitQuiz.stem: One data point on this dot plot was incorrectly typed in. After the data point is modified and corrected, Andeep notices the mode has changed. Which of these statements must be true? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: In order for the mode to change, at least one of the following must be true: the frequency of the modal value must decrease, or the frequency of a high frequency-value must increase.
exitQuiz.feedback: Visualise this as one data point moving from 14 to 16. The value with the most dots changes from 14 to 16, and therefore the mode has changed.

options.text: The data paint must be corrected to 14.
The data point must be corrected to 16.

exitQuiz.stem: The mean of this dot plot is currently 15.75. A new data point is collected and added to the data set. Laura re-calculates the mean and notices it has decreased. What could the new data point be? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: In order for the mean to decrease, a data point added to the data set must have a value less than the current mean.
exitQuiz.feedback: Adding on any value greater than 15.75 would increase the mean, whilst adding a value of 15.75 would keep the mean the same.

exitQuiz.stem: The mean of this dot plot is 15.75. A data point is no longer relevant and removed from the data set. Sam re-calculates the mean and notices it has decreased. What could the new data point be? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: In order for the mean to decrease, a data point removed from the data set must have a value greater than the current mean.
exitQuiz.feedback: Removing any value greater than 15.75 would decrease the mean, whilst removing a value of 15.75 would keep the mean the same.

exitQuiz.stem: A data point is removed from this dataset, as it is no longer relevant to an investigation. Which of the following are possible outcomes after the data point is removed? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: -3 is the only value that appears twice, and each other value appears once. What would happen if -3 was removed, or what would happen if a different value was removed?
exitQuiz.feedback: If a -3 was removed, then the data set would have no mode. If a different value was removed, the mode would remain the same.

options.text: The data set may become bimodal.
The mode of the data set may stay the same.
The mode of the data set may change to a different value.
There may be no mode in the data set.

exitQuiz.stem: Match each possible change to the data set to the correct description of its impact on the median. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: If a data point less than the median has to be added to a data set, the value of the median may either stay the same or decrease.
exitQuiz.feedback: 2 is less than the median, so if a data point of 2 is added, the location of the median shifts left by half a position, therefore changing it from 6.5 down to 4.

match.right: A data point of 2 is added
A data point of 4 is removed
A data point of 6.5 is added
4 is modified in value to a 7

exitQuiz.stem: Match each possible change to the data set to the correct description of its impact on the mean. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: If a data point had to be modified, where its value increases, then the mean must also increase. If a data point is added to a dataset, and the value of that data points is greater than the mean, then the mean must also increase.
exitQuiz.feedback: In this scenario, changing a 4 to a 20 has a greater impact on the mean than introducing a new data point of 20. This is because a value smaller than the mean is being "removed", then a value greater than the mean being added.

match.right: 4 is modified in value to a 20
9 is modified in value to a 1
A data point of 20 is added
A data point of 6.5 is added

lessons.title: Evaluating the range
lessons.outcome: I can evaluate the range as a measure of spread, including a consideration of outliers.
keyLearningPoints: The range can be affected by outliers in the data.
Removing these outliers will change the value of the range.
Outliers must be carefully considered and only removed if they were recorded in error.

keywords.definition: A data point that is extremely large or small compared to the rest of the dataset.
A measure of spread. It is found by finding the difference between the highest and lowest values.
Describes how far apart pieces of data in a dataset are.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these sentences describe the range?
starterQuiz.hint: The range is a measure of how spread out all the data points in a data set are.
starterQuiz.feedback: The range is a measure of dispersion, meaning it measures how spread out or varied a data set is. Its value is found by subtracting the smallest value in a data set from the largest value in a data set.

options.text: A measure of variance or varity
It is found by finding the difference between the highest and lowest values
It is found by putting a data set into size order and finding the middle value

starterQuiz.stem: Match the key parts of a calculation for the range with the correct values for this data set: 6, 3, 10, 4, 9, 1, 4
starterQuiz.hint: To find the range, it is important to look at a data set and write down the largest value and the smallest value.
starterQuiz.feedback: The largest and smallest value in a data set may not be the first or last numbers if the data set isn't ordered. 10 − 1 = 9. So, the range is 9.

match.right: Number not used to find range

starterQuiz.stem: Select the correct calculation to find the range of this data set: 19, 12, 16, 19, 9, 11
starterQuiz.hint: The range requires a subtraction.
starterQuiz.feedback: The largest value of 19 subtract the smallest value of 9 equals 10. So the range is 10.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each data set to its range.
starterQuiz.hint: The range is found by the largest data point subtract the smallest data point. It does not mean the last data point subtract the first data point, as the data may not be ordered.
starterQuiz.feedback: Ordering the data first is a good way of spotting what are the largest and smallest values to use when calculating the range.

starterQuiz.stem: A data set is presented on a dot plot. The range of the data is {{ }}. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: What is the value of the right-most dot subtract the value of the left-most dot?
starterQuiz.feedback: 73 − 66 = 7. The range is 7.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these dot plots have a range of 6?
starterQuiz.hint: What is the value of the right-most dot subtract the value of the left-most dot for each dot plot?
starterQuiz.feedback: Both dot plots b and c have a range of 6. The range of dot plot a is 7 − 2 = 5The scale of dot plot d goes up in 2s, and therefore its range is 12, not 6.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these sentences best describe what an outlier is.
exitQuiz.hint: An outlier is a data point in a data set whose value is very different than most other values in the dataset.
exitQuiz.feedback: An outlier is a value that is extremely large or extremely small compared to the majority of other data points in a data set. They will have an influence on the size of the range.

options.text: An outlier is always the largest value in a data set.
An outlier is extremely large or small compared to the rest of the data set.
An outlier is an extremely large or small value after a range is calculated.
Outliers lie close to all the other data points in a data set.
Outliers lie far away from where the majority of the data points are clustered.

exitQuiz.stem: What is the value of the outlier on this dot plot? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Outliers lie far away from where the majority of the data points are clustered.
exitQuiz.feedback: The data point of 63 is significantly far away from the rest of the data points on this dot plot.

exitQuiz.stem: How many outliers are there on this dot plot? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Outliers lie far away from where the majority of the data points are clustered. There can be more than one outlier in a data set.
exitQuiz.feedback: Even without the scale of a dot plot, outliers can still be identified if they look noticeably further away from the main cluster or clusters of data in a data set.

exitQuiz.stem: Match each piece of information to its value. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: With this data set, the outlier is a value much smaller than the rest of the data points.
exitQuiz.feedback: Without the outlier, the size if the range is less than half the size if it included the range.

exitQuiz.stem: For this ordered data set, calculate the range whilst including all outliers, and also calculate the range without the outliers. The difference between the two ranges is {{ }} [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The outliers are 4, 5 and 96. The calculation for the range whilst including all the outliers is 96 - 4.
exitQuiz.feedback: Without the data points of 4, 5, and 96, the range has decreased from 92 to 9. This is a change of 83.

exitQuiz.stem: Different outliers may need to be: kept, removed, investigated further, depending on the context with which these outliers have occurred. Match what should happen to the outlier to its context.
exitQuiz.hint: You definitely keep an outlier if it is realistic, but slightly higher than other values. You definitely remove if it seems implausible, and perhaps includes an error. You investigate further if its plausibility is uncertain.
exitQuiz.feedback: 28 days in a month is realistic for a summer month. However, walking 200 km to the supermarket is equivalent to walking from London to Cardiff - not very realistic. The plausibility of a cat being 11 kg is uncertain, so would require investigation.

match.left: An outlier of 28 for number of days in a month without rain.
A student walked 200 km to the supermarket.
19 cats had a mass of 4 - 6 kg. Outlier had a mass of 11 kg.

lessons.title: Comparing statistical representations
lessons.outcome: I can see that different statistical representations offer different insights into a set of data.
keyLearningPoints: A pie chart and a bar chart offer different insights.
There are certain features of any representation that make it useful.

keywords.definition: A pie chart (pie graph) is a circular graph where sectors represent different groups proportionally.
A bar chart (bar graph) is a graph consisting of bars visually representing the frequency of objects or groups.

starterQuiz.stem: The bar chart shows the weather over 40 days one winter. What is the modal type of weather? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Modal means the mode. The mode is the most frequently occurring type of data point in a dataset.
starterQuiz.feedback: Wind had the highest frequency of 20, as shown by the tallest bar on the bar chart.

starterQuiz.stem: The bar chart shows the weather over 40 days one winter. How many more days were dry than had hail? {{ }} days. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Find the heights of both dry and hail, then perform a subtraction.
starterQuiz.feedback: It was dry on 8 more days than when it hailed, because 11 − 3 = 8.

starterQuiz.stem: The bar chart shows the weather over 40 days one winter. On what fraction of days did it rain? Give your answer in its simplest form. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: To write this as a fraction, the numerator will include the number of days that it rained. The denominator will include the total number of days represented by the entire bar chart.
starterQuiz.feedback: It rained on 5 out of the 40 days. This simplifies to 1/8.

starterQuiz.stem: This pie chart shows 60 vehicles that passed the road nearby a school. What is the modal vehicle that passed nearby the school? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Modal means the mode. The most frequently occurring type of data point in a data set is also the largest sector of a pie chart.
starterQuiz.feedback: The sector representing cars had a larger angle than the other sectors, therefore cars were the modal vehicle.

starterQuiz.stem: This pie chart shows 60 vehicles that passed the road nearby a school. Which two vehicles were counted an equal number of times? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: If two sectors in a pie chart have equal size, then the vehicles those sectors represent are also equal.
starterQuiz.feedback: The sectors for both vans and buses had equal-sized sectors, and therefore their frequency with which both vehicles appeared are also equal.

starterQuiz.stem: This pie chart shows 60 vehicles that passed the road nearby a school. Complete the statement: {{ }} motorbikes passed nearby the school. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The sector for motorbikes has an angle of 90°. This represents a quarter of all vehicles that passed the school.
starterQuiz.feedback: 60 vehicles passed in total and the motorbike sector of the pie chart is 90° (which represents a quarter). So a quarter of 60 = 15 motorcycles.

exitQuiz.stem: Match each statement to the graph (bar chart, pie chart, or both) from which the statement can most easily be found. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The mode is the most frequently occurring data point. For a pie chart, this is the largest sector, and for a bar chart, this is the tallest bar.
exitQuiz.feedback: From a quick snapshot look at the data, it is easier to look at frequencies from a bar chart, and proportions from a pie chart.

exitQuiz.stem: The pie chart and bar chart represent the same data set. Match the bars on the bar chart to the sectors of the pie chart. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The larger the sector of the pie chart, the taller the equivalent bar will be on the bar chart.
exitQuiz.feedback: The largest sector in the pie chart is summer so this matches to the tallest bar (a). The smallest sector in the pie chart is spring so this matches to the shortest bar (c).

exitQuiz.stem: The angle of the sector representing autumn on the pie chart is 90°. Using the bar chart, what will the angle of the sector representing spring on the pie chart be? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The height of the bar representing autumn is 8, whilst the height of the bar representing spring is 4.
exitQuiz.feedback: The frequency of spring is half the frequency of autumn, therefore half of 90° is 45°.

exitQuiz.stem: The pie chart and bar chart represent the same data set. Which two school trips were equally popular? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Which two sectors of a pie chart have an equal angle? If it is difficult to spot by eye, using a protractor to accurately measure each angle is a sensible option.
exitQuiz.feedback: Both museum and beach were equally frequent, with their sectors having an angle of 80°.

exitQuiz.stem: The angle of the sectors for museum and beach are both 80°. What should the height of the bar representing theatre be on the bar chart? {{ }} [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The angle of the sector representing concert on the pie chart is half the angle for museum.
exitQuiz.feedback: The angle of the sector representing museum and beach are 80° and concert is 40°. So the angle of the sector representing theatre is 160°. So the bar representing theatre should be double the height of museum, at 20.

exitQuiz.stem: On this choropleth map, there is a new, quite densely populated settlement on the centre left of the map represented by 4 squares. The minimum population of this settlement is {{ }} people. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The four squares that represent the quite densely populated settlement on the centre left of the map are the three 3 squares and the one 4 square.
exitQuiz.feedback: 3 × 500 + 1 × 1000 = 2500 people in this settlement.

lessons.title: Comparing summaries of data
lessons.outcome: I can use the different measures of central tendency and spread to compare two sets of data.
keyLearningPoints: Statistical summaries of data can be used to make inferences about that data.
Two sets of statistical summaries can be used to compare the respective data sets.
Statistical summaries have their limitations.

keywords.definition: is a summary measure that attempts to describe a whole dataset with a single value that represents the middle or centre of its distribution.
The spread/dispersion of data values describes how far apart the pieces of data are.
The spread/dispersion of data values describes how far apart the pieces of data are.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these is not a measure of central tendency?
starterQuiz.hint: One of these options is a measure of dispersion or spread.
starterQuiz.feedback: The mean, median, and mode are all measures of central tendency - they aim to summarise a data set by values representing its centre. However, the range measures how spread out or varied a data set is.

starterQuiz.stem: Describe the modal properties of this data set: 12, 12, 9, 8, 8, 4, 0, 3, 12, 9, 9
starterQuiz.hint: It can be helpful to order the data set, so that data points with the same value are grouped together.
starterQuiz.feedback: Both 12 and 9 appear three times, whilst 8 only appears twice. Therefore, both 12 and 9 are modal values, and the data set is bimodal.

starterQuiz.stem: By how much is the range of data set A greater than the range of data set B? {{ }} [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Range is largest data value − smallest data value.
starterQuiz.feedback: The range of data set A is 16 − 1 = 15, whilst the range of data set B is 19 − 12 = 7. Data set A has a larger range by 8.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each of the mean, median, mode, and range to its value for this data set: 1, 1, 1, 3, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9
starterQuiz.hint: Remember mean, median and mode are measures of central tendency (averages) and range is a measure of spread.
starterQuiz.feedback: To find the mean find the total of all the data and divide by the number of values. The median is the middle value. The mode is most common value. Range is largest data value − smallest data value.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each summary statistic to its value for this dot plot. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The largest data point has a value of 19, and the smallest data point has a value of 10.
starterQuiz.feedback: The range is the easiest to spot from reasoning, as 9 is lower than any value in the data set; no measure of central tendency (mean, median, mode) can have a value lower than the lowest value in the dataset.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these is a reasonable estimate for the mean of this data set? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The mean can never be lower than the value of the smallest data point, and is rarely a value close to the smallest or largest data point, unless those values have high frequency. The mean is a measure of central tendency.
starterQuiz.feedback: 50.8 is the only value that is central to the dataset. 19 is smaller than all data points, and so cannot be the mean. 40, 42.5, and 58 are too close to the low-frequency smallest and largest data points in the data set.

exitQuiz.stem: Match the summary statistic to the word that can be used to help in its interpretation.
exitQuiz.hint: The range is the only summary statistic that doesn't represent a central measure; it measures how spread out the data points in the data set are.
exitQuiz.feedback: The mean is a typical value that is summarised from all data points in the data set, whilst the median is the middle value in an ordered list, and the mode is the most frequent value. The range represents the variation in a data set.

match.left: how varied the data set is

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these is a valid interpretation of the mean number of points Lucas and Sofia have scored when playing the new video game? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The mean measures the typical number of points a person would score in a mean average game.
exitQuiz.feedback: Sofia's mean of 87.1 is higher than Lucas' mean of 78.3. This means that in a typical game, Sofia is expected to score 8.8 points more than Lucas.

options.text: Both Lucas and Sofia's most frequent number of points per game is almost equal.
Sofia's typical number of points scored per game is lower than Lucas'.
Sofia's typical number of points scored per game is higher than Lucas'.
Lucas' middle-scoring game is lower than Sofia's middle-scoring game.
Lucas' middle-scoring game is higher than Sofia's middle-scoring game.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these is a valid interpretation of the range of points Lucas and Sofia scored when playing the new video game? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The higher the range, the greater the variety in the value of data points in a dataset.
exitQuiz.feedback: Sofia's range of 16 is lower than Lucas' range of 22. This means that Sofia has a lower variety in her scores, therefore the number of points she scored is more consistent than Lucas.

options.text: The variety of points Sofia scored is higher than Lucas'.
The variety of points Sofia scored is lower than Lucas'.
The variety of points Sofia and Lucas scored are almost equal.
Sofia has a lower consistency of points than Lucas.
Sofia has a higher consistency of points than Lucas.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these statements are true for the median and modal number of goals Jun and Aisha scored over 11 netball matches? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Remember the median is the middle value when the data is in order of size. The mode is the most common value.
exitQuiz.feedback: The median for Jun is 1 goal and for Aisha is is 2 goals. The mode for Jun is 1 goal. The modes for Aisha are 1 and 3.

options.text: The median number of goals scored by Jun in a match is higher than Aisha.
The median number of goals scored by Aisha in a match is higher than Jun.
The modal number of goals scored in a match by Aisha and Jun are equal.
Aisha's goals scored in a match is bimodal, with one mode higher than Jun's.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these statements are an accurate interpretation of the number of goals Jun and Aisha scored over 11 netball matches? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Find the mean and the range for both Aisha and Jun.
exitQuiz.feedback: The mean average number of goals scored by both Jun and Aisha is equal, at 2 goals each. However, Aisha will more consistently do this due to her smaller range, whilst Jun may sometimes score many goals, and sometimes none at all.

options.text: On a mean average match, Jun will score 2 goals more than Aisha.
On a mean average match, Jun and Aisha will score the same number of goals.
However, Aisha is more consistent at scoring goals.
However, Jun is more consistent at scoring goals.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these statements combine to make an accurate comparison of which class performed better on an end-of-topic quiz. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The typical score refers to the mean of a data set, and the consistency is measured by the range of a data set.
exitQuiz.feedback: Whilst the scores of class A were more consistent, they were more consistently lower than class B, as class B had the higher mean and median, with one of their modes being significantly higher than the mode of class A.

options.text: The typical score of a student in class A is 1.6 higher than class B.
The typical score of a student in class B is 1.6 higher than class A.
However, class A had a more consistent set of scores.
In conclusion, class B did better, as their middle-scoring student did better.
In conclusion, class A did better, as their most frequent score was higher.

lessons.title: Analysing different statistical representations
lessons.outcome: I can use the different statistical representations to compare two sets of data.
keyLearningPoints: Statistical summaries can be compared to graphical representations of data.
Statistical summaries can be used to produce a sketch of what the graphical representation could be.
Different statistical representations can help form a more complete picture.

keywords.definition: A statistical summary sums up the features of a data set. It may contain the averages (mean, median, mode). It may also contain the range.
is a summary measure that attempts to describe a whole dataset with a single value that represents the middle or centre of its distribution.
The spread/dispersion of data values describes how far apart the pieces of data are.

starterQuiz.stem: In which of these statistical graphs can the frequency of the data set be seen from the graph alone?
starterQuiz.hint: For two of the graphs where frequency can be seen, the number of data points plotted on the graph represents the frequency of the data points.
starterQuiz.feedback: The frequency on a bar chart can be found by adding the heights of the bars. The frequency on a line graph or scatter graph can be found by counting the number of data points. And on a pictogram, it can be found by adding the values of each symbol.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these statistical graphs is best at showing the change in the value of something over time?
starterQuiz.hint: In one of these graphs, the $$x$$-axis measures a period of time, whilst the $$y$$-axis shows the value of something at that point in time.
starterQuiz.feedback: A line graph shows how a value changes over time. It is sometimes called a time-series graph.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the following statements is true when describing the mode of these four bar charts? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: When looking at a bar chart to find the mode, you look at the bar or bars that are the tallest; the taller the bar, the greater the frequency.
starterQuiz.feedback: Data set B is bimodal, and data set C is trimodal. Data set A has a modal frequency of 14.

options.text: At least one data set is trimodal.

starterQuiz.stem: Match the statements that summarise these bar charts to the value that end each sentence. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: To find the range from a bar chart, you take the bar with the highest value (seen using the $$x$$-axis) and subtract the bar with the lowest value.
starterQuiz.feedback: Data set C has the largest range at 13, whilst data set D has the smallest range at 9. This means that the data points in data set D are more consistent than in data set C. The median of data sets A, B, and C are all 5.

match.right: The range of data set C is
The range of data set D is
The median of A, B, and C is
The mode of data set D is

starterQuiz.stem: How much larger is the mode of this dot plot compared to its mean? {{ }} [image]
starterQuiz.hint: There are 10 data points in this dataset, so the median will be the $${{10 + 1}\over{2}}={5.5^{th}}$$, which will be in between the fifth and sixth data point.
starterQuiz.feedback: The median is 13, whilst the mode is 15. Therefore, the mode is 2 bigger.

starterQuiz.stem: How much larger is the mean of this dot plot compared to its mode? Give your answer rounded to 1 decimal place. {{ }} [image]
starterQuiz.hint: There are 10 data points of 16 in this data set.
starterQuiz.feedback: The mean of this data set can be found by first adding the 10 lots of 16, or more simply 10 × 16. The full calculation for the mean is: $${{(10 \times 16) + 18 + 19 + 19}\over{13}}\approx{16.6}$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these statements is valid when comparing the height of Alex in year 6 to the "average" height of other year 6s at his primary school? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The modal height is 100 cm. Is Alex taller or shorter than 100 cm?
exitQuiz.feedback: Alex is around average height, as his height of 105 cm is approximately equal to the mean, median, and modal heights. Whether he is above or below "average" will depend on interpretation and which summary you choose to use.

options.text: Alex is taller than average because he is taller than the modal height.
Alex is taller than average because he is taller than the mean height.
Alex is shorter than average because he is shorter than the median height.
Alex is around average height because his height is close to frequent heights.
Alex is shorter than average because the maximum height is 150 cm

exitQuiz.stem: Select the data sets which match the following statistical summary: a range of 14 [image]
exitQuiz.hint: To find the range, you take the bar representing the highest value and subtract the bar representing the lowest value.
exitQuiz.feedback: Both datasets A and B have a range of 14, even if their minimum and maximum values are different from each other.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these is a representative median of the data set that has following statistical summary: a mode at 54, a range of 14, a mean of approximately 50? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The dataset that satisfies this statistical summary is dataset D.
exitQuiz.feedback: Data set A fits the statistical summary. The median is the central value in the data set so it can't be 58 as this is outside the range of the data. 44 and 54 are too close to the 'ends' of the data set, so it must be 51.

exitQuiz.stem: Sam asks 55 people how many times per month they visit the supermarket. Sam loses some of the data, but represents the rest on a bar chart. How many people's data did Sam lose? {{ }} people [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Add up the heights of all the bars that are shown on the incomplete bar chart. Subtract this number from 55.
exitQuiz.feedback: 55 people were asked in total, but only 1 + 1 + 6 + 5 + 6 + 8 + 7 = 44 pieces of data are represented by the bar chart. Therefore, 11 people's data are missing.

exitQuiz.stem: Here is an incomplete bar chart for a data set. The range of the data set is 12 days. What is the maximum number of days per month that the people surveyed visited the supermarket? {{ }} days [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The minimum number of days per month that could be represented is 1 (it cannot be 0, as they are already at the supermarket). The range is 12.
exitQuiz.feedback: The range is 12, therefore the maximum will be 12 greater than the minimum. 1 + 12 = 13. The maximum number of days is 13. The 14 bar must be correct, at a frequency of 0.

exitQuiz.stem: This bar chart has missing bars. 50 people were surveyed. The range is 7. The frequency of 11 days is 3 greater than the frequency of 10 days. Work out the frequency for 10 days. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The range is 7 so there are only two bars missing as 11 − 4 = 7
exitQuiz.feedback: The total frequency of the data shown is 7 + 10 + 6 + 3 + 5 + 6 = 37. So there are 50 − 37 = 13 missing values. There are 2 missing bars as the range is 7. 5 + 8 = 13 and 8 − 5 = 3, so the frequency is 5.

lessons.title: Correlation
lessons.outcome: I can recognise relationships between bivariate data represented on a scatter graph.
keyLearningPoints: The distribution of data points may suggest positive correlation.
The distribution of data points may suggest negative correlation.
The distribution of data points may suggest no correlation.
Correlation does not imply causation

keywords.definition: Correlation describes the extent to which the relationship is close to a linear relationship.

starterQuiz.stem: Bivariate data has {{ }} variables that are together.
starterQuiz.hint: The prefix 'bi' is also used in the words 'bicycle', 'binoculars' and 'binary'. With each word, the 'bi' prefix indicates a number of parts.
starterQuiz.feedback: Bivariate data has two variables, where each data point for one variable has a corresponding data point for the other variable.

starterQuiz.stem: Which type of graph can be used to display bivariate data by plotting coordinates on a grid?
starterQuiz.hint: The graph has two axis (one for each variable) and the data is plotted as points or crosses on the grid.
starterQuiz.feedback: A scatter graph displays bivariate data by plotting each data pairing as a coordinate on a grid.

starterQuiz.stem: Which variable is usually assigned to the horizontal axis of a scatter graph?
starterQuiz.hint: The axes could also be described using alternative wording: the explanatory variable is usually assigned to the horizontal axis, while the response variable is usually assigned to the vertical axis.
starterQuiz.feedback: The independent variable is usually assigned to the horizontal axis of a scatter graph.

starterQuiz.stem: Which scatter graphs shows a case where as one variable increases the other variable also tends to increase?
starterQuiz.hint: Points which are further across in the horizontal axis are also higher up in the vertical axis.
starterQuiz.feedback: As the variable in the horizontal axis increases, the variable is the vertical axis also tends to increase.

starterQuiz.stem: In which graph does the line have a positive gradient?
starterQuiz.hint: Points on the line which are further across in the horizontal axis are also higher up in the vertical axis.
starterQuiz.feedback: The gradient will be positive if the amount $$y$$ increases as the graph moves to the right.

starterQuiz.stem: The line in the graph has a {{ }} gradient. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The amount $$y$$ is decreasing as the graph moves to the right.
starterQuiz.feedback: The line in the graph has a negative gradient.

exitQuiz.stem: The word {{ }} describes the extent to which the association is close to a linear association.
exitQuiz.hint: It may be positive or negative, depending on whether one variable generally increases as another increases or whether it decreases.
exitQuiz.feedback: The word correlation describes the extent to which the association is close to a linear association.

exitQuiz.stem: A positive correlation suggests that as the independent variable increases, the dependent variable {{ }}.
exitQuiz.hint: When data has positive correlation, the points follows a direction that is similar to a line with positive gradient.
exitQuiz.feedback: A positive correlation suggests that as the independent variable increases, the dependent variable increases.

exitQuiz.stem: Which graph shows a negative correlation?
exitQuiz.hint: Negative correlation suggests that as the values on the horizontal axis increase, the values on the vertical axis tend to decrease.
exitQuiz.feedback: The points in that graph tend to be decreasing in height as the graph moves the right, so it suggests negative correlation.
