exitQuiz.stem: Which type of correlation best describes the data in the scatter graph? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The points do not appear to be increasing or decreasing as the graph moves the right.
exitQuiz.feedback: The bivariate data appears to have no correlation.

exitQuiz.stem: Which graph could be described as having an association/relationship which is not linear?
exitQuiz.hint: Having an association/relationship suggests that there is a pattern. If it was linear then the points would tend to follow the same direction a straight line.
exitQuiz.feedback: The graph could be described as having an association/relationship because there is a pattern, but it is not linear because it is curved.

exitQuiz.stem: True or false? Correlation always implies that one variable is affecting the other.
exitQuiz.hint: Correlation highlights that there may be an association between the variables but not necessarily causation.
exitQuiz.feedback: Correlation does not necessarily imply that one variable is affecting the other.

lessons.title: Statistical problems - data collection
lessons.outcome: I can choose what data needs to be collected to explore a statistical problem.
keyLearningPoints: Different statistical problems need investigating in different ways.
Effective data collection avoids bias where appropriate.
When sampling from a population, the sample size needs to be practical.

keywords.definition: The population is the entire set of people, creatures, plants or items that make up the whole group which is being studied.
Bias can be present in any sample collected from a population and may affect the results of a statistical investigation
A sample is a subset of the population

starterQuiz.stem: When you count how many individuals (people, animals etc.) are in each category of a data set you are finding the {{ }} for each category.
starterQuiz.hint: What is the number of times something occurs called?
starterQuiz.feedback: The number of times something occurs is called its frequency.

starterQuiz.stem: Put the stages of a data investigation in order.
starterQuiz.hint: It is helpful to decide what it is you want to find out before you start collecting any data.
starterQuiz.feedback: Each step of the data investigation provides what is necessary for the next step to happen.

order.text: choosing outcomes or actions based on the results

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these data sets can only contain integer values?
starterQuiz.hint: In which case would you not expect to have any decimal numbers?
starterQuiz.feedback: Data about the number of people travelling on a train would be frequencies, which always take integer values.

options.text: number of people travelling on a train

starterQuiz.stem: Which tool measures length?
starterQuiz.hint: Examples of units of length include centimetres and inches.
starterQuiz.feedback: A measuring tape can be used to measure length.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the frequency of 'moon' in the list? {{ }} [image]
starterQuiz.hint: How many times does the word 'moon' occur in the list?
starterQuiz.feedback: Moon is written 4 times in the list.

starterQuiz.stem: Which is an example of a tally chart?
starterQuiz.hint: A tally chart allows you to count things as they are observed.
starterQuiz.feedback: A tally chart allows you to count things by drawing an extra line each time they are observed.

exitQuiz.stem: Which tool could be used to collect data about how satisfied customers are after using their business?
exitQuiz.hint: Customers may be asked to rate their experience out of five or to press a scoring button on their way out.
exitQuiz.feedback: A questionnaire can be a useful tool for collecting people's opinions about something.

exitQuiz.stem: Which tool could you use to collect data about the frequencies of different species of birds that land in a garden?
exitQuiz.hint: A tool that helps you to keep count each species of bird as they land would be useful.
exitQuiz.feedback: A tally chart is helpful for counting things as they are observed, such as a bird landing in your garden.

exitQuiz.stem: Which word describes the entire set of people, creatures, plants or items that make up the whole group that is being studied in a data investigation?
exitQuiz.hint: Examples include: all the people in a region; all the fish in a lake; all the trees on an island; all subscribers to an online product.
exitQuiz.feedback: The population of a data investigation is the entire set of people, creatures, plants or items that make up the whole group that is being studied.

exitQuiz.stem: A {{ }} is a subset of the population of a data investigation.
exitQuiz.hint: Sometimes you cannot survey the whole population so you only investigate part of it.
exitQuiz.feedback: It is often not practical to survey the whole population, so you need to take a sample which is a representative part of the whole population.

exitQuiz.stem: Alex wants to investigate how much time 16 year-old pupils in the UK spend doing homework per week. What is the population in Alex's investigation?
exitQuiz.hint: The population reflects the research question that Alex is investigating.
exitQuiz.feedback: Alex wants to know about all 16 year olds in the UK so the population in Alex's investigation would be all 16 year-old school pupils in the UK.

options.text: all school pupils in the UK
all 16 year-old school pupils in the UK
all 16 year-old pupils in Alex's school

exitQuiz.stem: Laura wants to investigate how much time pupils in her school spend watching cartoons per week. Which of these samples would be the most representative of the population in Laura's investigation?
exitQuiz.hint: The population of Laura's investigation is all the pupils in her school but the amount of time spent watching cartoons may differ between ages.
exitQuiz.feedback: While any could be used as a sample, the sampling strategy which would represent the full range of ages in the school would be 4 people from each of the 5 year groups.

options.text: 20 people in the oldest year group
20 people in the middle year group
10 people from the oldest year group and 10 people from the youngest year group
4 people from each of the 5 year groups in the school

lessons.title: Statistical problems - statistical summaries
lessons.outcome: I can choose appropriate statistical measures to explore a statistical problem.
keyLearningPoints: The type of data may mean that certain statistical measures are not appropriate.
The nature of the data may mean that certain statistical measures are not appropriate.
Certain statistical measures may not make sense within the context of the data.

keywords.definition: A statistical summary sums up the features of a data set.

a summary measure that attempts to describe a whole set of data with a single value that represents the middle or centre of its distribution

starterQuiz.stem: Match each type of average with its description.
starterQuiz.hint: The 'mean' is sometimes referred to as the 'arithmetic mean'.
starterQuiz.feedback: There is a different process for finding each type of average, but they all express the central or typical value in a set of data.

match.left: the sum of the data divided by the number of data points
the most central (middle) piece of data
the data value with the highest frequency

starterQuiz.stem: The spread of a data set can be measured using the {{ }}, by subtracting the lowest value from the highest value.
starterQuiz.hint: This measure can be used as a statistical summary, but it is not a type of average.
starterQuiz.feedback: The range can by calculated by subtracting the lowest value from the highest value of a data set. It is a measure that indicates the amount of spread within the data.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the mode for the data represented in the dot plot? The mode is {{ }} [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The mode is the value with the highest frequency.
starterQuiz.feedback: The mode is 3 because it is the value with the highest frequency.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the median for the data represented in the dot plot? The median is {{ }} [image]

starterQuiz.feedback: The median is 4 because it is the most central (middle) piece of data.

starterQuiz.stem: Find the mean for following numbers: 1, 4, 7, 8. The mean is {{ }}

starterQuiz.feedback: The four numbers sum to 20, so the mean is 5.

starterQuiz.stem: Which set of numbers has the greatest range?

starterQuiz.feedback: The range in this data set is 29 − 20 =  9; the range in the other three data sets is 6.

exitQuiz.stem: Which statistical summary is not a type of average?

exitQuiz.stem: Select the type of average that could be used for the following data: dog, cat, dog, dog, fish, cat, cat, hamster, cat

exitQuiz.stem: Each data set has a mean of 50.  For which data set is this average the least representative of numbers in the set?

exitQuiz.stem: Select the type of average which would least represent the central tendency of the following data: 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 10, 10

exitQuiz.stem: The table provide a statistical summary of data about monthly rainfall in four regions. Which region tends to get the most rainfall? [image]

starterQuiz.stem: What type of correlation does the scatter graph show? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: As the values on the horizontal axis increase, the values of the vertical axis also tend to increase.
starterQuiz.feedback: A positive correlation indicates that as the values on the horizontal axis increase, the values of the vertical axis also tend to increase.

starterQuiz.stem: How many giraffes are represented in the pictogram? {{ }} giraffes [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The key shows how many animals are represented by each image.
starterQuiz.feedback: There are five giraffes represented by two and a half images.

starterQuiz.stem: The pie charts show the types of potato served by school canteens in two locations. Which statement is always true for the data represented in the pie charts? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The total frequency of each pie chart is unknown.
starterQuiz.feedback: The size of the sectors in a pie chart represent the proportion of data that belongs to each category. The pie charts do not tell you about the frequencies.

options.text: The frequency of mashed potato is greater in Location 4 than Location 5.
The proportion of mashed potato is greater in Location 4 than Location 5.
The amount of boiled potato served is the same in both locations

starterQuiz.stem: Which place had the same number of visitors on both Saturday and Sunday? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Each place has two bars above it: one for Saturday and one for Sunday.
starterQuiz.feedback: The bars for the theatre are the same height for both Saturday and Sunday.

starterQuiz.stem: This line graph shows data about journey times to work over a week. The median journey time is {{ }} minutes. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: You could find the journey time for each day and write them in ascending order. The median would be the middle journey time.
starterQuiz.feedback: The median journey time is 28 minutes.

exitQuiz.stem: Which type of graph would be the most appropriate for showing correlation between bivariate data?
exitQuiz.hint: Bivariate data can be represented visually by plotting data pairs as coordinates on a grid.
exitQuiz.feedback: A scatter graph can be used to show correlation between bivariate data.

exitQuiz.stem: Which type of graph visually illustrates the context of the data as well as the frequencies?
exitQuiz.hint: Frequencies could be represented by using images that relate to the context of the data.
exitQuiz.feedback: Pictograms represent frequencies using images that usually relate to the context of the data.

exitQuiz.stem: Which type of graph would be the most appropriate for showing how a single variable has changed over time?
exitQuiz.hint: The horizontal axis could be used to represent time and the vertical axis could be used to represent the values of the data at each time.
exitQuiz.feedback: A line graph can be a clear way to show how a single variable has changed over time.

exitQuiz.stem: True or false: the scale on scatter graphs always needs to start at zero.
exitQuiz.hint: You would ideally like for the shape of the data to be as clear as possible so that it is easy to see whether the data has correlation.
exitQuiz.feedback: The scale on scatter graphs does not always need to start at zero.

exitQuiz.stem: Which type of graph would be inappropriate for representing the data in the table? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: One of the graph types requires two variables.
exitQuiz.feedback: Scatter graphs are used for bivariate data.

exitQuiz.stem: Which elements are missing from this bar chart? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: It is not clear what the data in this bar chart is about.
exitQuiz.feedback: The bar chart needs labels on the horizontal and vertical axis to make it clear what the data is about.

options.text: an axis break on the vertical axis
label for the scale on the vertical axis
labels on the horizontal axis for the bars

lessons.title: Statistical problems - drawing conclusions
lessons.outcome: I can effectively summarise and communicate conclusions to a statistical problem.
keyLearningPoints: Conclusions can be drawn from statistical summaries and graphical representations.
Conclusions are understood to be limited by any biases.
Conclusions are understood to only be valid for this sample of data.

keywords.definition: The population is the entire set of people, creatures, plants or items that make up the whole group which is being studied
A sample is a subset of the population.
Bias can be present in any sample collected from a population. e.g. only asking year 7 pupils about a whole school issue.
A statistical summary sums up the features of a data set

starterQuiz.stem: In a data investigation, the __________ is the entire set of people, creatures, plants or items that make up the whole group which is being studied.
starterQuiz.hint: Examples include: all the people of a town, all the fish in a lake, all of the trees in a park.
starterQuiz.feedback: In a data investigation, the population is the entire set of people, creatures, plants or items that make up the whole group which is being studied.

starterQuiz.stem: {{ }} is the relationship between two variables on a scatter graph.
starterQuiz.hint: Sometimes there is no linear relationship. Sometimes the relationship is positive and sometimes it is negative.
starterQuiz.feedback: When bivariate data has positive correlation then as one variable increases, so does the other.

starterQuiz.stem: Extrapolation is the process of estimating unknown values that are {{ }}.
starterQuiz.hint: The prefix 'ext' is also used in other words such as 'external' and 'exterior'.
starterQuiz.feedback: Extrapolation is the process of estimating unknown values that are outside the range of existing data.

options.text: based on the mean of the data
inside the range of existing data
outside the range of existing data

starterQuiz.stem: What type of correlation does the scatter graph show? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: As the values on the horizontal axis increase, the values of the vertical axis tend to decrease.
starterQuiz.feedback: A negative correlation indicates that as the values on the horizontal axis increase, the values of the vertical axis tend to decrease.

starterQuiz.stem: A data investigation finds a positive correlation between temperature and ice cream sales. What does this suggest?
starterQuiz.hint: A positive correlation would mean that the points on a scatter graph would roughly follow the direction of a straight line that is sloping upwards.
starterQuiz.feedback: A positive correlation suggests that as one variable increases, the other variable increases too. The temperature rise causes people to eat more ice cream. People eating more ice cream doesn't cause the temperature to rise!

options.text: As the temperature increases, the number of ice cream sales decreases.
As the temperature increases, the number of ice cream sales also increases.
There is no relationship between the temperature and ice cream sales.
Ice cream sales cause the temperature to increase

starterQuiz.stem: The mean for the following numbers data set 8.2, 7.4, 11.3, 9.1 is {{ }}.
starterQuiz.hint: The mean is the sum of the data divided by the number of data points.
starterQuiz.feedback: The 4 numbers sum to 36, so the mean is 9.

exitQuiz.stem: Which is the least popular mode of transport in this school? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Consider which bar is the lowest for each year group.
exitQuiz.feedback: Train has the lowest frequency for each year group in the school.

exitQuiz.stem: An investigation surveys residents of two towns about which type of car they drive. The stacked bar chart shows the results. Which is the most popular type of car in this survey? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Which type of car has the longest total bar length?
exitQuiz.feedback: The bars for petrol cars are longer than the bars for diesel and electric cars for both towns.

exitQuiz.stem: The scatter graph shows the population of some towns and the number of phone towers the town has. Each point in the scatter graph represents a town or region. Match each town with its statement. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Check if each point is below, above or within the other points that are plotted in the scatter graph.
exitQuiz.feedback: Most towns with a similar population have between 2000 and 6000 phone towers. Town A has more than 6000 and Town C has less than 2000.

match.left: has a high number of phone towers for the population
has the expected number of phone towers for the population
has a low number of phone towers for the population

exitQuiz.stem: The scatter graph shows data about the sunshine duration and mean temperature for each month in a city. Which of the statements is the most valid? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Interpolation tends to be more reliable than extrapolation.
exitQuiz.feedback: Making a prediction within the range of available data is more reliable than making predictions beyond the range of the data.

options.text: A month with 10 hours of sunshine expect a mean temperature of 1 degrees C.
A month with 100 hours of sunshine expect a mean temperature of 12 degrees C.
A month with 330 hours of sunshine expect a mean temperature of 25 degrees C.

exitQuiz.stem: A data investigation surveys 100 people in Oxford about their preferred mode of transport. The most popular mode of transport was bicycle. Which is the most valid conclusion based on these results?
exitQuiz.hint: Conclusions based on a sample may only be valid for this sample of data.
exitQuiz.feedback: The preferred modes of transport may differ in other cities, regions or countries. So the most valid conclusion would be one that is limited to Oxford.

exitQuiz.stem: {{ }} can be present in any sample collected from a population and may affect the results of a statistical investigation (e.g. only asking year 7 pupils what food should be served in the school).
exitQuiz.hint: Another example would be investigating how many hours people spend exercising per week by conducting a survey at a gym.
exitQuiz.feedback: Bias can be present in any sample collected from a population and may affect the results of a statistical investigation.

lessons.title: Problem solving with numerical summaries of data
lessons.outcome: I can use my understanding of various data summaries to solve problems.
keyLearningPoints: Stated conclusions should be critically evaluated to ensure validity.
Certain statistical summaries may be omitted in the real world.
In order to make more accurate conclusions, you need the data set and the conditions it was collected in.

keywords.definition: A statistical summary sums up the features of a data set.
A summary measure that attempts to describe a whole set of data with a single value that represents the middle or centre of its distribution
The range is a measure of spread. It is found by finding the difference between the highest and lowest values

starterQuiz.stem: The dot plot represents a set of data. The mode for this data is {{ }}. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The mode is the value with the highest frequency.
starterQuiz.feedback: The mode is 2 because it has the highest frequency.

starterQuiz.stem: The dot plot represents a set of data. The median for this data is {{ }}. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The median is the most central (middle) data point.
starterQuiz.feedback: The median is 3 because that is the most central data point in the dot plot.

starterQuiz.stem: The dot plot represents a set of data. The mean for this data is {{ }} [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The mean is the sum of the data divided by the number of data points.
starterQuiz.feedback: The 7 numbers sum to 35, so the mean is 5.

starterQuiz.stem: The dot plot represents a set of data. The range for this data is {{ }} [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The range indicates how spread out the data points could be in a dataset by finding the difference between the highest and lowest value.
starterQuiz.feedback: The range is 8 because that is the difference between the highest and lowest values.

starterQuiz.stem: Select all of the measures that are types of averages.
starterQuiz.hint: Averages provide the central or typical value in a set of data in order to indicate where most of the data points are likely to be.
starterQuiz.feedback: The mean, median and mode are all averages. They indicate the central or typical value in a set of data

starterQuiz.stem: Two classes of pupils sit a test. The range of scores in Class A is 22; the range in scores for Class B is 35. Which conclusion is valid for this statistical summary?
starterQuiz.hint: The range indicates how spread out the data points could be in a data set by finding the difference between the highest and lowest value.
starterQuiz.feedback: The scores in Class A tended to be more consistent than the scores in Class B because they have a smaller range.

options.text: The scores in Class A tended to be higher than the scores in Class B.
The scores in Class A tended to be lower than the scores in Class B.
The scores in Class A tended to be more consistent than the scores in Class B.
The scores in Class A tended to be less consistent than the scores in Class B.

exitQuiz.stem: The central tendency of a dataset can be described by using an {{ }}, such as the mean, median or mode.
exitQuiz.hint: The mean, median and mode are all examples of this.
exitQuiz.feedback: The central tendency of a dataset can be described by using an average, such as the mean, median or mode.

exitQuiz.stem: The spread of a dataset can be described by using the {{ }}.
exitQuiz.hint: The spread of a dataset can be measured by finding the difference between the lowest and highest value.
exitQuiz.feedback: The spread of a dataset can be described by using the range.

exitQuiz.stem: The table shows summary statistics about how many points each person scored during a series of hockey games. The mode suggests that {{ }} tended to score the highest each game. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Look at the row for mode. Who has the highest mode?
exitQuiz.feedback: The mode suggests that Sofia tended to score the highest each game.

exitQuiz.stem: The table shows summary statistics about how many points each person scored during a series of hockey games. Which measure suggests that Jun tended to score the highest in each game? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Averages indicate the central or typical value in a set of data. For which measure does Jun have the highest average?
exitQuiz.feedback: The mean suggests that Jun tended to score the highest each game.

exitQuiz.stem: The table shows summary statistics about how many points each person scored during a series of hockey games. Which measure suggests that Aisha tends to score the highest in each game? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Averages indicate the central or typical value in a set of data. For which measure does Aisha have the highest average?
exitQuiz.feedback: The median suggests that Aisha tended to score the highest each game.

exitQuiz.stem: The table shows summary statistics about how many points each person scored during a series of hockey games. Whose scores tend to be the most consistent? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The range indicates how spread out the data could be for each person.
exitQuiz.feedback: Jun's scores tend to be most consistent because they have the smallest range.

units.title: Perimeter, area and volume
units.description: In this unit pupils extend their knowledge of shapes by exploring the properties of circles and composite shapes before developing understanding of 3-D shapes including surface area and volume.

lessons.title: Checking understanding of perimeter
lessons.outcome: I can find the perimeter of many polygons or compound shapes.
keyLearningPoints: The perimeter of any polygon can be found by summing the sides.
The perimeter of shapes made from polygons can be found.
Some methods for finding perimeters are more efficient than others.
Missing lengths can be found when the perimeter is known.

keywords.definition: the distance around a 2D shape
flat (2D), closed figure made up of straight line segments
a shape created using two or more basic shapes

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these units are a measure of length?
starterQuiz.hint: The base unit for metric units of length is metres.
starterQuiz.feedback: Both kilometres and millimetres are units of length. Other units of length include metres, centimetres, inches, feet, yards and miles.

starterQuiz.stem: The image shows a wall whose length has been measured in four parts. The total length of the wall is {{ }} m. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: How far would you travel in total if you started at one end of the wall and walked to the other end?
starterQuiz.feedback: The total length of the wall is 420 m.

starterQuiz.stem: Which length is equal to $$a$$? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Sides with the same dash markings have the same length.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$a = f$$ because their sides have the same dash markings.

starterQuiz.stem: A {{ }} shape is a shape created using two or more basic shapes.
starterQuiz.hint: An alternative term for this is a 'composite' shape.
starterQuiz.feedback: A compound shape is a shape created using two or more basic shapes.

starterQuiz.stem: Solve the equation: $$20 = 12 + a$$
starterQuiz.hint: What value, when added to 12, makes 20?

starterQuiz.stem: Solve the equation: $$2a + 8 = 18$$
starterQuiz.hint: Start by subtracting 8 from both sides of the equation.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$a = 5$$. This can be checked by calculating $$2 \times 5 + 8 = 18$$.

exitQuiz.stem: The {{ }} is the distance around a 2D shape.
exitQuiz.hint: You would calculate this by adding up the lengths of all the sides.
exitQuiz.feedback: The perimeter is the distance around a 2D shape.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the units could be used to measure perimeter?
exitQuiz.hint: Perimeter is a length.
exitQuiz.feedback: Perimeter could be measured in cm.

exitQuiz.stem: What is the perimeter of the rectangle? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Perimeter is the total distance around the edge of the shape.
exitQuiz.feedback: The distance around the edge of the rectangle is 14 m.

exitQuiz.stem: When $$a = 5$$ the perimeter of the octagon is {{ }} mm. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The perimeter of a regular polygon can be found by using multiplication.
exitQuiz.feedback: When $a = 5$ the perimeter of the octagon is 40 mm.

exitQuiz.stem: The perimeter of the hexagon is 24 cm. Find the value of $$a$$. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The markings on the sides of the hexagon mean that their lengths are all equal.
exitQuiz.feedback: Each length on the hexagon is 4 cm.

exitQuiz.stem: The perimeter of the compound rectilinear shape is {{ }} cm. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: All of the vertical lengths on the left side of the shape sum to the total height of the shape.
exitQuiz.feedback: The perimeter of the compound rectilinear shape is 180 cm.

lessons.title: Checking understanding of area
lessons.outcome: I can find the area of triangles, quadrilaterals and composite rectilinear shapes.
keyLearningPoints: The formula can be used to find the area of a triangle.
There can be more than one way to find the area of a trapezium.
The area of composite shapes can be found by splitting into shapes whose area can be found.

keywords.definition: The area is the size of the surface and states the number of unit squares needed to completely cover that surface.
A trapezium is a quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel opposite sides.
The plural of trapezium can be referred to as trapezia or trapeziums.
A composite rectilinear shape is a composite shape made from rectangles.

starterQuiz.stem: The {{ }} is the size of the surface and states the number of unit squares needed to completely cover that surface.
starterQuiz.hint: It can also be thought of as the amount of 2D space that is taken up by a shape.
starterQuiz.feedback: The area is the size of the surface and states the number of unit squares needed to completely cover that surface.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these units are a measure of area?
starterQuiz.hint: Area is measured is square units.
starterQuiz.feedback: Square units such as m$$^2$$ can be used to measure area.

starterQuiz.stem: The area of the rectangle is {{ }} m$$^2$$. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The area can be measured by counting the number of unit squares.
starterQuiz.feedback: The area of the rectangle is 12 m$$^2$$ because it is made of 12 unit squares.

starterQuiz.stem: Which line segments are perpendicular to each other? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Perpendicular lines or line segments are at right angles to each other.
starterQuiz.feedback: If you joined line segments A and B together, they would form a right angle. So they are perpendicular.

starterQuiz.stem: For which shape can the area be calculated by doing $${1}\over{2}$$ $$\times$$ base $$\times$$ perpendicular height?
starterQuiz.hint: A shape whose area can be calculated by doing base $$\times$$ height can be cut diagonally in half to make this shape.
starterQuiz.feedback: The area of a triangle can be calculated by doing $${1}\over{2}$$ $$\times$$ base $$\times$$ perpendicular height.

starterQuiz.stem: Select the rectangle with the largest area.
starterQuiz.hint: You can find the area of each rectangle by multiplying the length by the width.
starterQuiz.feedback: The areas of the rectangles are 12 cm$$^2$$, 18 cm$$^2$$ and 20 cm$$^2$$.

exitQuiz.stem: The area of the rectangle is {{ }} units$$^2$$. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The area of a rectangle can be calculated by multiplying the length by the width.
exitQuiz.feedback: The area of the rectangle is 30 units$$^2$$ as the product of 5 and 6 is 30.

exitQuiz.stem: The area of the parallelogram is {{ }} units$$^2$$. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The area of a parallelogram can be calculated by multiplying the base by the perpendicular height.
exitQuiz.feedback: The area of the parallelogram is 12 units$$^2$$ as 12 is the product of 3 and 4.

exitQuiz.stem: The area of the triangle is {{ }} units$$^2$$. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The area of a triangle can be calculated by doing $${1}\over{2}$$ $$\times$$ base $$\times$$ perpendicular height.
exitQuiz.feedback: The base and the perpendicular height are both 6.

exitQuiz.stem: A {{ }} is a quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel opposite sides.
exitQuiz.hint: Parallelograms have two pairs of parallel sides.
exitQuiz.feedback: Squares, rhombi and rectangles are all types of parallelograms. Therefore the only option left is trapezium.

exitQuiz.stem: The formula $$A=$$ $${1}\over{2}$$ $$\times (a + b) \times h$$ can be used to calculate area of a trapezium. Which calculation is correct for finding the area of the trapezium? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: In the formula, $$a$$ and $$b$$ are the parallel sides.
exitQuiz.feedback: This calculation finds half the sum of the parallel sides and then multiplies the result by the height.

exitQuiz.stem: This compound shape is made from a rectangle and a triangle. Its area is {{ }} units$$^2$$. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The height of the triangle is equal to the difference between the height of the whole shape and the height of the rectangle.
exitQuiz.feedback: The area of the rectangle is 50 units$$^2$$. The area of the triangle is 15 units$$^2$$. So the area of the compound shape is 65 units$$^2$$.

lessons.title: Multiplicative relationships in circles
lessons.outcome: I can recognise that there is a constant multiplicative relationship (π) between the diameter and circumference of a circle.
keyLearningPoints: There is a multiplicative relationship between the radius and diameter of a circle.
The ratio between the diameter and circumference of a circle is always the same.
That ratio is called π and it is an irrational number.
The formula for the circumference of a circle is C = πd.
Using the definition of the diameter you can also write this as C = 2πr.

keywords.definition: The diameter of a circle is any line segment that starts and ends on the edge of the circle and passes through the centre.
The radius of a circle is any line segment that joins the centre of a circle to its edge.
The circumference of a circle is the perimeter of the circle.

starterQuiz.stem: Round 50.26548246 to 1 decimal place.
starterQuiz.hint: Your answer should just have one digit after the decimal place. Use the next digit to decide whether it should round up or down.
starterQuiz.feedback: 50.26548246 is approximately 50.3 when rounded to 1 decimal place.

starterQuiz.stem: Round 3.14159265 to 3 significant figures.
starterQuiz.hint: Your answer should have just three digits.
starterQuiz.feedback: 3.14159265 is approximately 3.14 when rounded to 3 significant figures,

starterQuiz.stem: The perimeter of the parallelogram is {{ }} units. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Perimeter is the distance around the edge of the shape.
starterQuiz.feedback: The perimeter of the parallelogram is 16 units.

starterQuiz.stem: Select the rectangle with the largest perimeter.
starterQuiz.hint: The perimeter is the distance around the edge of the shape.
starterQuiz.feedback: The perimeters of the rectangles are 26 cm, 24 cm and 22 cm.

starterQuiz.stem: $$$a : b = 1 : 3$$. Find the value of $$b$$ when $$a = 6$$.
starterQuiz.hint: The value of $$b$$ is greater than the value of $$a$$.

starterQuiz.stem: $$$a : b = 1 : 3$$. Find the value of $$a$$ when $$b = 6$$.
starterQuiz.hint: The value of $$a$$ is less than the value of $$b$$.

exitQuiz.stem: Which part of the circle is labelled? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: It is a line segment that joins the centre of the circle to its edge.
exitQuiz.feedback: The radius is a line segment that joins the centre of the circle to its edge.

exitQuiz.stem: The {{}} of a circle is the perimeter of the circle.
exitQuiz.hint: It is the distance around the edge of the circle.
exitQuiz.feedback: The circumference of a circle is the perimeter of the circle.

exitQuiz.stem: If a circle has a radius of 12 cm then its diameter will be {{ }} cm.
exitQuiz.hint: The radius is a line segment that joins the centre of the circle to its edge. The diameter of a circle is any line segment that starts and ends on the edge of the circle and passes through the centre.
exitQuiz.feedback: The diameter will be 24 cm because it is double the radius.

exitQuiz.stem: Which symbol represents the ratio between the diameter and circumference of a circle?
exitQuiz.hint: The Greek letter for the ratio between the diameter and circumference is pronounced "pi".
exitQuiz.feedback: The symbol $$\pi$$ represents the ratio between the diameter and the circumference of a circle.

exitQuiz.stem: Which are the first three digits of $$\pi$$?
exitQuiz.hint: $$$\pi$$ is slightly greater than 3.
exitQuiz.feedback: The first three digits of $$\pi$$ are 3.14. However the number of digits in $$\pi$$ is infinite!

exitQuiz.stem: A circle with diameter 10 cm has a circumference of {{ }} cm.
exitQuiz.hint: The ratio between the diameter and the circumference of a circle is 1 : $$\pi$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: A circle with diameter 10 cm has a circumference of 10$$\pi$$ cm.

lessons.title: Circumference of a circle
lessons.outcome: I can use the relationship C=πd to calculate unknown lengths in contexts involving the circumference of circles.
keyLearningPoints: The formula can be used to find the circumference when you know the diameter.
The formula can be used to find the circumference when you know the radius.
The formula can be used to find the radius or diameter when you know the circumference.
These answers will be rounded to an appropriate degree of accuracy.
For the answer to be exact it needs to be left in terms of π.

keywords.definition: The circumference of a circle is the perimeter of the circle.
The radius of a circle is any line segment that joins the centre of a circle to its edge.
The diameter of a circle is any line segment that starts and ends on the edge of the circle and passes through the centre.

starterQuiz.stem: Which part of the circle is labelled? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: It is a line segment that starts and ends on the edge of the circle and passes through the centre.
starterQuiz.feedback: The diameter of a circle is any line segment that starts and ends on the edge of the circle and passes through the centre.

starterQuiz.stem: If a circle has a diameter of 12 cm then its radius will be {{ }} cm.
starterQuiz.hint: The radius is a line segment that joins the centre of the circle to its edge. The diameter of a circle is any line segment that starts and ends on the edge of the circle and passes through the centre.
starterQuiz.feedback: The radius will be 6 cm because it is half of the diameter.

starterQuiz.stem: $$$\pi$$ is the ratio between which two parts of a circle?
starterQuiz.hint: One of these parts is slightly more than three times the length of another part.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$\pi$$ is the ratio between the diameter and the circumference.

starterQuiz.stem: Which two formulae can be used to calculate the circumference of a circle?
starterQuiz.hint: The diameter is double the length of the radius.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$C = 2\pi d$$ and $$C = 2\pi r$$ both can be used to calculate the circumference because the diameter is double the length of the radius.

starterQuiz.stem: A circle with diameter 12 cm has a circumference of {{ }} cm.
starterQuiz.hint: The ratio between the diameter and the circumference of a circle is 1 : $$\pi$$.
starterQuiz.feedback: A circle with diameter 12 cm has a circumference of 12$$\pi$$ cm.

starterQuiz.stem: A circle with radius 20 cm has a circumference of {{ }} cm.
starterQuiz.hint: Either $$C = \pi d$$ and $$C = 2\pi r$$ both can be used to calculate the circumference because the diameter is double the length of the radius.
starterQuiz.feedback: A circle with radius 20 cm has a circumference of 40$$\pi$$ cm.

exitQuiz.stem: Which part of the circle is labelled? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: It is the distance around the edge of the circle.
exitQuiz.feedback: The circumference of a circle is the perimeter of the circle.

exitQuiz.stem: A circle with a diameter of 6 cm has a circumference of {{ }} cm, when rounded to 1 decimal place.
exitQuiz.hint: A formula to calculate circumference is $$C = \pi d$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: A circle with a diameter of 6 cm has a circumference of 18.8 cm, when rounded to 1 decimal place.

exitQuiz.stem: The circumference of the circle is {{ }} cm, when rounded to 3 significant figures. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The length given is equal to the radius of the circle.
exitQuiz.feedback: The circumference of the circle is 25.1 cm, when rounded to 3 significant figures.

exitQuiz.stem: Which calculation would find the radius of a circle with circumference 20 cm?
exitQuiz.hint: A formula to calculate circumference is $$C = 2 \pi r$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: The radius would be equal to $$20 \div 2\pi$$.

exitQuiz.stem: The circumference of a circle is 30 cm. The diameter of the circle is {{ }} cm, when rounded to 1 decimal place.
exitQuiz.hint: A formula to calculate circumference is $$C = \pi d$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: The diameter of the circle is 9.5 cm, when rounded to 1 decimal place.

exitQuiz.stem: Starting with the smallest, sort the circles in ascending order of size.
exitQuiz.hint: You could work out the circumference of each circle.
exitQuiz.feedback: The circumferences of the circles are 10 cm, 12.6 cm and 18.4 cm, when rounded to 1 decimal place.

lessons.title: Area of a circle
lessons.outcome: I can understand the derivation of the area of a circle.
keyLearningPoints: A circle can be cut into congruent sectors that are placed together to make a parallelogram.
The length of the parallelogram is half the circumference of the circle.
The height of the parallelogram is the radius of the circle.
The formula for the area of a circle can be derived from the area of this parallelogram.

keywords.definition: Area is the size of the surface and states the number of unit squares needed to completely cover that surface.
The radius of a circle is any line segment that joins the centre of a circle to its edge.
The diameter of a circle is any line segment that starts and ends on the edge of the circle and passes through the centre.

starterQuiz.stem: The {{ }} is any line segment that joins the centre of a circle to its edge.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the following formulae calculates the circumference of a circle, when the radius is known?
starterQuiz.hint: An alternative formula for circumference is $$C = \pi d$$, when the diameter is known.
starterQuiz.feedback: The circumference of a circle can be calculated by using the formula $$C = 2\pi r$$.

starterQuiz.stem: Which two calculations could be used to find the area of the parallelogram? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The area of a parallelogram can be found by multiplying the base by the perpendicular height.
starterQuiz.feedback: The area could be calculated using either $$a \times c$$ or $$b \times d$$, because each pair of lengths are perpendicular to each other.

starterQuiz.stem: The area of the shape is {{ }} m$$^2$$. [image]

starterQuiz.stem: Select the parallelogram with the smallest area.

exitQuiz.stem: Which is a correct formula for calculating the area of a circle?
exitQuiz.hint: Two of these formulae calculate the circumference rather than the area.

exitQuiz.stem: The area of the circle is equal to the area of the parallelogram. The circumference of the circle is 12$$\pi$$ cm. The base of the parallelogram is {{ }}. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The lengths of the longest pair of parallel sides sum to the circumference.
exitQuiz.feedback: The base of the parallelogram is 6$$\pi$$ cm because it is half of the circumference.

exitQuiz.stem: The area of the square is 10 cm. The area of the circle is {{ }}. [image]

exitQuiz.feedback: The area of the circle is $$10 times \pi$$, which is 10$$\pi$$ cm$$^2$$.

exitQuiz.stem: A circle has radius 6 cm. What is the area of the circle?

exitQuiz.stem: Which circle has an area of 9$$\pi$$ cm$$^2$$?

starterQuiz.stem: What is $${2\over3}$$ of 144 cm?
starterQuiz.hint: To find one third of 144, you divide by 3.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$${2\over3}$$ of 144 is 96. However, $${2\over3}$$ of 144 cm must include the units of cm; so the correct answer is 96 cm.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these formulae finds the area of a circle with radius $$r$$?
starterQuiz.hint: The area of a 2-dimensional shape will contain the multiplication of two variable lengths.
starterQuiz.feedback: The area of a circle can be found by multiplying the variable $$r$$ by the variable $$r$$, and then multiplied by the constant value of $$\pi$$.

starterQuiz.stem: Find the area of a circle with radius of 25 cm, giving your answer both in terms of $$\pi$$ and in decimal form, rounded to 1 decimal place.
starterQuiz.hint: To follow the correct order of operations, you must square the radius before multiplying by $$\pi$$.
starterQuiz.feedback: 25 squared is 625, and so the correct answer in terms of $$\pi$$ is 625$$\pi$$. When converted into decimal form, 1963.495... which when rounded to 1 decimal place is 1963.5

starterQuiz.stem: From its centre, this circle has been split up into 9 equally-sized sectors. How many degrees is the angle marked x?{{ }} [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Angles in a circle around its centre sum to 360°.
starterQuiz.feedback: 360° ÷ 9 = 40°. Each angle around the centre of the circle is 40°.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each statement to the correct value for a circle with a diameter of 80 units.
starterQuiz.hint: The diameter is twice the length of the radius.
starterQuiz.feedback: It is best to use the radius to find the area of a circle, but either the diameter or radius can be used to find its circumference.

exitQuiz.stem: A quarter-circular sector is cut out of a circle. The original circle had an area of 120$$\pi$$ cm². What is the area of the quarter-circle?
exitQuiz.hint: A quarter-circular sector has a quarter of the area of the full circle that the sector came from.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$ 120\pi \div 4 = 30\pi$$. So the area is $$30 \pi$$ cm², which is 94.25 cm² when written in decimal form, rounded to 2 decimal places.

exitQuiz.stem: A sector with a 60° angle is cut out of a circle. The original circle had an area of 3072 inches². The area of the sector is {{ }} square inches.
exitQuiz.hint: 360° divided by what number is 60°? How can the answer to this question be used to find the area of the sector?
exitQuiz.feedback: One sixth of the full circle was cut out, therefore 3072 inches² ÷ 6 = 512 inches²

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the following statements is true for this sector? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: This sector can be split up into three one-quarter circles.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$${3\over4}\times \pi \times 22^2 = 363\pi$$ cm²

The area of this sector is 16.5$$\pi$$ cm².
The area of this sector is 363$$\pi$$ cm².
The area of this sector is 484$$\pi$$ cm².

exitQuiz.stem: This composite shape is broken down into its component parts, made from circular sectors and quadrilaterals. Match each component part and composite shape to its area. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The radius of the semicircle is 1 cm, and the radius of the quarter-circle is 2 cm.
exitQuiz.feedback: The area of the quarter circle is $$\pi$$ cm², which is double the area of the semicircle. The full composite shape has a total area of (1.5$$\pi$$ + 4) cm².

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these shows the area (written in terms of $$\pi$$) of the shaded region of this composite shape composed of a circular sector and a square? [image]

exitQuiz.feedback: The semicircle has been removed from the square, and so the area of the semicircle should be subtracted from the area of the square: $$48 \times 48 -{1\over2}\times\pi\times r^2$$

exitQuiz.stem: What is the area (in cm²) of this composite shape, composed of only squares and circular sectors, rounded to the nearest integer? {{}}cm² [image]

exitQuiz.feedback: The four sectors that are component parts of this composite shape can be rearranged into a circle with radius of 8 cm. There are three squares, each with a side length of 8 cm. So the area is $$(3\times8^2+\pi \times8^2)$$ cm².

keywords.definition: An arc is part of a curve. When describing an arc of a circle, it is part of the circle's circumference.

starterQuiz.stem: What is $${1\over4}$$ of 76$$\pi$$ cm? Give your answer in decimal form and rounded to 2 decimal places. {{ }}
starterQuiz.hint: Calculating $${1\over4}$$ of something is the same as dividing that value by 4.
starterQuiz.feedback: 76$$\pi$$ ÷ 4 = 19$$\pi$$, which is 59.69 when written in decimal form and rounded to 2 decimal places. Because is written with the cm unit, your answer must include cm, too.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these units of measurement is appropriate for measuring the perimeter of something?
starterQuiz.hint: The perimeter is the distance around an object.
starterQuiz.feedback: Any distance can measured in cm or inches. However, inches² measures area, and mm³ measures volume. Degrees is an angle measure.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these formulae finds the circumference of a circle with radius $$r$$ and diameter $$d$$?
starterQuiz.hint: 2 lots of the radius is equal to the diameter.
starterQuiz.feedback: The circumference of a circle is equal to both $$2{\times} {\pi} {\times}r$$ and $${\pi} {\times}d$$. Either can be used, and sometimes using a specific one is easier, depending on the information about a circle that is given.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these describes the circumference of a circle with a diameter of 60 cm?
starterQuiz.hint: The circumference of a circle can be found by multiplying $$\pi$$ by the diameter of the circle.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$\pi\times d$$ means multiplying the diameter directly by $$\pi$$. In cases like this, there is no need to use the radius of 30 cm.

starterQuiz.stem: A circular hoop with a radius of 40 cm is cut into 12 equally-sized pieces. What is the length of one piece? Give your answer in cm, rounded to 1 decimal place. {{ }} cm
starterQuiz.hint: The circumference of the whole hoop can be found using $$2{\times} {\pi} {\times}r$$, or by first finding the diameter and then multiplying by $$\pi$$.
starterQuiz.feedback: The circumference of the whole hoop is 80$$\pi$$, and so the length of one of the 12 pieces can be found by 80$$\pi$$ ÷ 12.

starterQuiz.stem: Circle A has a radius of 49 cm. Circle B has a diameter of 1.33 metres. How much longer is the circumference of circle B than circle A? Give your answer in cm, rounded to the nearest integer.
starterQuiz.hint: To answer this question, one must first ensure all units of measure are the same. Is it possible to convert cm into metres, or vice versa?
starterQuiz.feedback: The circumference of circle A is 98$$\pi$$ cm and the circumference of circle B is 133$$\pi$$ cm.

exitQuiz.stem: A quarter-circular sector is cut out of a circle. The original circle had a perimeter of 60$$\pi$$ cm. What is the arc length of this sector?
exitQuiz.hint: An arc of a circle is a fraction of the circle's circumference, and therefore an arc length will only be a fraction of the circumference of that circle.
exitQuiz.feedback: The other two choices are not arc lengths, as they consider at least one radius on the sector (with each radius being 30 cm long).

exitQuiz.stem: A semicircular sector is cut out of a circle. The radius of the original circle is 31 cm, and its circumference is 194.8 cm (rounded to 1 decimal place). What is the perimeter of the sector?
exitQuiz.hint: The perimeter of a circular sector is the arc length plus the radius of the sector twice, once for each radius that bounds the angle of the sector.
exitQuiz.feedback: 97.4 + 62 cm is a representation of the perimeter that separates the arc length (97.4 cm) from the two radii (62 cm)

exitQuiz.stem: Calculate the perimeter of this sector, giving your answer in cm and rounding your answer to 1 decimal place. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The perimeter of a circular sector is the arc length plus the radius of the sector twice, once for each radius that bounds the angle of the sector.

exitQuiz.stem: This composite shape is composed of a circular sector and a square. Which of these statements are true about the perimeter of this composite shape that has been broken into component lengths. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The radius of the quarter-circular sector is 68 cm.
exitQuiz.feedback: On the perimeter of this composite shape, there are three of the four sides of the square, and one of the two radii of the sector. The arc length of this quarter-circular sector is 136$$\pi$$ cm ÷ 4 = 34$$\pi$$ cm.

options.text: There are three line segments of 68 cm.
There are four line segments of 68 cm.
There are five line segments of 68 cm.
The length of the arc is 68$$\pi$$ cm.
The length of the arc is 34$$\pi$$ cm.

exitQuiz.stem: This composite shape is composed of two quarter-circles and a rectangle. Match the statement about the component parts of the composite shape's perimeter to the correct value. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Each quarter circle has an arc length of $${1\over4}{\times}(2{\times}{\pi}{\times}8)$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: The line segment at the top has a length of 17 cm, and the line segment at the bottom has a length of $$a$$ + $$r$$ cm = 9 + 8 cm, where $$r$$ is the radius of the quarter circle.

exitQuiz.stem: The square at the centre of this composite shape has an area of 441 cm². Find the perimeter of the composite shape in cm, rounded to the nearest integer. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The four quarter-circles can be rearranged into a circle.
exitQuiz.feedback: The four quarter-circles can be rearranged into a circle with radius of 21 cm. The circumference of this circle is 42$$\pi$$ cm. There are also four line segments, each with length 21 cm.

starterQuiz.stem: Find the positive value of $$x$$ that is a solution to the equation: $$x^2 + 4 = 85$$. $$x=$${{}}.
starterQuiz.hint: The first operation is to subtract 4 from both sides of the equation.
starterQuiz.feedback: If $$x^2 = 81$$, and the positive square root of 81 is 9, then $$x = 9$$

starterQuiz.stem: Select the fully factorised form of this expression: $$42r + 56$$.
starterQuiz.hint: The highest common factor of 42 and 56 is 14.
starterQuiz.feedback: Both $$2(21r+28)$$ and $$7(6r+8)$$ are factorised, however $$14(3r+4)$$ is the most factorised form of $$42r + 56$$

starterQuiz.stem: Find the positive value of $$x$$ that is a solution to the equation: $$3{\times}7{\times}2x^2 = 3{\times}56$$. $$x=$${{}}
starterQuiz.hint: Dividing both sides by 3 will remove one factor of the expression on both the left-hand side and right-hand side of the equation.
starterQuiz.feedback: Dividing both sides by 3  gives: $$7{\times}2x^2 = 56$$. You can then divide both sides by 7 to give: $$2x^2 = 8$$. Dividing both sides by 2 gives: $$x^2 = 4$$, where $$x = 2$$ is the positive solution.

starterQuiz.stem: Select the fully factorised form of this expression: $$2kx^2 + 3kx$$.
starterQuiz.hint: Factors of terms can be both numerical and algebraic.
starterQuiz.feedback: Both $$x$$ and $$k$$ are factors of each term in this expression. When factorised out, it does not matter which order each factor is represented outside the brackets but it is usual to write it in alphabetical order.

starterQuiz.stem: A circle has a radius of 1.2 cm. Find the area of this circle. Give your answer in cm, rounded to 2 decimal places. Area = {{ }} cm².
starterQuiz.hint: The area of a circle is $${\pi} {\times}r^2$$, where $$r$$ is the radius of the circle.
starterQuiz.feedback: The area of this circle can be found by: $${\pi} {\times}1.2^2 = 1.44{\pi}$$

starterQuiz.stem: The area of a circle is 908 cm². Use the formula: $$area = {\pi} {\times}r^2$$ to form an equation and solve this equation to find the radius of the circle, rounded to the nearest integer. {{ }} cm.
starterQuiz.hint: By substituting 908 into the area formula, you can solve the equation: $$908 = {\pi} {\times}r^2$$
starterQuiz.feedback: By dividing both sides of $$908 = {\pi} {\times}r^2$$ by $$\pi$$, you will get $$r^2 = 289.03$$. Square rooting 289.03 will give a value which rounds to 17.

exitQuiz.stem: A quarter-circular sector is cut out of a circle. The quarter-circle has an area of 32$$\pi$$ cm². What was the area of the original circle?
exitQuiz.hint: If one quarter of a full circle has an area of 32$$\pi$$ cm², then four lots of 32$$\pi$$ cm² represents the area of the full circle.
exitQuiz.feedback: 4 × 32$$\pi$$ cm² = 128$$\pi$$ cm², which is 402.12 cm² when converted into decimal form and rounded to 2 decimal places.

exitQuiz.stem: A semi-circular sector is cut out of a circle. The semicircle has an area of 98$$\pi$$ cm². Which of these statements are true about the original circle?
exitQuiz.hint: If one half of a full circle has an area of 98$$\pi$$ cm², then two lots of 98$$\pi$$ cm² represents the area of the full circle.
exitQuiz.feedback: 2 × 98$$\pi$$ cm² = 196$$\pi$$ cm². The square root of 196 is 14, which is the radius of the circle.

options.text: The original circle has an area of 49$$\pi$$ cm².

exitQuiz.stem: This composite shape is composed of a quarter-circle and a square. The area of the composite shape is 114 cm². Which of these statements about the shape are correct? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The radius of the quarter-circle is equal in length of all sides of the square.
exitQuiz.feedback: If the radius of the quarter-circle is $$r$$, then the length of a side of the square is also $$r$$. The area of the square is therefore $$r^2$$, and the area of the quarter-circle is $${1\over4}{\times}{\pi}{\times}r^2$$.

options.text: Area of the whole shape is $${1\over4}{\times}{\pi}{\times}r^2 + r^2$$
Area of the whole shape is $${1\over4}{\times}{\pi}{\times}r+ r $$

exitQuiz.stem: This composite shape is composed of a quarter-circle and a square. The area of the composite shape is 216 cm². Which of these equations are correct steps in the method to find the radius? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: When factorising to solve the equation, you must fully factorise the algebraic representation of the area. This means factorising $$r^2$$ out of the left-hand expression.
exitQuiz.feedback: Once $$r^2$$ has been factorised, the value of $${{1\over4}{\times}{\pi}+1}$$ left in the brackets is just a number that you can type into the calculator to approximate the value of.

exitQuiz.stem: The area of this composite shape is: ($$9216\pi + 16384$$) cm². Find the value of $$r$$. $$r=$${{}}. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The area of the square component part can be represented algebraically as $$r^2$$, and represented numerically by the non-$$\pi$$ term of $$9216\pi + 16384$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: The value of $$r$$ can be found by solving the following equation: $$r^2 = 16384$$. Square-rooting gives $$r=128$$.

exitQuiz.stem: This composite shape is composed of two quarter-circles and a square. The area of this composite shape is 1360 cm². Find the value of $$r$$, rounded to the nearest integer. $$r=$$ {{}} [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The fully factorised form of the algebraic representation of this composite shape is: $$r^2\left( {{1\over2}{\times}{\pi}+1}\right)$$
exitQuiz.feedback: This equation that equates the algebraic and numeric representations of the area of composite shape can be solved: $$r^2\left( {{1\over2}{\times}{\pi}+1}\right) = 1360$$.
