exitQuiz.stem: Each of these compound shapes are different arrangements of six congruent squares. Which of the compound shapes are nets of a cube? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Arrangements of six cubes that only have two or fewer rows or columns can never fold up into a cube.
exitQuiz.feedback: Arrangements a, b, and e are all arrangements of a cube that have four squares distributed horizontally in a line, with one square abov, and one square below that line of four.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these compound shapes are nets of a cuboid? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: A cuboid has exactly six faces, and so the net of a cuboid must contain exactly six rectangles.
exitQuiz.feedback: Composite shape $$a$$ cannot be a cuboid, as the bottom rectangle is adjacent to the rectangle above it in a way that the two touches edges are not of the same length. Composite shape $$c$$ cannot be a cuboid, as it only has five rectangles in it.

exitQuiz.stem: This diagram shows six rectangles that can be connected together to create the net of a cuboid. Match each rectangles to its area. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Rectangle $$a$$ has a base length of 5 cm labelled directly below it. Its height is the value on the far right of the image.
exitQuiz.feedback: The remaining three rectangles in this diagram will also have the areas of 10 cm², 16 cm² and 40 cm², as a cuboid has three pairs of congruent faces.

exitQuiz.stem: This is the net of a cuboid. The surface area of the cuboid after this net is folded up is {{}} cm². [image]
exitQuiz.hint: What are the areas of the other three rectangles in this net?
exitQuiz.feedback: The area of the three labelled rectangles totals 29 cm². The other three rectangles must have an area that also totals 29 cm². Therefore, the total surface area of the cuboid is double 29 cm².

exitQuiz.stem: Some of the calculations to find the surface area of this cuboid are given. The value of $$b$$ is greater than the value of $$c$$. Match each missing length or area to its value.  [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The three visible faces are the top, right, and front faces. The total surface area of this cuboid is double the area of these three visible faces.
exitQuiz.feedback: This is an efficient method to find the total surface area of a cuboid - calculate the area of the three visible faces, add the areas of the three faces together, and then double the result to account for the three faces that cannot be seen.

exitQuiz.stem: A cuboid has been drawn on isometric paper, where each unit of isometric paper represents 1 inch. The total surface area of this cuboid is {{}} square inches. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Because the front face is a square, the left, right, top, and bottom faces are all congruent to each other.
exitQuiz.feedback: The front face is 9 inches², and the right and top faces are each 18 inches². The visible faces have a total area of 45 inches².

lessons.title: Properties of prisms
lessons.outcome: I can appreciate that all prisms have two congruent polygonal parallel faces (bases) with parallelogram faces joining the corresponding vertices of the bases.
keyLearningPoints: Prisms are 3D shapes with a cross-section that is a uniform polygon.
All prisms will have a pair of parallel faces that are congruent.
This polygon cross section is often used to name the prism.
The sides connecting the bases are parallelograms.

keywords.definition: A prism is a polyhedron with a base that is a polygon and a parallel opposite face that is identical.
A cross section is a 2D face made from cutting straight through any plane of a 3D object.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these polygons has exactly six sides?
starterQuiz.hint: The word polygon is the name for any 2D closed shape made from only straight line segments. It can have any number of sides greater than or equal to three.
starterQuiz.feedback: The word "hexagon" comes from "hexa" = six, and "gonia" = angles. A strategy to remember that a hexagon has six sides is that both six and hexagon both have the letter x in them.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each polygon to the number of sides it has.
starterQuiz.hint: A parallelogram is a type of quadrilateral. What number does the word "quad" mean?
starterQuiz.feedback: A pentadecagon can be broken down into "penta" = 5, "deca" = 10, and "gonia" = angles. Therefore, a pentadecagon has 5 + 10 = 15 angles, and therefore 15 sides.

starterQuiz.stem: This is a triangular-based pyramid. This 3D shape has 4 vertices and 6 edges. It has {{}} faces. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: All the faces of this triangular-based pyramid are triangles.
starterQuiz.feedback: This triangular-based pyramid has four triangular faces.

starterQuiz.stem: This is a triangular prism. Match the property of this object to its value. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: All the faces of this triangular prism are either triangles or parallelograms.
starterQuiz.feedback: This triangular prism has 9 edges: the 3 sides of the triangle at the top, another 3 sides on the triangle at the bottom, and then three edges that are adjacent to the three rectangles.

starterQuiz.stem: The front face of this cuboid is parallel to which other face? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Which face is on the opposite side of the cuboid to the front face?
starterQuiz.feedback: In a cuboid, a face is always parallel to the congruent face directly opposite it.

starterQuiz.stem: The front and right faces of this cuboid have equal area. Which faces of this cuboid are congruent to the front face? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Two faces are congruent if one face can fit exactly on top of a different face after a rotation, reflection, or translation.
starterQuiz.feedback: If two faces on a cuboid have the same area, then they are congruent - and the faces opposite to these two faces are also congruent to them. In this cuboid, there is a group of four congruent rectangles, and a separate pair of congruent rectangles.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these 3D shapes are prisms? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: A prism must have a polygonal base, and a circle is not a prism.
exitQuiz.feedback: Shape b is a quadrilateral-based pyramid, and c is a cylinder, which is not a prism.

exitQuiz.stem: This 3D shape is a prism. The base face and cross-section shown were used to help identify this shape as a prism. Which of these statements must be true? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The base face and cross-section are both pentagons. Can a parallelogram be a pentagon?
exitQuiz.feedback: Any cross-section taken parallel to the base of a prism must be congruent to the base.

options.text: The base face and cross-section must be parallel to each other.
The base face and cross-section must be perpendicular to each other.
The base face and cross-section must be congruent to each other.
The base face and cross-section must be equidistant to each other.
The base face and cross-section must both be parallelograms.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these names are appropriate for this prism? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The polygonal base of this prism is a hexagon with sides of different lengths.
exitQuiz.feedback: The polygonal base is an (irregular) hexagon. This is a right prism, as the parallelograms adjacent to the base are rectangles.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these words can used as part of the name of this prism? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The prism looks very slanted. There are hash marks shown on one of the base faces of the prism.
exitQuiz.feedback: The prism is very slanted so it is not right. The hash marks show the trapezium is isosceles. So this is an "oblique isosceles-trapezium prism".

exitQuiz.stem: Alex says: "This prism is a rectangular prism, because this face is a rectangle". Which of these statements is correct? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Cross-sections taken parallel to the base have to be congruent, not just the same shape.
exitQuiz.feedback: Alex is incorrect, as the base face is the right angled triangle. Alex may not even be correct about the fact this is a rectangle; it could be a general parallelogram, meaning the prism is oblique, not right.

options.text: Alex is correct because parallel cross-sections to this face are all rectangles.
Alex is incorrect because this is not the face that is the cross-sectional base.
This prism is a right angled triangular prism.
This prism is definitely a right prism because there is a right angle.

exitQuiz.stem: Match each property of an octagonal prism to its value.
exitQuiz.hint: There are two base faces, one at each end of the prism. The shape of the base face is reflected in how the prism is named.
exitQuiz.feedback: For a prism with a polygonal base of $$n$$ sides, there there $$2n$$ vertices, $$3n$$ edges, and $$(n + 2)$$ faces.

lessons.title: Surface area of prisms
lessons.outcome: I can find the surface area of 3D shapes in an efficient way.
keyLearningPoints: The surface area of a 3D shape is the sum of the area of all the faces.
The net of a prism can help find the surface area of a prism but can be time consuming.
By using known area facts, the area of all the faces can be found and summed.
It is important to find the surface area systematically and efficiently.

keywords.definition: polyhedron with base and identical parallel opposite side with corresponding edges joined by parallelograms.
Faces are the flat 2D surfaces of a 3D shape.
The net of a 3D object is a 2D representation of its faces that can be folded up into the 3D object.
The surface area is the total area of all the surfaces of a closed 3D shape. The surfaces include all faces and any curved surfaces.

starterQuiz.stem: The area of a rectangle with a width of 7 cm and a length of 12 m is {{ }}m².
starterQuiz.hint: Multiply the length by the width.
starterQuiz.feedback: Multiplication is commutative, so you could have multiplied the length by the width, or the width by the length and the answer will still be the same.

starterQuiz.stem: The area of a triangle with a base length of 14 cm and a perpendicular height of 8 cm is {{ }} cm².
starterQuiz.hint: $$${\text {Area}}={{1}\over{2}} \times {\text {base}} \times {\text {perpendicular height}}$$
starterQuiz.feedback: The area of a triangle is half the area of a parallelogram with the same base length and perpendicular height.

starterQuiz.stem: The area of a trapezium is being calculated $${\text {Area}}={{1}\over{2}} \times {(6+16)} \times {12} = 132  \text{ cm}^2$$. What is the perpendicular height of this trapezium?
starterQuiz.hint: In the formula for the area of a trapezium you sum the two parallel sides.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$${\text {Area}}={{{1}\over{2}} \times {(6+16)} \times {12}}={{{1}\over{2}} \times {6} \times {12}} + {{1}\over{2}} \times {16} \times {12} = 132  \text{ cm}^2$$ shows that the area can be found by summing the area of two triangles together.

starterQuiz.stem: A prism is a polyhedron with a base that is a {{ }} and a parallel opposite face that is identical. The corresponding edges of the two polygons are joined by parallelograms.
starterQuiz.hint: A flat (2D), closed figure made up of straight line segments.
starterQuiz.feedback: If the prism is a right prism, then the two polygons are joined by rectangles.

starterQuiz.stem: The perimeter of this shape is{{ }} cm. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Work out the missing edge lengths, before adding them to all together.
starterQuiz.feedback: This shape is an irregular hexagon but it is also a composite rectilinear shape.

starterQuiz.stem: Match the shape of the base with the name of the prism.
starterQuiz.hint: A prism with a hexagonal base is called a hexagonal prism.
starterQuiz.feedback: Cuboids can have a square base, however a cube has to have a square base.

exitQuiz.stem: The surface area is the {{ }} area of all the surfaces of a closed 3D shape. The surfaces include all faces and any curved surfaces.
exitQuiz.hint: To find the surface area you add all the faces and curved surfaces together.
exitQuiz.feedback: In many real-life contexts, the 3D shape may not be closed, so you need to consider carefully which surfaces are included.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these are nets for a cube?
exitQuiz.hint: A cube has six square faces.
exitQuiz.feedback: There are, in fact, 11 unique nets for a cube.

exitQuiz.stem: Here is a right prism. Which of these descriptions is correct? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The base is a quadrilateral with at least one pair of parallel sides.
exitQuiz.feedback: As the trapezium is an isosceles trapezium, two of the rectangles will have the same dimensions.

options.text: The prism has 6 different shaped faces.
The prism has 6 faces, two are parallelograms and four are rectangles.
The prism has 6 faces, two are trapeziums and four are rectangles.
The prism has 6 faces, two are isosceles triangles and four are rectangles.

exitQuiz.stem: The areas of the faces of a triangular prism are $$24\text{ cm}^2,24\text{ cm}^2,50\text{ cm}^2, 40\text{ cm}^2\text{ and }30\text{ cm}^2$$ respectively. The surface area is {{ }} $$\text{ cm}^2$$.
exitQuiz.hint: Find the total of all the areas.
exitQuiz.feedback: The surface area is the total area of all the faces. 24 cm² + 24 cm² + 50 cm² + 40 cm² + 30 cm² = 168 cm²

exitQuiz.stem: The surface area of this right-angled isosceles triangular prism is {{ }} $$\text{ cm}^2$$. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: To find the area of the triangles, make sure you are using the perpendicular lengths.
exitQuiz.feedback: Area of triangular faces = $$2 \times \frac{1}{2} \times 7 \times 7 = 49 \text{cm}^2$$. Area of base and side faces = $$2 \times 7 \times 8 = 112 \text{cm}^2$$. Area of slanting face = $$8\times9.9 =79.2 \text{cm}^2$$. Find the total of these areas.

exitQuiz.stem: In a right prism, the rectangular faces can be seen as one large rectangle. The dimensions of the large rectangle are the {{ }} of the base by the length of the prism. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Each of the rectangles would be along each edge of the base face.
exitQuiz.feedback: This is a really efficient way to find the surface area of a prism, just be careful not to add the areas of the bases as well.

lessons.title: Surface area of cylinders
lessons.outcome: I can find the surface area of cylinders.
keyLearningPoints: Drawing the net of a cylinder helps deduce the formula for the surface area.
The formula can be used to find the surface area of any cylinder.
Unknown lengths can be found when the surface area is known.

keywords.definition: a 3D shape with a base that is a circle and a parallel opposite face that is identical. Cross sections parallel to the base are uniform.

starterQuiz.stem: The area of a rectangle with a width of 6 cm and a length of 14 cm is {{ }} $$\text{ cm}^2$$.
starterQuiz.hint: To find the area of a rectangle you multiply the width and the length together.
starterQuiz.feedback: 6 cm × 14 cm = 84 cm²

starterQuiz.stem: What is the area of a circle, with a radius of 5 cm?
starterQuiz.hint: The formula for the area of a circle is $$\pi r^2$$, where $$r$$ is the radius of the circle.
starterQuiz.feedback: Make sure you square the radius and then multiply the result by $$\pi$$. $$\pi \times 5^2 = 25\pi$$.

starterQuiz.stem: The area of a circle with a diameter of 16 cm, has an area of {{ }} $$\pi \text{ cm}^2$$.
starterQuiz.hint: The formula for the area of a circle, requires the radius. The diameter is twice the length of the radius.
starterQuiz.feedback: The radius is 8 cm, so the area is $$8^2 \times \pi$$. $$64\pi$$ is approximately 201 $$\text{ cm}^2$$.

starterQuiz.stem: The surface area is the total area of all the surfaces of a closed {{  }} shape. The surfaces include all faces and any curved surfaces.
starterQuiz.hint: Cubes, spheres, triangular prisms and cones are all examples of these type of shapes.
starterQuiz.feedback: Cones and spheres are examples of 3D shapes that have curved surfaces.

starterQuiz.stem: A cuboid has dimensions 4 cm, 6 cm and 15 cm. Select all the areas of its surfaces.
starterQuiz.hint: A cuboid has rectangular faces. One of the rectangles will has an area of 6 cm × 4 cm
starterQuiz.feedback: Find the area of each rectangular face. 6 cm × 4 cm = 24 cm²;  4 cm × 15 cm = 60 cm²; 6 cm × 15 cm = 90 cm².

starterQuiz.stem: A cube has a surface area of 294 $$\text{ cm}^2$$. The area of each face is {{ }} $$\text{ cm}^2$$.
starterQuiz.hint: A cube has six identical faces. The surface area is therefore 6 lots of the area of each face.
starterQuiz.feedback: There are 6 faces. So the area of one face is 294 cm² ÷ 6 = 49 cm².

exitQuiz.stem: A cylinder is a type of prism. True or false?
exitQuiz.hint: A circle is not a polygon, as it doesn't have straight edges.
exitQuiz.feedback: The structure of prisms and cylinders are very similar, but technically a cylinder is not a prism.

options.text: True - it has a uniform cross-section throughout the length.
False - the uniform cross-section is not a polygon.

exitQuiz.stem: A {{ }} is a 3D shape with a base that is a circle and a parallel opposite face that is identical. A cross-section of a cylinder made parallel to the base is congruent to the base.
exitQuiz.hint: Try drawing a 3D shape with a circular base and face that is opposite it that is identical.
exitQuiz.feedback: Cylinders can be oblique, however most of the time when we are speaking about cylinders, they are right prisms.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these is a net of a cylinder?
exitQuiz.hint: The length of the rectangle is the circumference of the circle.
exitQuiz.feedback: The circles must be congruent and on opposite sides of the rectangle. In practice it would be very difficult to make a net of a cylinder as the circles would be only touching the edge of the rectangle at one particular point.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these is the formula for the surface area of any cylinder, where $$r$$ is the radius and $$h$$ is the height?
exitQuiz.hint: The surface area of a cylinder is the sum of the two circle's areas and the curved surface which is a rectangle with dimensions of the circumference of the circle and the height of the cylinder.
exitQuiz.feedback: The surface area is $$\text{Surface area}=2\pi r^2+2\pi rh$$ as the curved surface unfolds to be a rectangle with dimensions: circumference of the circle by the height of the cylinder. You can factorise this to find another formula.

exitQuiz.stem: The surface area of a cylinder with a diameter of 10 cm and a height of 7 cm is {{ }}$$\pi \text{ cm}^2.$$
exitQuiz.hint: You have been told the diameter of the cylinder, whereas the radius is needed for the area of a circle.
exitQuiz.feedback: Radius of circular end face = 5 cm. So the surface area = $$2\pi \times 5^2+2\pi \times 5 \times 7$$

exitQuiz.stem: A cylinder has a surface area of $$72\pi \text{ cm}^2$$ and a radius of 3 cm. What is the length of the cylinder?
exitQuiz.hint: Subtract the area of the two circular faces from the surface area first. This will then give you the area of the curved face which has the dimensions: circumference of the circle by the height of the cylinder.
exitQuiz.feedback: Area of circular end faces = $$2 \times \pi \times 3^2=18$$ cm². So, area of curved face = $$72 \pi - 18 \pi = 54 \pi$$ cm². Area of curved face = $$2 \times \pi \times 3 \times h = 54 \pi$$. So, $$h = 9$$

lessons.title: Volume of prisms
lessons.outcome: I can use the constant cross-sectional area property of prisms to determine their volume.
keyLearningPoints: The shape and area of the base of a prism can be found.
The area of the cross-section multiplied by the length gives the volume of the prism.
This can be used to find the volume of any prism.
Unknown lengths can be found when the volume of a prism is known.

keywords.definition: a 2D face made from cutting straight through any plane of a 3D object.
the amount of space occupied by a closed 3D shape.

starterQuiz.stem: The area of a triangle with a base length of 12 cm and a perpendicular height of 7 cm is {{ }} $$\text{ cm}^2$$.
starterQuiz.hint: The area of any triangle is found by multiplying the base by the perpendicular height and then dividing by two.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these calculations, will correctly work out the area of this composite rectilinear shape? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: You can split the shape into two rectangles and sum the areas or surround the shape and subtract the extra area.
starterQuiz.feedback: Splitting this composite shape into two rectangles vertically was the most efficient as you had the dimensions for both rectangles on the diagram.

starterQuiz.stem: A prism is a polyhedron with a base that is a polygon and a parallel opposite face that is identical. The {{ }} edges of the two polygons are joined by parallelograms.
starterQuiz.hint: The edges that are in the same position on both of the polygons.
starterQuiz.feedback: The edges that are the same position on both of the polygons are called corresponding edges.

starterQuiz.stem: Select all the units of area.
starterQuiz.hint: A hectare is a unit of area equivalent to 10 000 square metres.
starterQuiz.feedback: The units of area are square units, as two perpendicular lengths have been multiplied together within an area calculation.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these equations has a solution of $$x=4$$?
starterQuiz.hint: Substitute $$x=4$$ into each equation and see if it holds true.
starterQuiz.feedback: 7 × 4 + 5 ≠ 19 and 12 × 4 − 19 ≠ 17, so $$ x = 4$$ is not a solution of $$7x+5=19$$ and $$12x-19=17$$. All the other equations are true when $$x=4$$.

starterQuiz.stem: Starting with first line, put the lines of working in the correct order to solve an equation.
starterQuiz.hint: The solution $$x=2$$ will be the final stage.
starterQuiz.feedback: The first stage will be the most complicated looking equation which is $$7x+6=20$$. The solution $$x=2$$ is the final stage.

exitQuiz.stem: {{ }} is the amount of space occupied by a closed 3D shape.
exitQuiz.hint: $$$\text{cm}^3$$ is an example of a unit for this.
exitQuiz.feedback: Volume and capacity are closely linked measures. Only hollow objects have capacity.

exitQuiz.stem: All units for volume are {{ }} units, such as cm³ or feet³.
exitQuiz.hint: What do you call the numbers that equal $$1^3$$, $$2^3$$ and $$3^3$$?
exitQuiz.feedback: Volume is calculated by multiply three perpendicular lengths together at some point of the calculation, so the units are cubed.

exitQuiz.stem: The volume of a cuboid with dimensions 8 cm by 9 cm by 15 cm is {{ }} $$\text{ cm}^3$$.
exitQuiz.hint: Multiply the three dimensions together.
exitQuiz.feedback: This works as the cross-section of a cuboid is a rectangle, so it is length × width and then multiply by the height of the cuboid.  8 cm × 9 cm × 15 cm = 1080 cm³.

exitQuiz.stem: Select the triangular prism with the volume of 1800 cm³.
exitQuiz.hint: To find the volume, find the area of the cross-section, which in this case is the triangle and then multiply by the length of the prism.
exitQuiz.feedback: Volume of a triangular prism = $$ \frac {1}{2}$$ base × height. So volume = $$\frac{1}{2}$$ 25 × 8 × 18 = 1800 cm³.

exitQuiz.stem: An L-shaped prism has a volume of 250 m³. It also has a length of 12.5 m. The area of the 'L-shape' is {{ }} m².
exitQuiz.hint: The volume would have been calculated by multiplying the length by the area of the 'L-shape', so use division to calculate the area.
exitQuiz.feedback: Volume = area of cross-section × length. So, 250 = area of L-shape × 12.5, so area of L-shape = 250 ÷ 12.5

exitQuiz.stem: The volume of this triangular prism is 2100 cm³. The length marked $$x$$ is {{ }} cm.  [image]
exitQuiz.hint: By dividing the volume by 20 (the length) you then know what the area of the triangle (the cross-section) is.
exitQuiz.feedback: Solve this equation: $$(\frac{1}{2}\times15\times x)\times20=2100$$. So, $$150 x=2100$$ which gives $$x=14$$

lessons.title: Volume of cylinders
lessons.outcome: I can use the constant cross-sectional area property of cylinders to determine their volume.
keyLearningPoints: A cylinder is not a prism but has a similar structure.
The formula for the volume of a cylinder can be derived by using the formula for a prism.
This can be used to find the volume of any cylinder.
Unknown lengths can be found when the volume of a cylinder is known.

keywords.definition: a polyhedron with a base that is a polygon and a parallel opposite face that is identical joined by parallelograms.
any line segment that joins the centre of a circle to its circumference.
3D shape with a base that is a circle and a parallel opposite face that is identical and uniform cross-section.

starterQuiz.stem: The area of a circle with radius 6 cm is {{ }} $$\pi\text{ cm}^2$$.
starterQuiz.hint: The formula for the area of a circle is $$\pi r^2$$.
starterQuiz.feedback: Remember to square the radius and then multiply by $$\pi$$. Area of circle is $$\pi \times 6^2 = 36 \pi$$.

starterQuiz.stem: A circle has an area of $$49\pi \text{ cm}^2$$. Which of the following statements about the circle are true?
starterQuiz.hint: To work out the circumference of a circle, you can multiply $$\pi$$ by the diameter or two times the radius.
starterQuiz.feedback: Since $$\pi r^2=49 \pi$$ then $$r^2 = 49$$ which means  $$r =7$$. The circumference is $$2 \times \pi \times 7 = 14 \pi$$ cm.

options.text: The radius (in centimetres) is the square root of 49.

starterQuiz.stem: A cuboid with a width of 3 m, a length of 8 m and a height of 6 m has a volume of {{ }} cm³.
starterQuiz.hint: The volume of a cuboid is the product of the three lengths.
starterQuiz.feedback: Volume of cuboid = 3 m × 8 m × 6 m = 144 m³.

starterQuiz.stem: A cylinder is a 3D shape with a base that is a {{ }} and a parallel opposite face that is identical. A cross-section of a cylinder made parallel to the base will be congruent to the base.
starterQuiz.hint: If you were to cut through a cylinder, parallel to the ends, what shape would you see?
starterQuiz.feedback: A cylinder is not a polyhedron as it does not have polygonal faces.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these triangular prisms has a volume of 2250 cm³?
starterQuiz.hint: To find the volume: multiply the area of the cross-section by the length of the prism.
starterQuiz.feedback: Volume of a triangular prism = $$ \frac {1}{2}$$ base × height. So volume = $$\frac{1}{2}$$ 18 × 10 × 25 = 2250 cm³.

starterQuiz.stem: A cuboid has a volume of 90 cm³. Its length is 5 cm. What could the dimensions of the cross-section be?
starterQuiz.hint: The cross-section needs to have an area of volume ÷ length.
starterQuiz.feedback: Volume = area of cross-section × length. So, area of cross-section = 90 ÷ 5 = 18 cm². The cross-section is a rectangle, so you need pairs of lengths that multiply to give 18 cm².

exitQuiz.stem: Volume is the amount of space occupied by a closed {{ }} shape.
exitQuiz.hint: Spheres, cylinders, cubes and pyramids are all shapes which have a volume.
exitQuiz.feedback: Some units for volume are $$\text{cm}^3$$ or $$\text{m}^3$$ or $$\text{inch}^3$$

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the following is the formula for the volume of a cylinder, where $$r$$ is the radius and $$h$$ is the height?
exitQuiz.hint: A cylinder has a similar structure to a prism.
exitQuiz.feedback: Volume of a cylinder is the area of the circle multiplied by the height = $$\pi r^2 h$$

exitQuiz.stem: A cylinder with a radius of 6 cm and a height of 10 cm, has a volume of {{ }} $$\pi \text{ cm}^3$$.
exitQuiz.hint: The formula for the volume of a cylinder is $$\pi r^2h$$, where $$r$$ is the radius and $$h$$ is the height.
exitQuiz.feedback: Volume of a cylinder is the area of the circle multiplied by the height = $$\pi r^2 h =\pi 6^2 \times 10 = 360 \pi$$

exitQuiz.stem: If the radius of a cylinder was to stay the same but the height was to change, what would happen to the volume?
exitQuiz.hint: How could the height change? What would happen to the volume in each case?
exitQuiz.feedback: The volume is dependent on both the radius and the height. If the radius stays the same and the height increases then the volume will also increase. However, the question only says 'change' so you can't tell if the volume will increase or decrease.

exitQuiz.stem: A cylinder has a radius of 9 cm and a volume of $$810\pi\text{ cm}^3$$. What is the length of the cylinder?
exitQuiz.hint: Divide the volume by the area of the circular base to find the length.
exitQuiz.feedback: Volume = area of base × length. Area of base = $$\pi \times 9^2 = 81\pi\text{ cm}^2$$, so length = $$810\pi \div 81 \pi$$

exitQuiz.stem: If you know the volume of a cylinder and its length, what other information can you work out?
exitQuiz.hint: When you divide the volume by the length, you are left with the area of the cross-section, which is a circle.
exitQuiz.feedback: If you know the radius of the circular face, then you also know the diameter and circumference of the circular face.

options.text: The radius of the circular face.
The area of the circular face.
The surface area of the cylinder.

lessons.title: Problem solving with perimeter, area and volume
lessons.outcome: I can use my knowledge of perimeter, area and volume to solve problems.
keyLearningPoints: The volume and surface area of shapes made from prisms and cylinders can be found.
The volume and surface area of shapes made from parts of prisms and cylinders can be found.
Unknown lengths can be found when surface area or volume are known.
Volume and surface area can be used in context to solve problems.

keywords.definition: polyhedron with a base that is a polygon and identical parallel opposite face whose corresponding edges are joined by parallelograms.
3D shape with a circle base and an identical parallel opposite face. Cross sections made parallel to the base will be congruent to the base.
the total area of all the surfaces of a closed 3D shape. The surfaces include all faces and any curved surfaces.

starterQuiz.stem: A hexagonal prism has a cross-sectional area of 62 cm² and a length of 5 cm. What is the volume of the prism?

starterQuiz.stem: A cylinder has a volume of $$252\pi\text{ cm}^3$$ and an integer length. Which of these could be the radius?
starterQuiz.hint: Find factors of 252 that are also square numbers.
starterQuiz.feedback: The volume is found from squaring the radius and multiplying by the length and $$\pi$$. So you need to find some square factors of 252 which are 1, 4, 9 and 36. So the radius could be 1 cm, 2 cm, 3 cm or 6 cm.

exitQuiz.stem: A composite prism can be created by using two or more {{ }}.

exitQuiz.stem: A cube has a volume of 125 cm³. The edge length of the cube is {{ }} cm.

exitQuiz.feedback: The volume of a cube is the edge length cubed, so to undo cubing you need to cube root. The cube root of 125 is 5.

exitQuiz.stem: A cube has a volume of 64 cm³. The area of one face is {{ }} cm².
exitQuiz.hint: Find the edge length of the cube and then find the area of a square with that edge length.
exitQuiz.feedback: The cube root of 64 is 4, so the edge length is 4 cm and the area of one face is 4 cm × 4 cm = 16 cm²

exitQuiz.stem: A cylinder has a volume of $$300\pi\text{ cm}^3$$ and a length of $$3\text{ cm}$$. The surface area of the cylinder is {{ }} $$\pi\text{ cm}^2$$.
exitQuiz.hint: Start by finding the area of the circular cross-section.
exitQuiz.feedback: Area of circular end face = $$300 \pi \div 3 = 100 \pi $$. Since area  = $$\pi r^2$$ then $$r^2 = 100$$ and $$r=10$$. The area of the curved surface is $$2 \pi \times 10 \times 3 = 60 \pi$$. So the total surface area is $$100 \pi+100 \pi +60 \pi $$.

units.title: Geometrical properties: polygons
units.description: In this unit pupils will investigate internal and external angles of polygons and angles made with a transveral and parallel lines. Pupils will develop their ability to formally prove properties of polygons to generalise.

lessons.title: Checking understanding of angles from KS2

keyLearningPoints: Angles that meet at a point can be identified in diagrams.
Angles that make a straight line can be identified on a diagram.
Vertically opposite angles can be identified on a diagram.

keywords.definition: Supplementary angles are a pair of angles that sum to 180°.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these properties of a polygon always remain invariant when the polygon is reflected?
starterQuiz.hint: When any polygon is reflected, the size of the object remains invariant, but the location of some of its vertices will change.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these properties of a polygon always remain invariant when the polygon is positively enlarged?
starterQuiz.hint: After a positive enlargement, an image will never be a rotation or reflection of its object.
starterQuiz.feedback: After an enlargement, the length of the sides of the polygon may change, but the angles both interior and exterior to the polygon will remain the same.

exitQuiz.stem: Which expression can be used to calculate the sum of interior angles in a polygon by substituting $$n$$ for the number of sides?

exitQuiz.stem: A tetracontagon is a polygon with 40 sides. Its interior angles sum to {{}}°.

exitQuiz.stem: A polygon has interior angles which sum to 720°. The polygon has {{ }} sides.
exitQuiz.hint: You could make an equation by equating $$180(n - 2)$$ to the sum of interior angles.
exitQuiz.feedback: Simplifying $$180(n - 2)=720$$ gives $$n-2=4$$. So a polygon with interior angles summing to 720° has 6 sides.

starterQuiz.hint: Start by finding the sum of the interior angles in a pentagon, either by splitting it into triangles or using a formula.

exitQuiz.stem: Each interior angle in a regular pentagon is {{}}°.

exitQuiz.stem: Is it possible for an octagon to be regular if one of its interior angles is 45°?
exitQuiz.hint: You can work out the sum of interior angles in an octagon by splitting into triangles or using a formula.
exitQuiz.feedback: Interior angles in an octagon sum to 180° × (8 − 2) = 1080° but 8 × 45° = 360°. So it is not possible for an octagon to be regular if one of its interior angles is 45°.

exitQuiz.stem: Which calculations can be used to find the size of the shaded angle? [image]

keywords.definition: Corresponding angles are a pair of angles at different vertices on the same side of a transversal in equivalent positions.
A pair of angles both between or both outside two line segments that are on opposite sides of the transversal that cuts them.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each pair of angles with the keywords that describe the relationship between them. [image]

starterQuiz.stem: Each interior angle in a regular octagon is {{}}°.
starterQuiz.hint: An octagon has eight sides.
starterQuiz.feedback: The sum of the exterior angles for any polygon is 360° and an octagon has 8 sides. So each exterior angle for a regular octagon is 360° ÷ 8 = 45°. The exterior and interior angles lie on a straight line, so the interior angle is 180° − 45°= 135°.

exitQuiz.hint: Angles in a quadrilateral sum to 360°.

exitQuiz.hint: Imagine you knew the value of $$x$$ in each diagram and then consider what calculations you would do to find the value of $$y$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: The sides of the parallelogram are parallel, so $$y=180-x$$ because co-interior angles sum to 180°.

exitQuiz.stem: The size of the angle marked in the diagram is {{}}°. [image]

exitQuiz.feedback: The interior angles in a regular hexagon are 120° and the triangle is isosceles. So the size of the angle marked in the diagram is 30°.

exitQuiz.stem: The size of the angle marked in the diagram is {{}}°. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Start by finding the size of interior angles in a regular hexagon.
exitQuiz.feedback: The marked angle = interior angle of hexagon - exterior angle of hexagon. The exterior angles in a regular hexagon are all 360° ÷ 6 = 60° and so the interior angles are all 120°. So the size of the angle marked is 120°−60° = 60°.
