exitQuiz.hint: Work out the diameter of each circle.
exitQuiz.feedback: The diameter of the large circle is 20 cm and the diameter of the small circle is 12 cm. Therefore the distance from A to D is 32 cm.

exitQuiz.stem: The image shows a circle with centre at point A. Sofia draws a circle with radius 4 cm with its centre at point B. How many times will the two circles intersect? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Work out the shortest distance between point B and the circle shown.
exitQuiz.feedback: The shortest distance between point B and the circle shown is 3 cm. So a circle with radius 4 cm would insect the large circle twice.

exitQuiz.stem: Aisha draws two circles. One has a radius 5 cm, the other has a radius 9 cm. The distance between the centre points of each circle is 14 cm. Which image matches Aisha's drawings?
exitQuiz.hint: Find the sum of the two radii.
exitQuiz.feedback: The circles must intersect exactly once with each centre outside of the other circle. The distance between the two centre points would then be 14 cm.

lessons.title: Understanding constructing a circle
lessons.outcome: I can recognise a circle as a collection of points equidistant from a fixed point.
keyLearningPoints: A pair of compasses can be used to draw circle with a particular radius.
All the points on the circle will be the same distance from the centre.
The centre of a circle is the point that is the same distance from every point on the circle.
The collection of points an equal distance from a given point form a circle.

keywords.definition: A fixed point is a point that does not change or move.
The circumference of a circle is the perimeter of the circle.
An arc is part of a curve. An arc of a circle is part of the circle’s circumference.
Points A and B are equidistant from a third point C if the distance AC is equal to the distance BC.

starterQuiz.stem: Which part of the circle is highlighted and labelled with a question mark? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: It is part of the distance around the edge of the circle.
starterQuiz.feedback: An arc of a circle is part of the circle’s circumference.

starterQuiz.stem: What are the co-ordinates of point A? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: A pair of co-ordinates shows the horizontal position followed by the vertical position.
starterQuiz.feedback: Point A is at (-4, 2).

starterQuiz.stem: Izzy tries to draw a circle with a pair of compasses without moving the ruler. The pencil starts at the 2 cm mark on the ruler. Half way around, the pencil touches the {{ }} cm mark on the ruler. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Start by working out the distance between the needle and pencil tip.
starterQuiz.feedback: The circle will have radius 6 cm. The centre of the circle is at the 8 cm mark on the ruler, so it will touch the ruler again at the 14 cm mark.

starterQuiz.stem: The image shows a circle with centre at point A. Sofia draws a circle with radius 2 cm with its centre at point B. How many times will the two circles intersect? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Work out the shortest distance between point B and the circle shown.
starterQuiz.feedback: The shortest distance between point B and the circle shown is 3 cm. So a circle with radius 2 cm would not intersect the large circle.

starterQuiz.stem: The diagram is not to scale. Points A, B, C and D lie on a straight line. The distance from A to D is 20 cm. The radius of the large circle is 8 cm; the radius of the small circle is {{ }}. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Start by finding the diameter of each circle.
starterQuiz.feedback: The diameter of the large circle is 16 cm, so the diameter of the small circle is 4 cm. Therefore, the radius of the small circle is 2 cm.

starterQuiz.stem: Laura draws two circles. One has a radius 5 cm, the other has a radius 9 cm. The distance between the centre points of each circle is 16 cm. Which image matches Aisha's drawings?
starterQuiz.hint: Find the sum of the two radii.
starterQuiz.feedback: The sum of the radii is 14 cm but the centres are 16 cm apart. So the circles must not intersect.

exitQuiz.stem: A circle is a shape such that every point is {{ }} to its centre.
exitQuiz.hint: The radius is a line segment from the centre of the circle to its edge. The radius is the same length in every direction.
exitQuiz.feedback: A circle is a shape such that every point is equidistant to its centre.

exitQuiz.stem: Sam is stood in the centre of a circle. Which pupil is the closest to Sam? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Every point on the circle is equidistant from its centre.
exitQuiz.feedback: Jun is the closest because he is inside the circle.

exitQuiz.stem: The pair of compasses in the image are used to draw a circle around the origin of the co-ordinate grid. Which point would lie on the circle? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Start by working out the radius of the circle.
exitQuiz.feedback: The radius of the circle is 4 units so it would go through (0, -4), as well as (0, 4) and (-4, 0).

exitQuiz.stem: The pair of compasses in the image are used to draw a circle around the origin of the co-ordinate grid. The diameter of the circle is {{ }} units. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Start by working out the radius of the circle. The diameter is double the radius.
exitQuiz.feedback: The radius of the circle is 4 units, so the diameter is 8 units.

exitQuiz.stem: The images show a wrecking ball swinging from a fixed point on a crane. Which image correctly shows the movement of the wrecking ball?
exitQuiz.hint: The wrecking ball will remain equidistant from the fixed point.
exitQuiz.feedback: The wrecking ball will swing in the arc of a circle. Every point on the arc of a circle is equidistant to its centre.

exitQuiz.stem: Which arc will the pair of compass draw? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Each point on the arc of a circle is equidistant to a fixed point.
exitQuiz.feedback: Each point along arc D is equidistant from the needle of the pair of compasses.

lessons.title: Constructing triangles
lessons.outcome: I can use intersecting circles to construct triangles from given lengths.
keyLearningPoints: A construction is an accurate drawing made using geometrical properties.
A scalene triangle can be constructed using intersecting circles with different radii.
An equilateral triangle can be constructed using intersecting circles with equal radii.
An isosceles triangle can be constructed using intersecting circles.

keywords.definition: Scalene triangles have three different-sized angles and three edges of different lengths.
Isosceles triangles have two equal-sized angles. Two of the edges are equal in length.
Equilateral triangles have three equal-sized angles and three edges of equal length. They are regular triangles.
The radius is any line segment that joins the centre of a circle to any point on its circumference.

starterQuiz.stem: Match the angle size to the type of angle.
starterQuiz.hint: Obtuse angles are more than $$90^\circ$$ and less than $$180^\circ$$.
starterQuiz.feedback: Right angles are shown by using a square angle marker.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these sketched triangles are definitely isosceles?
starterQuiz.hint: Isosceles triangles have two equal-sized angles. Two of the three edges are equal in length.
starterQuiz.feedback: The first isosceles triangle (choice 1) has exactly two equal edges labelled as 12 cm = 120 mm. The second isosceles triangle (choice 4) has exactly two equal-sized angles marked.

starterQuiz.stem: Lucas has used a centimetre ruler to draw a line of 8.2 cm. Which image shows his line?
starterQuiz.hint: Each of the shorter marks on the ruler indicates one tenth of a centimetre: a millimetre.
starterQuiz.feedback: Being accurate when drawing a line segment of a particular length is very important.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these shows the best set up of a pair of compasses?
starterQuiz.hint: The sharp tip of the pencil needs to be level with the needle point of the pair of compasses.
starterQuiz.feedback: Although any pencil is fine, having a shorter pencil is more useful as it is less likely to collide with your hand when using the pair of compasses.

starterQuiz.stem: An arc of a circle is part of the circle’s {{ }}.
starterQuiz.hint: It is the correct word for the perimeter of a circle.
starterQuiz.feedback: All points along the arc are a fixed distance (the radius) from the centre of the circle.

starterQuiz.stem: A triangle has a perimeter of 65 mm. Two of the edges are 23 mm and 26 mm respectively. How long is the third edge of the triangle?
starterQuiz.hint: The perimeter is the distance around a 2D shape.
starterQuiz.feedback: The third edge can be calculated by $$65 - (23 + 26) = 16$$.

exitQuiz.stem: Which description matches this sketch? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: All three of the edges need to be in the correct positions relative to the vertices.
exitQuiz.feedback: If you were to sketch any of the descriptions, the physical size of the triangle would be correct but the vertices would be in the wrong positions.

options.text: Triangle PQR, where PQ  = 7 cm, PR = 12 cm and QR = 14 cm
Triangle PQR, where PQ  = 7 cm, PR = 14 cm and QR = 12 cm
Triangle PQR, where PQ  = 12 cm, PR = 14 cm and QR = 7 cm
Triangle PQR, where PQ  = 14 cm, PR = 7 cm and QR = 12 cm
Triangle PQR, where PQ  = 14 cm, PR = 12 cm and QR = 7 cm

exitQuiz.stem: When constructing a triangle from three edge lengths, we use a pair of compasses to draw {{ }} circles.
exitQuiz.hint: The circles overlap with each other. The point of intersection is the location of the vertex.
exitQuiz.feedback: The three edge lengths are the radii of the circles/arcs that are being drawn using the pair of compasses.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the following shows a partial construction of an equilateral triangle?
exitQuiz.hint: The radii of the arcs will be the same length as the base edge.
exitQuiz.feedback: To finish the construction, the point of intersection needs to be joined to the ends of the base edge with line segments.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the following lengths could be the edge lengths of a triangle?
exitQuiz.hint: The sum of the two shortest edges needs to be greater than the longest edge length.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the points C, D or E when connected to AB would create a triangle with three edges of different lengths? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: AD = AB
exitQuiz.feedback: If each circle's radius is one unit more each time, then the edges of triangle ABC are 5 units, 3 units and 4 units. This is a right-angled scalene triangle.

exitQuiz.stem: Triangle ABE is an {{ }} triangle. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: AE has a length of 3 units; what is the length of BE?
exitQuiz.feedback: As two of the edges of triangle ABE are equal, it is an isosceles triangle.

lessons.title: Constructing rhombi
lessons.outcome: I can use intersecting circles to construct rhombi from given lengths.
keyLearningPoints: A rhombus can be created from two isosceles triangles.
An isosceles triangle can be constructed from a given base and side lengths using intersecting circles.
A rhombus can be constructed from intersecting circles using triangles.

keywords.definition: A rhombus is a parallelogram where all sides are the same length.
The plural of rhombus can be referred to as rhombi.

starterQuiz.stem: {{ }} triangles have two equal-sized angles. Two of the three edges are equal in length.
starterQuiz.hint: The word comes from two ancient Greek words, isos = equal and skelos = legs.
starterQuiz.feedback: Isosceles triangles have two equal-sized angles. Two of the three edges are equal in length.

starterQuiz.stem: As this triangle is isosceles, the angle marked $$a$$ is {{ }}$$^\circ$$. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The unmarked angle is also $$74^\circ$$ as this is an isosceles triangle and the sum of the interior angles in a triangle is $$180^\circ$$.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these could be a sketch of an equilateral triangle?
starterQuiz.hint: An equilateral triangle has three equal angles, all of which are $$60^\circ$$.
starterQuiz.feedback: If the edges marked with the hash marks are also 7 cm, then all three edges are equal and it is an equilateral triangle.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of the following sets of lengths could be the edges of a triangle?
starterQuiz.hint: The sum of the two shortest lengths needs to be more than the longest length.
starterQuiz.feedback: 6 + 8 > 10, 1.2 + 4.7 > 5.2 and 10 + 12 > 18 so these three form triangles with those lengths.

starterQuiz.stem: Select all the statements which are true of all quadrilaterals.
starterQuiz.hint: A kite does not have a set of parallel sides.
starterQuiz.feedback: As all quadrilaterals can be split into two triangles, and each triangle's interior angles sum to $$180^\circ$$ then a quadrilateral's interior angles must sum to $$2\times180^{\circ} = 360^\circ$$.

options.text: Interior angles of all quadrilaterals sum to $$180^\circ$$.
All quadrilaterals have at least one set of parallel sides.
All quadrilaterals can be split into two triangles.
All quadrilaterals have a right angle.

starterQuiz.stem: Put the steps of constructing an equilateral triangle in order.
starterQuiz.hint: The first step is to draw an edge, the last step is connecting the point of intersection. It might be helpful to construct an equilateral triangle yourself and think of each step to put these in order.
starterQuiz.feedback: If you draw the full circle rather than arcs, you will see that the other two vertices are on the circumference of the circle around the third vertex.

order.text: Use your pencil and ruler to draw one edge to the required length.
Set the width of the pair of compasses to the length of the drawn edge.
With the needle point on one end of the line segment, draw an arc.
Put the needle point on the other end of the line segment.
Check the width of the pair of compasses is still the length of the edge.
Draw an arc, which intersects with the first arc.
Connect the point of intersection to the ends of the line segment.

exitQuiz.stem: This kite has be created by using two triangles, joined by a common edge length. The two triangles are ... [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Each triangle has two equal edges, so they are isosceles.
exitQuiz.feedback: If the two isosceles triangles were congruent then this would be a rhombus.

exitQuiz.stem: A rhombus is a {{ }} where all sides are the same length.
exitQuiz.hint: This shape is a quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel and equal sides.
exitQuiz.feedback: A rhombus is a special case of a parallelogram, which means all rhombi are parallelograms but not all parallelograms are rhombi.

exitQuiz.stem: A rhombus is a quadrilateral where ...
exitQuiz.hint: A rhombus can be constructed using two congruent isosceles triangles because there is symmetry.
exitQuiz.feedback: When the angles are equal in a rhombus, then it is a special case, which is a square.

options.text: ...there are two sets of parallel sides.
...there are two sets of equal angles.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these show the correct construction of a rhombus?
exitQuiz.hint: A rhombus needs to have equal edges, so the intersecting arcs need to have the same radius.
exitQuiz.feedback: One of the constructions is with congruent equilateral triangles and the other is with congruent isosceles triangles.

exitQuiz.stem: If Jun and Jacob were to both construct a rhombus with edge lengths of 8 cm, would their constructions be identical?
exitQuiz.hint: The base length of the isosceles triangles that are used to construct the rhombus doesn't matter, it is the equal edges that are necessary to construct the rhombus.
exitQuiz.feedback: When equilateral triangles are used to construct a rhombus, the angles are fixed at 60$$^\circ$$ and 120^$$\circ$$, whereas the angles are not fixed with isosceles triangles.

options.text: Yes - both of the rhombi would have edge lengths of 8 cm, so they are the same.
No - they can have the same edges but the angles can be different.
Maybe - if they both constructed the rhombus using equilateral triangles.

exitQuiz.stem: Sofia is constructing a rhombus from one given edge AB. She has nearly finished the construction of rhombus ABCD. Where is vertex D? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The distance between each pair of vertices needs to be the same. All the circles in the construction have the same radius.
exitQuiz.feedback: $$$D_1$$ is not on the circumference of the circle around A, so that length is too short and likewise, $$D_3$$ is not on the circumference of the circle around C.

lessons.title: Diagonals of a rhombus
lessons.outcome: I can appreciate that the diagonals of a rhombus bisect one another at right angles and the angles are bisected.
keyLearningPoints: An isosceles triangle has a line of symmetry that splits it into two congruent triangles.
In a rhombus each diagonal splits the rhombus into two congruent isosceles triangles bisecting the angles.
The two diagonals meet at right angles.
The two diagonals bisect each other.

keywords.definition: To bisect means to cut or divide an object into two equal parts.
The altitude of a triangle is a line segment from a vertex of a triangle to the opposite edge. It is perpendicular to that edge.

starterQuiz.stem: If two lines are perpendicular to each other then they create a {{ }} $$^\circ$$ angle.
starterQuiz.hint: Two perpendicular lines create a right angle at the point of intersection.
starterQuiz.feedback: A right angle has a value of 90$$^\circ$$.

starterQuiz.stem: Match the type of triangle to the interior angles.
starterQuiz.hint: A right-angled triangle must have a 90° angle.
starterQuiz.feedback: The angles of an equilateral, regardless of edge length, are always 60°. The right-angled triangle here is scalene as well.

starterQuiz.stem: How many lines of symmetry does a rhombus have?
starterQuiz.hint: A rhombus can be constructed using two congruent isosceles triangles, joined by the base edge.
starterQuiz.feedback: The base edge of the isosceles triangles that create the rhombus is a line of symmetry.

starterQuiz.stem: The missing angle in this triangle is {{ }}°. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The total of the three angles is 180°.

starterQuiz.stem: Select all of the properties of a rhombus.
starterQuiz.hint: A rhombus is a quadrilateral.
starterQuiz.feedback: By being a quadrilateral, a rhombus has four edges and four angles. By being a rhombus, the opposite angles are equal, the edges are all the same length and there are two sets of parallel sides.

options.text: It has one set of parallel sides.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these is not a construction of a rhombus?
starterQuiz.hint: In a construction of a rhombus, the arcs should have equal radii.
starterQuiz.feedback: The two constructions that are correct for a rhombus have used congruent isosceles triangles.

exitQuiz.stem: To {{ }} means to cut or divide an object into two equal parts.
exitQuiz.hint: 'Bi'cycles have two wheels.
exitQuiz.feedback: The word bisect comes from 'bi' meaning two and the Latin 'secare' which means to cut.

exitQuiz.stem: How many of the altitudes of an isosceles are also a line of symmetry?
exitQuiz.hint: The altitude of a triangle is a line segment from a vertex of a triangle to the opposite edge. It is perpendicular to that edge.
exitQuiz.feedback: The isosceles triangle has three altitudes, but only one of them is a line of symmetry. An isosceles triangle only has one line of symmetry.

exitQuiz.stem: The diagonals of a rhombus ...
exitQuiz.hint: The diagonals are only equal in length when the rhombus is a square.
exitQuiz.feedback: The diagonals of a rhombus are also the lines of symmetry.

exitQuiz.stem: In this diagram of a rhombus and its diagonals, the angle marked b is {{ }}°. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Opposite angles in a rhombus are equal and the diagonal bisects the angle that it passes through.
exitQuiz.feedback: The angle that was given was 58°, so there would be another 58° on the other side of the diagonal. The angle marked $$b$$ is equal to the sum of the two 58° angles.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of the following statements are true about this image? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: $$$a=90$$ as the diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular to each other.

exitQuiz.stem: A rhombus has diagonals with lengths of 8 cm and 12 cm. Which of the following calculations will work out the area of the rhombus?
exitQuiz.hint: Splitting the rhombus into two congruent isosceles triangles may help.
exitQuiz.feedback: The area of this rhombus is $$48\text{ cm}^2$$.

lessons.title: Bisecting an angle
lessons.outcome: I can use the properties of a rhombus to construct an angle bisector.
keyLearningPoints: A rhombus can be constructed from two congruent isosceles triangles.
The diagonals of a rhombus bisect the angles.
It is possible to construct an angle bisector without drawing the rhombus.

keywords.definition: To bisect means to cut or divide an object into two equal parts.
A rhombus is a parallelogram where all sides are the same length.
If one shape can fit exactly on top of another using rotation, reflection or translation, then the shapes are congruent.

starterQuiz.stem: This quadrilateral is a rhombus. What is the size of angle $$x$$? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Opposite angles in a rhombus are equal in size.
starterQuiz.feedback: Opposite angles in a rhombus, or any parallelogram, are always equal in size. So, $$x$$ also equals 128°.

starterQuiz.stem: This quadrilateral is a rhombus. What is the size of angle $$r$$? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: 152° and $$r$$° are co-interior angles.
starterQuiz.feedback: Adjacent angles in a rhombus are always co-interior. Since they share a side of a rhombus that is transversal to two parallel lines, both adjacent angles will always sum to 180°. Therefore, $$r$$ = 180 - 152 = 28°.

starterQuiz.stem: This quadrilateral is a rhombus. What is the perimeter of this rhombus (in cm)? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: All sides on a rhombus are equal in length.
starterQuiz.feedback: Since all sides on a rhombus are equal in length, the perimeter of a rhombus is four times the length of one of its sides. 4 × 36 = 144 cm.

starterQuiz.stem: The rhombus on the right is congruent to the rhombus on the left, with one diagonal drawn. Which of these statements correctly describes the rhombus after its diagonal has been drawn on? [image]
starterQuiz.feedback: Drawing on any diagonal of a rhombus splits the rhombus into two congruent, isosceles triangles that share a base length (the diagonal of the rhombus). This bisects the angle the diagonal passes through, but the other angle does not change.

options.text: The rhombus has been split into two scalene triangles.
The rhombus has been split into two isosceles triangles.
The angle of 80° has been bisected.
The angle of 80° has been cut exactly in half.
All angles in the rhombus are now 40°.

starterQuiz.stem: Both rhombi are congruent, with the right-hand rhombus having both diagonals drawn on. Match the angles in the rhombus to its size. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Angle $$b$$ is the angle 62° after it has been bisected.
starterQuiz.feedback: The angles at the intersection of the two diagonals of a rhombus are always perpendicular.

starterQuiz.stem: Which of these quadrilaterals have the correct feathers, hash marks, and/or angle markers that confirm the shape is a rhombus? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: A pair of sides with a single hash mark are different in length to a pair of sides with a pair of hash marks.
starterQuiz.feedback: Shape a does not show the lengths of its sides, and so could be a parallelogram. Shape c is definitely a parallelogram, as the different hash marks show two different pairs of side lengths. Shape d is impossible.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these diagrams shows the compass width being accurately set to 5 cm? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The needle end and pencil end of the pair of compasses need to be at the two endpoints of a line segment in order to set them to the length of that line segment.
exitQuiz.feedback: In diagram a, the pencil end is at a random point of the line segment, and in diagram c, the needle end is at a random point of a different line segment. Unless there are further construction markings, these diagrams will never give a specific width.

exitQuiz.stem: What is the value of $$r$$, the radius of the circle drawn? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: What width has the pair of compasses been set to?
exitQuiz.feedback: Any correctly drawn circle will have a radius of the same length as the width of the pair of compasses used to draw the circle.

exitQuiz.stem: Which statements are correct about this construction? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The quadrilateral drawn is not a rhombus.
exitQuiz.feedback: Both circles are different in size. Therefore, the point at which both circles intersect does not create the fourth vertex of a rhombus, rather it is the vertex of a random quadrilateral.

options.text: A rhombus has been constructed as both legs of the angle are of equal length.
A rhombus has been constructed as both circles use endpoints A and B as centres.
A rhombus hasn't been constructed as all four sides aren't of equal length.
A rhombus hasn't been constructed as both circles are not the same size.
A rhombus hasn't been constructed as a pair of compasses haven't been used.

exitQuiz.stem: The two legs of the angle are different in length. Which compass placement is correct in order to create a pair of shorter legs of equal length? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The compass needle needs to be at the vertex of the angle.
exitQuiz.feedback: Option a is the only sensible option. The compass needle needs to be at the vertex of the angle, and not at the open endpoint of either leg. The compass width also has to be at a length less than or equal to the shorter leg of the angle.

exitQuiz.stem: This diagram shows the correct constructions to bisect an angle. Which point of intersection between two circles must the bisecting line pass through? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The leftmost circle has a centre at the vertex of the angle, whilst the other two circles have centres at different points on the legs of the angle.
exitQuiz.feedback: The only purpose of the leftmost circle is to shorten the length of each leg so that each leg is the same length, meaning that the new endpoint of each leg can be used as the centres of the other two circles.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these construction arcs could be the first to be drawn in a construction to bisect an angle? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The first step to bisecting an angle is to shorten the lengths of both legs so that they are the same length.
exitQuiz.feedback: The first two arcs must always intersect the two legs of the angle.

lessons.title: Perpendicular bisector of a line segment
lessons.outcome: I can use the properties of a rhombus to construct a perpendicular bisector of a line segment.
keyLearningPoints: A rhombus can be constructed from two congruent isosceles triangles.
The diagonals of a rhombus meet at right angles and bisect each other.
It is possible to construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment without drawing the rhombus.

keywords.definition: To bisect means to cut or divide an object into two equal parts.
A rhombus is a parallelogram where all sides are the same length.

starterQuiz.stem: This quadrilateral is a rhombus with one of its diagonals drawn on. What is the size of angle $$p$$? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The diagonal of a rhombus bisects an angle.
starterQuiz.feedback: The angle 86° is bisected by the diagonal that passes through it, and half of 86° is 43°.

starterQuiz.stem: This quadrilateral is a rhombus with one of its diagonals drawn on. What is the size of angle $$m$$? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The triangle created by the diagonal bisecting the rhombus is an isosceles triangle. The diagonal line segment is also the base side of the triangle.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$m$$ + 35 + 35 = 180, as the unlabelled angle in the triangle is a base angle, just like 35°. Solving the equation gives $$m$$ = 110°.

starterQuiz.stem: This quadrilateral is a rhombus with both of its diagonals drawn on. Match the angles in the rhombus to its size. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: When angle $$b$$ is bisected, the resultant angles are of equal size to angle $$a$$ and the 22° angle.
starterQuiz.feedback: The angles at the intersection of the two diagonals of a rhombus are always perpendicular.

starterQuiz.stem: What is the area of this rhombus? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The area of a rhombus can be found by multiplying the two diagonals, which are always perpendicular to each other.
starterQuiz.feedback: The side length of 5 cm is not used to calculate the area of a rhombus; only the product of the two diagonals (6 cm and 8 cm) is needed.

starterQuiz.stem: A rhombus has side length of 41 cm, and diagonals of length 18 cm and 80 cm. What is the area of this rhombus (in cm²)?
starterQuiz.hint: The area of a rhombus can be found by multiplying the two diagonals, which are always perpendicular to each other.
starterQuiz.feedback: The side length of 41 cm is not used to calculate the area of a rhombus; only the product of the two diagonals (18 cm and 80 cm) is needed.

starterQuiz.stem: This triangle is reflected with the line of reflection at its base side. The resultant quadrilateral is a rhombus. What is the area of this rhombus (in cm²)? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: One diagonal of the rhombus will be 10 cm, and the other diagonal will be double the perpendicular height of the original isosceles triangle.
starterQuiz.feedback: The rhombus will be reflected on the side of length 10 cm. This means that the side length of the rhombus will be 13 cm, and the other diagonal will be of length 2 × 12 = 24 cm.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these diagrams show a perpendicular bisector on a rhombus? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Two of the diagrams show a perpendicular, as the two diagonals of the quadrilateral intersect at right angles. However, notice how both diagonals do not intersect at the midpoint of the other diagonal.
exitQuiz.feedback: Both diagrams a and c are kites, and so whilst the diagonals do meet at a right angle, one diagonal does not bisect the other. Diagram e shows a parallelogram, whose diagonals do bisect each other, but not at a right angle.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these compass widths are suitable when constructing the perpendicular bisector of the given line segment? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: It is possible to construct a perpendicular bisector with any compass width over half the length of the line segment.
exitQuiz.feedback: Compass width a is shorter than half the length of the line segment, and so it is not possible to construct a perpendicular bisector. Whilst it is possible with compass width c, it can be tricky to draw accurate circles when the compass is too wide.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these constructions can be used to draw on the perpendicular bisector of the line segment given? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Both circles must intersect enough that two distinct pairs of intersections are visible.
exitQuiz.feedback: The circles on construction e intersect, but only once, making it impossible to construct a perpendicular, even if the one point with which the two circles intersect bisects the line segment. One circle on construction c has an inappropriate centre.

exitQuiz.stem: Each of the two circles has been drawn with a radius of 7 cm, one with centre Y, and the other with centre Z. Match the statement to the point it describes. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Any point to the left of the perpendicular bisector is closer to point Y, and any point to the right of the perpendicular bisector is closer to point Z.
exitQuiz.feedback: Whilst point B is on the circle with radius Y, it is to the right of the perpendicular bisector, and so is closer to point Z.

match.left: 7 cm away from Y and greater than 7 cm away from Z.
7 cm away from Y and less than 7 cm away from Z.
7 cm away from Z and greater than 7 cm away from Y.
7 cm away from both Y and Z.

exitQuiz.stem: Lucas wants to construct the perpendicular bisector of line segment RS, which has a length of 18 cm. Which of these construction methods are possible?
exitQuiz.hint: The radius of the arcs cannot be less than or equal to half the length of the line segment.
exitQuiz.feedback: In order for a perpendicular bisector to be constructed, the radii of both arcs must be the same, and so whilst option 5 has circles large enough to intersect, they will not produce a bisector.

options.text: Constructing arcs of radius 6 cm at both points R and S.
Constructing arcs of radius 9 cm at both points R and S.
Constructing arcs of radius 12 cm at both points R and S.
Constructing arcs of radius 18 cm at both points R and S.
Constructing an arc of radius 12 cm at R and an arc of radius 18 cm at S.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these statements is true about this construction? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The perpendicular bisector to a line segment can only be constructed through the two intersections of two different pairs of arcs.
exitQuiz.feedback: It is impossible to tell whether a perpendicular bisector has or has not been constructed, but the construction to fully show that the line is a perpendicular bisector is incomplete. Two more intersecting arcs need to be drawn below XY.

options.text: A perpendicular bisector to YZ has definitely been constructed.
A perpendicular bisector to YZ has definitely not been constructed.
The construction of the perpendicular bisector to YZ is incomplete.
The angle between the two line segments is 88°.
Two more arcs need to be constructed.

lessons.title: Perpendicular to a given line through a given point
lessons.outcome: I can use the properties of a rhombus to construct a perpendicular to a given line through a given point.
keyLearningPoints: A rhombus can be constructed from two congruent isosceles triangles.
This can be used to construct a perpendicular to a line through a point.
This perpendicular has special properties that can be investigated.
Shortest distances can be found using constructions with perpendicular lines.

keywords.definition: To bisect means to cut or divide an object into two equal parts.
A rhombus is a parallelogram where all sides are the same length.

starterQuiz.stem: This quadrilateral is a kite. Find the value of angle $$a$$, in degrees. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The interior angles in a quadrilateral sum to 360°.
starterQuiz.feedback: One pair of opposite angles in a kite are equal. Since 113° and 47° are not equal, the $$a$$° and the unmarked angle must be equal. 360 - 113 - 47 = 200, and so 200° must be distributed equally between these two angles.

starterQuiz.stem: This diagram shows an accurate construction of a perpendicular bisector. YZ has a length of 8.4 cm. Which of these is the smallest value of $$r$$ that can be used in this construction? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: In order for the two circles in this construction to intersect, their radius must be over half the length of the line segment.
starterQuiz.feedback: Whilst 4.3 cm makes the construction possible, the rhombus drawn from this construction will be very short and difficult to use in practice. A circle with a radius in between 4.3 and 8.4 cm will be easier to use in this construction.

starterQuiz.stem: Match the sentence to the diagram. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: A single hash mark to the left and right of the intersecting line means both the left and right parts of line segment QV are equal in length.
starterQuiz.feedback: Diagram c is the only perpendicular bisector, as the line intersects at a right angle, and divides QV into two equal parts. Whilst b intersects QV at a right angle, it intersects closer to point V.

match.left: A bisector to line segment QV
A perpendicular to line segment QV
A perpendicular bisector to line segment QV
An intersecting line to line segment QV

starterQuiz.stem: This is an incomplete construction to find the perpendicular bisector of YZ. Which of these steps is missing from this construction? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: In a different construction of a perpendicular bisector, the perpendicular bisecting line would pass through the two intersections of two full circles.
starterQuiz.feedback: The perpendicular bisector must pass through two pairs of intersecting arcs - you can never assume perpendicularity from just one intersection.

options.text: A circle with centre at point Y.
A line segment connecting the intersection to point Z.
An arc below YZ with centre at point Z.
An arc above YZ with centre at point Z.
A line through two pairs of intersecting arcs.

starterQuiz.stem: This is an accurate construction to draw a rhombus. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the rhombus that can be drawn from this construction? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The radius of the circle is equal to the distance between the endpoint of the line segment and an intersection between two arcs.
starterQuiz.feedback: The perimeter of a rhombus constructed in this way is four times the radius of the circles used in the construction.

starterQuiz.stem: Sofia starts her construction of a perpendicular bisector to EF. She is about to move the pair of compoasses to construct a second circle. Which of these statements are true? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Both circles need to have the same radius when constructing a perpendicular bisector.
starterQuiz.feedback: If Sofia doesn't first readjust the compass width by placing the compass needle at point E, and the pencil at a point on the circumference of the already drawn circle, both circles will be different sizes, and the construction will be incorrect.

options.text: Sofia needs to place the compass needle at the midpoint of EF.
Sofia should draw a circle with centre at the intersection of EF and the circle.
Sofia needs to draw an arc with centre at point F next.
Sofia should adjust the compass width so that both circles drawn are congruent.
Currently, the next circle Sofia draws will be smaller than the first.

exitQuiz.stem: The line segment EF has been shortened by constructing a circle of radius 8 cm, with a centre at point K. What is the length (in cm) of the shortened line segment? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The shortened line segment is the diameter of the circle that has been constructed.
exitQuiz.feedback: When shortening a line segment to construct a perpendicular, the length of the shortened line segment will always be twice the compass width you set to construct the circle.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these diagrams shows the most appropriate first step when constructing the perpendicular to line segment TU through point Z? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The circle must intersect TU twice.
exitQuiz.feedback: Whilst both diagrams c and d make it possible to construct a perpendicular through point Z, the circle in diagram c is very small, and may reduce the precision with which subsequent constructions are made.

exitQuiz.stem: Izzy has shortened line segment LM by drawing a circle with centre at point Z. Izzy wants to draw four arcs of radius $$k$$ cm to construct a perpendicular. What value must $$k$$ be greater than? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The radius of the arcs needed to construct a perpendicular must be greater than half the length of the shortened line segment.
exitQuiz.feedback: The compass width must be set to greater than 12 cm so that the arcs can intersect each other.

exitQuiz.stem: A line segment is extended so that a perpendicular can be constructed through point Z. Which of these diagrams shows a suitable extension of the line segment? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: The line segment must be extended so that the line segment intersects the circle twice. The current line segment only intersects it once.
exitQuiz.feedback: Diagram b is the only diagram whose extended line segment intersects the circle twice. Diagrams a and c have extended the line segment, but not enough or not in the correct direction, whilst diagram d has prematurely attempted a perpendicular.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these four circles can help in the construction of the perpendicular to line segment WU through point Z? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Line segment WU can be extended if this helps intersect with an appropriate circle twice.
exitQuiz.feedback: Circle a is too small, and circle d has its centre at point W, when the centre should be at point Z.

exitQuiz.stem: Match the values to their statements. [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Point J is further away from X than point K. Therefore the distance from X to J cannot be the shortest distance from X to the line segment.
exitQuiz.feedback: It is important to be aware of the difference between the shortest distance to a line segment, and the shortest distance to an extension of a line segment. Both measurements have their benefits in different contexts.

match.left: the shortest distance from X to an extension of JK
the shortest distance from X to line segment JK
the radius of circle with centre at point X
the shortest distance from X to point J

lessons.title: Problem solving with constructions
lessons.outcome: I can use my knowledge of constructions to solve problems.
keyLearningPoints: Shapes made from triangles can be constructed.
By investigation it is possible to accurately construct multiple polygons.
Shortest distances can be found using constructions with perpendicular lines.

keywords.definition: To bisect means to cut or divide an object into two equal parts.
A rhombus is a parallelogram where all sides are the same length.

starterQuiz.stem: This quadrilateral is a rhombus. Find the value of $$a+b+c$$. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: Angle $$a$$ has the same value as the bisection of angle $$b$$. This means that angle $$b$$ is twice the size of $$a$$.
starterQuiz.feedback: $$$a$$ = 90 - 65 = 25, and therefore $$b$$ = 50. The angle at the intersection of the diagonals of a rhombus is always 90°. Therefore, the sum of $$a$$, $$b$$, and $$c$$ is 25 + 50 + 90 = 165.

starterQuiz.stem: This triangle is reflected with the line of reflection at its base side. The resultant quadrilateral is a rhombus. What is the area of this rhombus (in cm²)? [image]
starterQuiz.hint: One diagonal of the rhombus will be 22 cm, and the other diagonal will be double the perpendicular height of the original isosceles triangle.
starterQuiz.feedback: The rhombus will be reflected on the side of length 22 cm. This means that the side length of the rhombus will be 61 cm, and the other diagonal will be of length 2 × 60 = 120 cm.

starterQuiz.stem: This hexagon is regular. Find the size of angle $$v$$, in degrees. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: An interior angle of a regular hexagon is 120°.
starterQuiz.feedback: This value can be found in several ways. One way is to use the isosceles triangle on the bottom of the hexagon. Its two base angles are both 30°. The bottom left angle in the hexagon is then split into two parts, the 30° and the 120 - 30 = 90° parts.

starterQuiz.stem: The triangle is equilateral, with two angle bisectors extending from the bottom two angles of the equilateral triangle and intersecting inside the triangle. Find the size of angle $$w$$. [image]
starterQuiz.hint: An interior angle of an equilateral triangle is 60°, and therefore its angle bisected is 30°. The triangle that exists inside the equilateral triangle is isosceles.
starterQuiz.feedback: The isosceles triangle inside the equilateral one has base angles of 30° each. Therefore, the interior angle at the top of the isosceles triangle is 180 - 30 - 30 = 120°. Angles around a point sum to 360°, therefore $$w$$ = 360 - 120 = 240°.

starterQuiz.stem: This diagram shows a kite enclosed by a rectangle. If the rectangle has an area of 780 cm², find the area of the kite, in cm². [image]
starterQuiz.hint: The diagonals of the kite split the larger rectangle up into four smaller rectangles. A part of the kite takes up half the area of each smaller rectangle.
starterQuiz.feedback: The area of this kite can be found by halving the product of its two diagonals, as the product of the two diagonals equals the area of the rectangle that encloses it.

starterQuiz.stem: This kite has an area of 270 cm². What is the area of the shaded region: the right-angled triangle on the top, right of the kite? Give your answer in cm². [image]
starterQuiz.hint: If the area of the kite is 270 cm², and the diagonal height is 30 cm, then its diagonal width is 18 cm.
starterQuiz.feedback: If the diagonal width of the kite is 18 cm, then the width of the shaded triangle is 9 cm. The height of the shaded triangle is 30 - 24 = 6 cm. Therefore, the area of this shaded triangle is $$1\over2$$ × 6 × 9 = 27 cm².

exitQuiz.stem: In this six-petal flower construction, at how many points does circle A intersect with at least one other circle? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: Circle A intersects with some circles more than once, and intersects with more than one circle at a given point.
exitQuiz.feedback: Each circle not at the centre of the construction intersects five times. However, it intersects with two circles twice, and intersects with five other circles at the very centre of the construction.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these polygons can be formed by joining up combinations of intersections between any line segment or circle? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: What type of triangle can be formed by joining up each endpoint of the line segment with one of the intersections of the two circles?
exitQuiz.feedback: A right-angled, scalene triangle can be formed by creating an equilateral triangle and drawing on the perpendicular bisector of the original line segment.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these polygons can be formed by joining up combinations of intersections between any line segment or circle? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: What polygon can be formed by joining up each endpoint of the line segment with both intersections of two of the circles?
exitQuiz.feedback: A pentagon can be formed by joining up the four intersections between pairs of circles and one endpoint of the line segment. This pentagon will have two right angles and three 120° angles.

exitQuiz.stem: Which of these statements is true about the construction of a perpendicular bisector?
exitQuiz.hint: If two circles are of different sizes, a kite can be constructed. One diagonal of a kite does not bisect the other diagonal of a kite.
exitQuiz.feedback: A perpendicular bisector can be constructed by joining an intersection of a pair of congruent circles with an intersection of a different pair of congruent circles, as long as their centres are the endpoints of the line segment.

options.text: It is formed from the intersections of two congruent circles.
It is formed from intersections of different pairs of congruent circles.
It can be formed from the intersections of any two circles.
At least one circle must have its centre at the midpoint of a line segment.
All circles must have their centres at the endpoints of a line segment.

exitQuiz.stem: Which two pairs of points need to be joined with a line segment to find the fourth point in the kite? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: One point on the larger circle must be joined with a point on the smaller circle.
exitQuiz.feedback: The point where the two new line segments intersect is joined up to the vertex of the angle in order to bisect that angle. This can be done to bisect either the acute/obtuse angle or the reflex angle.

exitQuiz.stem: This "crescent moon" logo can be formed using the construction of an equilateral triangle that uses two congruent circles of radius 9 cm. What is the perimeter of this logo (in cm, rounded to 1 dp)? [image]
exitQuiz.hint: A formula for the circumference of a circle is $$2{\times}{\pi}{\times}r$$.
exitQuiz.feedback: The two arcs that form the logo can be rearranged into a full circle with radius 9 cm. The circumference of this circle is 18$$\pi$$.
